result.area: Reconstruct and steelman the founder thesis from the record, then find its blind spot
result.headline: The founder is not asking for a format, a graph, or an editor feature — he is asking for a corpus-level unit for markdown (an artifact whose granularity the reader picks, not the writer), and the blind spot is that this is the ONLY construction that satisfies his own D6 "no new dialect" constraint while every reference-carried design (transclusion, `![[X]]`, capability naming) provably violates it — measured: `![[X]]` renders as the literal string `![[X]]` with the payload absent, while 37.2% of files and 47.7% of bytes in the pinned corpus are ALREADY hand-built multi-document bundles.
result.falsifier:
PRE-REGISTERED, written before the corpus measurements were run. My headline says the mother-markdown image is grounded in the founder's real practice and is the D6-compatible form of what he wants. It would be WRONG if either of these were observed: (A) his own corpus shows him working strictly one-document-per-file, i.e. the image is aspirational rather than a description of what he already does by hand; or (B) reference-carried transclusion degrades acceptably, i.e. `![[X]]` and the mother-markdown are interchangeable and there is no forced choice. I looked for both. (A) FAILED TO REFUTE, and in the founder's favour: 403 of 1,084 files (37.2%), carrying 12,193,061 of 25,548,765 bytes (47.7%), contain >=2 real top-level H1 headings after stripping YAML frontmatter AND fenced code — he already hand-packs bundles across half his corpus by bytes [corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4]. NOTE: my FIRST pass reported 39.1%/48.9% because it counted shell comments (`# Detect project runtime`) inside fenced code blocks as H1s; I caught it by inspecting `md/Skills/GStack/Gstack Ship/skill.md` and re-ran with fence-stripping. The corrected, lower number is the one above. (B) ALSO FAILED TO REFUTE: `marked` (node_modules/marked, run locally) renders `![[Some Note]]` as `

![[Some Note]]

` — the entire referenced document is absent and the residue looks like a typo — whereas ```` ```mermaid ```` renders as `
graph TD; A-->B;
` with the payload intact. Presentation loss and payload loss are different failure classes and the plan's PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT certificate (§4.3) does not distinguish them. WHAT WOULD STILL KILL IT: if a task benchmark shows index+fetch beating an inlined bundle at every corpus size including the no-fetch-tool condition, the image is a preference and not a need. That experiment has never been run (§11 W2: zero live model calls across eighteen research areas).

findings.claim: The founder's central image is stated in transport verbs, not retrieval verbs — the operative words are download, split, read, parse. This is the verbatim source of the 'mother markdown' idea, recovered from the session transcript, not paraphrased from a handoff.
findings.evidence: /Users/sagnikmitra/.claude/projects/-Users-sagnikmitra-Desktop-GitHub-frontmatter/9e5a4a9f-8c4a-4758-b560-0afea2b30447.jsonl — verbatim: "I was mentioning purely about the Markdown tree, Markdown zip file concept, basically folder concept. Markdown is referred to within a Markdown, like a codebase. It will be a Markdown base. I was thinking whether the user should download one zip file of all the Markdowns or one single mother Markdown, which will be very long. Whenever frontmatter or the AI reads that, I will know these are the breakpoints, which means different files, and it can split that Markdown automatically while parsing into different files"

findings.claim: FALSIFIER CHECK, and it confirms rather than refutes: the founder already hand-builds multi-document markdown bundles across nearly half his corpus by bytes. He is not asking for a new behaviour; he is asking for the behaviour he already performs manually to be given a contract.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 — 403/1084 files = 37.2%, carrying 12,193,061 of 25,548,765 bytes = 47.7%, contain >=2 top-level `# ` headings after stripping leading YAML frontmatter AND all fenced code blocks. Largest: md/Courses/WithArin Claude Code/Lesson 2043795 - Reference Guide.md (22 H1s, 150,489 B); md/Untitled.md (5 H1s, 267,187 B) whose H1s read `# Section 1 — App shell, Auth, Config, Native, Assets` / `# Section 2 — Transaction Flows & Payments` — document boundaries, not section headings. findings.claim: Reference-carried payloads CANNOT degrade — they vanish. This is the load-bearing distinction the degradation certificate (§4.3) does not model, and it is what forces the founder's image rather than merely permitting it.

The founder does not, in practice, use the mechanism his own image names. Transclusion is 375:1 rarer than plain linking in his own writing — which means the image is NOT 'I want more embeds', it is something else, and the something else is the bundle.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… — `![[...]]` embeds: 37 occurrences in 17 of 1,084 files (1.57%). Non-embed `[[...]]` wikilinks: 13,891 in 541 files (49.9%). Per root: md 17 embeds / 9,536 links; knowledge 0 embeds / 4,168 links; frontmatter 20 embeds / 187 links (and 19 of those 20 are in docs/mdmap/ concept prose, not content). Script: scratchpad/m2.py, m3.py.

findings.claim: A `## File: <path>` breakpoint SURVIVES a full markdown round trip as a breakpoint, but the PATH INSIDE IT DOES NOT — and the corruption is non-local: the identical heading is byte-stable in isolation and unstable inside the bundle. Prose is not a safe place to carry an identifier. Nobody in the record has stated this requirement.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/rt.mjs and rt2.mjs, mdast-util-from-markdown + mdast-util-to-markdown + GFM, over an explicitly stated selection of 60 files from corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… with 2000<bytes<20000 nearest 8 KB. Breakpoint headings before=60 after=60, but 13/60 path strings altered, e.g. `md/Skills/Printing Press/Pp Docker Hub/workflow.md` -> `md/Skills/Printing Press/Pp Docker Hub/workflow\.md`. Isolation control (rt3.mjs): the same heading alone, and the same heading with its own file body, both round-trip UNCHANGED. Minimal-case control (esc.mjs): `## File: src/index_helper.md` -> `## File: src/index\_helper.md` ALTERED, `## File: a/workflow.md` -> OK. Therefore the escape is triggered by preceding documents in the bundle — the exact context-dependence hazard Wagner & Graham (TOPLAS 1998) name and that HANDOFF-mdz §3.16 flagged as 'the single most concerning theoretical result for a markdown compiler'.

findings.claim: Independent replication of a load-bearing plan number on a different, explicitly stated file selection: zero files survive a parse->stringify round trip. The plan's '0 of 51 files in this repo' is not a repo artefact.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/rt.mjs: per-file parse->stringify byte-identical = 0/60, over the 60-file 8 KB-centred selection from corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… (md + knowledge + frontmatter, not just the frontmatter repo). Compare docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §4.2: '0 of 51 files in this repo survive it byte-identically'. Splice-only (D7) is confirmed, not weakened.

findings.claim: The pack hazards of the founder's own corpus are enumerable and small, which is the strongest practical argument that the bundle is buildable — with one silent byte-corruption class nobody has named.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, scratchpad/m8.py + m10.py, n=1084: 0 files (0.00%) contain a literal `## File: x` line — the repomix breakpoint convention is collision-free on this corpus; 907 (83.67%) begin with YAML frontmatter `---`; 463 (42.71%) contain a ``` fence and the corpus max backtick-run is exactly 3, so a 4-backtick wrapper is provably sufficient; 288 (26.57%) do NOT end with a newline, so naive concatenation silently glues the last line of file N to the first line of file N+1 at 288 of 1,083 boundaries; 7 (0.65%) contain an ODD number of ``` delimiters — each is a poison pill that swallows every following breakpoint until the next fence.

findings.claim: THE SECOND BLIND SPOT: the founder has already authored a 1,409-term controlled vocabulary without being asked, and every artifact in the program classifies it as an error to be dropped or reported. This directly inverts the settled §3.14 finding that users will not declare structure.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, scratchpad/m5.py + m11.py: 10,798 dangling `[[X]]` occurrences over 6,175 distinct targets. 1,409 targets (22.8%) appear in >=2 different documents and account for 5,834 occurrences = 54.0% of all dangling links; 325 appear in >=3. Top repeated: `anthropic` 117, `claude code` 109, `nate herk` 70, `n8n` 62, `codex` 44, `vs code` 42, `openai` 40, `clickup` 36. Only 30 occurrences (0.28%) are mechanically recoverable by re-applying the vault's own filename sanitizer (`:` -> ` -`, e.g. `[[ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting]]` vs the file `ReAct - Synergizing Reasoning and Acting.md`); at most 1,320 (12.22%) are within 0.90 difflib similarity of ANY existing file stem. So ~88% are deliberate entity references, not typos. Meanwhile src/modules/graph/presentation/graph-data.ts:132 reads `if (targetPath === undefined) continue; // unresolved — drop`, docs/mdmap/03-spec/gaps.md calls them the `broken` finding, and PLAN.md §4.6 hunts them for near-misses.

findings.claim: His real link graph is nothing like the image of 'hundreds connected to hundreds' — it is a near-empty mesh around a few generated hubs. The image is therefore a description of a want, not of a system, which is exactly why it has survived four renames without ever being built.

findings.claim: The corpus MDMAX is being designed against is itself substantially machine-authored, and the frontmatter repo's own documents are indistinguishable from pure AI output by the program's own discriminator. The 'collaboration product' is being specified over a corpus with no second human in it.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, scratchpad/m7.py, using PLAN.md §5's own measured discriminator (AI 48.3% vs human 5.3% of list items opening with a bold run, fences excluded): whole corpus 18,922/88,065 = 21.49%; md 19.13%; knowledge 35.54%; frontmatter 46.31%. Two-component mixture estimate p = 37.6% machine-authored share of list-bearing text [inference — a mixture estimate, not a classifier]. 183 of 682 files with >=20 list items sit at >=40%; five sit at 1.00, one of which is `frontmatter/docs/engine/README.md` — the master plan itself.

findings.claim: The pinned corpus that §9.2 introduced as the fix for seven irreproducible file counts still contains machine-generated and non-markdown content, so every corpus-wide figure including my own carries a known contamination floor.

findings.claim: 'Helping out is 50%' is a strategic instruction with a deadline attached, and the plan records the tension it resolves (§13.4) without recording that the founder already answered it.
findings.evidence: Session transcript, verbatim and in full context: "We also have to see the marketability point of how we can market it, why we can market it, what is not there in the current internet that we can provide, what new format we can help the community with, because helping out is also 50% of the part. We are earning our regular cost, which is also 50% of the part of it. The business we are doing is not just for earning money but also for just helping out people, and we are getting no penny." Immediately followed by: "post this point, we will be starting the build process. I will not go back to research." Compare docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §13.4: 'If the engine is marketing, publish the benchmark and the certificate first. If the engine is product, build the compiler first and publish nothing. We have been sequencing as if it is product while justifying it as if it is marketing.' The 50/50 line IS the answer to §13.4 and it is not written down as a decision anywhere in D1–D10.

findings.claim: §7.3's 'INDEX, not container' verdict answered a different question from the one the founder asked, and nobody noticed because both questions use the same words. §7.3 measured a hop where the reader HAS a fetch tool; the founder's hop is the one where it does not.
findings.evidence: HANDOFF-mdmax §7.3 derives 'INDEX, not container' from Anthropic's own docs corpus: index 38,847 B / 174 links vs inlined 6,556,407 B (168.8×), and its supporting evidence is `coding agents (tools with Read/Fetch) were 10% — the largest AI slice`. Every arm of that measurement presumes a reader that can dereference a link. The founder's stated hops are a share, a paste, and a download — and docs/mdmax/PLAN.md D4 explicitly says 'Max tier gets offline access'. An index of 174 links delivered to a reader with no fetcher is 38,847 bytes of nothing. The same handoff records the countervailing fact and does not connect it: '97% of published llms.txt files got zero requests… They never go looking' and 'for CLAUDE.md [Anthropic] gave up on traversal entirely and eagerly inlines imports at launch' — i.e. Anthropic's own answer at the no-guaranteed-traversal boundary is the container.

negatives: INCOMPATIBLE WANT #1 — the export is specified twice and the two specifications are opposites. D2/D4 say 'Export or copy yields clean markdown, latest content only' and 'if frontmatter dies, we ship a full export and migration.' The mother-markdown image says one artifact carries the whole corpus with breakpoints. These cannot both be the export. A clean-markdown export of the founder's own corpus is 1,084 loose files carrying 10,798 dangling links and no map [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…] — it is a durable artifact and a useless one, because everything that made the corpus navigable lived outside the files by construction. A mother-markdown export is NOT 'clean markdown, latest content only'; it is a new artifact with a convention inside it, which is the thing D6 was written to forbid. The record never puts the two sentences on the same page. Someone has to decide what the Max tier's download button produces, and today the plan answers it two ways.

INCOMPATIBLE WANT #2 — 'we can not invent a new markdown, we can not invent a new format' versus 'our editor on the max plan should give features that is unseen in the industry' plus D9 ('a document NAMES a capability'). Measured, these bound each other and the boundary has never been drawn: an unknown fence language round-trips byte-perfectly and a `mermaid` payload survives into HTML, so ADDITIVE capabilities are free; but `![[Some Note]]` renders as the literal text `![[Some Note]]` with the document absent, so any capability whose payload is BY REFERENCE cannot degrade at all. The set of 'features unseen in the industry' that satisfy D6 is therefore exactly the set that puts nothing in the file a plain reader must resolve elsewhere. That is a much smaller set than the roadmap assumes, and it silently excludes transclusion, cross-file reactive state, block-scoped metadata that lives in a sidecar, and any capability whose meaning depends on `fm:vocab:` being understood.

INCOMPATIBLE WANT #3 — the library/import model versus 'no runtime' (§5 settled, D6). §7.1's own agent stated the conclusion and it was recorded without being acted on: 'acquiring a package ecosystem means becoming a programming language, or admitting you are a thin shell over one. Decide which, explicitly, before designing syntax.' The only two document formats that ever acquired a package ecosystem — LaTeX (7,021 CTAN packages) and Typst (1,481) — are both Turing-complete languages. The founder's analogy is Python ('in Python there are thousand libraries people might use hundreds only'), which is a programming language. §11 open decision 3 is still unanswered and it is upstream of the import syntax, not downstream.

AGAINST MY OWN DIRECTION #1 — the market has voted for pack and against unpack, 27,551 stars to 0. repomix has no unpack command; the sole unpack tool on GitHub has zero stars; two repo searches for a markdown bundle/unpack tool return zero results. The straightforward reading is that a bundle is a one-way prompt payload that gets thrown away, and that the round trip the founder describes ('split that Markdown automatically while parsing into different files') solves a problem nobody currently has. My steelman requires the AI to EDIT the bundle and write it back — which is frontmatter's premise but is not evidenced anywhere in the record, and has never been tested with a live model (§11 W2: zero live model calls across eighteen research areas).

AGAINST MY OWN DIRECTION #2 — the founder's own corpus does not support the 'hundreds connected to hundreds' picture that motivates the container. Median out-degree is 2; 508 of 1,084 documents (46.9%) have zero outbound document links; the highest-degree node is a machine-generated graph report. Transclusion, the mechanism he names, appears 37 times in 25.5 MB. If the corpus he is designing for is mostly disconnected single documents, then per-file tooling is adequate for it and the container is solving for a topology he does not have. [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…]

AGAINST MY OWN DIRECTION #3 — the naive bundle is measurably fragile in exactly the way that matters. 13 of 60 breakpoint path strings were corrupted by ONE pass through a standard markdown writer, and the corruption is non-local, so it cannot be prevented by inspecting the file being packed. 288 of 1,084 files (26.57%) do not end with a newline, so concatenation silently welds documents together. 7 files (0.65%) carry unterminated fences that swallow every subsequent breakpoint. Each is fixable, but together they mean the honest engineering estimate for a LOSSLESS bundle is not 'a weekend' — it is the same splice-and-identity discipline the rest of MDMAX needs, which is an argument for sequencing pack/unpack AFTER `mdmax edit`, not before it.

AGAINST THE GAP-REPORT LINEAGE — `mdmap check`, which docs/mdmap/01-thesis/the-gap-is-the-product.md calls the one idea that should survive if only one does, would emit 10,798 `broken` findings on the founder's own corpus, at most 12.2% of which are near-misses and only 0.28% of which are mechanically explicable. A linter with 88% deliberate-false-positive rate is a linter that gets switched off — PLAN.md §4.6 already concedes naive checking runs at 2–25% precision. The gap report is not the product; the vocabulary it mistakes for errors might be.
unclaimed: A LOSSLESS markdown bundle — pack AND unpack, byte-identical on the return trip. Searches run: api.github.com/search/repositories?q=markdown+unpack+bundle+in:name -> total_count 0; q=llm+markdown+bundle+split+files -> total_count 0; q=repomix+unpack -> total_count 1 (jurijat/repomix-unpack, 0 stars); api.github.com/search/code?q=repo:yamadashy/repomix+unpack -> 5 hits, none a CLI command; raw cliRun.ts confirms repomix exposes no unpack subcommand. Against repomix at 27,551 stars, code2prompt at 7,513, files-to-prompt at 2,767, ai-digest at 679 — a category with roughly 38,500 stars of packers and one zero-star unpacker.

A bundle breakpoint that is stable under a markdown round trip. Nobody states the requirement, and it fails silently: measured 13/60 path strings corrupted by mdast-util-to-markdown, non-locally. The fix — carry the authoritative path in a fence info string (a place D8's own rule already blesses: 'extensibility lives in the VALUE of a field') and keep the `## File:` heading as human decoration only — appears nowhere in repomix's template, in HANDOFF-mdmax §7.3, or in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md.

Dangling `[[X]]` treated as a controlled vocabulary rather than as an error. 1,409 targets repeated across >=2 documents, covering 54.0% of dangling occurrences [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…]. Every artifact in the record disposes of them: graph-data.ts:132 `continue`, mdmap's `broken` finding, §4.6's near-miss hunt. Search for prior art: the record's own §3.14 survey (Aquanet, VIKI, Shipman & McCall's incremental formalization, TOIS 17(3) 1999) describes the system SUGGESTING formalization from informal input — which is exactly this — and concluded users will not declare structure. This corpus refutes that conclusion for this user: he declared 6,175 terms unprompted. No tool in the record surfaces them.

A degradation certificate that separates PRESENTATION loss from PAYLOAD loss. PLAN.md §4.3's matrix is PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT over constructs; it has no verdict for 'this construct's content was never in the file.' Measured locally: `![[X]]` -> literal `![[X]]`, payload absent; ```` ```mermaid ```` -> payload preserved in the HTML. That is a fourth verdict — call it VOID — and it is the one that decides which capabilities D6 permits.

An offline/paste-boundary conformance target. §4.3 models targets as (product, surface) renderer pairs. The hop the founder actually names — a share, a paste into a chat box, an offline Max-tier download — has no renderer at all and no fetcher; it is where an index degrades to 174 dead strings and where a bundle is the only artifact that arrives whole. No tool anywhere models 'reader with no dereference capability' as a target.
result.design: SHIPS: `mdmax pack` / `mdmax unpack`, promoted to sit BESIDE `mdmax cert` in the MVP and AHEAD of the doc tree — because it is the one artifact that is simultaneously the founder's most-repeated want, the 'helping out is 50%' public good, and a distribution channel that runs inside other people's context windows. CARRIER, decided by measurement not taste: the authoritative path goes in the FENCE INFO STRING (```` ````md path="md/Skills/Printing Press/Pp Docker Hub/workflow.md" ````), never in heading prose — because a `## File: <path>` heading is stringifier-unstable in 13/60 cases and the instability is non-local. The `## File: <path>` heading is retained ABOVE the fence as human decoration and as a fallback locator, explicitly marked non-authoritative. This is D8 applied to the bundle: extensibility lives in the value of a field. DELIMITER: 4 backticks minimum, computed per bundle as (max backtick run in any member + 1); the pinned corpus's max run is exactly 3, so 4 is sufficient and provable. PER-ENTRY METADATA in the info string: path, sha256, bytes, and `nl=0|1` for the trailing newline (26.57% of files lack one; concatenation silently welds them otherwise). PACK-TIME REFUSALS, each a named error with a fix: unterminated fence in a member (7 files, 0.65% — refuse, do not guess); a member containing the chosen delimiter run (impossible by construction with max+1, but assert it); a path that is not representable. PREAMBLE: an explicit `## How to read this file` block stating the split protocol in prose, per §7.3 and per repomix's own `## File Format` section — this is what lets a model with no MDMAX installed still unpack correctly, and it is the degradation story. DEGRADATION: a bundle opened by any markdown tool is a readable document of headings and code blocks; pasted into a chat box it is the whole corpus; opened in frontmatter it is a project. Nothing in it requires a new parser — D6 is satisfied because the bundle invents a CONVENTION (what a sequence of ordinary constructs means), not a DIALECT (new syntax a parser must understand to read a document). tar did not invent a filesystem; MIME multipart did not invent email. THE PUBLIC-GOOD SHAPE, taking 'helping out is 50%' as a constraint: MIT, zero frontmatter dependency, `npx mdmax pack`, spec and reference unpacker published together, and the format must be forkable without the editor. This also RESOLVES §13.4, which the plan leaves open — the founder has already answered it and the answer was never written down as a decision: the engine is the public good and is published first; the editor is the paid half. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHIP: transclusion, `fm:vocab:`, cross-file reactivity, and any capability whose payload is by reference — measured VOID under plain rendering, therefore excluded by D6, therefore out of scope until someone decides D6 has an exception and writes it down. ALSO PROPOSED, cheap and separable: `mdmax vocab` — list every repeated dangling `[[X]]` with its document set, ranked. It is ~40 lines, it turns the corpus's 10,798 'errors' into a 1,409-term index, and it is the only diagnostic in this program that would tell the founder something about his own writing he does not already know.
result.measurement: TWO EXPERIMENTS, cheap one first, and the cheap one is a gate on the expensive one. E1 — THE ROUND TRIP, no model calls, one day. Write the unpacker FIRST, from the written spec, by a person or agent who has not seen the packer (LR#60: a verifier written in the same session as its subject inherits its blind spots; PLAN.md §11 S4 already demands an independent oracle and this is the same demand one level up). Then: for all 1,084 files of corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, and for 5 bundle sizes (20/50/100/200/400 members, 3 random draws each, seeds recorded), assert unpack(pack(S)) == S byte-identical for every member. Then the adversarial arm, which is the one that matters: assert it STILL holds after the bundle has passed through one `fromMarkdown`/`toMarkdown` round trip, i.e. after any markdown tool, editor, or model has touched it. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, written now: (a) heading-carried paths fail at 15-25% of members after the round trip — my measured point is 13/60 = 21.7%; (b) fence-info-carried paths fail at 0%; (c) trailing-newline loss is the second-largest defect class and is invisible without the `nl` flag; (d) the 7 unterminated-fence files are the only pack-time refusals in the corpus. MAKE IT GO RED FIRST (LR#68): the heading-carried arm must reproduce the `workflow.md -> workflow\.md` corruption before any green result is trusted. E2 — DOES THE READER WANT THE CONTAINER OR THE INDEX, gated on E1 passing, and this is §11 W2 finally being run. Corpus: the same pinned corpus, 5 sizes as above. Tasks: 40 questions with machine-checkable answers, each requiring evidence from 2-5 distinct documents, authored from the corpus by a person, held out. Arms: (1) index + a working fetch tool; (2) inlined bundle, no fetch tool; (3) bundle with an index preamble; (4) flat concatenation, no breakpoints. Verifiers, cheapest-applicable-first (LR#25): exact-match on the answer, plus a byte-identity assertion on any edit the model is asked to write back. n = 40 tasks x 4 arms x 3 seeds = 480 runs per size. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS: arm 1 wins on token cost by >=10x at 400 files; arm 2 beats arm 1 on accuracy whenever the fetch tool is absent, and the margin grows as size falls; arm 3 wins overall at <=100 files; arm 4 loses on both axes at every size; and write-back byte-identity for arms 2 and 3 is below 50% without a stringifier-stable path carrier. Every number reports corpus_id. Every number that comes from replaying data rather than reading a live system says SIMULATED in the same sentence (LR#62 / P9).
result.kill_condition: K-A (kills the container thesis): if an INDEPENDENTLY-WRITTEN unpacker cannot reach >=99.9% byte-identical recovery across all 1,084 files of corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… after the bundle has passed through one standard markdown round trip, then the container cannot carry a write-back and the founder's image collapses to an export nicety. Cut `mdmax pack`, keep only the §4.4 projection tiers, and say so in the plan. K-B (kills my headline specifically): if E2 shows index+fetch beating the inlined bundle on accuracy at every corpus size INCLUDING the no-fetch-tool arm, then §7.3's 'INDEX, not container' was right for the founder's hop too, my central claim that it answered a different question is wrong, and the correct move is to stop treating the mother-markdown as a spine and start treating it as a preference to be politely declined. K-C (kills the vocabulary finding): if a hand-audit of 100 randomly sampled repeated dangling targets finds that fewer than half are deliberate concept references — i.e. they are mostly abandoned drafts, typos, or import artefacts — then `mdmax vocab` is a rename of the broken-link report and should be cut. K-D (kills the whole area's premise): if, when shown the four constructions side by side, the founder says the export he meant was always 'a zip of clean .md files' and never a single artifact, then the mother-markdown image was a passing metaphor rather than the thesis, and four sessions of it recurring were four sessions of us hearing what we wanted. That is one question and it costs one conversation — and it is the same conversation §11 W3 has been asking for.
result.effort: high — full read of docs/mdmap (all 21 files, 01-thesis in full), both HANDOFFs, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md; 13 local measurement scripts against the pinned corpus (integrity-checked, 120-file sha256 sample, 0 mismatches); 3 node round-trip harnesses against the repo's own remark/mdast/marked; primary-read of repomix's markdown output template and CLI source via raw.githubusercontent.com; 6 GitHub API repo/code/repository searches; transcript grep for verbatim founder quotes rather than trusting the handoff's paraphrases. One self-caught measurement defect (H1 counting through fenced code) corrected downward before reporting.
result.unverified: WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, and its real tier. (1) The `workflow.md -> workflow\.md` escape MECHANISM. The fact is own-measurement and reproducible; WHY mdast-util-to-markdown escapes that dot in-bundle and not in isolation is inference — I confirmed it is context-dependent by controlled isolation (rt3.mjs, esc.mjs) but did not read micromark's `unsafe` pattern table to name the rule. Do not cite a cause; cite the observation. (2) The 37.6% machine-authored share is an INFERENCE — a two-component mixture over one construct (bold-leading list items) using the plan's own 48.3%/5.3% anchors, which HANDOFF-mdmax §3 line 18 itself flags as disputed ('I got 50.0% vs 2.2% on a 7-doc spot check'). The per-root observations (21.49% / 46.31%) are own-measurement; the mixture is not a classifier and must never be reported as one. (3) The 12.22% near-miss figure uses difflib SequenceMatcher at 0.90 with no human audit; inspection of the top examples shows several are systematic filename sanitization rather than typos, so 12.22% is an UPPER BOUND on 'probably meant an existing file' and the true rate is likely far closer to the exact-recovery 0.28%. (4) `cyclotruc/gitingest` and `bodo-run/yek` returned null from api.github.com — probably renamed or moved; I did not chase them, so my packer-category star total (~38,500) EXCLUDES gitingest and is therefore an undercount, which cuts against my own 'crowded category' warning. (5) npm weekly download counts for repomix and ai-digest — api.npmjs.org returned Cloudflare `error code: 1015` (rate limit). All adoption claims here are GitHub stars only, which is a weaker signal than downloads. (6) I did NOT read Open Knowledge Format SPEC.md v0.2. §11 S1 flags it as decided-against-twice-unread and it remains unread by me; if OKF v0.2 already specifies a container or a multi-document envelope, my 'unclaimed' list is wrong and would need rewriting. This is the single largest hole in this report. (7) The `![[X]]` degradation test used `marked` only, not the 24-renderer matrix §4.3 describes; one parser is one data point, and marked is not GitHub, Obsidian, or Google Docs paste. (8) Every claim about what the founder MEANS is inference over a written record. I have quoted him verbatim from the transcript rather than from handoff paraphrase wherever the quote is load-bearing, but 'what he is reaching for' is my reconstruction and he is the only person who can confirm or refute it — which is exactly the one-conversation test in K-D. (9) I did not re-derive the 99.627% anchor figure, the 168.8x llms.txt ratio, the 443/655 CommonMark figure, or the 24-renderer degradation matrix; those remain at the tier the plan assigns them, and §9.4's warning stands — the flagship anchor number has still been re-derived by nobody, including me.

result.area: First-mover advantage — what is actually defensible in MDMAX and what gets cloned in a weekend
result.headline: Five of MDMAX's six capabilities are leads measured in weeks, not moats: the reference implementation of content-derived re-anchoring is 182 lines of MIT code shipping in production today, provenance was taken by Google's own OKF v0.2 on 2026-07-25 and by C2PA before that, budgeted projection was taken by llms.txt in 2024 — and the empirical clone latency for a big-company markdown convention is under 24 hours (scaccogatto/okf-skills created 2026-06-14T11:15Z, one day after Google's 2026-06-13 OKF announcement, now 206 stars, with 69 third-party repos in the first 8 days and 287 in 49 days); the only capability with no prior art found and a structurally decaying dataset is the (product, surface) degradation certificate, and the only durable moat in the whole program is the multi-tenancy work in S5 that the plan itself labels "uninteresting."
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED, written before the search: my headline ("these are leads, not moats") is wrong if (a) I cannot find a shipping, permissively-licensed implementation of the core mechanism of block identity, splice writing, projection or provenance; (b) markdown-category first movers turn out to have won on capability rather than distribution/business model; or (c) the degradation certificate turns out to already exist, which would mean I am wrong in the OTHER direction and even the one moat is gone. I looked for all three. (a) FALSIFIED AGAINST ME: dom-anchor-text-quote@4.0.2 lib/index.js is 182 lines over diff-match-patch (2,217 lines), in production at Hypothes.is, 13,103 npm downloads/week; mdast-util-from-markdown ships node.position.offset, which makes a splice writer a one-day job; llms.txt (AnswerDotAI/llms-txt, 2,541 stars, created 2024-09-01, 1,659 repos mention it) is budgeted projection; OKF SPEC.md v0.2 §5.1 and C2PA are provenance. (b) FALSIFIED AGAINST ME: Dendron — the most technically innovative markdown-native tool in the category — has 0 commits in 52 weeks and its founder's own words are "we were ultimately not able to find product market fit for a venture backed business," a business failure with no technical cause; meanwhile the four single-player first movers (iA Writer, Ulysses, Bear, Craft) all shipped updates in July 2026 and were never overtaken at all. (c) NOT FALSIFIED: three GitHub repo searches for a markdown renderer-compatibility matrix returned total_count 0, 0 and 1 (an unrelated MCP tool), and npm has no `markdown-compat`/`markdown-conformance`/`babelmark` package. So the headline stands, and the certificate is the single exception I am NOT calling a lead. Residual risk I could not close: I could not measure Roam or Typora directly (no public API), and I could not test Google Docs' markdown round-trip fidelity myself.

findings.claim: The core mechanism of MDMAX §4.1 block identity — exact match, then context-scored disambiguation, then fuzzy fallback — is 182 lines of already-shipping MIT code. This is a weekend, not a moat.
findings.evidence: Downloaded npm tarball of dom-anchor-text-quote@4.0.2 (the anchoring library Hypothes.is ships). `wc -l dom-anchor-text-quote/package/lib/index.js` = 182. package.json dependencies: {"diff-match-patch":"^1.0.0","dom-anchor-text-position":"^4.0.0"}. diff-match-patch index.js = 2,217 lines (Google, Neil Fraser, Apache-2.0). Source comment in the file: "// The DiffMatchPatch bitap has a hard 32-character pattern length limit. var SLICE_LENGTH = 32; var CONTEXT_LENGTH = SLICE_LENGTH;" — i.e. it already does prefix/suffix context scoring, MDMAX's S2. Weekly downloads: dom-anchor-text-quote 13,103; diff-match-patch 5,971,159 (api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week, week 2026-07-24..2026-07-30).

findings.claim: Empirical clone latency for a markdown convention published by a big company is under 24 hours, and the ecosystem produces ~70 independent implementations in the first week. This is the single most decision-relevant number in my area.

findings.claim: MDMAX §4.5 declared provenance is no longer an unoccupied slot. Google's OKF SPEC.md v0.2 ships provenance, trust, lifecycle AND attestation as first-class frontmatter, including per-claim attribution — and its stated rationale is verbatim MDMAX's own identity rationale.

findings.claim: The brief's 'uncomfortable case' is materially wrong. Obsidian did NOT conclude markdown was the wrong place. Bases keeps all DATA in the markdown files and lets the view definition live EITHER in a .base sidecar OR in a fenced code block inside a .md — which is decision D8 (extensibility in the value of a field) validated by the best-resourced actor in the ecosystem.
findings.evidence: obsidianmd/obsidian-help, en/Bases/Introduction to Bases.md: "All the data in Obsidian Bases is stored in your local [[Basic formatting syntax|Markdown]] files and their [[properties]]. The views are described by the [[Bases syntax]], which can be saved as a `.base` file or [[Create a base#Embed a base|embedded]] in code blocks within your Markdown files." en/Bases/Create a base.md, §Embed a base as a code block, shows a literal ```base fence containing YAML. Obsidian shipped exactly one true sidecar for a thing markdown structurally cannot hold — spatial arrangement (.canvas) — which docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §5 already concedes was right.

findings.claim: Obsidian's answer to block identity was to write a DECLARED id INTO the markdown, not into a sidecar — the opposite of the concession the brief asks for, and the direct competitor to MDMAX's derived anchor.
findings.evidence: obsidianmd/obsidian-help, en/Linking notes and files/Internal links.md, §"Link to a block in a note": "A block is a unit of text in your note, such as a paragraph, block quote, or list item. You can link to a block by adding `#^` at the end of your link destination, followed by a unique block identifier. For example: `[[2023-01-01#^37066d]]`." The help file itself carries a live block id on its own opening line: "...you can create a network of knowledge. ^b15695". JSON Canvas 1.0 spec (2024-03-11) file nodes even depend on it: "`subpath` (optional, string) is a subpath that may link to a heading or a block."

findings.claim: Across the pinned corpus, declared block identity has ZERO adoption: 0 `{#id}` heading attributes over 31,630 ATX headings and 0 Obsidian `^blockid` declarations across 1,084 files. This cuts BOTH ways and the second cut is the one nobody has written down.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4. I re-read all 1,084 files listed in docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json and verified sha256 on every one: sha_match=1084, sha_drift=0; total bytes 21,068,853 + 3,570,923 + 908,989 = 25,548,765, which reproduces PLAN.md's stated corpus size exactly. Result: ATX headings 31,630; headings carrying `{#id}` = 0 (0.0000%); `^blockid` declarations = 0; `[[note#^id]]` uses = 4, and all 4 are prose ABOUT the syntax (docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md:93, HANDOFF-graph-engineering-2026-07-30.md:232, docs/mdmap/01-thesis/not-a-graph-view.md:63), not real links. FOR MDMAX: K4's declared-attribute threat has no observed adoption. AGAINST MDMAX: a mechanism Obsidian has shipped since 2020 and auto-completes on a keystroke was used zero times in a 756-file vault — which is evidence that AUTHORS do not feel the block-identity pain. Only the APP feels it.

findings.claim: Independent re-derivation on the pinned corpus CONFIRMS and strengthens the splice-only theorem at 21× the sample size the plan used — but the plan's byte figure does not reproduce and should be struck.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…; node v24.6.0; mdast-util-from-markdown + mdast-util-to-markdown + mdast-util-gfm from this repo's node_modules; 1,080 non-empty files, 0 parse errors. Result: byte-identical round trip 5/1,080 = 0.463%; lines absent after round trip 124,534/423,410 = 29.41%; bytes 25,548,765 → 26,576,149 = +4.02%. PLAN.md §4.2 says the round trip "rewrites 24.98% of lines and drops 18.94% of bytes; 0 of 51 files in this repo survive it byte-identically." The line figure reproduces in shape (29.41% vs 24.98%) on a 21× larger corpus, but the byte direction INVERTS: I measure +4.02% growth, not an 18.94% drop. The sign of the byte delta is a config artifact (frontmatter handling); the destruction is not. Report the line figure, drop the byte figure.

findings.claim: The 'data moat' for anchoring does not exist: the pinned corpus is 80 days of one author's commits, and a strictly larger, older, multi-author, public markdown corpus is one git clone away — roughly 1,000× the bytes.
findings.evidence: Local: `cd ~/Desktop/GitHub/md && git log --oneline | wc -l` = 416; `git shortlog -sn HEAD` = "416 Sagnik Mitra" (one author, 100%); first commit Wed May 13 03:44:01 2026, last Fri Jul 17 22:04:53 2026 — an 80-day, single-author history. This is the repo the 294 revision pairs / 41,642 block-versions came from. Public alternatives via api.github.com/repos: MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs size 27,070,691 KB (~27 GB), created 2016-11-02; mdn/content 501,827 KB, "over 14,000 pages"; kubernetes/website 560,330 KB. The frontmatter corpus is 25,548,765 bytes total. A competitor gets ~1,000× more revision pairs, from thousands of authors, for free.

findings.claim: The big-company entry the founder is worried about already happened, two years ago, and it was Google. Google Docs has imported and exported markdown since 2024-07-16 and has supported composing in markdown since 2022.
findings.evidence: workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2024/07/import-and-export-markdown-in-google-docs.html, dated July 16, 2024: "In 2022, we introduced expanded support for composing with Markdown in Google Docs on web. Today, we're introducing highly-requested features that enhance Docs' interoperability with other Markdown supporting tools. These include the ability to: Convert Markdown to Docs content on paste / Copy Docs content as Markdown / Export a Doc as Markdown (from File > Download) / Import Markdown as a Doc (from File > Open or 'Open with Google Docs' from Drive)". Note the exact verb: "Convert Markdown to Docs CONTENT." The durable artifact remains a Doc. That single word is the entire surviving differentiator for D4.

findings.claim: No prior art exists for the degradation certificate. Three independent GitHub searches and four npm lookups came back empty. This is the one capability I could not find already built, which is why it is the only one I put on the moat side.
findings.evidence: api.github.com/search/repositories: q="markdown renderer compatibility matrix" → total_count 0; q="markdown degradation certificate" → total_count 0; q="markdown target conformance report" → total_count 1 (P4ST4S/mcp-migrate, unrelated). Earlier queries markdown+compatibility+matrix, markdown+conformance+renderer+differential, markdown+block+id+anchor+stable, markdown+splice+patch+in-place+edit all returned empty item sets. npm: babelmark, markdown-compat, markdown-conformance all return {"error":"package … not found"}. jgm's babelmark differs SPEC FRAGMENTS across PARSERS; nothing differs a DOCUMENT across (product, surface) pairs.

findings.claim: The certificate's dataset genuinely decays, which is what makes it the only compounding asset — but it decays on a slow, public, major-version cadence, so the moat is months of freshness, not years.
findings.evidence: api.github.com/repos/github/markup/releases: v6.0.0 published 2026-05-05, v5.0.1 and v5.0.0 both 2024-06-17, v3.0.4 2019-04-02. A major-version bump of the library that decides how GitHub renders markup landed three months ago. github/cmark-gfm: created 2016-12-01, pushed 2026-07-13, not archived. The closed-target rows in the matrix have a measurable shelf life; a competitor who re-measures once catches up in a week.

findings.claim: The category's one clear death was a business failure, not a technical one — and it was the most technically innovative, markdown-native, local-first, open-source entrant. This is the most important first-mover lesson available and it argues against every engineering-led defensibility story.
findings.evidence: api.github.com/repos/dendronhq/dendron/stats/participation: 0 commits in the last 52 weeks. README.md line: "Dendron is currently in maintenace only, active development has ceased." linking discussion #3890 (opened 2023-01-25). Founder @kevinslin's announcement, quoted verbatim in that thread: "we spent the past two years building a better way for humans to manage knowledge. While we made great strides there, as a business, we were ultimately not able to find product market fit for a venture backed business." Also: "we are also updating the Dendron license from 'GPLV3' to 'Apache 2.0' … this was a frequent ask from our customers working at big tech companies." Dendron had 244 all-contributors, 7,459 stars, and shipped nothing after 2025-06-01.

findings.claim: The first movers in single-player markdown editing were NOT overtaken — every one of them is still shipping in July 2026. The category did not consolidate, which means 'first mover' has produced neither a winner nor a graveyard; it has produced a stable, small, fragmented market.

Ulysses: Writing App, Ulysses GmbH & Co. KG, listing first release 2017-08-10, current 40.2 on 2026-07-13, 2,072 ratings at 4.586. findings.claim: The category winner won on a plugin registry and a business model, not on format capability — and its most active repository is the registry, not the app.
findings.evidence: api.github.com/repos/obsidianmd/obsidian-releases: 20,328 stars, description "Community plugins list, theme list, and releases of Obsidian"; stats/participation 1,934 commits in 52 weeks with 1,181 of them in the last 13 weeks and 333 in the first 13 — a 3.5× acceleration in the repo whose only job is accepting third-party plugins. Obsidian launched in 2020, after Ulysses, iA Writer, Bear, Roam and simultaneously with Dendron. It was not first.

findings.claim: The direct 'Google Docs for markdown' first mover has had the exact feature frontmatter is building deadlocked in its issue tracker for six years, in BOTH directions. That is a real market opening and the strongest pro-frontmatter datum I found.
findings.evidence: docs/engine/research/wf-mdmax-capability-2026-08-01.result.json, quoting HedgeDoc issue #657: open 2020->2026 and "doctrinally deadlocked in BOTH directions — in-file CriticMarkup 'pollutes every other pipeline and makes comment-only permission impossible', out-of-file vetoed as 'meta data that are not part of the markdown code'. Users left for HackMD/Google Docs." Corroborating liveness: api.github.com/repos/hedgedoc/hedgedoc created 2019-03-27, 7,337 stars, 385 commits in 52 weeks (43 in the last 13) — against outline/outline's 1,914 and logseq/logseq's 3,806. I did not open issue #657 myself; this is secondary, quoted from this program's own prior research, and it should be re-read before it is used in a pitch.

findings.claim: OKF's own conformance section forecloses the near-miss reference checker as a differentiator inside OKF, and OKF's deferred list is a declared Google roadmap — so the two remaining 'gaps' in the spec are not safe places to build a moat.
findings.evidence: OKF SPEC.md v0.2 §11: "consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle because of: Missing optional frontmatter fields. Unknown `type` values. Unknown additional frontmatter keys. Broken cross-links. Missing `index.md` files." §12 Considered and deferred: "The full runtime protocol: receipt and verdict wire formats, and the attestation lifecycle around a run. The attester ABI, portability, and sandboxing, likely bundled with future work on serving and Skills. Attestation caching." Building the receipt/attester layer is building inside a published Google roadmap slot.

findings.claim: MOAT vs LEAD, stated plainly. Leads (time, eroding): block identity ~1 weekend to clone, splice writing ~1 day, budgeted projection ~hours, provenance already taken, near-miss checking ~1 weekend. Moat candidates (structural): exactly two, and neither is a compiler capability.
findings.evidence: Derived from the findings above. (1) The closed-renderer observation series behind `mdmax cert` — a decaying-dataset moat of the caniuse / HaveIBeenPwned shape, worth months of freshness, defensible only while continuously re-measured (github/markup v5.0.1 2024-06-17 → v6.0.0 2026-05-05). (2) Multi-tenancy, accounts and shared documents — switching costs and per-document network effects. docs/mdmax/PLAN.md S5 describes this as having "zero engine content" and predicts it "will keep losing priority to compiler work precisely because it is uninteresting." 100% of the durable defensibility and 0% of the eighteen research areas. A third, weaker candidate is reputational: 'the editor that has never corrupted a byte of your file,' earned by a public continuously-running byte-fidelity CI — a brand asset, not an algorithm.

findings.claim: Today the lead is zero. There is no MDMAX code, so none of the clock has started.
findings.evidence: In /Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter: `grep -rli mdmax src test` returns nothing; `git log --oneline | wc -l` = 20; src is 21,415 lines of TypeScript, all product shell (modules/editor, vault, share, preview, graph, ai). Every day of 'first-mover advantage' discussed in this plan is currently a day of someone else's.

negatives: NEGATIVE 1 — BLOCK IDENTITY IS NOT DEFENSIBLE, and this is the one the founder believes in most. The full production algorithm is 182 lines (dom-anchor-text-quote@4.0.2 lib/index.js) on top of a 2,217-line Google library, both permissively licensed, both downloadable in ten seconds, and it already implements MDMAX's S1/S2/S3 shape including the 32-character context window. The design is a W3C standard (TextQuoteSelector) with prior art back to MSR-TR-2001-107 — PLAN.md §8.3 already concedes 'no precedent' is REFUTED. What MDMAX actually owns is three tuned scalars (3-gram shingles, jaccard >= 0.20, margin <= 0.05) measured on a corpus that git says is 416 commits by exactly one author over 80 days. If those scalars are published, a competitor copies them in an afternoon; if they are withheld, the 99.627% figure is unverifiable and nobody outside the company will believe it. Either way it is a lead of weeks. And the plan's own §4.1 correction already demotes it to 'the fallback and the verifier, not the primary mechanism' — a capability that is a fallback cannot also be the moat.

NEGATIVE 2 — DECLARED PROVENANCE IS ALREADY TAKEN, TWICE, AND THE PLAN'S EVIDENCE FOR THE GAP IS NOW STALE. §4.5 justifies provenance with 'MCP (all six schema versions) and Google A2A contain zero fields for provenance, citation, confidence or lineage.' That was measured before OKF v0.2. OKF SPEC.md v0.2 (37,544 bytes, in GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog, 8,134 stars) now specifies `sources` with `author`/`usage_count`/`last_modified`/`usage_window`, `generated`/`verified` with a three-tier trust ladder, `status`, `stale_after`, and an entire Attested Computation type with `executor.receipt` and `attester` — in markdown with YAML frontmatter, which is MDMAX's exact substrate. Independently, C2PA has had a public specification repo since 2021-11-12 and c2pa-rs was pushed 2026-08-01. MDMAX would be the third entrant behind Google and an Adobe/Microsoft-led coalition. Related and equally fatal: BUDGETED PROJECTION (§4.4) was taken by llms.txt in September 2024 — AnswerDotAI/llms-txt has 2,541 stars, 1,659 GitHub repos mention llms.txt, and the plan's own corroborating example (Anthropic's llms.txt at 38,847 B vs llms-full.txt at 6,556,407 B) is a demonstration that the competitor already ships it.

NEGATIVE 3 — THE CORPUS IS NOT AN ASSET, IT IS A LIABILITY. The plan's W1 says 'everything we have measured comes from one operator's vault' but never reports how thin that vault is. It is 416 commits, one author (100% of shortlog), 80 days old, and heavily AI-co-authored. MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs is a 27 GB public markdown repo with a decade of multi-author edit history — roughly 1,000× the bytes, free, and a far better anchoring corpus. Any competitor who wants the benchmark gets a better one than ours by cloning a public repo. There is no corpus moat anywhere in MDMAX.

NEGATIVE 4 — THE MARKET HISTORY DOES NOT SUPPORT AN ENGINEERING-LED MOAT. The most technically innovative markdown-native entrant (Dendron: hierarchical namespaces, local-first, open source, 244 contributors, 7,459 stars) is at 0 commits in 52 weeks and its founder's stated cause is 'not able to find product market fit for a venture backed business' — zero technical content. The winner (Obsidian) was not first and its fastest-growing repository is its plugin registry (1,181 of 1,934 52-week commits in the last 13 weeks). The four surviving first movers (iA Writer, Ulysses, Bear, Craft) all shipped in July 2026 and were never overtaken by anyone. In this category, capability has never been the thing that decided anything.
unclaimed: A per-document, (product, surface)-scoped degradation certificate — PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT per construct per target. result.design:
WHAT SHIPS, given that five of six capabilities are leads. Keep the MVP as written in PLAN.md §10 but re-label what each artifact is FOR, because the current framing sequences as if the engine is product while justifying it as if it is marketing (§13.4, still open).

1. `mdmax cert` — SHIP IT, AND SHIP IT AS THE PUBLIC ASSET. Carrier: an npm CLI plus a dated, versioned JSON dataset published on its own (e.g. targets.json with an ISO snapshot date and a hash per target). Degradation behaviour: an OSS target row is REPRODUCIBLE (vendored, version-pinned renderer, anyone can rerun it); a CLOSED target row is OBSERVED and carries `observed_at` plus the product build/version string it was observed against, and EXPIRES — a row older than 90 days renders as STALE, not as PASS. CLI surface: `mdmax cert <file> --targets github-blob,github-comment,github-pages,slack,notion --fail-on BROKEN --json`. This is the only capability with no prior art found and the only dataset that decays, so it is the only thing here that can compound. The expiry field IS the moat mechanism: it makes a stale copy visibly stale.

2. `mdmax edit` — SHIP IT, BUT CALL IT WHAT IT IS: a correctness guarantee, not an invention. Splice writer + receipt + post-write re-anchor assertion. Degradation behaviour: refuse rather than write when the anchor is AMBIGUOUS or LOST. The defensible artifact is not the splice — it is a PUBLIC, CONTINUOUSLY-RUNNING byte-fidelity CI over a public corpus (azure-docs or mdn/content, not our vault), with the green badge on the README. That is a reputation asset, and reputation is the one thing a weekend clone cannot copy.

3. BLOCK IDENTITY — VENDOR IT, DO NOT INVENT IT. Take dom-anchor-text-quote's shape (182 lines, MIT) and diff-match-patch (Apache-2.0) as the S1/S3 substrate, add the block gate and the refusal policy, and spend the saved weeks on S5. Publish the parameters. Withholding them buys nothing (a competitor re-sweeps in an afternoon on a bigger public corpus) and costs credibility (the 99.627% becomes unverifiable). PLAN.md §4.1 already demotes this to fallback-and-verifier; the build plan should match that demotion.

4. PROVENANCE — DO NOT BUILD A FORMAT. Emit OKF v0.2 §5.1 `sources`/`generated`/`verified`/`stale_after` verbatim. Being the best OKF-conformant editor is a distribution position with 287 repos of existing gravity; being a third provenance vocabulary behind Google and C2PA is not.

5. S5 MULTI-TENANCY — PROMOTE IT TO P0 AND SAY OUT LOUD THAT IT IS THE MOAT. Accounts, workspaces, share links with enforced roles, per-document membership. The plan predicts it will lose priority for being uninteresting; that prediction is the single largest risk in this document, because it is where 100% of the structural defensibility lives. UI surface: the boring one — a share dialog. K6 already says that without it there is no Google-Docs story.

6. WHAT NOT TO BUILD: a competing provenance vocabulary, an OKF-alternative format, an attester ABI, a projection format, or anything whose pitch is 'nobody has this' without the P8 search attached.
result.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES THE OPEN QUESTION — "is the certificate a moat or another lead?"

CLONE-TIME MEASUREMENT (settles the whole area, and it is cheap and adversarial by construction).
Corpus: 30 documents drawn from the pinned corpus (corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…) stratified by construct — 10 frontmatter-bearing, 10 fence-bearing with an unknown language, 10 containing an HTML comment or a link reference definition.
Targets: 12 (product, surface) pairs — github-blob, github-comment, github-pages, vscode-preview, obsidian-reading, slack, discord, notion-paste, gitlab-blob, bitbucket, npm-readme, pypi-readme.
Tasks: for each (document, construct, target) emit PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT.
Verifiers: OSS targets verified by vendored, version-pinned renderers (rules-based, per Learned Rule 25); closed targets verified by a screenshot/DOM diff captured on a stated date against a stated product build.
n: 30 x 12 = 360 cells, plus a second independent capture 60 days later on the closed rows only.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, written now:
  P1 — >= 3 of the 12 targets disagree on at least one construct that a real README author would actually use (if fewer, K5 fires and the certificate is cut).
  P2 — at the 60-day recapture, >= 1 of the 7 closed targets has changed at least one cell. If ZERO cells move in 60 days, the dataset does not decay, it is a one-time artifact, a competitor copies it once and is permanently level, and the certificate is a LEAD not a MOAT — in which case the only moat left in the entire program is S5 multi-tenancy and the roadmap must be re-ordered around that fact.
  P3 — the github-blob/github-comment/github-pages triple disagrees on the HTML comment. PLAN.md §4.3 already measured that blob view deletes it; if this does not reproduce, §9.7's whole correction is wrong too.
GATE, and it must go RED first (per S2): assert "an HTML comment survives to a GitHub blob view" and require it to FAIL before any cell in the matrix is trusted.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, one day, settles the anchoring moat directly: run the 384-configuration sweep against MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs or mdn/content instead of the 80-day single-author vault, and publish both numbers side by side. If the tuned parameters transfer, the number is real and publishable and the moat is still zero (a competitor reproduces it from the same public corpus). If they do NOT transfer, the flagship number was fitted to one author's prose and K2 fires. Either outcome is more informative than re-deriving on our own vault a second time.

THIRD, half a day, and it is the cheapest high-value thing in this whole report: run `mdmax cert` against an OKF bundle from one of the 287 public OKF repos. That single run tells you whether §13.5's "OKF is a column, not a host" is a real position or a slogan.
result.kill_condition:
KILL THE FIRST-MOVER THESIS IF ANY OF THESE IS TRUE.

K-FM1 — At the 60-day recapture, zero closed-target cells have changed. Then the certificate dataset does not decay, a single copy is permanently level with ours, and NOTHING in MDMAX is a moat. The correct response is to stop describing the compiler as defensible, publish all of it openly as marketing (settling §13.4 in favour of "the engine is marketing"), and move the entire team to S5.

K-FM2 — Google's OKF v0.3, or any Google/Anthropic/Microsoft release, specifies intra-document block identity (a derived anchor, a block id convention, or a range selector). That is the last unoccupied slot in the spec; §12's deferred list shows the spec is actively acquiring exactly this kind of surface. If it lands, MDMAX's remaining novelty is the certificate alone.

K-FM3 — A third party ships a target-scoped markdown conformance matrix before we do. Given a measured clone latency of under 24 hours for a Google convention and 69 repos in 8 days, assume this is possible the week after we describe the idea in public. Corollary and standing rule: do NOT publish the certificate's DESIGN before the certificate's DATASET. The design is a weekend; the dated observation series is not.

K-FM4 — S5 multi-tenancy does not ship within one quarter of `mdmax edit`. This is PLAN.md's own K6 with a clock attached. If the compiler ships and the sharing does not, we have built a library with no moat and no product, and the honest move is to position it as a standalone open-source library and stop calling frontmatter a company.

K-FM5 — We publish the 99.627% without re-deriving it on a public multi-author corpus. Not a market kill, a credibility kill: the one number eight research areas rest on would be defended by an 80-day single-author vault, and the first competent outside reader will notice.
result.unverified:
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND THE TIER IT ACTUALLY SITS AT.

1. Google Docs' markdown ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY. I have Google's own words that it converts markdown to Docs content and can export back (primary-read). I did NOT run a round trip through Google Docs and measure byte loss. My assertion that the durable artifact is a Doc rather than a file is INFERENCE from the verb "convert", strengthened by my own measured 0.463% byte-identical AST round-trip rate — but it is inference. Do not put a number on Google Docs' markdown loss without running it.

2. HedgeDoc issue #657. SECONDARY — quoted from this program's own wf-mdmax-capability result JSON, not read by me at github.com/hedgedoc/hedgedoc/issues/657. It is the strongest pro-frontmatter datum in my report and it is the weakest-sourced one. Read it before it appears in any pitch.

3. Roam Research and Typora. NOT MEASURED. Neither has a public API or repo I could query. I deliberately made no claim about either; the brief asked about them and I am declining rather than guessing.

4. "How long would a competent team take" for each capability. My clone-time estimates are INFERENCE anchored on two measured quantities — the LOC of shipping reference implementations, and the OKF ecosystem's 24-hour/69-repos-in-8-days response curve. They are estimates. I did not run a build-it-in-a-weekend experiment, and nobody should quote "a weekend" as if it were measured.

5. The corpus_id itself. The manifest reproduces perfectly on content — I re-read all 1,084 files and every sha256 matched (sha_drift=0), and the byte total 25,548,765 matches PLAN.md exactly. But I could NOT reproduce the declared hash 3a010b16… from the (path, sha256) list; my guessed serialization produced a55879ba…. That is almost certainly my serialization guess being wrong, not a defect in the manifest — I am reporting it because P1 makes the corpus id load-bearing and nobody should assume it has been independently reconstructed. It has not. Someone should commit the derivation script (P2).

6. Dendron's funding. I quote the founder saying "venture backed" (primary, from the discussion HTML). I did NOT verify the round size or investor and make no claim about either.

7. C2PA's actual overlap with markdown provenance. I verified the repos exist and are active (contentauth/c2pa-rs pushed 2026-08-01, c2pa-org/specifications pushed 2026-07-27). I did NOT read the C2PA specification. My claim is that a well-funded provenance standard exists and is active — not that it covers markdown spans. Read it before relying on it.

8. iA Writer / Ulysses / Bear founding dates. The App Store releaseDate is the LISTING date, not the product's birth. Ulysses dates to 2003 and iA Writer to 2010 as products; I report only what the iTunes API returned and label it as the Mac App Store listing. Do not repeat these as founding dates.

9. Whether MDMAX's exact 384-configuration parameter set outperforms dom-anchor-text-quote's defaults. UNMEASURED and it is the single most important open question for Negative 1. If the tuned parameters beat the 182-line baseline by a wide margin on a public corpus, my "weekend clone" verdict weakens materially and should be revisited. Nobody in this program has run that comparison, and it belongs in the S4 benchmark as an arm alongside diff3-assisted.
