result.design:
WHAT TO IMPORT, PORTED, AND WHAT TO REFUSE.

1. THE GATE REGISTRY — port, do not copy. Rewrite `sgnk-regression-gate.sh` as `specs/harness/gate.mjs` in the frontmatter repo, storing to `specs/gates.jsonl`. Keep the contract verbatim: `--add` requires `--assert` AND `--broke`; refuse with distinct codes on already-red assertion (2), vacuous gate (3), missing repro (4), write-did-not-land (5); `--verify-all` re-proves every gate can still fail and treats a reserved REPRO_NOOP as INCONCLUSIVE, never as proof. Two deliberate changes: (a) Node, not bash — this deletes the entire bash-3.2/zsh/heredoc false-RED class (LR#64/65/66) at the root rather than papering it with a preflight; (b) add the preflight the shell version lacks anyway, as an environment fingerprint written into every gate row, so a green from a different environment is visibly a different measurement.

2. THE VERIFY LADDER — already present, needs one AIOS refinement. `npm run verify` (typecheck → lint → test → build → arch) is already a cheapest-first ladder that stops at first failure. Import the one rule it lacks, taken verbatim from verify-ladder.sh: a rung that TIMES OUT is `infra`, never `fail`, so a wedged candidate cannot masquerade as a quality failure. Emit one JSON line per run: `{verdict, rung_reached, pass, timeout, rungs}`. This is the substrate for any best-of-N agent selection later.

3. THE FIRST THREE GATES TO REGISTER, each with its `--broke` written first. (a) SPLICE CONFORMANCE: bytes written == bytes requested, for every splice; `--broke` reintroduces AST regeneration and must go red on the repo's own 51 files (the plan already measures 0/51 survive a tree round-trip). (b) ANCHOR SAFETY: `resolve()` never returns a wrong index; `--broke` reintroduces content-hash-plus-nearest-position, which the plan measures at 22.20% false. (c) UTF-8 INTEGRITY: no artifact leaves the writer undecodable; `--broke` swaps `perl -CSD` for `head -c` and must go red on a Devanagari fixture — I have the reproduction already (216 bytes in, 200 out, decode error at position 198).

4. THE BUILD HARNESS FOR A SMALL TEAM PLUS AGENTS. Worktree isolation is already wired (2 exist) and already stale (16 commits behind, one dirty). Add: a preflight that refuses to dispatch an agent into a worktree more than N commits behind main; and capture `git rev-parse HEAD` before AND after every parallel run and reconcile the delta, because LR#48 measured that a prompt-level 'do not commit' is advisory and five subagent commits landed anyway. Parallel branches must operate on disjoint, explicitly-named artifacts (LR#20) — for a compiler that means one agent per module boundary (parser / anchor resolver / splice writer / degradation matrix), never two agents on the same file. Adversarial review stays, but as a GATE: a claim that a defect is fixed does not close a ticket; a registered gate that goes red under the old code does.

5. THE RESEARCH→BUILD BOUNDARY. Nothing enters the build backlog on a headline. A backlog item requires: the corpus_id it was measured against, a command that reproduces the number, and — if the claim was adversarially verified — the verifier's verdict attached. The orchestrator refuses to open a ticket whose headline appears in its own `killed` list. That single rule is what the previous run was missing and it costs one conditional.

6. AGENTIC MARKDOWN — the product shape the measurement implies. Agents are already the dominant writers of .md in this repo's sessions (54 of 114 write-tool calls, more than .ts), they rewrite whole files 55.6% of the time, and when they splice they anchor on a median 232 verbatim bytes. So: expose a splice API whose unit IS that anchor — `splice(anchor_bytes, replacement)` returning `OK | AMBIGUOUS | LOST` — and make whole-file rewrite the deprecated path, because it is the mechanism by which an agent silently destroys a concurrent human edit. Every agent write lands as a SUGGESTION, never a commit, carrying (agent id, model, prompt hash, anchor bytes, resolve verdict, verify-ladder line) — all of it in the sidecar, none of it in the .md (D2). The measured live baselines the resolver must beat are 1.31% not-found and 26 stale-read collisions on .md; the review loop for machine authors is the same one humans get, with one addition: an agent suggestion that resolved AMBIGUOUS is presented as a refusal, not a diff.

7. DO NOT IMPORT: the bash guard (blocks read-only greps on token match), the routing bandit / model router / calibration curve (their own author says the loop cannot close), the judge panels (no measured kappa), the trace ledger's reward path. Import the trace ledger ONLY as a one-line-per-build-run record if you want build telemetry, and fix sgnk-trace-append.sh:334 before you do.
result.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES WHETHER THE AIOS HARNESS EARNS ITS PLACE IN THE MDMAX BUILD.

CORPUS. Two, named separately and never mixed. (A) Format/compiler claims: the pinned corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 — 1,084 files, 25,548,765 bytes, roots md@02c22ec4 / knowledge@464eb666 / frontmatter@798ebbf3. (B) Agent-behaviour claims: an explicitly re-pinned transcript manifest, because today's selection (1,944 files, 1,024,743,426 bytes, two named project dirs) is a moving target — hash the (path, size, mtime) list and publish the id, exactly as the format corpus does.

TASKS. n=200 real agent markdown edits replayed from corpus B against the MDMAX splice API — sampled stratified by outcome so the 40 known failures (14 not_found, 26 file_modified) are all included, not sampled away. Each replay is a (document_before, anchor_bytes, replacement, document_after_truth) tuple.

VERIFIERS, cheapest first, three rungs. R1 mechanical: bytes changed == bytes requested (splice conformance); artifact decodes as UTF-8. R2 differential: resolver verdict versus the ground-truth CodeMirror ChangeSet where one exists. R3 judged: only for the AMBIGUOUS bucket, and only if R1/R2 leave it undecided.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, written before the run. P1 splice writer: 0 unrequested bytes on 200/200; any nonzero kills the design, not the parameter. P2 resolver: not_found ≤ 1.31% (the measured live agent baseline) and false-anchor exactly 0 — refusal is cheap, a silently wrong anchor is not. P3 UTF-8 gate: catches 100% of injected orphaned-lead-byte truncations and repairs 0% of the four other invalid classes (stray continuation, invalid start, overlong, encoded surrogate). P4 concurrency: with two agents splicing the same document, 0 lost writes and 0 silent overwrites; the current whole-file Write path must be shown to LOSE a write in the same fixture, or the concurrency claim is unmotivated.

GATE DISCIPLINE ON THE EXPERIMENT ITSELF, all four mandatory. (i) Every gate's `--broke` is demonstrated RED before its green is counted — a passing test on a rare fault proves nothing until it has failed against the unfixed code (LR#68; the UTF-8 defect fires in ~0.34% of artifacts, so 0/120 clean is the expected draw with the bug fully intact). (ii) Three runs minimum before any number is quoted, and any stochastic input pinned (LR#63). (iii) Anything with a shell component runs under BOTH bash and zsh, and a disagreement means the check is measuring the shell (LR#66). (iv) Every reported figure states its corpus id and whether it came from live artifacts or a replay through modified code — the latter is labelled SIMULATED (LR#62).

COST OF THE HARNESS, measured alongside. Log, for 30 days: gates registered, gates that went red, of those how many were TRUE regressions versus environment artifacts, and engineer-minutes spent repairing rotted repros. That ratio is the only honest answer to whether the AIOS machinery paid for itself.
result.kill_condition: THREE, any one of which ends this direction. (1) THE HARNESS IS CEREMONY: if in the first 30 days of the build the ported gate registry catches zero true regressions while costing more than two engineer-hours per week in repro repair, drop it entirely and keep only `npm run verify`. The prior for this is not good — 21 gates exist in AIOS and the only recorded in-the-wild catch is the parity gate catching its own author mid-session. (2) THE HARNESS MEASURES THE MACHINE: if the Node port still yields environment-dependent verdicts after the preflight — same commit, different cwd or different machine, different result, the way the shell version does today at 17/4 versus 21/0 — then it is not a gate, it is a location detector, and it must move to CI where the environment is pinned or be deleted. (3) THE PRODUCT PREMISE FAILS: if the splice conformance gate cannot be made to go red under AST regeneration on this repo's own files, then the theorem the whole design rests on is not observable here and the splice-only decision (D7) is unfalsifiable as stated — which would mean the gate is vacuous and, under this harness's own rule, must be refused rather than registered.
result.effort: GATE REGISTRY PORT: ~1 day. The shell original is 9,232 bytes and its entire contract is five refusal codes plus a REPRO_NOOP sentinel; the Node rewrite is mostly the selftest, which must be ported first and must pass before the tool is trusted (its own selftest is 10 cases and already covers the write-did-not-land case that the first shell version shipped wrong). VERIFY LADDER: ~2 hours — `npm run verify` already exists; the work is the timeout→`infra` distinction and emitting one JSON line. THE THREE FIRST GATES: splice conformance and anchor safety are BLOCKED on the splice writer and resolver existing, so they are not harness work, they are the definition of done for the first two engine milestones; the UTF-8 gate is ~2 hours and can land today because its repro already exists. WORKTREE PREFLIGHT + HEAD RECONCILIATION: ~3 hours, and it should land before the first parallel agent run, not after. RESEARCH→BUILD BOUNDARY RULE: one conditional plus a backlog schema field; under an hour, highest leverage per minute of anything here. WHAT TO BUDGET ZERO FOR: the bandit, router, calibration, judge panels, preference log, trace reward path. DEPENDENCIES: everything above depends only on Node and git, which is the point — the bash/zsh dependency is what makes the AIOS originals fragile, and the port is what removes it.
result.unverified: WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND ITS REAL TIER. (1) The 151/188/69/1 discrepancy — I verified the registry file does not produce those counts, but I could NOT find the source that does. It is possible a second grading pass exists outside ~/.claude that I did not reach; my search covered `find . -name \"test-registry*.json\"` under ~/.claude (one hit) and `git log` on that path (two commits). Tier: own-measurement for the non-reproduction, INFERENCE for 'therefore the handoff number is wrong'. (2) The heredoc mechanism — I measured the cwd dependence deterministically (3 trials × 6 directories) but I did NOT establish WHY frontmatter and $TMPDIR work while ~/Desktop/GitHub, ~/Desktop/GitHub/md, ~/.claude and ~/.sgnk do not. Setting TMPDIR to a provably writable path does not fix it, which rules out the simplest explanation, and my hypothesis (the sandbox's `.` write-allowance tracks the session's own launch directory) is INFERENCE, not measured. Do not repeat the mechanism; repeat the probe. (3) The SKILL.md description figure — PyYAML is not installed, so my 79,003 bytes comes from a regex over the YAML block, not a parse. The 41.71x is therefore a regex-derived ratio; the 3,295,299-byte body total is exact and reproduces PLAN.md to the byte. (4) Gate maintenance cost — I have no measurement of repro-rot rate or of how many of the 21 gates have ever caught a true regression; the negative I raise about ceremony is INFERENCE from the absence of a recorded catch, not from a count of catches. (5) 'Unclaimed' item 3 (anchor-failure telemetry as a product signal) and item 4 (a published markdown UTF-8 conformance gate) — I ran NO external search for either. They are inference and must not be quoted as prior-art gaps. (6) My agent-behaviour numbers are from a MOVING selection: 1,944 transcript files with no pinned manifest, measured once. Under this program's own rule that is not yet a measurement anyone else can reproduce — it needs a corpus id before it is quoted in the plan. (7) The two stale worktrees — I read `git worktree list` and `git status --short` but did not determine whether they are abandoned or in active use by another session; treating them as a hazard is inference. (8) I did not run the deep-route battery or sgnk-doctor, so I cannot confirm or refute the master handoff's 70/0, 32/0 and 90/3/0 figures; those remain secondary-tier, and given that its 21/0 gate figure is environment-dependent and its registry figure did not reproduce, they should be re-run before being quoted.

result.area: What frontmatter currently misses, against every product it must beat — claimed-vs-real feature audit, review-loop competitive analysis, and 2026 entrant sweep
result.headline: frontmatter's gap is not its feature list — the solo-editor features are largely real — it is that there is exactly one user (`isAllowed()` compares a login to a single `ALLOWED_GH_LOGIN` string; `firestore()` has zero callers; `firestore.rules` declares a members/roles model and no `comments` collection), so every review-loop item in the mockups is unreachable, while the one collaboration-adjacent write path that already ships (Publish) round-trips only 3.64% of the pinned corpus byte-identically and rewrites a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` into an ISO timestamp in 84.78% of the files it can parse.
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED, two parts. (1) "If `src/` contains any multi-user data access — a Firestore read/write against `vaults`/`notes`, any `memberUids`/`roles` handling, or any code path admitting a second identity — the 'one user' half of the headline is wrong." I looked. It PARTIALLY FIRED and I revised the claim: a multi-user model *does* exist, but only as a specification in `firestore.rules` (`roles: map<uid, "owner"|"editor"|"viewer">`, `memberUids`, per-vault membership functions at lines 154–183). It has zero implementation — `getFirestore` appears in exactly one file (`src/shared/infrastructure/firebase/client.ts:14`) and the exported `firestore()` helper has zero callers anywhere in `src/`. The rules declare users/billing/usage/vaults/notes/revisions/shares/months and NO comments or suggestions collection. So the headline changed from "no model" to "a specified, unimplemented model that does not even name comments." (2) "If the destructive frontmatter write path never fires in normal use, the 3.64% figure is inflated rhetoric." I looked. It did NOT fire: `share-writer.ts::writeSlug` is reached from `setShare` → `POST /api/share`, i.e. the Publish button, and again on unpublish (DELETE). It fires on every publish/unpublish of every note. Worse for the codebase, a correct comment-and-order-preserving path already exists in the same repo (`src/modules/preview/presentation/frontmatter.ts`, eemeli/yaml Document AST) and Publish does not use it. Both falsifier probes made the finding narrower and more defensible, not broader.

findings.claim: frontmatter is structurally single-user. The allowlist is not a list — it is one string compared for equality — and it is fed by a single env var, so no second person can ever authenticate.
findings.evidence: `src/modules/auth/domain/allowlist.ts:5-10`: `export function isAllowed(login: string | undefined, allowed: string): boolean { ... return login.trim().toLowerCase() === allowed.trim().toLowerCase(); }` — the parameter is `allowed: string`, not an array. Its only caller is `src/modules/auth/infrastructure/auth-options.ts:82`: `return isAllowed(ghProfile?.login, authEnv.ALLOWED_GH_LOGIN);`. `ActorContext` (`src/modules/auth/domain/actor.ts`) carries only `{login, name, avatarUrl}` — no uid, no email, no org, no role.

findings.claim: The multi-tenant model exists only as unimplemented security rules, and those rules do not declare comments or suggestions at all. Firestore is wired but never called.
findings.evidence: `firestore.rules:45-49` declares `memberUids: list<string> (required, <=100 entries)` and `roles: map<uid, "owner"|"editor"|"viewer">`, with `isVaultMember`/`vaultRole`/`isVaultEditor` helpers at lines 154–183. `grep -oE "match /[a-zA-Z{}/_]+" firestore.rules | sort -u` yields exactly: billing, months, notes, revisions, shares, usage, users, vaults — no `comments`, no `suggestions`. In `src/`, `grep -rn 'getFirestore|firestore'` returns 3 hits, all inside `src/shared/infrastructure/firebase/client.ts`; the exported `firestore()` at line 38 has zero callers.

findings.claim: The Publish write path destroys the file the product is named after. A no-op write through `share-writer.ts` leaves only 3.64% of the pinned corpus byte-identical, and throws outright on 171 files.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, 1084 files, all sha256-verified (0 mismatches). 907 have frontmatter. Replicating `src/modules/share/infrastructure/share-writer.ts` exactly (`matter(c)` then `matter.stringify(parsed.content, {...parsed.data})`): byte_identical=33 (3.64% of 907), gray-matter throws=171, byte_changed=703. Of the 736 that parse, 4.48% survive.

findings.claim: The damage is semantic, not cosmetic: a bare date in frontmatter becomes an ISO timestamp in 84.78% of parseable files. `title: 2026-05-26` becomes `title: 2026-05-26T00:00:00.000Z` — a user-visible title change in Obsidian, a broken Dataview filter, a broken Hugo/Jekyll build.
findings.evidence: Same corpus_id. files_where_a_bare_date_became_an_ISO_timestamp = 624 of 736 parsed = 84.78%. Example rows: `md/Daily/2026-05-26.md -> title=2026-05-26`; `md/Research/Knowledge Base/AI/12-Factor Agents (Dex Horthy).md -> created=2026-06-27, updated=2026-06-27, mirrored=2026-07-27`. Crucially, `of_changed_js_data_stable: 703, of_changed_js_data_differs: 0` — re-parsing the mangled output yields identical JS data, so ANY test asserting on `matter().data` round-trips green while the bytes on disk are wrong.

findings.claim: The source comment on the destructive path claims to do the correct thing and does not. It says 'splicing' and calls a whole-document serializer — a documentation defect that would let a reviewer approve it.
findings.evidence: `src/modules/share/infrastructure/share-writer.ts:1-5` header: "writes the `public_slug` frontmatter field of a note by reading the current body via the vault reader, **splicing the key into the YAML frontmatter**, and committing through commitChanges." The body at line ~28 is `const next = matter.stringify(parsed.content, data);` — a full re-serialisation of the whole YAML map from a plain JS object. This violates D7 (splice-only) in the one shipped write path.

findings.claim: The repo already contains a correct preserving path that Publish does not use — and even that path only reaches 31.86% safe, so a library swap is NOT the fix. Splice is required.
findings.evidence: `src/modules/preview/presentation/frontmatter.ts` (eemeli/yaml `parseDocument`, header: "edits mutate the AST and PRESERVE comments / quoting / key order"), consumed by `PropertiesPanel.tsx:79` via `EditorPane.tsx:647`. Ported exactly and run on the same corpus_id: byte_identical=119, refused-and-left-untouched=170, changed=618 → 31.86% safe vs 3.64%. Dates ARE preserved. But `[daily]` → `[ daily ]` and long flow arrays explode to multi-line block flow. Retesting with `doc.toString({lineWidth:0})` moves it only 119→126 (31.86%→32.64%), so the reflow is flow-style spacing, not line width.

findings.claim: 18.9% of a real Obsidian vault's frontmatter is not valid YAML under ANY standard parser, because `related: [[a]], [[b]]` is the Obsidian wikilink idiom and YAML reads `[[a]]` as a closed nested sequence. This breaks the stated Phase-1 gate feature (Obsidian round-trip fidelity) at the parser level.

The 'mother file' would be 24.4 MB. The graph is mostly dust, and the mechanism the vision is built on is a rounding error. NEGATIVE 2 — 'our editor on the max plan should give features unseen in the industry' is contradicted by the demand corpus, which asks almost exclusively for table stakes. Of the 89 sourced feature requests in docs/research/frontmatter-raw-corpus.json, request #1 is "Always-visible sync status indicator (what synced, what is pending, when last synced)". NEGATIVE 3 — the graph view is shipped, carries a runtime dependency, and has zero demand in the evidence base. `react-force-graph-2d ^1.29.1` is in package.json; `src/modules/graph/` and `GraphButton.tsx` are built; FEATURE-GAP-REPORT lists it under shipped 'Rendering & knowledge'.
