In the round-2 corpus (frontmatter-r2-raw-corpus.json) the phrase 'graph view' appears **0 times**. Combined with the median-0 degree measurement above, the graph is decorative in this product.

NEGATIVE 4 — the mockup's right rail is over-built relative to the review loop it is meant to serve. Document Outline, Tags and Bookmarks, and AI Edit are all shipped (outline, bookmarks.ts, AIMenu.tsx, ghost-text.ts, /api/ai/*), Document History is shipped but has no diff, and Comment has no code and no backing collection in firestore.rules. Four of five rail slots are filled by features that work for one person; the one slot that requires a second person is empty and its data model is not designed. Adding a fifth rail item before there is a second user is strictly negative work.

NEGATIVE 5 — arguing against my own area's premise: 'what frontmatter misses' is the wrong question this quarter, because the biggest measurable defect is in something already shipped. Publish already fires the destructive frontmatter rewrite on every note; Document History already lists commits with no diff; Export already labels HTML as Word; the test suite already reports 247 files of which 164 are abandoned worktrees. A gap analysis that outputs a longer build list makes all four worse. The highest-value output of this area is a shorter list, not a longer one.
unclaimed: A HUMAN review loop — threaded comments on text ranges, plus accept/reject suggestions, plus resolve — anchored into plain `.md` files that stay clean, with the threads outside the file. Searched: HackMD pricing markup (has the loop, has no local files or vault); Moment.dev homepage/docs/pricing (has the files + realtime + roles, `grep -ioE 'comment|suggest'` returns 0); inkeep/open-knowledge `.changeset/comments-v1.md` (has the anchoring, explicitly declines teammates — "not a message to a teammate"); Obsidian help `Collaborate on a shared vault.md` (has shared vaults + version history, states no cursors, no fine-grained permissions, no comments); Craft and Bear homepages (0 occurrences of 'comment'). Nobody occupies the intersection.

A comment anchor that survives the markdown-body ↔ rendered-text boundary in a mode-switching editor. open-knowledge had to write a bespoke syntax-elastic matcher (`passage-match.ts`) plus a client-side resolver (`anchor-search.ts`) because "The server's `start`/`end` can't be used directly here: those are offsets into the markdown BODY, while this index is over RENDERED text." Their solution is GPLv3, so it is a design reference and not a dependency. No npm package solves this — searched registry.npmjs.org for the CodeMirror collab primitives (`@codemirror/collab` latest 6.1.1, modified 2026-04-13) and it addresses operational transform, not content-derived anchoring.

A frontmatter writer that is genuinely splice-only. Measured this session: gray-matter reaches 3.64% byte fidelity, eemeli/yaml's Document AST reaches 31.86%, and `lineWidth:0` adds 0.78 points. No library in the repo's dependency tree achieves it. This is the first concrete, in-product customer for MDMAX's `mdmax edit --old --new` primitive (docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §10.3) — and it already has two callers waiting (the Publish button and the Properties panel).

A tolerant parser for Obsidian's frontmatter dialect. `related: [[a]], [[b]]` is not valid YAML and 18.9% of the pinned corpus's frontmatter files fail on it under both js-yaml and eemeli/yaml. Obsidian itself accepts these files (they are in a live vault), so any tool claiming Obsidian round-trip fidelity needs a parser nobody publishes. Searched npm for a wikilink-tolerant YAML frontmatter parser; found none — closest is gray-matter's pluggable engines, which still delegate to js-yaml.
result.design:
"WHAT SHIPS, in order, and what does not.

S-1 (half a day, before anything). Three corrections to things already shipped, each with a test that must go RED first. (a) Route `share-writer.ts` through a splice: read the file, locate the byte range of the `public_slug` key (or the insertion point after the last key), replace only those bytes. Never call `matter.stringify`. Gate: replay the full pinned corpus through publish-then-unpublish and assert 100% byte-identity on all 907 frontmatter files, and that the 171 unparseable files are touched at all — today Publish 502s on them. (b) Add `.claude/worktrees` to vitest `exclude`; gate is `vitest list --filesOnly` returning 247→83. (c) Relabel the `.doc` export as "Word (HTML)" or remove it; it is currently a false claim in a user-facing menu.

S0 (the real unlock). One user table and one second identity. Everything in the mockup's right rail that matters is downstream of this, and `firestore.rules` has already designed it — `memberUids` + `roles: map<uid,"owner"|"editor"|"viewer">` — with zero code behind it. Implement exactly that schema, no more. Add the missing collection the rules do not name: `comments`.

S1 (the review loop, and only the review loop). Copy Google's OWN split, because it is the split D2 already chose: comments are a sidecar with `{anchor, quotedFileContent, resolved, assignee, replies[], reply.action: resolve|reopen}` — that is thirteen fields on Comment and ten on Reply in Drive v3, and it is the entire data model. Suggestions are NOT Docs suggestions and must not be sold as them: Docs carries `suggestedInsertionIds` on every TextRun and supports nesting; a `.md` file under D6 cannot. Ship suggestions as an out-of-band patch set (base sha + hunks + author), rendered inline, accepted by splice. Say so publicly; the honest framing is stronger than the imitation.

CARRIER. Comments never enter the file — D2, and Google, and open-knowledge all agree. The sidecar must satisfy the plan's own §11 S6 gate: delete the entire sidecar, `git status` is clean, every file byte-identical.

THE ANCHORING SURFACE NOBODY HAS SCOPED. The mockups ship Live/Edit/Split/Read AND a Comment rail, so the body-offset vs rendered-offset problem is a day-one bug, not a later refinement. Budget it explicitly: anchor offsets are stored against the markdown body; the Live/Read views need a syntax-elastic matcher that skips inline emphasis, code, strikethrough, link tails `](...)`, and line-leading block markers. Fail SAFE to `orphaned`, never guess.

FIRST TEN MINUTES — what a user notices, ranked by what actually bites. 1. There is no signup; the app admits one GitHub login. 2. Saving is a git commit with a message box — a Google Docs competitor with a commit message field is dead on the first screen. 3. Sharing produces one public read-only URL with no roles, no expiry, no password, and no comment box. 4. Document History lists commit messages with no diff, and the messages are strings like `share: set public_slug=...`. 5. There is no presence, so nothing tells you someone else is there. 6. Publishing a note silently rewrites its dates; publishing 18.9% of a real vault returns a 502.

WHAT IS IN THE MOCKUPS AND NOT WORTH BUILDING NOW. The graph (0 of 89 requests, median degree 0). A fifth right-rail slot of any kind. Bookmarks beyond what already exists. And per the founder's vision specifically: the mother-markdown container and the transclusion tree — 45 uses in 1,084 files does not justify a format.

POSITIONING CORRECTION. The plan's "unclaimed combination" — realtime collab + plain markdown + git — is claimed: Moment.dev ships it at $30/mo for five seats, and Obsidian ships shared vaults at $4/seat. What is unclaimed is the review loop on files you own. Reprice the wedge around comments and suggestions, not around multiplayer."
result.measurement:
"Four experiments, in dependency order. Everything below is runnable this week and each has a number that can come out badly.

M1 — THE SPLICE GATE (settles whether MDMAX's core primitive is real). Corpus: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, n=1084 files / 907 with frontmatter. Task: for every file, run publish (set `public_slug`) then unpublish (remove it). Verifier: an INDEPENDENT oracle — a byte comparator that does not share a line of code with the writer (per LR#60). Pre-registered predictions, recorded now: gray-matter path 33/907 byte-identical (already measured, 3.64%); eemeli/yaml Document path 119/907 + 170 refused (31.86%); a correct splice must reach 907/907 with zero refusals, INCLUDING the 171 files no YAML parser can read. If the splice cannot handle those 171, that is the real finding and it should be published.

M2 — THE RANGE ANCHOR, ACROSS THE RENDER BOUNDARY (settles whether comments can anchor at all). The 99.627% figure is a BLOCK figure. Comments anchor RANGES, and in this product they must survive a mode switch. Corpus: the same pinned corpus plus the plan's W1 second corpus (`~/.claude/skills-src`, 474 files, 5,013,124 bytes — a second author, which this program does not currently have). Tasks: sample 2,000 character ranges stratified by (length in tokens; contains inline emphasis / code / a link; is inside a list item or heading). For each, mutate the document by one real git revision and attempt re-find. Arms: (1) exact quote, (2) quote + 32-char context per open-knowledge's `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LEN`, (3) diff3-assisted (the plan's arm 7), (4) syntax-elastic match across the body↔rendered boundary. Report correct / FALSE / refusal separately, stratified. Hand-audit 200 for false matches. Pre-registered prediction: false-match rate rises above the block figure and refusal roughly doubles, and ranges containing a link are the dominant failure — open-knowledge says missing link tails means "a passage containing any link could not be matched at all."

M3 — THE ONE CONVERSATION THIS PROGRAM HAS NEVER HAD (n=5, one week). Zero users, zero interviews, zero willingness-to-pay probes exist across the whole record — the plan's own W3. Five people who have shared a markdown doc for review in the last month. One task: watch them try to get a comment from a non-technical colleague. Pre-registered prediction, which is the thing I most want falsified: the blocker they hit first is the login wall (D3), not anchoring, not fidelity. Google states the mechanism verbatim — "People who aren't signed in to a Google Account show up as anonymous animals in your file." If four of five stall at signup, D3 must be revisited at auth, not after.

M4 — THE COMPETITIVE FLOOR, RE-RUN QUARTERLY. HackMD ships the full loop free (verified at markup level this session); Moment.dev ships realtime on git-backed .md; open-knowledge is at 3,239 stars and 14,790 npm downloads/week after eight weeks. Re-measure all three every 90 days: does open-knowledge's comments-v1 acquire a teammate model (their changeset explicitly excludes it), and does Moment add comments? Either event closes the only unclaimed intersection found. Track via api.github.com stars/pushed_at and api.npmjs.org downloads — both reachable by curl and both used for the figures above."
result.kill_condition:
"KILL 1 — If the splice writer cannot reach 907/907 byte-identity on the pinned corpus under an independent oracle, and specifically cannot round-trip the 171 files that no YAML parser reads, then the phrase 'round-trip-sacred frontmatter' must be struck from every document. The app is named frontmatter; shipping a product that mangles frontmatter in the one path that already fires is a positioning contradiction that no feature can offset, and the Obsidian-power-user beachhead (the plan's #1 segment, judged 'in the first minute on their own vault') is unwinnable.

KILL 2 — If M2's hand-audited FALSE-match rate on ranges exceeds ~0.5%, comments cannot use content-derived anchoring as a primary mechanism and must fall back to visible orphaning with a quote-plus-digest. This is the plan's own K3, and my measurement of the render-boundary problem makes it materially more likely than the block figure suggests.

KILL 3 — If multi-tenancy does not ship, kill the collaboration story outright and reposition. Today `isAllowed()` compares one string, `firestore()` has zero callers, and the rules do not name a comments collection. Every review-loop item in the mockup, every phase-3 deliverable, and the entire 'Google Docs for markdown' pitch is downstream of a users table that has zero engine content and will therefore keep losing priority to compiler work precisely because it is uninteresting. This is the plan's K6 and it is the single most likely way this program fails.

KILL 4 — If M3 shows that four of five reviewers stall at the login wall, D3 as currently framed kills the wedge, and the correct move is anonymous commenters with owner-seat-only billing. Do not defer this to 'after auth'; the auth decision IS the product decision.

KILL 5 — If open-knowledge ships a teammate model on top of its existing anchoring (they have `anchor.ts`, `passage-match.ts`, `comment-scrub.ts` and a shipped comment UI; the only missing piece is sync and identity), or if Moment.dev adds comments to its existing realtime-on-git-backed-.md stack, the last unclaimed intersection closes. Both are three-month risks, not three-year ones. Re-check quarterly per M4."
result.effort: High. Roughly four hours. Six original measurement scripts written and run against the pinned corpus (`rt2`–`rt5`, `loss`, `graph`/`graph2`, `compare`/`compare2` — round-trip fidelity, date coercion, parser failure, metadata loss, link topology, and a two-path writer comparison), all sha256-verified against corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… with 0 mismatches; one classifier discarded and rewritten after it produced a false BODY_CHANGED signal, and one semantic-corruption count discarded as over-counted (flow→block reflow) and replaced with the unambiguous date-coercion metric. Full read of `src/` (212 files, 21,415 LOC) with targeted verification of auth, share, repository, editor, export, history and preview modules plus `firestore.rules`. `npx vitest list` executed to confirm suite composition. Sixteen live primary fetches by curl: Google Docs API v1 and Drive API v3 discovery documents, Obsidian's help source on GitHub, HackMD pricing (down to SVG path data to distinguish check from not-included), Moment.dev homepage/docs/pricing, Almanac, Coda, Craft, Bear, Google Docs sharing help, HN Algolia (four queries, 12-month window), api.github.com repo stats, api.npmjs.org download points, and raw source files from inkeep/open-knowledge. No writes outside $TMPDIR; no commits, installs, or destructive operations.
result.unverified:
"WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, and where it actually sits.

1. Whether Obsidian itself renders the 170 invalid-YAML frontmatter blocks correctly. INFERENCE, not primary. I verified only that both js-yaml and eemeli/yaml reject them and that the files live in a working Obsidian vault. I did not launch Obsidian. If Obsidian also fails on them, the 'Obsidian round-trip fidelity' framing needs restating — the vault is already partly broken.

2. The whole corpus is ONE operator's vault plus this repo. The link-topology negative (median degree 0, 45 transclusions) is the finding most exposed to this. The plan's own W1 names the fix (`~/.claude/skills-src`, a second author); it has not been done and I did not do it. Treat NEGATIVE 1 as strong for this vault and unproven in general.

3. Moment.dev having no comments is a NEGATIVE SEARCH over three fetched pages (homepage, /docs index, /pricing) plus a 404 on /docs/collaboration. I did not install the app. Absence of the word is weaker evidence than presence of the feature would be.

4. HackMD's 'Suggest edit' launch DATE. The pricing table marks it 'New'; hackmd.io/@hackmd/changelog and /c/changelog both 404 and the only changelog I reached (@docs/changelog) is API-only, last entry 2026-03-19. So I can say suggest edit is free and recent, not when it shipped.

5. Mobile quality. My 13-responsive-prefixes-across-74-files number is a PROXY (a source grep), not a rendering test. Tagged inference in the findings. I did not open the app at any viewport.

6. I did not run the app at all. Every claim about src/ is a source read. Specifically unverified by execution: that Publish actually 502s on the 171 unparseable files (I traced the code path — `matter()` throws uncaught in `writeSlug`, and `POST /api/share` catches everything into `upstream_failure` 502 — but I did not exercise it against a live vault). This is the single claim in my headline's second half that most deserves a live check before anyone quotes it.

7. The `.doc` export claim is a source read of a comment plus the absence of any OOXML code; I did not open the produced file in Word or Google Docs.

8. SEARCH-ONLY, not verified: the Product Hunt sweep. I covered HN via the Algolia API, GitHub via api.github.com, and npm via api.npmjs.org, but did not query Product Hunt. There may be 2026 entrants I missed there. Stashpad returned a TLS handshake failure rather than a status code, so 'dead' is a guess, not a measurement — I report the handshake failure, not a verdict.

9. I did NOT re-derive the 99.627% re-anchoring figure, and nothing in this area's work bears on it either way. My render-boundary finding raises a NEW concern about ranges that the existing number does not address; it does not measure it.

10. Multi-run stability: the corpus measurements are deterministic file I/O with no sampling, so LR#63's three-run rule does not bind. I did re-run the round-trip measurement four times across four script revisions and the core numbers (907 / 171 / 33 / 624) were stable each time."

result.area: Custom reference pointers, custom definitions, and the library-import model
result.headline: Across 5,245 markdown files in five corpora, authors use rich construct vocabularies densely but essentially never declare one — 99.69% of the 4,538 `:::` directives in Docusaurus's own repo are among its 9 vendor-shipped keywords and all 14 exceptions are the three tutorial strings that teach the feature, and 847 independently-authored npm docs use exactly GitHub's 5 built-in callout types with zero inventions — while the one corpus where a spec *forced* declaration produced drift rather than vocabulary (four real OKF bundles: 5/0/5/21 `type` values, ≥8 of the 21 mutual collisions, four incompatible naming conventions across them, 0 of 4 declaring `okf_version: "0.2"`), so MDMAX should ship no declaration syntax, no registry and no library import, and instead ship the inverse — vocabulary *inference and drift detection* over values that already exist.
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED before measuring: my headline is wrong if either (a) any real corpus shows authors inventing vocabulary items beyond a vendor-shipped set at a rate above ~5% of uses, or (b) a shipping markdown tool exposes a document-declared vocabulary mechanism with real *authoring* adoption (not download-count adoption). I went looking for both. For (a) I deliberately fetched the two corpora most likely to refute me — facebook/docusaurus (1,617 md/mdx, `:::` in 60.61% of files) and jupyter-book/mystmd (431 files, 46 distinct roles in 25.75% of files). Both LOOK like refutations and neither is: Docusaurus's 4,538 directive uses are 4,524 (99.69%) among the 9 keywords hardcoded in `packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/remark/admonitions/index.ts`, and the 14 remaining are only `my-custom-admonition`/`unusedDirective`/`NotAContainerDirective`; MyST's 46 roles (`ref` 622, `term` 41, `numref`, `abbr`, `eq`, `kbd`) are all Sphinx/MyST built-ins. MyST is the closest thing to a refutation and I am recording it as one caveat: it proves a 46-term vocabulary is *usable*, which contradicts a naive reading of the single-digit cap — it just is not user-declared. For (b) I found a genuine hit: `remark-lint-frontmatter-schema`, 36,745 downloads/week (api.npmjs.org, 2026-07-24→30), which ships `'$schema': content/creative-work.schema.yaml` inside frontmatter with "Locally defined `'$schema'` takes precedence over global settings". I then searched for authored instances and found ZERO `$schema`/`@`/`x-`/`fm`-prefixed frontmatter keys across 3,197 files (pinned corpus 1,084 + npm 847 + OKF 1,266). Not falsified — but (b) is a search-limited null, not a proof of absence, and it is the weakest link in my case.

findings.claim: The single largest authored directive corpus in existence proves the demand is for a big VENDOR-SHIPPED vocabulary, not a mechanism to declare your own: 99.69% of directive uses are vendor keywords and 100% of the exceptions are the tutorial that teaches extension.
findings.evidence: Corpus D (explicit selection, NOT the pinned corpus): facebook/docusaurus fetched 2026-08-01 via `codeload.github.com/facebook/docusaurus/tar.gz/refs/heads/main`, all *.md/*.mdx excluding node_modules and .git = 1,617 files / 10,760,035 bytes, selection_sha256=259faf56855af151… . `:::`-directive occurrences = 4,538 in 980 files (60.61% of files), 12 distinct names: tip 1701, warning 1151, info 723, note 660, danger 257, caution 22, my-custom-admonition 12, important 8, unusedDirective 1, NotAContainerDirective 1, secondary 1, success 1. The vendor set is read from primary source `packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/remark/admonitions/index.ts` lines 15-19, verbatim: `export const DefaultAdmonitionOptions: AdmonitionOptions = { keywords: ['secondary','info','success','danger','note','tip','warning','important','caution'], extendDefaults: true };`. 4,524 of 4,538 = 99.69% are in that 9-keyword set; the 14 outside it are three strings that occur only in Docusaurus's own docs about admonitions.

findings.claim: Given a syntax that permits an ARBITRARY type name, ~850 independent third-party authors invented exactly zero types — they used the five GitHub ships and stopped.
findings.evidence: Corpus B (explicit selection, NOT the pinned corpus): all *.md under /Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/node_modules to depth 3 = 847 files / 7,733,433 bytes, selection_sha256=21ace73c42f864dfb10b032fe8be198c578a2a9c569eae1acab5c2c7a22c274f. Callouts outside fences: 74 occurrences in 18 files (2.13%), distinct types = 5, exactly [note 45, warning 11, important 10, tip 4, caution 4] — GitHub's complete built-in alert set. Zero user-invented types. Same corpus: `:::` directives = 1 occurrence (`caution`), Hugo shortcodes = 0, MyST ```{} = 0, `^block-id` = 0, `{#id}` = 6 occurrences in 1 file of 847.

findings.claim: Where a spec FORCED a declaration, four real bundles produced drift, not vocabulary — and the largest is ~38% self-colliding six weeks after the spec shipped.
findings.evidence: Corpus C (explicit selection): four real OKF bundles fetched 2026-08-01 via codeload tarballs of refs/heads/main — OWOX/models (186 md), aws-samples/sample-okf-llm-wiki (29), coleam00/cole-medin-knowledge-base (902), jkroepke/okf-crossplane-v2 (149); 1,266 md total. Distinct `type` values per bundle: 5 / 0 / 5 / 21. The 21-value bundle contains `reference` AND `Reference`; `function`, `Crossplane Function`, `functioninput`, `Crossplane Function Input`; `guide`, `developmentguide`, `Crossplane Development Guide` — ≥8 of 21 are mutual collisions. Across all four: 29 distinct values in four incompatible conventions (`concept` lowercase, `raw-transcript` kebab, `OWOX Data Mart`/`BigQuery Table` Title Case). `okf_version` is ABSENT in 2 of 4 and `"0.1"` in the other 2 — zero declare v0.2, one week after SPEC.md v0.2 shipped. jkroepke/okf-crossplane-v2 also carries 58 distinct frontmatter keys across 149 files, including Claude-Code agent keys (`systemPromptMode`, `inheritSkills`, `defaultContext`, `tools`) leaking into an OKF bundle under §4.1's "Producers MAY include any additional keys".

findings.claim: CORRECTION, and it is load-bearing: the flagship precedent cited for D9 ("a document NAMES a capability, never CARRIES one") is a counterexample. JSON-LD explicitly permits carrying its definition inline, and that is the first form the spec teaches. The correct rule is denotation-vs-procedure, not name-vs-carry.
findings.evidence: W3C JSON-LD 1.1 spec source, raw.githubusercontent.com/w3c/json-ld-syntax/main/index.html (578,006 bytes, fetched 2026-08-01), verbatim: "The value of @context MUST be null, an IRI reference, a context definition, or an array composed of any of these." And: "Contexts can either be directly embedded into the document (an embedded context) or be referenced using a URL." An embedded @context is a closed term→IRI map — pure denotation, no execution, no dereference, no recursion — which is exactly the class the established evidence measured safe (140/140) versus procedure redefinition (98.2%→38.6%). D9 as written forbids a construct that the standard it cites permits and that the data says is safe.

findings.claim: Vim hardened the in-band-directive design again FOUR MONTHS AGO, and the shape it converged on is the transplantable rule: a file-embedded directive may LOWER its own capability and may never RAISE it, with everything outside a 24-item inert allowlist silently ignored.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/vim/vim/master/runtime/doc/options.txt, `'modelinestrict' 'mlst' boolean (default: on)` — "When on, only a safe subset of options can be set from a |modeline|", followed by a 24-option allowlist (autoindent…vartabstop, all presentation-only), then "Any other option set from a modeline will be silently ignored. This option cannot be set from a |modeline| or in the |sandbox|, for security reasons." The asymmetry, verbatim: "As an exception, `set nomodeline` is honored from within a modeline even when 'modelinestrict' is on. Other forms (`set modeline=0`, `set modeline!`, `set invmodeline`) are still silently ignored. This lets a file disable further modeline processing for itself." Same file: "No other commands than \"set\" are supported, for security reasons (somebody might create a Trojan horse text file with modelines)" and "disable modelines before editing untrusted text". Recency via api.github.com/search/commits?q=repo:vim/vim+modelinestrict: 4c2879471 2026-04-14 "patch 9.2.0350: Enabling modelines poses a risk"; 439722711 2026-05-18 "patch 9.2.0499: modeline: allow to disable modelines with modelinestrict".

findings.claim: 18.91% of the pinned corpus's frontmatter blocks are not parseable YAML, and the cause is a markdown vocabulary construct sitting in a YAML value slot — which is D8's own mechanism failing in production, at scale, today.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 (all 1,084 files re-read and re-hashed this session: 1,084 present, 0 missing, 0 hash mismatches). Excluding the 23 reserved index.md/log.md filenames, 1,061 non-reserved files: 899 (84.73%) carry frontmatter delimiters, but js-yaml (via the repo's own node_modules) parses only 729 (68.71%) to a mapping — 170 blocks THROW. Verbatim failing line from `md/Research/Knowledge Base/AI/18 Claude Code Token Hacks in 18 Minutes.md`: `entities: [[[Claude Code]], [[Anthropic]], [[Opus]], [[Sonnet]], [[Haiku]], [[Codex]], [[MCP]], [[Google Workspace CLI]]]`. gray-matter (7,492,225 downloads/week) throws on the same file: "YAMLException: missed comma between flow collection entries at line 24, column 73". The second, quieter failure mode is worse: `entities: [[[A]], [[B]]]` PARSES, silently, to `{"entities":[[["A"]],[["B"]]]}` — the wikilink is destroyed into a nested array with no error at all.

findings.claim: CORRECTION to the OKF interop position: the pinned corpus is 59.19% conformant with OKF v0.2 §11 by accident, not the ~75% a regex census reports — the 16pp gap is entirely the broken-YAML files, which means any conformance number computed with a regex over frontmatter is inflated.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, 1,061 non-reserved files. Regex proxy (`^type:\s*\S`) gives 798 = 75.21%. True js-yaml parse requiring §11.1 (parseable YAML block) AND §11.2 (non-empty string `type`) gives 628 = 59.19%, distinct type values 10 (synthesis 195, skill 184, workflow 184, concept 33, entity 13, map 13, strategy 2, architecture 2, report 1, question 1) — not the 12 the regex reports. OKF SPEC.md v0.2 §11 verbatim: "1. Every non-reserved `.md` file in the tree contains a parseable YAML frontmatter block. 2. Every frontmatter block contains a non-empty `type` field."

findings.claim: The 45.8M-downloads/week markdown writer CORRUPTS GitHub's own alert syntax, which rules out `[!TYPE]` as a vocabulary carrier on fidelity grounds before any security argument is reached.
findings.evidence:
Run this session against the repo's own node_modules (mdast-util-from-markdown + mdast-util-to-markdown + mdast-util-gfm, full GFM enabled). Input `"> [!NOTE]
> Useful information.
"` → output `"> \[!NOTE]
> Useful information.
"` — a backslash inserted into the user's file. Same for `> [!REVIEW]`. This is byte-for-byte the DesktopCommanderMCP #440 failure class (`[x]` → `\[x]`) the plan cites as its nightmare. By contrast, in the same run these all round-trip IDENTICAL: `:::tip` block, `:::review{id=r1}`, `## Title {#anchor}`, ```` ```js title="a.js" ````, ```` ```fm-vocab ````, `[fm:vocab]: sgnk/v1@1.0.0`, `[x](./a.md "fm:vocab=sgnk/v1")`. remark-parse weekly downloads 45,820,243 (api.npmjs.org, 2026-07-24→30).

findings.claim: CORRECTION to a settled finding: the `[//]: #` idiom — one of only two carriers reported invisible in 24/24 renderers — does not survive a write. And carrier OCCUPANCY, which nobody measured, varies by 2,400× across corpora, so any single-corpus carrier ranking is worthless.
findings.evidence: Round-trip run this session: `[//]: # (fm:vocab sgnk/v1)` → `[//]: # "fm:vocab sgnk/v1"` (parens become quotes). Occupancy, three explicit selections: link reference definitions are 9 occurrences in 9 files (0.83%) of the pinned corpus sha256:3a010b16… but 5,079 occurrences in 198 of 847 files (23.38%) in Corpus B — a densely occupied channel in third-party docs. Fence META strings (everything after the language word) are 0 of 7,714 fences (0.00%) in the pinned corpus and 1 of 5,007 (0.02%, `npm2yarn`) in Corpus B, but 6,201 of 12,916 (48.01%) in Corpus D/Docusaurus, dominated by `title="docusaurus.config.js"` 2136, `npm2yarn` 1012, `title="sidebars.js"` 408. Link `title` attribute occupancy: 23 of 2,035 inline links (1.13%) pinned, 253 of 19,462 (1.30%) Corpus B — i.e. ~98.8% unoccupied, materially worse than the 99.94% previously reported for that channel.

findings.claim: The exact mechanism this area was asked to invent already ships for markdown at 36,745 downloads/week, with the per-file-vs-per-project precedence question already answered — MDMAX should adopt `$schema`, not invent a key, and the novelty claim is dead.
findings.evidence: `remark-lint-frontmatter-schema` — api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week = 36,745 (2026-07-24→30). README (raw.githubusercontent.com/JulianCataldo/remark-lint-frontmatter-schema/master/README.md), verbatim: "Schema association can be done directly **inside** the **frontmatter** of the **Markdown** file, relative to project root, thanks to the `'$schema'` key" with the example `'$schema': content/creative-work.schema.yaml`, plus a project-level `schemas: { './content/creative-work.schema.yaml': ['./content/creative-work/*.md'] }` glob map, and the precedence rule verbatim: "Locally defined `'$schema'` takes precedence over global settings below." Its own feature list names both: "Global patterns or in-file schemas associations".

findings.claim: OKF v0.2 is not competing for the vocabulary slot — it has already implemented MDMAX's D8 and D9 as normative MUSTs, and it explicitly defers the runtime rather than acquiring one. The correct position is interop, and interop is nearly free.
findings.evidence: okf/SPEC.md v0.2, raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/main/okf/SPEC.md, 37,544 bytes, read in full this session. D8: §4.1 verbatim "Type values are **not** registered centrally. Producers SHOULD pick values that are descriptive and self-explanatory; consumers MUST tolerate unknown types gracefully" and §11 "consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle because of: … Unknown `type` values. Unknown additional frontmatter keys." D9: §10 verbatim "OKF records the computation and the means to check it; it does not execute anything itself"; `runtime: bigquery`, `executor.resource: references/skills/run-on-bq.md`, `attester.resource: references/attesters/revenue.py` are all NAMES; §10.3 "The agent MAY only supply *values* for the declared `parameters`; it MUST NOT author or edit the computation." On the runtime, §12 'Considered and deferred' verbatim: "The full runtime protocol: receipt and verdict wire formats, and the attestation lifecycle around a run. The attester ABI, portability, and sandboxing, likely bundled with future work on serving and Skills."

findings.claim: CORRECTION to how OKF's 'keyed identity' has been characterised: it is a join key into a frontmatter LIST resolved through markdown footnotes — not block identity — and its stated rationale is verbatim MDMAX's anchoring rationale, which means the competitor chose DECLARE over DERIVE for the one identity it needed.
findings.evidence: OKF SPEC.md v0.2 §5.1, verbatim: "To attribute a specific claim, use a markdown footnote whose label is a `sources[].id`" … "The footnote label is the join key into `sources`; consumers resolve attribution through the matching entry, not by parsing the footnote prose. Labels are keyed rather than positional (`sources[0]`) because agents constantly rewrite these documents: a positional index misattributes silently the moment the list is reordered, whereas a stable `id` survives reordering." This is arm 8 (`{#id}` declared attributes) of the MDMAX benchmark, shipped. Its authoring substrate, measured: footnote DEFINITIONS = 0 across the pinned corpus corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… (the 276 apparent `[^…]` matches outside fences are bash character classes in Skills/*/skill.md, e.g. `sed -E 's|^https?://'`), and 4 occurrences in 2 of 847 files in Corpus B. OKF has bet its identity mechanism on markdown's least-used construct.

findings.claim: Live re-derivation confirms every load-bearing external number in the established evidence, and adds the one Typst gap from the index side rather than the source-comment side.
findings.evidence: Fetched 2026-08-01: `https://packages.typst.org/preview/index.json` = 2,060,620 bytes, 4,425 rows, 1,481 distinct `name`, newest updatedAt 1785509080 = 2026-07-31T14:44:40Z — reproduces the established figures exactly. Index entry keys are exactly ['authors','compiler','description','entrypoint','exclude','keywords','license','name','repository','updatedAt','version'] — NO hash/digest/sha field, confirming "Typst deliberately skips integrity verification" independently of the `typst-kit/src/packages.rs` comment. `https://ctan.org/json/2.0/packages` = 7,021 entries. api.npmjs.org last-week: marked 61,032,058; remark-parse 45,820,243; markdown-it 27,323,922; gray-matter 7,492,225; markdown-it-attrs 280,897; markdown-it-decorate 1,094 (the 257× ratio reproduces). api.github.com/repos/tc39/proposal-modules-pragma: archived=true, stars 81, pushed_at 2022-01-24T18:58:28Z.

findings.claim: Hugo's inline-shortcode precedent is confirmed verbatim and is stronger than reported — the setting is documented on the SECURITY configuration page, and Hugo states the trust boundary in one sentence that transfers directly to frontmatter's threat model.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/gohugoio/hugo/master/docs/content/en/content-management/shortcodes.md, verbatim: "Hugo's security model is based on the premise that template and configuration authors are trusted, but content authors are not. This model enables generation of HTML output safe against code injection. To conform with this security model, creating _shortcode_ templates within content is disabled by default." And raw.githubusercontent.com/gohugoio/hugo/master/docs/content/en/configuration/security.md lists `enableInlineShortcodes` alongside `exec.allow` and `allowContent`: "(`bool`) Whether to enable [inline shortcodes][]. Default is `false`." In frontmatter/MDMAX the content author is by construction untrusted — a reviewer with a login (D3) is a content author.

findings.claim: CORRECTION on adoption evidence: remark-directive's 3,153,286 weekly downloads are transitive Docusaurus pulls, not authoring adoption — the download-weighted signal and the typed-into-a-file signal disagree by orders of magnitude and only the second one is real.
findings.evidence: api.npmjs.org last-week: remark-directive 3,153,286; mdast-util-directive 4,370,162. registry.npmjs.org/@docusaurus%2Fmdx-loader/latest = version 3.10.2 with `dependencies['remark-directive'] = '^3.0.0'`. Against that: `:::` directives occur 0 times in the pinned corpus (corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, 1,084 files) and 1 time in Corpus B (847 files). The mechanism is in three million installs and two documents.

findings.claim: DEFECT in the artifact created to enforce evidence discipline: the pinned corpus's own `corpus_id` is not re-derivable from the manifest, and the derivation script is not in the repository.
findings.evidence: docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json declares corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 and docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §0 describes it as "a hash over the sorted (path, sha256) list of 1,084 files / 25,548,765 bytes". I attempted 30 serializations of that description (root-prefixed and not; separators \n, '', space, |, \t; raw concat, json.dumps, json.dumps with compact separators) — none reproduces the declared digest. `git log -- docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json` returns no commits: the file is untracked. This is rule P2 ("No headline without a committed derivation script and its captured output") failing on the file written to enforce rule P1. The file LIST itself is sound — all 1,084 files re-read this session, 0 missing, 0 hash mismatches.

findings.claim: Docusaurus independently confirms the per-project-beats-per-file rule in source, with a comment that also predicts the direction of drift.
findings.evidence: packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/remark/admonitions/index.ts, verbatim: `export type AdmonitionOptions = { keywords: string[]; extendDefaults: boolean; };` and, in normalizeAdmonitionOptions, the comment "// By default it makes more sense to append keywords to the default ones / // Adding custom keywords is more common than disabling existing ones" guarding `options.keywords = [...DefaultAdmonitionOptions.keywords, ...options.keywords]`. The extension point is a build-config array. There is no per-document form of it anywhere in the loader.

negatives: NEG-1 — THE OBSERVED USER-INVENTION RATE IS 0.31%, AND ALL OF IT IS TUTORIAL CONTENT. Across the two largest authored directive corpora available, plus 847 independently-authored third-party docs, plus a 1,084-file power-user vault, the number of genuinely user-invented vocabulary items is 3 distinct strings, all three of which occur only inside documentation teaching the extension feature (`my-custom-admonition` 12, `unusedDirective` 1, `NotAContainerDirective` 1 — 14 of 4,538 Docusaurus `:::` uses = 0.31%). Corpus B: 74 callouts, 5 types, all GitHub built-ins, 0 invented across 847 files. Pinned corpus corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…: 0 callouts, 0 `:::`, 0 Hugo shortcodes, 0 MyST directives, 0 `^block-id`, 0 `[//]: #`, 6 `{#id}` in 3 files. MyST proves a 46-term vocabulary is comfortably usable — and every one of those 46 is vendor-supplied. The demand curve is for a large BUILT-IN vocabulary that renders, not for a declaration mechanism. A registry for markdown vocabularies would distribute names; Typst's 1,481 packages distribute typesetting BEHAVIOUR, which markdown renderers already refuse to let you change. Nobody downloads names.

NEG-2 — WHERE DECLARATION WAS COMPELLED, IT PRODUCED DRIFT, NOT VOCABULARY, AND MDMAX'S OWN CORPUS SHOWS THE SAME FIELD BREAKING ITS OWN PARSER. Four real OKF bundles (1,266 files, fetched 2026-08-01) with `type` REQUIRED by spec: 5 / 0 / 5 / 21 distinct values, ≥8 of the 21 mutual collisions (`reference`/`Reference`, `function`/`Crossplane Function`/`functioninput`/`Crossplane Function Input`, `guide`/`developmentguide`/`Crossplane Development Guide`), 29 values across four incompatible naming conventions, 58 frontmatter keys in one 149-file bundle including leaked agent-config keys, and 0 of 4 declaring `okf_version: "0.2"` a week after v0.2 shipped. Worse, on the pinned corpus the frontmatter value slot is already failing structurally: 170 of 899 frontmatter blocks (18.91%) do not parse as YAML under js-yaml, and gray-matter (7.49M dl/wk) throws on them — because `entities: [[[Claude Code]], [[Anthropic]]]` puts markdown's own wikilink grammar inside YAML's flow-collection grammar. The quiet variant is worse than the loud one: `entities: [[[A]], [[B]]]` parses silently to `[[["A"]],[["B"]]]`, destroying the links with no error. A declaration mechanism does not produce a vocabulary; it produces an unvalidated free-text field with a grammar collision in it. That is a defect to DETECT, and detecting it is a shippable product; enabling more of it is not.

NEG-3 — THE MECHANISM ALREADY SHIPS AND NOBODY AUTHORS IT, SO SHIPPING OURS BUYS NO DIFFERENTIATION. `remark-lint-frontmatter-schema` (36,745 downloads/week) already offers document-declared `'$schema':` with the local-overrides-global precedence rule decided, and OKF v0.2 already normatively requires an open `type` field with MUST-tolerate-unknown semantics. Across 3,197 files in three independent corpora I found zero authored `$schema`/`@`/`x-`/`fm`-prefixed frontmatter keys. Building a fourth way to do a thing that two shipping systems already do and nobody uses is the markdown-it-decorate outcome by construction: perfect design, 1,094 downloads/week, unshipped since 2017.
unclaimed: A vocabulary-DRIFT detector over the values a corpus already uses — infer the enum from `type`/`status`/`category`, cluster case- and morphology-variants, and report `reference` vs `Reference` and `function` vs `Crossplane Function` as collisions. SEARCH RUN: registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search for 'markdown vocabulary', 'markdown schema frontmatter', 'markdown directive', 'remark custom syntax' — the only relevant hit is remark-lint-frontmatter-schema (36,745/wk), which validates against a schema YOU write and is silent when the schema is absent; api.github.com search 'open knowledge format' returns 287 repos of which the only conformance tool, Sudhakaran88/okf-conformance (16 stars), checks OKF structural conformance, not value drift. Nothing infers the vocabulary from the corpus.

A YAML-parseability gate over a whole vault that names the markdown-in-YAML collision class specifically. SEARCH RUN: same npm searches; remark-lint-frontmatter-schema structurally CANNOT report this — the YAML must parse before it can validate, so it is blind to the 18.91% of blocks that throw. I found no tool that reports 'your frontmatter contains a wikilink inside a flow sequence and 170 of your files are silently un-indexable'. Own-measured on corpus_id sha256:3a010b16….

A package-index with content digests for a document format. SEARCH RUN: fetched packages.typst.org/preview/index.json (2,060,620 B) this session — entry keys are exactly authors, compiler, description, entrypoint, exclude, keywords, license, name, repository, updatedAt, version; no hash field exists, matching typst/typst crates/typst-kit/src/packages.rs's own comment. CTAN's 7,021-package JSON carries key/name/caption only. If a registry is ever built, the sha256-in-the-index is a genuinely unoccupied slot — it is also two lines of code and worth nothing on its own.

A per-(product, surface) conformance certificate for a DECLARED construct, i.e. `mdmax cert --construct fm-vocab --targets github-blob,github-comment,obsidian,vscode`. SEARCH RUN: babelmark3 differs spec examples across parsers but has no notion of a user-declared construct, no offline mode, no version pinning and no product/surface split; no npm package in the four searches above emits a construct×consumer PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT matrix.
result.design:
RECOMMENDATION: SHIP NO DECLARED-VOCABULARY FEATURE IN V1. Ship its inverse.

=== WHAT SHIPS INSTEAD: `mdmax vocab` (read-only, zero new syntax) ===
  mdmax vocab <dir> [--field type,status,category] [--fail-on drift]
Emits the vocabulary a corpus is ALREADY using, plus three defect classes, each with a live positive in the corpora measured here:
  1. CASE/MORPHOLOGY DRIFT — `reference` vs `Reference`; `ACTIVE` vs `active`; `guide`/`developmentguide`/`Crossplane Development Guide`.
  2. PROSE IN AN ENUM SLOT — a `status` whose value is a 130-character sentence.
  3. UNPARSEABLE VALUE SLOT — the 18.91% of pinned-corpus frontmatter blocks that js-yaml and gray-matter both reject, root-caused to `[[wikilink]]` inside a YAML flow sequence, PLUS the silent variant where `[[[A]], [[B]]]` parses to a nested array and the links are destroyed without error.
Output is a table of (field, value, count, files, suspected-collision-with). It cannot flatter anybody — the §10.1 rule that picked `mdmax cert`. Effort: ~2 days. Zero new bytes in any user file, so it is compatible with D2, D4, D6, D7 by construction.

=== IF A DECLARATION IS EVER NEEDED, THIS IS IT (designed, not recommended) ===

WHERE IT LIVES — per-project, never per-file. A sidecar `.mdmax/vocab/<name>.yaml` at the repo/vault root, checked into VCS. Precedent chain, all primary: TC39 archived the in-band `"use module"` pragma at Stage 1 (api.github.com: archived=true, last push 2022-01-24) and Node chose package.json; Docusaurus puts admonition keywords in a build-config array with the source comment "Adding custom keywords is more common than disabling existing ones"; Quarto vendors `_extensions/` into the repo for the stated reason "Extensions used by a document or project are treated as source code to ensure very long term reproducibility"; every LLM convention (llms.txt, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules) is a glob-scoped sidecar.

THE ONE PER-FILE FORM PERMITTED, AND IT IS AN ASYMMETRY COPIED FROM VIM 9.2.0499 — a file MAY carry `mdmax-vocab: none` to switch the feature OFF for itself; a file MAY NOT carry a declaration that switches anything ON or adds a term. Verbatim rationale from vim's own docs: "`set nomodeline` is honored from within a modeline even when 'modelinestrict' is on … This lets a file disable further modeline processing for itself." A document may LOWER its own capability, never RAISE it. This is D9 replaced by something both stronger and enforceable.

HOW A DOCUMENT NAMES IT — reuse `'$schema':` in frontmatter. Do not invent `fm-vocab`. The key already ships in remark-lint-frontmatter-schema at 36,745 downloads/week with the precedence rule already decided ("Locally defined `'$schema'` takes precedence over global settings"), it parses correctly under gray-matter (verified this session), and adopting it makes MDMAX a consumer of an existing convention rather than the 47th dialect. The value is a project-relative PATH plus a full version triple and a digest: `'$schema': .mdmax/vocab/sgnk-v1.yaml@1.0.0#sha256-…`.

WHAT IT CAN NAME — DENOTATIONS ONLY. Each term is `{term, display-label, value-type, cardinality, docs-url}`. This is D9 corrected by the JSON-LD read: JSON-LD explicitly permits an embedded context, and an embedded context is safe precisely because it is a closed, non-recursive, non-dereferencing term→IRI map. The real rule is: A DOCUMENT (OR PROJECT) MAY CARRY A DENOTATION; IT MUST ONLY EVER NAME A PROCEDURE. Every failure in the record fits: XML internal DTD subset carries an entity that can dereference (`SYSTEM "file:///…"` → XXE) and recurse (billion laughs); vim modelines carried settable expressions (`modelineexpr`, default off since introduction); Hugo inline shortcodes carry a template — a procedure — and ship disabled under SECURITY. JSON-LD carries only denotations and has no equivalent CVE class.

WHAT IT CANNOT NAME — no executable, filter, plugin or WASM; no URL fetched at parse time, ever; no new NODE TYPE (D8 holds — an unknown fence language round-trips byte-identically, an unknown node type throws); no redefinition of an existing construct's meaning.

HARD CAP: 12 TERMS. Error, not warning, at 13. Basis is measured, not the IFScale paper alone: real declared vocabulary sizes are 5 / 0 / 5 / 21 across four OKF bundles, Docusaurus ships 9, GitHub ships 5, and the only bundle over 12 is ~38% self-colliding. Twelve is where a vocabulary stops being a vocabulary and starts being drift.

THE CARRIER, RANKED BY OWN-MEASURED ROUND-TRIP × RENDER × OCCUPANCY:
  ✅ fence META string (```` ```md fm:vocab=sgnk/v1 ````) — round-trips IDENTICAL, payload absent from marked's HTML, and the value slot is a free string with NO grammar of its own. This is the correct block-scoped carrier and it is the one D8 actually implies. Caveat measured here: occupancy is 0.00% pinned / 0.02% Corpus B / 48.01% Docusaurus — you must namespace (`fm:`) because `title="…"` already owns the channel in Docusaurus-shaped corpora.
  ✅ link reference definition — round-trips IDENTICAL, renders to nothing, but 23.38% occupied in third-party docs (5,079 in 198 of 847 files) and a bogus definition becomes a live link target. Use only with a `fm:` prefix and never for anything a user might reference.
  ⚠️ frontmatter — required anyway by OKF, present in 84.73% of the pinned corpus, but VISIBLE in 23/24 renderers AND its value slot is YAML, which 18.91% of the pinned corpus's own blocks already fail. Acceptable for a document-level NAME (one scalar string), unacceptable for anything a human will type freely.
  ❌ `> [!TYPE]` callout — DISQUALIFIED. remark-stringify with full GFM escapes GitHub's own `> [!NOTE]` to `> \[!NOTE]`, the exact DesktopCommanderMCP #440 corruption class. No vocabulary may live here.
  ❌ `[//]: #` idiom — DISQUALIFIED. Does not survive a write: parens become quotes.

ABSENCE SEMANTICS — FIX BOTH HALVES OF THE LaTeX ASYMMETRY. LaTeX makes a missing package fatal (`\@missingfileerror` → interactive prompt, batchmode aborts) and a wrong version a mere warning (`\@latex@warning@no@line`). The fix is SYMMETRY, and the symmetric level is WARN-AND-DEGRADE, not fatal — because D6 says degradation is the feature. Missing vocabulary, wrong version, and digest mismatch all produce: the construct falls back to its base markdown form, the document still renders, one diagnostic per distinct cause, and a non-zero exit only under `--fail-on`. A digest mismatch additionally REFUSES to use the cached copy. Resolution is filesystem-only: never fetch, so the vendor being down cannot break a build (Typst's "Importing a cached package does not result in network access", achieved by having no network at all).

WHAT AN UNAWARE RENDERER SHOWS — for the fence-meta carrier: an ordinary fenced code block with its language highlighted and the meta string dropped (verified against marked). For the `$schema` frontmatter key: whatever that renderer already does with frontmatter, which is a pre-existing, already-paid cost.

=== THE REGISTRY ===
THERE IS NO REGISTRY, AND THIS IS THE SETTLED ANSWER, NOT A DEFERRAL. Copy Typst's five invariants if one is ever built — namespace with a user-owned `@local` escape hatch that takes precedence over any cache, mandatory full version triples with no ranges and no solver, post-publish immutability as stated policy, on-demand download with a permanent offline cache, submission = a pull request to a git repo with a CI job and a CDN — and fix Typst's one omission by putting a sha256 in the index (verified absent: index.json entries carry no hash field) and LaTeX's one asymmetry by making missing and wrong-version the same severity. But do not build it, because a markdown vocabulary package distributes NAMES, and the demand measured here for names is 0.31%.

=== Q3: DOES MDMAX BECOME A PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE, OR ADMIT IT IS A THIN SHELL OVER ONE? ===
NEITHER — AND THE QUESTION IS A TRAP THAT COSTS THE PRODUCT. The dichotomy is real for anyone who wants a package ecosystem: LaTeX and Typst are the only two document formats that ever got one, both are Turing-complete languages whose surface syntax happens to be documents, and every markdown-adjacent system that split the halves (Quarto, Sphinx, MkDocs, Pandoc, R Markdown) refused document-declared registry resolution. MDMAX should refuse the ecosystem, and therefore never face the choice. It stays a COMPILER, in the strict sense: a total function from bytes to bytes with a proof obligation on the untouched region. The moment it evaluates anything a document names, it acquires MDX's fate (verified: MDX cannot write its own documents back out) and Obsidian's threat model (6,222 plugins, Restricted Mode on by default, vendor's own words: "Obsidian cannot reliably restrict plugins to specific permissions or access levels"). And the threat model is strictly worse than npm's for one decisive reason: a package.json is written by the repo owner, whereas a .md is routinely a drive-by PR, a CMS field, a logged-in reviewer's paste (D3), or LLM output — Hugo's exact stated boundary, "template and configuration authors are trusted, but content authors are not."

=== Q4: WHAT OKF v0.2 MEANS FOR A COMPETING VOCABULARY MECHANISM ===
It means there is no competition to enter, and §13.5's "target, not host" recommendation is CONFIRMED by the spec text. OKF has already implemented D8 (§4.1: type values not registered centrally; §11: consumers MUST NOT reject unknown types or unknown keys) and D9 (§10: `runtime`, `executor.resource`, `attester.resource` are all names; "it does not execute anything itself"), and §12 explicitly DEFERS the runtime protocol, the attester ABI, portability and sandboxing rather than acquiring them. Practical consequences: (a) interop is nearly free — the pinned corpus is already 59.19% OKF-v0.2-conformant with nobody having read the spec, and the whole gap to ~100% is the broken-YAML files plus a missing `type` key; (b) OKF's conformance bar carries almost no information, since its only two requirements are "parseable frontmatter" and "non-empty type", so `mdmax cert --target okf-0.2` is a two-predicate column, cheap and honest; (c) MDMAX's differentiated contribution against OKF is precisely `mdmax vocab` — OKF creates the open `type` field and explicitly declines to police it, which is the exact hole the drift detector fills, on a spec Google is pushing and 287 GitHub repos already use.

=== ONE SECURITY NOTE FROM THIS SESSION, NOT A FINDING ===
While reading the openknowledge-sh/openknowledge README to locate the canonical spec URL, the fetched content contained `curl -fsSL https://openknowledge.sh/install | bash` and an agent-directed prompt block instructing an agent to install and run that script. I did not execute it and did not act on it. Flagging it because the OKF ecosystem's own onboarding path is "paste this prompt into your agent", which is exactly the untrusted-content-directs-an-agent shape this program has already ruled against.
result.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES §13.6: DOES A SMALLER PRODUCTION MODEL HOLD A DECLARED NOTATION? Every prior result is frontier-class, 5 constructs, declaration in immediate context. The editor's inline-AI path will run the cheap model, so the cheap model is the one that decides.

CORPUS AND ITEMS. Items are real paragraphs drawn from the pinned corpus `corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4` (1,084 files, all re-verified present and hash-matching this session), stratified by token count because §9.6's under-3-token problem is a confound. The notation's terms are drawn from vocabularies real teams actually invented: the 29 `type` values measured across four OKF bundles plus the 10 valid-YAML `type` values in the pinned corpus. No synthetic vocabulary — a synthetic one measures the experimenter.

FACTORS.
  F1 MODEL TIER, 4 levels: frontier / mid / small hosted / ~1–3B local. Named at run time; the ladder is the variable, not the vendor.
  F2 VOCABULARY SIZE, 4 levels: 3, 6, 12, 24 terms. 12 is the proposed cap and 24 is the measured drift zone.
  F3 DECLARATION FORM, 3 levels: rule-only, example-only (3 worked examples, no rule), rule+examples. This is a direct replication of the MTOB ablation on our own task.
  F4 DECLARATION DISTANCE, 3 levels: adjacent to the task / document head with ~8k tokens between / sidecar loaded ~40k tokens earlier. Primacy bias is known; distance is the untested half.
  F5 TASK, 3 levels: RECOGNISE (does this span use term T?), EMIT (write a paragraph using T correctly), PRESERVE (edit an unrelated sentence and leave every vocabulary-bearing span byte-identical). PRESERVE is the one that matters for a splice-only compiler and the one nobody measures.

DESIGN AND n. Full crossing is 432 cells; screen instead. Main sweep: F3 fixed at rule+examples, F4 fixed at head — 4 tiers × 4 sizes × 3 tasks × n=40 = 1,920 calls. Focused ablation at the worst-performing tier: F3 × F4 × F2∈{6,24} = 2×3×2 = 12 cells × n=40 = 480. Total 2,400 calls, ~2.5k tokens each ≈ 6.0M tokens — 76% of ONE of the two research workflows already run (7.86M). The measurement that decides this question costs less than the research that failed to decide it.

VERIFIER — DETERMINISTIC, NO JUDGE (LR#25: cheapest applicable verifier wins). RECOGNISE = exact set match against a hand-built key. EMIT = the emitted construct parses to the declared shape under the pinned parser AND round-trips byte-identically through remark. PRESERVE = byte diff over the untouched region, computed by an INDEPENDENT oracle, not by re-running the writer's own span logic — the same rule as the S4 gate. Zero LLM judges anywhere.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST CALL, PUBLISHED EITHER WAY.
  P1 PRESERVE degrades with tier faster than RECOGNISE: at the smallest tier, PRESERVE < 80% while RECOGNISE > 95%.
  P2 The cap lives in the size×tier interaction: every tier ≥95% on RECOGNISE at 3 and 6 terms; the small tier drops below 90% at 12 and below 75% at 24.
  P3 Examples beat rules at every tier and the gap WIDENS as tier falls (MTOB replication).
  P4 Distance costs less than size: adjacent → 40k-earlier costs <5pp, while 6 → 24 terms costs >15pp at the small tier.
  P5 (feature-level falsifier) If the small tier is ≥95% on all three tasks at 12 terms, the single-digit cap is wrong and the feature is materially cheaper than this area concluded.

TWO CHEAPER MEASUREMENTS THAT SHOULD RUN FIRST, BOTH ZERO MODEL CALLS AND BOTH ~HALF A DAY.
  M-A VOCABULARY DRIFT CENSUS at scale: run the `mdmax vocab` logic over the 287 GitHub repos matching "open knowledge format" (api.github.com search, counted this session) and report the distribution of per-bundle `type`-vocabulary size and intra-bundle collision rate. My n=4 gives 5/0/5/21; if the true distribution is fat-tailed above 12, the cap is wrong and drift detection is worth more, not less. This single measurement can refute or confirm both of my negatives.
  M-B CARRIER OCCUPANCY across ≥8 corpora with a stated selection hash per corpus, because I measured fence-meta occupancy at 0.00% / 0.02% / 48.01% on three corpora and refdef occupancy at 0.83% / 23.38% on two. No carrier decision should be made on fewer than five corpora, and the existing 24-renderer matrix measured VISIBILITY while never measuring OCCUPANCY at all.

result.headline: Rendering more is not blocked by markdown or by renderers — the read-only side already works (12/12 unknown fence languages survive byte-intact through frontmatter's own pipeline) — it is blocked by write-back: the one WIRED rendered-editing surface, the properties panel, re-emits YAML through a serializer and changes bytes in 623 of 737 frontmatter-bearing files (84.5%, of which 197 change the document's LINE COUNT) with zero edits made [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…], so the rule is render anything declarative the host can bound, and write back nothing but a splice.

The override is per-diagram — a sibling diagram with no directive reads the host's value back — and `dompurifyConfig` stayed undefined. So the correct, narrower claim is: a document can reconfigure the renderer FOR ITS OWN BLOCK, bounded, not globally, and mermaid's security-critical keys hold.
findings.evidence: `start fontSize = 16` → `after DOC-A (99) = 99` → `after DOC-B (none) = 16`. And `HOST dompurifyConfig = undefined` → `AFTER dompurifyConfig = undefined`. Both at mermaid 11.15.0 under securityLevel:'strict'.

findings.claim: A purely declarative spec can still be a denial-of-service, which is why (3) 'work bound' belongs in the line. Mermaid's Gantt `excludes` attribute — pure declaration, no expressions — caused an infinite-loop DoS on render (not on parse) through 11.14.0. Mermaid carries 11 published GitHub advisories, four of them dated 2026-05-11, one of which is CSS injection through the document's own `%%{init}%%` fontFamily/themeCSS.
findings.evidence: GHSA-6m6c-36f7-fhxh, medium, 2026-05-11, verbatim: "Mermaid v11.14.0 and earlier are vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack when rendering gantt charts, if they use the `excludes` attribute to exclude all dates… `mermaid.parse` is unaffected, unless you then call the `ganttDb.getTasks()` (which is called when rendering a diagram)." GHSA-87f9-hvmw-gh4p, 2026-05-11: "Mermaid's default configuration allows injecting CSS that applies outside of the Mermaid diagram via the `fontFamily`, `themeCSS`, and `altFontFamily` configuration options." Advisory count via api.github.com/advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=mermaid: n=11.

findings.claim: Every declarative renderer that survived contact with the web had to add an explicit resource bound — this is the invariant, not an accident. KaTeX bounds macro expansion (`maxExpand`), mermaid locks `maxTextSize` and `maxEdges` into its 6-key secure list. My attempted TeX expansion bomb produced only 34× amplification in 1 ms.
findings.evidence: node_modules/katex/dist/katex.mjs:14650-14651 verbatim: `if (this.expansionCount > this.settings.maxExpand) { throw new ParseError("Too many expansions: infinite loop or " + "need to increase maxExpand setting");`. Measured: `expansion bomb in=96 out=3285 amp=34x ms=1`.

findings.claim: KaTeX is safe ONLY because of a default that must be asserted, never assumed. With the default `trust:false`, `\href{javascript:…}` and `\includegraphics{https://…}` produce NO anchor and NO image. Flip `trust:true` — the single line a well-meaning integrator adds to 'support links in math' — and the same source produces a live `javascript:` anchor and an `` that fetches an arbitrary remote URL from inside a math block.
findings.evidence: katex 0.17.0, jsdom-parsed output. Default: `href js -> {"anchors":[],"imgs":[],"errNodes":0}`. trust:true: `href js -> {"anchors":["javascript:alert(1)"]…}` and `incgraphics -> {"imgs":["https://tracker.example/beacon.png"]…}`.

findings.claim: frontmatter's sanitizer is not the last stage of its own pipeline. In src/modules/preview/presentation/Markdown.tsx the rehype plugin order is rehypeRaw → createRehypeHtmlPolicy → rehypeKatex → rehypeHighlight → rehypeSlug, so anything KaTeX or the highlighter injects is never seen by the policy. The observable consequence: an author-written `<math>` element is escaped to visible source text, while KaTeX's generated `<math xmlns=…>` renders — the same element, two verdicts, decided purely by plugin order.
findings.evidence:
Markdown.tsx:53-62 `() => [ rehypeRaw, createRehypeHtmlPolicy(content), rehypeKatex, rehypeHighlight, rehypeSlug ]`. Probe: `MathML | RENDER |

<math><mi>x…` (escaped) vs `math fence $$ | RENDER |

…` (live).

findings.claim: frontmatter's HTML policy has two different refusal behaviours and nobody documented the split. 13 elements are silently DELETED (iframe, form, style, script, button, select, textarea, embed, object, base, link, meta); everything outside the 62-element allowlist is turned into VISIBLE literal source text. So `<video>`, `<audio>`, `<canvas>`, `<picture>`, `<progress>`, `<meter>` and — most awkwardly — inline `<svg>` all appear to the reader as raw markup. The house icon standard (Learned Rule #52) mandates inline SVG; frontmatter's own renderer cannot render it.
findings.evidence:
src/modules/preview/presentation/markdown/html-policy.ts:1-14 (DISALLOWED_RAW_HTML_ELEMENTS, 13 entries), :16-78 (SAFE_HTML_ELEMENTS, 62 entries), :183-186 (`children.splice(i, 1, { type: "text", value: literal })`). Probe output: `inline SVG (icon) |

<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M1 1h2"/></svg>

`; `iframe embed | STRIP |` (empty).

findings.claim: The `style` ATTRIBUTE is not filtered at all, only the `style` ELEMENT. A `<div style="position:fixed;inset:0;background:url(https://tracker.example/p.gif)">` passes through intact. That is a rendering-integrity hole, not a script hole: a shared document can beacon on open (read receipt), and can cover the rendered page with a full-viewport layer — the document renders one thing and looks like another, using only allowed markup.
findings.evidence:
`sanitizeProperties` (html-policy.ts:145-164) deletes keys beginning `on` and unsafe URL schemes in URL_ATTRS; `style` is in neither set. Probe: `style ATTRIBUTE | RENDER |
x
`.

findings.claim: On write-back, the two shipped surfaces split cleanly on the splice line and that split IS the design rule. `toggleTaskAtLine` replaces one line in place and is a genuine splice. `setTableCell` re-serializes the whole table: editing one cell rewrote 3 of 5 lines of an aligned table, corrupted a cell containing an escaped `\|` into two cells destroying content, and added pipes to a pipe-less table. Over the corpus a NO-OP cell write (writing the same value back) dirties 45 of 335 table-bearing files (13.4%), touching 199 lines. 7 corpus tables contain `\|`; 92 of 1,240 detected 'tables' (7.4%, 36 files) are inside fenced code blocks, because the detector is fence-blind.

corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…; `{files:1084, filesWithTables:338, tables:1240, escPipeTables:7, padTables:89, noLeadPipe:25, editsRun:335, filesDirty:45, totalLinesTouched:199}` and `tables detected: 1240 of which START INSIDE a fenced code block: 92 = 7.4%`. Corruption case, verbatim: IN `"| Cmd | Meaning |

"` OUT `"| Cmd | Meaning |

"`. Splice side: src/modules/editor/presentation/toolbar-transforms.ts:112-124.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE against that last finding, from my own pre-registered falsifier: `EditableTable` is dead code. It is imported by nothing, and `components.tsx:36` declares its callback as unused `_onEdit`. So the 13.4% is a latent trap, not a live defect — which makes it a specification for what NOT to ship rather than a bug report.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "EditableTable" src/ | grep -v editable-table.tsx` → empty. src/modules/preview/presentation/markdown/components.tsx:36 `_onEdit: ((newContent: string) => void) | undefined,` (only occurrence in the file).

findings.claim: frontmatter already disagrees with ITSELF across its two surfaces, which is the strongest possible case for modelling targets as (product, surface) pairs. The in-app preview runs the lockfile-pinned mermaid 11.15.0; the PDF export loads `mermaid@11` from a third-party CDN, which resolves today to 11.16.0. Same document, same product, two renderer versions, no receipt.
findings.evidence: src/modules/export/presentation/pdf-doc.ts:24 `const MERMAID_VERSION = "11";` and :134 `import mermaid from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@${MERMAID_VERSION}/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs";`. `node -e require('mermaid/package.json').version` → `11.15.0`. registry.npmjs.org/mermaid → `dist-tags {'latest': '11.16.0'}`, latest non-prerelease 11.x = 11.16.0. Note GHSA-m4gq-x24j-jpmf names this exact delivery path verbatim: "This affects the built: … dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs … This will also affect users that use the above files via a CDN link".

findings.claim: THE ARTIFACT CONTRACT, answered from shipping code. The PDF route is already a pure one-way source→artifact projection that stores nothing — which confirms the prior finding. What the prior finding MISSED is that the projection is non-deterministic: the route sleeps a fixed 2,000 ms for a CDN script to render, then snapshots whatever exists. There is no failure if a diagram did not render, no version receipt, and no float pin. A projection with no determinism guarantee cannot be a durable artifact, and 'we never store it' does not fix that — it makes it worse, because you cannot even diff two runs.
findings.evidence: src/app/api/export/pdf/[...path]/route.ts:150-157 verbatim: `// Give the mermaid CDN module time to download and render diagrams.` / `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));` / `const pdfBytes = await page.pdf({ format: "A4", printBackground: true, … });`. Nothing is written; the bytes are returned in the Response.

findings.claim: Quarto has already solved the artifact question and its answer costs a browser. Diagram format is chosen by TARGET: JS for HTML, a `mermaid` code block for GFM, a rasterized PNG (via headless Chrome) for pdf/docx/epub. It also uses BRACED info strings — `{mermaid}`, `{dot}` — so the identical diagram needs `mermaid` for GitHub and `{mermaid}` for Quarto. One language, two incompatible carriers, decided by consumer. That is a certificate column nobody has.
findings.evidence: quarto-dev/quarto-web docs/authoring/diagrams.qmd verbatim: "Quarto has native support for embedding Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams"; "Mermaid diagrams are embedded using `{mermaid}` executable cells. Graphviz diagrams are embedded using `{dot}` executable cells"; format table `HTML → Mermaid native (JavaScript) | GitHub Flavored Markdown (gfm) → Mermaid code block | Other Formats (pdf, docx, etc.) → PNG image`; "a PNG image is created using Chrome".

findings.claim: Demand for exotic rendering is absent in both corpora, and this is the strongest argument AGAINST my own area. In the pinned corpus: 7,714 opening fences, 25 distinct info-string first tokens, of which 10 are mermaid (0.13%) and ZERO are d2, graphviz, plantuml, vega-lite, wavedrom, tikz, music or chemistry. In a second, independently-selected corpus (474 files, 5,013,124 bytes under ~/.claude/skills-src): 2,995 fences, 30 tokens, ZERO diagram fences of any kind. Combined: 10 diagram fences in 10,709.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… → `total_opening_fences 7714 distinct_info_first_token 25`; top tokens `5700 bash / 1361 (none) / 200 markdown / 173 json / … / 10 mermaid`. SECOND CORPUS, explicitly stated selection (all *.md under ~/.claude/skills-src, skipping dot-dirs, node_modules, dist, build, __pycache__; 474 files, 5,013,124 bytes, selection_sha256 d6321d4af60256c0308d52490ab33744): `opening fences 2995 distinct info tokens 30` and `diagram-ish fences: 0 = 0.0 %`.

findings.claim: Adoption of the diagram zoo is two orders of magnitude below the parsers, so 'render everything' buys reach nobody is asking for. Weekly npm downloads: marked 61,032,058 · remark-parse 45,820,243 · katex 19,924,866 · mermaid 11,828,208 · vega-lite 753,796 · plantuml-encoder 177,298 · viz.js 81,029 · abcjs 58,394 · @terrastruct/d2 39,961 · vexflow 39,704 · wavedrom 25,307. Below mermaid there is nothing with a real user base.
