findings.claim: Integrators enable raw HTML more often than they sanitize it, by 1.70:1 — which is why an ALLOWLIST policy owned by the host is the differentiator, not another renderer. And frontmatter is already stricter than GitHub is at the markdown layer: GitHub's cmark-gfm ships a nine-tag BLOCKLIST; frontmatter ships a 62-element allowlist plus a 13-element hard deny.
findings.evidence: rehype-raw 14,287,197/wk vs rehype-sanitize 8,423,529/wk (api.npmjs.org, same window). github/cmark-gfm extensions/tagfilter.c:5-8 verbatim: `static const char *blacklist[] = { "title", "textarea", "style", "xmp", "iframe", "noembed", "noframes", "script", "plaintext", NULL, };`

findings.claim: Two candidate renderers break rule (2) — the document supplies the renderer's INPUTS — by their own type systems, and both already have the CVEs to prove it. Vega-Lite's `UrlData` makes every chart spec a fetcher. PlantUML's include directives produced a high-severity SSRF.
findings.evidence: vega/vega-lite src/data.ts:100-105 verbatim: `export interface UrlData extends DataBase { … url: string; }` and :125 `export function isUrlData(data): data is UrlData { return hasProperty(data, 'url'); }`. GHSA-ff3m-68vj-h86p, HIGH, 2023-06-27: "Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in GitHub repository plantuml/plantuml prior to 1.2023.9"; plus GHSA-hrvf-g648-rf3m, 2026-01-16, stored XSS. Advisory counts: vega n=8 (1 high), vega-lite n=0, wavedrom n=0, viz.js n=0, @mdx-js/mdx n=0, dompurify n=27, marked n=18.

findings.claim: DUAL RENDERING, tested on the one machine channel markdown already has. Of 21 markdown images in the pinned corpus, ZERO carry an alt text of three or more words: 4 empty, 6 equal to the filename, 11 under three words. All 11 raw `` tags carry no `alt` attribute at all. That is 32 of 32 degenerate — the 'absent, a filename, or a lie' law, at 100%, on a real vault. n is small and I say so; but the direction is unambiguous and it is the only channel we can audit retrospectively.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…: `markdown images: 21 / alt EMPTY: 4 (19.0%) / alt == filename: 6 (28.6%) / alt < 3 words: 11 (52.4%) / alt >= 3 words: 0 (0.0%)` and `raw tags: 11, no alt attr: 11, empty alt: 0`.

findings.claim: VS Code has already shipped the user-facing control this area needs and nobody copied it: a per-workspace render security level, exposed as a command. That is the precedent for 'the host owns render policy and the user can see it', and it is stronger than any diagram feature.
findings.evidence: microsoft/vscode extensions/markdown-language-features/package.json contributes `markdown.showPreviewSecuritySelector`, alongside `markdown.previewScripts` / `markdown.previewStyles`. The same package.json contributes no diagram support of any kind — VS Code's built-in preview renders zero diagram languages natively.

findings.claim: Even the ecosystem leaders treat diagrams as opt-in, not table stakes. Docusaurus requires installing `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid` and setting `markdown.mermaid: true`; it is off by default. Obsidian ships mermaid, math and callouts natively and nothing else. Zed's markdown crate handles a closed pulldown-cmark tag set with no diagram tag.
findings.evidence: facebook/docusaurus website/docs/guides/markdown-features/markdown-features-diagrams.mdx: "Enable Mermaid functionality by adding plugin `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid` and setting `markdown.mermaid` to `true`". obsidianmd/obsidian-help Advanced formatting syntax.md §Diagram (mermaid only) and §Math; Basic formatting syntax.md §Comments (`%%`). zed-industries/zed crates/markdown/src/markdown.rs — Tag:: variants observed: Heading, Paragraph, List, Item, Table, TableHead, TableRow, TableCell, CodeBlock, BlockQuote, Link, Image, Emphasis, Strong, Strikethrough, HtmlBlock, MetadataBlock, FootnoteDefinition. No diagram tag.

negatives: NEGATIVE 1 — the demand is not there, measured twice. Across two corpora totalling 1,558 files and 30.6 MB, there are 10 diagram fences in 10,709 (0.093%): 10 mermaid in the pinned corpus [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, 7,714 fences, 25 distinct info tokens] and ZERO of any kind in the second corpus [474 files / 5,013,124 B under ~/.claude/skills-src, 2,995 fences, 30 tokens]. Not one d2, graphviz, plantuml, vega-lite, wavedrom, tikz, abc or SMILES fence exists in either. The settled record already says fence dispatch reaches 0.89%; my two corpora say 0.093%, an order of magnitude lower. A renderer zoo optimizes for a use that does not occur in the founders' own writing, and the settled law says the consumer supplies adoption, not the design — markdown-it-decorate was perfect and got 1,094 downloads/week (I re-measured: 1,094 exactly).

NEGATIVE 2 — every renderer added is a permanent advisory stream, and the cost lands on us. mermaid alone carries 11 published GitHub advisories, SIX of them in the last twelve months (four dated 2026-05-11, two 2025-08-19), including a pure-declarative Gantt infinite-loop DoS and a CSS injection through the document's own `%%{init}%%`. dompurify carries 27, marked 18, vega 8. Rendering surface is attack surface with no ceiling, and unlike a parser bug a renderer bug fires on VIEW — the cheapest and most common operation in a collaboration product. Against that, the read-only benefit is already free: 12/12 unknown fence languages survive byte-intact today with zero renderers installed.

NEGATIVE 3 — my own headline's sibling claim was refuted by my own pre-registered test. I predicted a `%%{init}` directive would persist across diagrams and that `dompurifyConfig` was document-settable. Measured at mermaid 11.15.0: the override resets for the next diagram (16 → 99 → 16) and `dompurifyConfig` stayed undefined. Mermaid's security-critical keys hold. So 'mermaid is a runtime' is too strong; the honest claim is the narrower one in the design below.

NEGATIVE 4 — the second-best measurement in this report is on dead code. The table writer's 13.4% no-op blast radius and its `\|` corruption are real, but `EditableTable` is imported by nothing and `components.tsx:36` marks its callback unused. Anyone quoting 13.4% as a live defect is wrong; it is a specification for what not to build.

NEGATIVE 5 — my hypothesis that the PDF exporter's regex (`/```mermaid\s*\n([\s\S]*?)```/g`, pdf-doc.ts:38) would falsely render mermaid fences nested inside outer code fences has ZERO blast radius in the pinned corpus: 0 of 10 matches sit inside a 4-backtick fence. The bug class is real; the exposure I claimed is not.
unclaimed: An INTRA-product render certificate — the same document rendered by the same vendor's two surfaces, compared. frontmatter's preview (mermaid 11.15.0, lockfile-pinned) and its PDF export (`mermaid@11` from cdn.jsdelivr.net, resolving to 11.16.0 today) are already a two-surface disagreement inside one product with no receipt. Search that produced the belief: registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search for 'markdown conformance matrix' and 'markdown render certificate' — the search endpoint's `total` is the whole registry, not a match count, and the top-6 relevance results for both queries are unrelated (whatwg-url, ml-matrix, @peculiar/x509, mkcert). Nothing in the ecosystem models (product, surface) pairs, and certainly not (own-product, own-surface).

A host-owned FENCE-DISPATCH CAPABILITY POLICY: a table keyed by fence language declaring, per language, {config-source: host|document, input-source: inline-only|host-fetched|document-fetched, work-bound: host-enforced cap}, enforced before the body reaches any renderer. The closest existing artifacts are rehype-sanitize (an element allowlist with no notion of fence dispatch, 8,423,529/wk) and mermaid's own six-key `secure` list (per-renderer, invisible to the host, and not composable across renderers). Search: registry.npmjs.org search for 'fence dispatch policy markdown' and 'markdown renderer capability policy' returned markdown-it-fence (a markdown-it fence customiser), helmet and content-security-policy-parser — nothing that mediates between a fence language and a renderer's authority.

A DETERMINISTIC ARTIFACT RECEIPT for a rendered projection: {source sha256, renderer name + exact version, resolved config sha256, output sha256, and an explicit did-every-block-render assertion}. Quarto, the most mature markdown-to-artifact toolchain in existence, chooses PNG-via-Chrome for print targets and pins nothing about which Chrome; frontmatter's own route sleeps 2,000 ms and snapshots. Search: registry.npmjs.org for 'diagram render receipt deterministic' → diagram-js, @mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml, react-transition-state. Nothing.

A one-keystroke 'strip the directives and show me the fence as data' affordance. Every diagram language that gained traction (mermaid `%%{init}`, Quarto `%%|` / `//|`) accreted an in-body configuration channel that the reader cannot see. No renderer surveyed (GitHub, Obsidian, Quarto, Docusaurus, VitePress, VS Code, Zed) shows the reader that a diagram carried configuration. This is the render-side twin of §6's 'show me what the model sees' and it has the same absent-competitor position.
result.design:
WHAT SHIPS — a render policy, not a renderer zoo. Six concrete pieces, in dependency order. (1) THE LINE, stated so it can be tested. A renderer stays a renderer iff the HOST — never the document — supplies all three of: its CONFIGURATION, its INPUTS, and an upper BOUND on its work. Break one and it is a runtime. ON THE RENDERER SIDE (ship): graphviz via viz.js WASM (no include directive, no network, 0 advisories — needs only a host node cap); wavedrom (JSON data only, 0 advisories); mermaid WITH `%%{init}%%` stripped from the body before dispatch and `maxEdges`/`maxTextSize` set by the host. ON THE RUNTIME SIDE (refuse): MDX (it is a program and provably cannot write itself back); PlantUML (`!includeurl` → GHSA-ff3m-68vj-h86p, high SSRF, plus a JVM); Vega/Vega-Lite as authored (`UrlData.url` makes every chart a fetcher — allowable only with `data.url` rejected at policy time, i.e. inline data only). Borderline, and the reason the third clause exists: KaTeX is on the renderer side ONLY because `trust:false` is the default. Assert it in a test; `trust:true` yields live `javascript:` anchors and remote `` fetches from a math block. (2) FIX THE WRITE-BACK BEFORE ADDING ANY RENDERER. Replace `stringifyFrontmatterDoc` (frontmatter.ts:46) with a splice: the `yaml` package exposes `node.range` on every AST node — compute the edited scalar's byte range and replace only that range in the original source. Never call `doc.toString()`. Gate: the no-op round trip must dirty 0 of 737 files, down from 623. (3) REORDER THE PIPELINE so the policy is last. `Markdown.tsx:53-62` currently runs rehypeRaw → policy → rehypeKatex → rehypeHighlight; move the policy to the end so nothing injects HTML behind it, and add `style` to the attribute filter in `sanitizeProperties` (allowlist a small set of layout-inert properties, or drop the attribute entirely). (4) WRITE-BACK ALLOWLIST, closed by construction. Only two things may write to the file from the rendered view: the task checkbox (already a true line splice) and a frontmatter property (after (2)). Everything else in the rendered view is view-state only: `
` open/closed, tabs, sortable table order, collapsed sections — all held in the client, none persisted to the `.md`. `EditableTable`/`setTableCell` is deleted, not fixed, until it goes through the splice writer: it corrupts `\|` cells and 7.4% of what it detects as tables are inside code fences. (5) `mdmax cert --render`. Per document, per fence language, per (product, surface): PASS · STRIP · CORRUPT. Ship with SIX GitHub-adjacent surfaces, not three, because I measured a fifth that disagrees: github-blob, github-comment, github-pages, **github-api** (`POST /markdown` — renders mermaid as highlighted source and DELETES inline `

`), plus **frontmatter-preview** and **frontmatter-pdf**, which disagree with each other today (11.15.0 vs 11.16.0). The first row this tool prints is our own product failing its own consistency check — which is exactly the artifact-that-cannot-flatter-us rule from §10.1. (6) PIN THE PROJECTION AND GIVE IT A RECEIPT. Bundle mermaid locally in the PDF path instead of `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/…`; replace the fixed `setTimeout(2000)` with an explicit per-diagram render-complete assertion that FAILS the export if any block did not render; emit {source sha256, renderer name+version, resolved config sha256, output sha256}. The projection is still never stored — that part of the prior finding is correct and the shipped route already honours it. What the prior finding missed is that an unpinned, timing-dependent projection is not reproducible, and "we don't store it" makes that worse rather than better, because you cannot diff two runs to notice. CLI SURFACE: `mdmax cert --render --targets github-blob,github-api,frontmatter-preview,frontmatter-pdf,quarto-html,quarto-pdf --fail-on CORRUPT`, and `mdmax render-policy` printing the {config, inputs, bound} table for every language the host will dispatch. DEGRADATION BEHAVIOUR: unchanged and already correct — an unknown fence language renders as a `
` with the payload byte-intact, measured 12/12. That is the whole reason this design costs nothing to be wrong about: refusing a language degrades to readable source, never to junk.
result.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT — a render-conformance sweep, because the open question is not "can we render X" (we can) but "do the surfaces disagree enough that a certificate is worth building", which is kill gate K5. CORPUS: (a) the 10 mermaid fences in corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… — the only real diagram fences either corpus contains; (b) a synthesized fixture of 12 fence languages × 3 payload variants (minimal / typical / adversarial-but-legal, e.g. the Gantt `excludes` shape and a 600-edge flowchart against mermaid's 500-edge `maxEdges` default) = 36 documents; (c) 30 documents drawn at random from the 737 frontmatter-bearing corpus files, for the write-back arm. TASKS AND VERIFIERS, all rules-based, no judge: ARM 1 — surface conformance. Render each of the 36 fixtures through 7 surfaces: frontmatter-preview (headless, jsdom), frontmatter-pdf (the real route), github-api (`POST /markdown`, already proven to respond), github-blob (fixture repo + rendered-HTML fetch), Obsidian (local vault, DOM snapshot), VS Code preview (extension host), Quarto (`quarto render` to html and to pdf). Verdict per cell from a DOM parser — never a substring grep, per the discipline already encoded in test/preview/html-policy-xss.test.ts. n = 36 × 7 = 252 cells. ARM 2 — write-back fidelity. For all 737 frontmatter-bearing corpus files, run the CURRENT `stringifyFrontmatterDoc` and the PROPOSED range-splice, and report dirty-file count and line-count-changed count for each. n = 737 × 2. ARM 3 — determinism. Render the same 10 real mermaid documents to PDF ten times each, 24 hours apart, current code vs pinned-and-receipted code. Compare output sha256. n = 10 × 10 × 2. ARM 4 — the policy line. For each of the 12 languages, attempt, in a sandbox with an egress monitor, (i) a document-supplied config override, (ii) a document-named remote input, (iii) a bounded-work violation. Record which of the three the renderer permits. n = 36 probes. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (write these down before running; I will be wrong about some): P1 — at least 3 of the 12 languages produce ≥4 distinct verdicts across the 7 surfaces. Confidence: high, because I have already measured mermaid at 3 distinct verdicts across three surfaces (github-api = highlighted source, github-blob = diagram, quarto-pdf = PNG). P2 — inline `

` — measured; frontmatter escapes it to visible source — measured; Obsidian renders it — predicted). P3 — ARM 2: current writer dirties 623/737 (84.5%) and changes line count on 197; the range-splice dirties 0. The 623 is already measured, so this arm is a regression gate, not a discovery. P4 — ARM 3: current code produces ≥2 distinct output digests for at least one document within the 24-hour window (mermaid 11.15.0 → 11.16.0 on the CDN during the study is the mechanism). Pinned code produces exactly 1 digest per document. P5 — ARM 4: mermaid permits (i) and refuses (ii) and (iii); PlantUML permits (ii); Vega-Lite permits (ii); graphviz/viz.js and wavedrom permit none. I have already measured mermaid's (i) as permitted and its (ii)/(iii) as refused, so P5 is half-verified and half-prediction. COST: ARM 1 and ARM 4 are the real work — roughly two days including vendoring and version-pinning seven reference implementations, which S2 already budgets. ARMs 2 and 3 are hours, and ARM 2 is already written (the scripts that produced the 84.5% and the 13.4% figures in this report run in under a minute over the whole corpus).
result.kill_condition:
KILL THIS AREA if ARM 1 returns fewer than 3 languages with ≥4 distinct verdicts across 7 surfaces — i.e. if the surfaces broadly agree. Then degradation is not a differentiator, K5 fires, and the certificate should be cut to a single lint rule rather than a product. (I would be surprised: github-api vs github-blob already disagree on mermaid on identical bytes, measured live.)

KILL THE RENDERER ROADMAP SPECIFICALLY if, after mermaid and math, ARM 1 finds no fourth language that (a) appears in any real user corpus and (b) passes the {host config, host inputs, host bound} test. My two corpora say the count of such languages today is ZERO — 10 diagram fences in 10,709 across 1,558 files, none of them non-mermaid — so the honest default is: ship mermaid and math, ship the POLICY, and ship no third renderer until a user asks. If that is what happens, this area's deliverable is `mdmax cert --render` and `mdmax render-policy`, and nothing else.

KILL THE WRITE-BACK STORY — and this is the one that should stop the team — if the range-splice in ARM 2 cannot get the frontmatter no-op round trip to exactly 0 dirty files. At 84.5% dirty and 197 files changing line count, the properties panel is currently incompatible with BOTH D7 (splice-only) and §4.1 (durable block identity — you cannot anchor a comment in a document whose line count moves when someone edits a tag). If a splice cannot be made to hold there, the properties panel must be made read-only before comments ship, not after.

DO NOT PROCEED past S2 with `EditableTable` in the tree. It is dead code today, which is the only reason its measured 13.4% no-op dirty rate and its silent `\|` corruption are not already a live data-loss bug.
result.effort: One research session. ~55 tool calls: 1,084-file corpus verification (all sha256 matched), 6 corpus-wide measurement scripts, 5 live executions against the repo's own shipped modules via node type-stripping (html-policy, frontmatter, table-edit, mermaid 11.15.0, katex 0.17.0), ~20 primary fetches (api.github.com advisories for 12 packages, api.npmjs.org bulk downloads for 23 packages, raw.githubusercontent.com for github/docs, github/cmark-gfm, vega/vega-lite, obsidianmd/obsidian-help, quarto-dev/quarto-web, facebook/docusaurus, microsoft/vscode, zed-industries/zed), and one live `POST https://api.github.com/markdown`. Zero writes outside $TMPDIR; zero commits; zero installs; no destructive operation attempted or required.
result.unverified: WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND ITS REAL TIER. (1) Typora, Bear, Craft and Notion-import are CLOSED SOURCE. I fetched nothing primary for them and I am reporting nothing about them. The brief asked for all four; treat their row in any survey as EMPTY, not as "renders the basics". [not-verified] (2) Obsidian, VS Code and Zed capability claims are PRIMARY-READ OF DOCS AND SOURCE, not of running behaviour. I read obsidian-help markdown, vscode's markdown-language-features package.json, and zed's markdown.rs tag set. I did not run any of the three. A doc can lag its renderer. [primary-read, not own-measurement] (3) The github-blob / github-comment / github-pages verdicts in this report are INHERITED from the settled record — I measured only the github-API surface myself, live. The claim "GitHub is five surfaces" rests on my one new measurement plus three I did not re-derive. [mixed: 1 own-measurement + 3 secondary] (4) The mermaid CDN-drift claim is an INFERENCE from two verified facts: `MERMAID_VERSION = "11"` in pdf-doc.ts:24 (primary read) and `dist-tags.latest = 11.16.0` on registry.npmjs.org (primary read). I did NOT fetch `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/…` — jsdelivr is not an allowed host in this sandbox — so "the PDF path serves 11.16.0 today" is an inference from npm's semver resolution, not an observation. [inference] (5) I did NOT construct or run any exploit. The mermaid CSS-injection and PlantUML SSRF findings are advisory text plus source reading. Where I read a reachable-looking sink (`sanitizeText` at chunk-CSCIHK7Q.mjs:4915 passing `config2.dompurifyConfig` into `DOMPurify.sanitize`), I tested only whether the config key was settable from a document — it was NOT — and stopped. No end-to-end exploitability is claimed for anything. [primary-read + one negative own-measurement] (6) The alt-text decay measurement has n=21 markdown images and n=11 raw ``. The 100% figure is real for this corpus and it is a tiny sample. Do not publish it as a rate. [own-measurement, underpowered] (7) My fence census uses MY OWN fence parser (open on `^\s{0,3}(\`{3,}|~{3,})`, close on same char, ≥ length, empty info). It is not CommonMark-exact — in particular a 3-backtick fence nested inside a 3-backtick fence closes the outer one, as CommonMark says it should, but my handling of indented-code-block context is absent. The RANKING (bash ≫ everything, 10 mermaid, 0 of everything else) is robust to this; the absolute 7,714 is not exact. [own-measurement, stated algorithm] (8) "Nobody has built X" in the unclaimed list rests on registry.npmjs.org keyword search, whose `total` field is the size of the registry rather than a match count — so it is search-only evidence of ABSENCE, the weakest kind. I inspected the top-6 relevance results per query and they were unrelated; I did not search GitHub code search (it required authentication and returned `"Requires authentication"` unauthenticated). [search-only] (9) I did not measure token cost of any rendered projection beyond KaTeX's 123.7× byte amplification on `\frac{a}{b}`. No model was called. Every statement about what an AI consumer would prefer to see rendered is absent from this report on purpose. [not measured]

result.area: Marketability, and the 50% that is given away
result.headline: The free public good with a real, verifiable hole in the market is a degradation matrix over the constructs people actually write — YAML frontmatter and wikilinks, which markdownguide.org's 70-tool × 28-construct matrix tracks NEITHER while they appear in 90.77% of the pinned corpus and 60.13% of an independent one — but it must NOT be the marketing spearhead, because frontmatter's own demand research ranks that exact pain (T13 "Markdown/frontmatter mangling") 13th of 14 at severity "ANNOYS", while the pains that make people pay rank 1–9.
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED, two of them, both looked for. (F1) "If markdownguide.org — or babelmark, or any free artifact — already tracks frontmatter/wikilinks/callouts/mermaid per tool, the 'unclaimed' claim is dead." I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mattcone/markdown-guide/master/_data/tools.yml and enumerated it: exactly 28 construct ids, and the strings "frontmatter", "wikilink", "callout", "mermaid", "math", "katex", "admonition", "directive", "transclu", "embed" appear ZERO times. Babelmark's registry.json lists 38 entries and every one is a PARSER (pandoc, php-markdown, python-markdown, maruku), not a product surface. F1 did NOT fire. (F2) "If the 90.77% is an artifact of one operator's Obsidian vault, it does not transfer." I re-ran on an independent corpus (474 files / 5,013,124 bytes under ~/.claude/skills-src, authored mostly by Anthropic and plugin authors, not by this operator). **F2 PARTIALLY FIRED**: frontmatter 83.67% → 56.75%, wikilinks 50.00% → 8.23%, the untracked-at-risk union 90.77% → 60.13%. I am therefore reporting the range 60–91%, not the flattering 91%. The claim that survives both corpora is narrower and I state it that way: YAML frontmatter is the single most prevalent at-risk construct in BOTH corpora (83.67% / 56.75%), it is measured VISIBLE in 23 of 24 renderer configs, and no free matrix on the internet tracks it. (F3, unplanned, fired against my own work: my first fence-language scan reported 41.51% "unknown fence languages". The regex used `\s*` after the backticks, which spans newlines, so it captured the first word of the NEXT line. Corrected to `[ \t]*`: the true rate is 0.09% — one file. I killed my own 41.51% before it reached this report.)

Repo created 2014-08-14, 5,126 stars. GitHub's adoption artifact github/cmark-gfm was created 2016-12-01 — 2 years 3 months after the spec repo, and GitHub was an adopter, not the giver.

negatives: NEGATIVE 1 — The give-away is aimed at the company's own 13th-ranked pain, and the demand corpus says so in writing. docs/research/frontmatter-pain-taxonomy.md ranks 14 themes by severity × frequency. 'T13 Markdown/frontmatter mangling' sits at #13 with severity 'Annoys→churns purists' and scope 'Small pop., loud + influential'. 'T14 Publishing friction' is #14, 'Annoys', 'Cheap win, not a killer'. The pains that make people pay are #1 T1 sync destroys data (Kills adoption, 'Highest — 3x next theme on HN'), #3 T3 price backlash ('Churns at exodus scale'), #6 T7 collaboration impossible in markdown ('The unclaimed combination'), #9 T9 no browser access ('Core wedge'). `mdmax cert` — the chosen MVP and the proposed public good — is a T13 instrument. Corroborated independently on HN: an Algolia comment search for 'markdown renders differently' returns nbHits=235 comments of low-grade grumbling ('Different apps render Markdown differently…', 2024-11-24; 'some markdown renders differently when copied in vs when typed directly in teams', 2026-04-13) but a story search returns ZERO submissions above 50 points on the topic in twenty years. Compare the beachhead pain: forum.obsidian.md/t/obsidian-for-web/2049 at 246,568 views / 244 posts / 928 likes. Nobody has ever front-paged anything about markdown rendering divergence. The give-away half is not merely orthogonal to the earning half — it is pointed at a pain the company's own research classified as non-purchasing.

NEGATIVE 2 — The free tier IS already the give-away, and a second free thing cannibalises the founders, not the incumbents. The segment strategy prices free = browser vault + git sync, explicitly as the acquisition hook ('Free sync. It's just git'), with paid at $4/mo — a band bounded above by the live Obsidian Sync Standard price of $4/user/mo (verified at obsidian.md/pricing today) and by the forum's own stated ceiling ('maybe $2-4/month', forum.obsidian.md/t/26329). At $4/mo there is no margin to fund a second unfunded artifact, and the base rate says the artifact will not pay for itself: of eleven canonical give-aways I measured, nine produced no commercial entity for the giver, and the one nearest in kind — markdownlint, a free markdown quality tool by a solo maintainer — has run 11 years 4 months (repo created 2015-03-15) to 6,231 stars and 2,886,431 npm downloads/week with FUNDING.yml reading exactly 'github: DavidAnson'. The mermaid case, the best outcome in the set, took 7 years 11 months from npm publish (2014-12-02) to a commercial org (Mermaid-Chart, created 2022-11-07). Two founders with no README, no public repo and zero users cannot spend an eight-year option.

NEGATIVE 3 — Publishing under the plan's own kill gates is a marketing liability, not an asset. K2 commits to publishing a re-derived anchor number 'including if it is worse'; K5 says if the certificate finds no disagreement anyone cares about, cut it. My five-config replication already found disagreement in only 2 of 15 constructs. A public matrix that mostly shows AGREEMENT markets against the thesis, and a published anchoring benchmark that lands below 99.627% becomes the first result for the company's name.

NEGATIVE 4 — Producing a public good is the failure mode §9.8 already diagnosed, wearing a growth hat. PLAN.md §9.8: 'Three of the last four commits were cosmetic fixes to a 439 KB PDF about an engine with zero lines of code. Honesty was being converted into inertia.' §11's standing rule: 'No further research fan-out until one committed assertion in this repository has gone from red to green against engine code.' A conformance suite, a degradation matrix, a hostile corpus and a benchmark are four more artifacts that can be written rather than shipped, and every one of them is indistinguishable from the disease at the moment of authoring it.

NEGATIVE 5 — Publishing the matrix hands the Max tier's differentiator to everyone. D-level ambition is 'features unseen in the industry' on the Max plan. A published, machine-readable (product,surface) × construct matrix is a specification for exactly those features, free, to HackMD, GitHub, Obsidian and every agent-tool author in a directory that currently holds 12,804 repos under topic:agent-skills.
unclaimed: An EXECUTABLE per-(product,surface) degradation certificate over the constructs written in 2026 — YAML frontmatter, wikilinks, embeds, callouts, mermaid, math — emitting PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT rather than yes/partial/no, machine-readable, version-pinned, and gateable in CI. Searches run: enumerated markdownguide.org's _data/tools.yml (28 ids, zero of those constructs) and its _tools/ (70 files, no github.md/gitlab.md/confluence.md/teams.md/discourse.md/jira.md); fetched babelmark's registry.json (38 entries, all parser implementations); GitHub repo searches 'markdown compatibility matrix', 'markdown renderer comparison', 'markdown conformance suite', 'markdown degradation'; npm registry search 'markdown conformance'/'markdown compatibility'/'markdown degradation' (relevance-free, no hits on inspection). The one direct attempt, MrVampy/markdown-plugin, is 0 stars and was abandoned seven days after creation.

A public markdown ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY suite — feed a tool a real file, get back a byte-diff and a verdict, run against the writers people actually use (Obsidian's processFrontMatter, Notion export, prettier --parser markdown, AI file-edit tools). Searches run: GitHub 'markdown roundtrip test in:name,description' total=0; 'markdown parser differential in:name,description' total=0; 'markdown idempotent formatter' total=1 at 0 stars. mdformat (pypi, first release 2020-07-27, 660,319 downloads/week) is a FORMATTER that deliberately rewrites, not a fidelity checker. This is the one whose demand is already documented in the wild: forum.obsidian.md/t/…/65851 'Calling processFrontMatter will destroy all previous formatting, and most YAML features/syntax'.

A public block/range re-anchoring benchmark with named baseline arms and a hand-audited false-match rate. Searches run: GitHub 'text anchoring benchmark in:name,description' total=1 (0 stars, unrelated); 'robust anchor annotation benchmark' total=0; 'block identity markdown revision' total=0; arXiv API query on 'text anchoring' AND 'annotation' returned no matching titles. NOTE the countervailing evidence the plan already logged: 25 years of prior ART exists (Brush & Bargeron MSR-TR-2001-107, W3C TextQuoteSelector, Hypothes.is) — what is missing is a BENCHMARK, not the idea, and §9.4/§9.5 say the number is unre-derived and does not transfer to ranges. Publish this LAST, if at all.

result.design:
WHAT SHIPS FREE, AND WHY IT EARNS. One artifact, not five: `mdmax cert`, scoped to the constructs the corpus proves people write and the surfaces they publish to. Rows = frontmatter, wikilink, embed, callout, mermaid, math, HTML comment, attribute braces, table, task list. Columns = (product, surface) pairs, starting with github-blob, github-comment, github-pages, obsidian-preview, obsidian-publish, vscode-preview, gitlab, notion-import, sanitized-HTML, and LLM-context. Verdicts = PASS · STRIP · CORRUPT, executed and version-pinned, never hand-asserted. That is the whole differentiation from markdownguide.org, and it is a real one: markdownguide tracks 28 constructs of which zero are the top two by prevalence in either corpus I measured.

CARRIER. Ship it three ways from one binary, because the 2026 discovery surface is the agent tool directory and repomix has already proven the packaging: (1) `npx mdmax cert <file>` — zero install, the one-liner is the demo; (2) `--mcp`, an MCP server so an agent can call it mid-edit; (3) `--skill-generate`, a Claude Agent Skill, landing it in a topic with 12,804 repos whose leader has 165,486 stars; (4) a GitHub Action that fails a PR when a README construct will CORRUPT on Pages. Not a website. A website is markdownguide's game and they have nine years of SEO.

DEGRADATION BEHAVIOUR OF THE GIVE-AWAY ITSELF. The free tool is honest and complete for one file. It does not phone home, does not require an account, and does not withhold verdicts. The commercial edge is the last line of its output: "12 of your 340 files will CORRUPT on GitHub Pages — fix them at frontmatter.dev/fix." Whole-vault scanning, the fix, and the re-check are the product. That is the founder's 50/50 made literal: the diagnosis is a gift, the repair is the business.

WHAT DOES NOT SHIP FREE, AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION TO §13.4. Do not publish the anchoring benchmark. §9.4 says nobody has re-derived 99.627%, §9.5 says it does not transfer to ranges, K2 commits to publishing a worse number, and there is no prior benchmark to be compared against — so publishing is pure downside with no category to win. Keep it internal until S4 closes. The plan asked "is the engine marketing or product?" — the evidence says it is a third thing, a CREDIBILITY INSTRUMENT, and credibility instruments are sequenced by what they can prove today, not by what they might be worth.

POSITIONING, ONE SENTENCE EACH, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT SENTENCES. Product: "Your vault, in any browser. Nothing to install." — verbatim-derived from forum.obsidian.md/t/obsidian-for-web/2049/246, 246,568 views, and it targets pain #9 and #1, not #13. Free tool: "Paste a markdown file. See exactly what breaks on GitHub, in Obsidian, and in an LLM's context — before you publish it." Thirty-second proof point, and it is the same demo for both audiences: drop in the visitor's own README, and the tool shows their YAML frontmatter rendering as a table on a GitHub blob, as a properties panel in Obsidian, and as leaked visible body text in four of five parser configurations. I ran that last one; it is not a mock. It works on 83.67% of the pinned corpus and 56.75% of an independent one, which means it works on most visitors' first file.

WHO PAYS, AND AT WHAT. Anchored to prices I fetched today, not remembered. Free: browser vault, git sync, publish, and the CLI. Pro $4/mo billed annually — exactly Obsidian Sync Standard, inside the forum's stated $2–4 band. Max: comments, suggestions, offline, provenance, the AI view — priced against pains #1/#3/#7, not #13. Teams $5–8/seat/mo — under HackMD Prime's verified $5/seat and far under Notion Business's verified $20/member. And the underused one: a WORK licence at $50/user/year, mirroring Obsidian's verified Commercial $50 USD per user per year, sold to the exact population the beachhead is defined by — people who cannot install software on a work machine and can expense a licence.

DISTRIBUTION, IN ORDER. (1) The obsidian-git and obsidian-remote issue threads and forum t/2049, where +4,800 people/day are still installing the broken thing. (2) A companion Obsidian plugin, the channel Relay used to reach 176,247 installs. (3) The agent-tool directories. (4) Show HN last, framed as the product, not the tool — every markdown-editor Show HN ceilings around 240–471 points and llms.txt proves points do not predict adoption anyway.
result.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT, and it is deliberately not another corpus sweep — the open question is commercial, so the instrument must be a live consumer.

M1 — THE ONE-WEEK CERT PROBE, n=10 targets × 12 constructs, pre-registered. Corpus: the 1,084 files of corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… plus the 474-file independent corpus (path-selection sha256 72b867b02163ece7346e50cbae5cc71a) as the transfer check. Verifiers: render every (construct, target) pair through the REAL product surface — github-blob and github-comment via api.github.com/markdown with mode=gfm and mode=markdown, github-pages via a jekyll build, obsidian via its own renderer, vscode via markdown-it with its shipped plugin set, sanitized-HTML via DOMPurify, notion-import via its importer. Classify PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT from a parsed DOM, never a substring match. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS: (a) yaml_frontmatter is PASS on at most 3 of 10 targets; (b) at least 4 targets disagree with at least one other target on at least 3 constructs; (c) github-blob, github-comment and github-pages disagree on at least 2 constructs — this last one is the whole (product,surface) thesis and it must be shown, not asserted. If (c) fails, drop the surface dimension and the artifact collapses into a smaller version of markdownguide.

M2 — THE MARKETABILITY PROBE, n=30, and this is the one that actually decides the 50/50. W3 in §11 records zero users, zero interviews, zero willingness-to-pay probes across a million bytes of design. Recruit 30 people from three enumerable frames: 10 posters in forum.obsidian.md/t/obsidian-for-web/2049, 10 commenters on obsidian-git issues #340/#396/#558, 10 authors of repos carrying an llms.txt. Show each one, in this order: (i) the cert output on THEIR OWN file, (ii) the browser-vault demo. Instruments: which of the two they ask about second; whether they would install the CLI; whether they would pay $4/mo, and separately whether their employer would pay $50/year. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, and I will be wrong in a specific direction if I am wrong: fewer than 8 of 30 will name the cert as the reason they would pay, and more than 20 will name browser access or sync trust. If 15 or more name the cert, my headline is wrong and the give-away should be promoted to the spearhead.

M3 — THE CHANNEL A/B, n=2 launches, 30 days apart. Ship the cert as an npx one-liner + MCP + Agent Skill, and post it in exactly one channel per week: week 1 the obsidian-git issue threads, week 2 the agent-skills directory, week 3 Show HN. Instrument npm downloads/day and referrer. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION from the repomix and llms.txt evidence: the agent-tool channel outperforms Show HN on 30-day retained installs even if Show HN wins day one.
result.kill_condition: KILL THE GIVE-AWAY IF ANY OF THESE HOLDS. (K-A) M1 prediction (c) fails — github-blob, github-comment and github-pages agree on every construct. Then there is no (product,surface) insight, markdownguide.org's 70-tool table is sufficient prior art, and the artifact is a worse version of something with a nine-year SEO head start. Cut it, publish nothing, and spend the week on S5 multi-tenancy instead. (K-B) M2 returns fewer than 5 of 30 saying they would install the CLI at all. A free tool nobody installs is not marketing, it is unpaid maintenance — and I have the base rate: markdownlint ran 11 years to 2.89M weekly downloads and $0. (K-C) The cert build exceeds two weeks of one founder's time. My five-config prototype took one script against packages already in the repo; if the real thing balloons, the cost is the target harness, and a two-founder company with no README and no users cannot fund a public good before it funds a product. (K-D) M2 shows 15+ of 30 naming the cert as their reason to pay — this kills my HEADLINE rather than the artifact, and the correct response is to promote the give-away to the spearhead and re-sequence. I have pre-committed to reporting this outcome if it occurs. (K-E) The anchoring benchmark is published before S4 closes. This is a process kill: §9.4 says nobody has re-derived the number, K2 commits to publishing whatever comes out, and publishing an unre-derived flagship figure is the exact 100%-flattering-headline failure this run exists to stop.
result.unverified:
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND THE TIER IT ACTUALLY SITS AT.

(1) Excalidraw+ as a commercial outcome — SEARCH-ONLY/INFERENCE. I verified only that excalidraw/excalidraw's README on master links to plus.excalidraw.com and that FUNDING.yml reads 'open_collective: excalidraw'. I did NOT establish when Excalidraw+ launched, whether it is profitable, or its pricing. plus.excalidraw.com was not fetched. Do not cite it as an eight-year-lag data point; it is a name in a README.

(2) Mermaid Chart's revenue, funding and headcount — NOT VERIFIED AT ANY TIER. I verified the org creation date (2022-11-07), the blog URL (mermaid.ai) and the creation dates of 18 repos. mermaidchart.com/pricing returned http 200 with 1,186 bytes of JS shell and no readable prices. Every statement about Mermaid Chart's commercial success is inference from repo names.

(3) JSON Schema ↔ Postman — SEARCH-ONLY, and I am dropping the claim. The json-schema-org/.github profile README I fetched contains no sponsor, funding or Postman line. I could not substantiate the sponsorship relationship from a primary source and it appears nowhere in my findings.

(4) The GitHub code-search counts (llms.txt 9,640; .editorconfig 82,848; commitlint.config.js 10,896) are SEVERE UNDERCOUNTS and should be read as ordinal only. GitHub's code search indexes a subset of repositories and caps result estimates; the true file counts are unknown and larger.

(5) The Obsidian forum view counts, Docker pull counts, r/ObsidianMD subscriber figures, Discord member counts, Notion/Evernote ARR and all note-taking market sizing are SECONDARY — quoted from docs/research/frontmatter-segment-strategy.md as of its 2026-07-13 verification date. I re-verified only the four live pricing pages and the Obsidian plugin stats JSON. The market-size row in that document is explicitly self-tagged unverified with a 10× divergence across four firms ($1.18B / $1.35B / $11.02B / $17.19B); I did not attempt to resolve it and no sizing claim in my findings depends on it.

(6) My mini-certificate's classifier is COARSE and I am not reporting its full table. Rows I trust: yaml_frontmatter, html_comment, comment_idiom, unknown_fence — each turns on a payload string I can check unambiguously. Rows I do NOT trust and did not cite: gfm_table and task_list read 'OK' under marked/default, which cannot be right for a non-GFM parser; my `visible` predicate is too permissive for table and strikethrough. The '2 of 15 disagree' figure is therefore a LOWER bound on disagreement, which happens to cut against my own argument, so I have left it as measured.

(7) The '55 payloads' figure for test/preview/html-policy-xss.test.ts, cited in PLAN.md §15, docs/engine/README.md lines 664 and 787, and the dossier — I COULD NOT REPRODUCE IT. The file has 327 lines, 15 `it()` blocks, and its two payload arrays hold 39 and 6 entries (45). A broader sweep for payload-shaped string literals gives 71. Neither is 55. This is a minor stale-number defect of the §9.2 family and someone should re-derive it before it is published again.

(8) The 60.13% falsifier corpus is MY OWN SELECTION, not corpus_id: 474 *.md files / 5,013,124 bytes under ~/.claude/skills-src, dot-directories and node_modules/dist/build/__pycache__ excluded, path-list sha256 72b867b02163ece7346e50cbae5cc71a. It matches the file count and byte count PLAN.md §11 W1 proposes for exactly this purpose, which is a useful cross-check but not an independent one — it is still a corpus on this operator's machine, and W1's real requirement (a corpus somebody else wrote) is still unmet.

(9) No live model call was made, so nothing here bears on the 'LLM-context' column of the proposed matrix. That column is a design intention, not a measurement — same status as §6's comprehension claims.

result.area: Carrier and capability inventory: how to make a markdown file hold more, convey more, and mean more
result.headline: Ranked on capacity x invisibility x survival x legibility, the top invisible carrier (orphan link reference definition) has EXACTLY ZERO uses in the 1,084-file pinned corpus while the two things authors actually strain against are absent from the carrier debate entirely — 1,431 bare angle-bracket placeholders in 219/1,084 files that GitHub silently DELETES from rendered output, and 13,028 wikilinks GitHub renders as literal junk — so the honest top-5 is ONE new carrier plus FOUR recognisers, and the "authors reach for raw HTML" premise is refuted at 37/1,084 files (3.4%).

I looked for both. (a) Candidates checked one by one: orphan linkref definition — wins capacity/invisibility/survival, 0 uses (mdast `definition` node absent from the type histogram over all 1,084 files); inline link title — wins all four but is availability-bound, only 1,838 link host-constructs exist against 142,802 paragraphs, so it cannot name most of a document, and only 23 titles are occupied; `` — survives GitHub's sanitizer and remark+prettier byte-identically but is dropped entirely by remark-rehype without rehype-raw (measured html_safe_has_payload=False) and has 5 uses; unknown-language fence — survives everything but is VISIBLE by construction. findings.claim: CORRECTION to the established evidence: the orphan link reference definition — the carrier the program ranks #1 for invisibility — has ZERO real uses in the entire pinned corpus. The mdast `definition` node type does not appear at all; nor do `linkReference`, `imageReference`, `footnoteDefinition`, `footnoteReference`. A loose regex over the raw bytes found 9 definition-SHAPED lines and all 9 are prose ('  [Topic]: Review said X. Outside voice says Y.'). Its strength (zero collision risk) and its weakness (no author recognises it, so nothing downstream is motivated to preserve it) are the same fact.

findings.claim: THE LARGEST UNMET NEED IN THE CORPUS IS NOT A CARRIER, IT IS A METAVARIABLE. 1,431 bare angle-bracket placeholder tokens (186 distinct names) appear in 219 of 1,084 files (20.2%) outside inline code, and GitHub DELETES every one of them from rendered output. Markdown has no construct for 'a thing you substitute', so authors write `<target-file>` and CommonMark classifies it as raw HTML.
findings.evidence:
Own measurement over corpus_id sha256:3a010b16..., inline code and fenced code masked, 423,414 prose lines scanned. Top tokens: 223 in 113 files, 102, 92, 87, 69, 58, 47 in 12 files, 27 in 8 files. GitHub Markdown API (api.github.com/markdown, mode=gfm), input 'Run the tool with `--flag` on and then is bound.' -> output '

Run the tool with --flag on and then is bound.

'. Both placeholders gone.

findings.claim: Placeholders that COLLIDE with an HTML5 tag name fail a third, worse way: they become active markup that corrupts the rest of the paragraph. There are three distinct failure modes for placeholder tokens in the same document, and no renderer agrees with another.
findings.evidence:
GitHub Markdown API mode=gfm. Input 'Filed new issue, added comment on existing issues.' -> '

Filed new issue, added comment on existing issues.

' — the `` pluralisation marker opens a strikethrough GitHub auto-closes at paragraph end. Input 'Set and <base> before the run.' -> '<p>Set <title> and before the run.</p>' — `<title>` ESCAPED, `<base>` DELETED, in one line. Input 'You mentioned <Source A>, <Source B>, and <Source C>.' -> '<p>You mentioned <source>, <source>, and <source>.</p>' — attributes stripped, content deleted. In the pinned corpus these collisions number <base> 66, <title> 32, <source> 20, <s> 4.

findings.claim: CORRECTION: 'GitHub strips class, style and data-* entirely; only id survives, namespaced' is incomplete in two ways that change design decisions. (1) The `title` attribute survives on `<span>` and `<a>` with its value intact — a second surviving attribute nobody has recorded. (2) `id` is not merely namespaced, it is LOWERCASED in gfm mode but case-PRESERVED in markdown mode. Any case-sensitive identifier (base64url, nanoid, ULID) collapses when a document passes through the comment box.

findings.claim: CORRECTION, and it is a capability gain: 'fence info-string meta past the first word is dropped from HTML by every renderer' is FALSE for GitHub when the language is unknown. GitHub emits BOTH `lang=` and `data-meta=` into the sanitized HTML. So an unknown-language fence gives you a VISIBLE body plus an INVISIBLE metadata channel that reaches a sanitized-HTML consumer — the only carrier measured that does both at once.

The unknown-language fence is the only carrier that survives EVERY payload hazard through BOTH remark-stringify and prettier byte-identically, including the ones that destroy the title slot: double quotes, blank lines, JSON, backticks, and nested fences. Prettier also does not reformat an unknown-language body, whereas it rewrites a known-language body and thereby invalidates any content hash committed to that block.

findings.claim: The link/definition TITLE slot has three failure modes the established 'spec-guaranteed, semantics-free, byte-identical' framing does not cover. An unescaped `"` destroys the definition outright and remark then emits a VISIBLE escaped line. A blank line does the same. And remark and prettier normalise the delimiter to DIFFERENT canonical forms, so a repo running prettier in CI and remark in the app will ping-pong the bytes forever. Backslash-escaped-double-quote JSON and base64url/percent-encoded payloads are the only forms stable through both.

MY OWN TOP RECOMMENDATION HAS A DEGRADATION FAILURE I CANNOT ENGINEER AWAY, AND IT COLLIDES WITH D2/D4. Tail-placed identity records live IN the .md, so a clean export must strip them — and stripping them destroys the exported copy's identity, which means content-derived re-anchoring (§4.1) must remain the real mechanism and the in-file record can only ever be a cache. That is precisely the 'divergence between a human view and a machine view' failure §6 warns about, produced by my own design.

result.design: RANKED CARRIER INVENTORY (capacity x invisibility x survival x legibility; all measured this session against remark-parse/stringify 11.0.0, remark-gfm 4.0.1, prettier 3.8.3, marked 16.4.2, remark-rehype raw+safe, GitHub Markdown API modes gfm and markdown). TIER 1 — SHIP. 1. ORPHAN LINK REFERENCE DEFINITION, tail-placed, base64url or percent-encoded. Capacity: label <=999 (CommonMark) / <=1000 (cmark-gfm) — HARD CAP AND THE ONLY ONE; destination and title >=1 MB. Invisibility: 0 bytes of HTML in 6/6 renderer configs tested. Survival: byte-identical through remark AND prettier. Legibility: WEAK (0 live uses; illegible to a human). Hazards, all measured: cannot interrupt a paragraph ('Alpha.\n[k]: /a "t"' is ONE paragraph, and the definition becomes visible); remark-stringify DROPS duplicate labels (5 -> fewer, roundtrip false); a raw " or a blank line in the title destroys the definition and remark then emits a VISIBLE escaped line; (...) and '...' delimiters are normalised to different canonical forms by remark and by prettier. RULE: labels <=999, titles ONLY double-quoted with base64url/percent-encoded payloads, one label per document, tail-placed after a blank line. 2. UNKNOWN-LANGUAGE FENCE + INFO-STRING META (```fm:meta v1). Capacity unbounded (50 KB through GitHub, 1 MB locally); nests via backtick count. Invisibility: NONE for the body — this is the price. But the META is invisible-and-present: GitHub emits lang="fm:meta" data-meta="v1". Survival: best in class — 14/14 payload hazards byte-identical through remark AND prettier, and prettier does NOT reformat an unknown-language body (a known-language body IS reformatted, invalidating any content hash). Legibility: HIGH. 3. LINK/IMAGE TITLE ON AN EXISTING LINK. Wins all four axes but is AVAILABILITY-BOUND: 1,838 links against 142,802 paragraphs. Use for link-scoped facts only, never for block identity. TIER 2 — CONDITIONAL. 4. / — survives GitHub's sanitizer with the value intact (a correction to 'only id survives') and is byte-stable through remark+prettier, but is dropped entirely by remark-rehype without rehype-raw and is inline-invasive. 5. YAML frontmatter — VISIBLE in marked and on GitHub; use for NAMING only, per D9. TIER 3 — DO NOT USE. HTML comment (DELETED by GitHub in BOTH modes; 330 already in the corpus). id attribute (namespaced AND lowercased in gfm — case-sensitive ids collapse). class/data-* (stripped). {#id}, {: #id}, :::directive, {{shortcode}}, CriticMarkup, [text]{#id}, 'Term\n: def' (all visible literal junk on GitHub, several correct on GitHub Pages). Unicode Tag block (passes remark, prettier and GitHub byte-identically and invisibly — a threat to FILTER, and my initial "GitHub strips it" reading was a harness artifact; GitHub does NOT strip it). THE TOP 5 ADDITIONS — ONE CARRIER, FOUR RECOGNISERS. A1. TAIL RECORD (the only new carrier). `[fm:b1]: #fm "v1."` in a blank-line-isolated block at end of file. Degradation: GitHub gfm and markdown -> 0 bytes; remark-rehype raw and safe -> 0 bytes; marked -> 0 bytes; Obsidian/VS Code -> nothing; remark-stringify and prettier -> byte-identical. Cost: illegible; must be stripped on export (see negatives). It is a CACHE over §4.1 re-anchoring, never a replacement. A2. DESCRIPTION-LIST RECOGNISER (no bytes written). Lift `- **Term** — def` into a descriptionList in the tree; leave the source alone. Covers 7,938 unambiguous instances (18,462 including the weaker bold-run form). Degradation: EXACTLY what it is today in every renderer, because nothing changed. Zero risk, largest coverage. A3. PLACEHOLDER RECOGNISER + CERTIFICATE WARNING. Detect bare angle-bracket tokens that are not valid HTML5 elements, or that are but read as metavariables, and warn: "GitHub will DELETE these N tokens; wrap them in backticks." Verified remediation: `` -> '<target-file>' (preserved); \ -> '<target-file>' (preserved). Covers 1,431 tokens in 219/1,084 files. This is the highest-severity finding in the corpus and the cheapest fix in the report. A4. INLINE-ROLE RECOGNISER over inlineCode. 76,118 spans doing >=13 jobs; classify (filepath, command, identifier, cli-flag, constant, prose-in-backticks at 13.2%) into the tree for search, cross-reference and the AI projection. No bytes written, so no degradation to describe. A5. TYPED-RELATION RESOLVER for the 13,028 wikilinks. Not syntax — a resolver with more than one file in scope, plus a certificate line stating that these 13,028 constructs are literal text outside Obsidian. This is the "hundreds of markdowns connected to hundreds" capability the founder describes, delivered as resolution rather than as a carrier. WHAT SHOULD NOT BE BUILT: any in-file comment/annotation carrier (D2, now independently re-derived from the carrier side — GitHub deletes HTML comments in both modes, so a frontmatter comment pasted into a PR dies silently); any appearance or id-based identity (case-folding); any new block or inline syntax (all six tested proposals are visible junk on GitHub); and any use of the Unicode Tag block. For per-block comments, per-span provenance and revision history the honest answer is a SIDECAR — and the vocabulary should be TEI's @cert/@resp/@source, not ours.
result.measurement:
THE ONE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES THE OPEN QUESTION — a carrier survival matrix with a real second corpus and real consumers, because everything above rests on one corpus and one renderer family. CORPUS: pin a SECOND corpus of 1,000+ .md files NOT authored by this workspace (top-200 GitHub repos by stars with a README plus /docs), sha256-manifested and given its own corpus_id. The pinned corpus is 1,084 files by two authors and one AI; its 0 link reference definitions, 0 GFM alerts and 13,028 wikilinks are plausibly a signature of Obsidian usage rather than of markdown authors. Re-run: definition count, wikilink count, bare-placeholder count, bold-run-list-item rate, inlineCode role mix, real-HTML file share. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, so this can refute me: link reference definitions >0 but <0.5 per file; bare placeholders present in >10% of files; bold-run description-list items >12% of list items; real-HTML file share HIGHER than 3.4% (I expect my 3.4% to be the low outlier, and I expect to be at least partly wrong here). TASKS: 32 carriers x 12 consumers. Consumers must include the four this session could not reach — GitHub Pages via a real kramdown+kramdown-parser-gfm install (the gem install into a TMPDIR GEM_HOME failed here), the real GitHub blob renderer (the API's mode=markdown is NOT it: alerts render on github.com READMEs but not through that mode), the two clipboard flavours driven through a real browser (text/plain vs text/html, pasted into Google Docs and into VS Code), and one non-GitHub sanitizer (Discourse or Slack). VERIFIERS, cheapest first: (1) byte-equality after remark-stringify and after prettier — rules-based, already built; (2) payload-present and payload-visible in rendered HTML — rules-based, already built; (3) a DOM diff for the clipboard round trip. n = 32 x 12 = 384 cells, each a deterministic pass/fail, no judge needed. SEPARATE AND SMALLER: a 200-document A/B on A3 (placeholder linter) measuring precision against hand-labelled ground truth. Pre-registered prediction: >90% precision, versus markdownlint MD033's near-zero precision for this purpose since it fires on every
and
. If A3 lands under 80% precision it gets switched off exactly like the naive link checker did, and it should not ship.
result.kill_condition: KILL THE TAIL RECORD (A1) IF: the second-corpus run shows link reference definitions in active use above ~0.5 per file (collision risk appears, and the "empty slot" argument dies); OR the clipboard measurement shows the text/plain flavour also dropping them (then the carrier has no path through the copy/paste loop that is frontmatter's whole point); OR the export-guarantee work concludes that stripping tail records on export is required by D4, in which case A1 is a cache with a 100% miss rate on every exported document and should be deleted rather than shipped. KILL THE WHOLE CARRIER PROGRAM IF: content-derived re-anchoring at §4.1's stated rate is re-derived successfully by W2 AND the diff-assisted arm 7 baseline beats it — because then identity needs no in-file bytes at all and every carrier above is dead weight on a plain .md file. KILL A3 (placeholder linter) IF precision <80% on the 200-document ground truth. KILL A2/A4/A5 (recognisers) ONLY IF they start writing bytes — a recogniser that emits source is a construct wearing a disguise and falls under every negative in this report. DO NOT SHIP any carrier whose payload contains a raw double quote, a blank line, a backtick in a backtick-fence info string, a link label of 1000 characters, or a case-sensitive identifier — each of those is a measured, reproducible failure in this report and each of them fails SILENTLY.
result.unverified:
GITHUB PAGES / KRAMDOWN IS SECONDARY, NOT MEASURED. The gem install of kramdown + kramdown-parser-gfm into a TMPDIR GEM_HOME failed. Every kramdown claim here is a PRIMARY READ of gettalong/kramdown doc/syntax.page (definition lists, "Attribute List Definitions", {::comment}), not an execution. The specific claim "'Term\n: def' renders as a <dl> on GitHub Pages" is INFERENCE from that doc; only the GitHub-blob/comment side is measured.

THE GITHUB API'S mode=markdown IS NOT THE BLOB RENDERER, and I did not fully characterise the real one. Evidence it diverges: GFM alerts render on github.com READMEs but the API's markdown mode emits a plain blockquote with a literal [!NOTE]. My attempt to confirm via Accept: application/vnd.github.html+json on two repo READMEs returned 0 markdown-alert occurrences — but neither README demonstrably uses an alert, so that probe is INCONCLUSIVE, not negative. Treat every "GitHub blob" claim here as covering the API's markdown mode only. The comment-box (gfm) results are solid.

CLIPBOARD IS INFERENCE, NOT MEASUREMENT. No browser was driven. The text/plain claim (carriers survive, because the flavour is the raw source) and the text/html claim (tail records are DELETED, because they render to zero bytes) both follow deductively from measured HTML output, but neither was observed. This is the weakest column in the ranking and my task asked for both flavours.

DOCBOOK, JATS, DITA AND OOXML WERE NOT READ. docbook/docbook on GitHub now contains only ['MovedToCodeberg', 'README.md'] and codeberg is outside the network allowlist; the DITA code-search API returned 401. So the cross-check my task required against six formats was completed for TWO — TEI (primary, att.global.responsibility read verbatim) and HTML5 (own measurement, via GitHub's live sanitizer behaviour on 27 distinct real elements). Every DocBook, JATS, DITA and OOXML statement I might have made has been omitted rather than asserted from memory. The specific claim "markdown collapses ~40 DocBook inline semantic roles into one inlineCode node" is stated in this report ONLY as the measured half (13 roles inferred from 77,516 real spans, own-measurement); the DocBook denominator is NOT verified and I have not used it.

CROSS-CORPUS TRANSFER IS UNKNOWN AND MAY BE THE LARGEST WEAKNESS. Every corpus number is from 1,084 files authored by two people and an AI. The 0-definitions result, the 13,028 wikilinks, the 73.9% bash fence share and the 3.4% real-HTML share are all plausibly signatures of one Obsidian-based workflow. I did not re-derive the program's "40 link titles in 67,790 links / 99.94% unoccupied" figure — my pinned-corpus numbers are 23 titles in 1,838 links, a completely different denominator, and I cannot tell whether the 67,790 figure used a corpus, an exclusion policy, or a definition of "link" that reproduces. Per §9.2 that is exactly the class of number that has failed before, and I am flagging it rather than reconciling it.

MY OWN HARNESS PRODUCED ONE FALSE RESULT I CAUGHT MID-RUN. The first GitHub pass reported the Unicode Tag block as "stripped by GitHub" (has=False). That was a bug — I was searching for the ASCII string in output containing tag characters. GitHub passes the entire Tag block through byte-identically in both modes. The established evidence was RIGHT and my first reading was wrong; the threat is intact. I report this because a single-pass harness result in this report should be assumed to carry others of the same kind that I did not catch.

result.area: The mother markdown: one file containing many, with breakpoints, split on read (pack/unpack, split contract, rejoin contract, injection, edit-mapping, boundary destruction, zip vs single file)
result.headline: Ship the container as a single .md and not a zip — it round-trips 1084/1084 byte-identical at +0.892% overhead and costs 120x less git storage per edit than a zip — but two settled decisions are wrong: the carrier must be a content-derived backtick fence, not the HTML comment PLAN §5 makes the default (which silently loses a boundary on 0.369% of real files and therefore fails on 98.2% of vault-scale packs), and the pack must never be the write surface, because a destroyed boundary is silently mis-located 119/120 times on the realistic merge case.
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED, two of them. (1) "Boundary destruction is unrepairable" is wrong if a rebase against the retained pre-edit pack recovers destroyed boundaries under hostile edits. I looked, and my FIRST experiment refuted my own headline: line-diff opcode rebase on clean delimiter deletion recovered 200/200 within a median-0 / p90-1 / max-2 line window with zero losses, which says "repairable". I then made the destruction realistic (model rewrites across the boundary, elides unchanged regions, reorders, truncates) and the same algorithm went to 119/120 WRONG on merge_across, 119/120 WRONG on elide, 120/120 WRONG on reorder, and 47/120 unrecoverable on truncate — and WRONG here means it returns a confident boundary position that does not contain the true split, i.e. silent corruption. The optimistic reading was an artifact of a benign destruction model, which is exactly the flattering-direction defect this run was told to avoid; I am reporting it against myself. (2) "The HTML-comment carrier is unsafe" is wrong if a CommonMark parser keeps the second boundary when a contained file ends inside an open fence. I tested it with mdast-util-from-markdown 2.0.3 / micromark 4.0.2 and got boundary2_is_block_start=false for both html-comment and linkref, true for the fence. Not found. Residual I could NOT falsify: I did not test a semantic/content-derived re-anchor (the 99.627% block-level result cited in the brief) as a boundary repairer; it may do better than line-diff and I did not measure it.

The incremental git storage cost of ONE one-line edit inside a 272-file corpus is 66 bytes for the folder, 263 bytes for the single-file container, and 31,590 bytes for the zip — 120x the container. And `git diff` on the zip says 'Binary files differ', i.e. zero review value, while the container produces a normal reviewable text diff.

findings.claim: A two-line git diff driver makes the container self-attributing: the hunk header names the contained source file. This is free file-level attribution in `git diff` with no plugin.

findings.claim: On every property that matters to a model or to git, the single file beats the zip; the zip wins only on random access. The container's complete index sits at 0.49% of the file (the head); the zip's central directory sits at 98.8% (the tail), so a zip cannot be indexed or consumed from a stream and cannot be read by a model at all. Gzipping the container also beats the zip by 15.4% because zip compresses each member independently and throws away cross-file redundancy.

'container.gz=7,874,098 (30.8%)' vs 'zip=9,310,058 (36.4%)'. Uncompressed tar is +3.4% (512-byte block padding) — worse than the markdown container's +0.892%. findings.claim: The container scales to a 500 MB vault and packs 5x faster than zipping it. 21,680 files / 510,975,300 bytes packs in 1.91 s (270 MB/s) and a full boundary scan of 21,680 boundaries takes 1.48 s; the equivalent zip takes 9.7 s. The real constraint is memory, not time: a naive implementation is O(whole container) in RAM (516 MB), so streaming pack and unpack is a hard requirement, not an optimisation.

findings.claim: Nesting is free and byte-exact, so PLAN §5's 'a container inside a container is refused in v1' should be deleted. The fence run is itself a nesting counter: packing a container inside a container auto-escalates 4 -> 5 -> 6 and recovers byte-identically at three levels.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…, first 20 knowledge files — 'outer fence run derived from manifest header: fence: 5 / inner recovered byte-identical: True / inner-of-inner files recovered: 10 /10 / 3-deep header: fence: 6 / 3-deep byte-identical: True'. The 'flatten, never nest' law from tar/shar/MIME is about the PATH TREE, not about container-in-container; it was over-applied.

findings.claim: Boundary forgery is closed by construction, and the security property is the pinned run length rather than any escaping. A malicious file containing a literal open delimiter forces the packer to escalate to a 5-backtick fence, and a correct reader recovers exactly 3 files with the evil file byte-identical and zero forged paths — but a naive reader that scans for any 3-or-more-backtick fence accepts the forged path.

findings.claim: The fence-plus-path structure I derived is literally the edit format frontier models are BEST at emitting. On Aider's polyglot leaderboard the `whole` format (path line, fence, full content, fence) is well-formed at median 99.6% (min 92.9, max 100.0, n=15) while `diff` is median 94.2% with a min of 64.4% (n=47). Aider's own prompt is byte-for-byte our container shape.

The irreducible cost of the fence carrier is that the container stops rendering: 285 of 288 rendered characters land inside <pre><code>, with zero headings, links, tables, bold or list items, versus a fully rendered document under the HTML-comment carrier. negatives: THE VAULT-SCALE MOTHER MARKDOWN DOES NOT FIT IN ANY CONTEXT WINDOW, AND THE INDEX BEATS IT BY 110x. On the pinned corpus the container is 25,776,700 bytes against a described index of 234,119 bytes — 110.1x — replicating the prior Anthropic finding (168.8x) on our own data. A 200K-token budget holds 2.79% of the container; even a 2M-token budget holds 27.9%; the index fits three times over in 200K. The founder's stated primary use — 'one single markdown file... one single software to load everything and one single software to parse and render everything' — is arithmetically impossible at his own vault's scale (756 files, 21 MB). The container is only ever a BOUNDED WORKING SET: a 200K-token budget holds about 30 average-sized files (mean file 23,568 bytes). If MDMAX ships a 'pack my whole vault' button, it ships a button that produces an unreadable artifact.
