verdicts.claim: DESIGN S-1 — gates: vitest exclude .claude/worktrees moves `vitest list --filesOnly` 247→83; relabel the .doc export because it is a false claim.
verdicts.reason: [own-measurement + primary-read] The vitest half is exact: I counted 247 test files including .claude/worktrees and 83 excluding it, and vitest.config.ts declares no `exclude` key at all, so the leak is real. The .doc half is not a false claim. src/modules/export/presentation/ExportMenu.tsx:93 carries the honest comment "Word opens HTML-based .doc files natively; reuse the HTML renderer.", line 95 sends `application/msword`, and line 158 labels the item "Export Word (.doc)" — it never claims OOXML, and HTML-with-a-.doc-extension is a real, working Word import path that has shipped for two decades. Calling it a user-facing falsehood overstates a labelling nit into a correctness bug and would waste a slot in a half-day pre-flight.
verdicts.correction: The vitest gate (247→83) is correct and worth shipping. The .doc export is a naming preference, not a false claim; drop it from S-1.

verdicts.claim: FALSIFIER HONESTY — did the researcher genuinely hunt its own pre-registered falsifier?
verdicts.reason: [primary-read] Yes, and this is the strongest procedural improvement over the prior run. Part (1) was aimed at something that could realistically have fired, it PARTIALLY DID, and I verified the revision it forced is the correct one: firestore.rules genuinely specifies memberUids/roles with real enforcement clauses (lines 253-291), genuinely names no comments collection, and firestore() genuinely has zero callers — so "a specified, unimplemented model that does not even name comments" is the accurate framing and is narrower than the original. Part (2) traced writeSlug → setShare → POST /api/share to the Publish button and did not fire. Both probes made the headline smaller. THE GAP: both falsifier arms point at the qualitative half of the headline. Nothing was pre-registered that could have killed a NUMBER — and both of my confirmed kills (the 31.86%-vs-3.64% accounting asymmetry, the 18.9% denominator) live in the quantitative half. A falsifier that only guards the prose leaves the arithmetic unprotected.

survived: The whole headline. Every component reproduces: one string-equality allowlist with one caller and no uid anywhere; a specified-but-unimplemented Firestore membership model with zero comments collection and zero firestore() callers; 3.64% byte-identity (33/907); 84.78% bare-date-to-ISO (624/736). Corpus rebuilt independently from corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 — 1084 files, 0 missing, 0 sha mismatches, all three pinned heads live-matched.
C1 in full, and strengthened: env.ts:47 hard-defaults ALLOWED_GH_LOGIN to "sagnikmitra" and the dev bypass synthesizes an actor from that same single string.
C3's arithmetic to the digit (33 + 171 + 703 = 907; 33/907=3.64%; 33/736=4.48%), plus the 502: route.ts POST returns status 502 'upstream_failure' on any gray-matter throw.

C4 in full, including the 703-stable / 0-differ green-test corollary — the single most decision-relevant number in the report, because it means every existing frontmatter test passes while the bytes on disk are wrong.
C5 verbatim: the header says 'splicing the key into the YAML frontmatter', line 26 says matter.stringify. A real D7 violation in the only shipped write path.
C6's raw measurements exactly: 119 / 170 / 618, and lineWidth:0 moving 119→126. Only the 31.86%-vs-3.64% framing dies, not the data, and not the conclusion that splice is required.

C7's mechanism: eemeli/yaml parses 0 of the 170 gray-matter failures (I measured the set overlap; both fail on identically the same 170 files), and markdown-parser.ts catches to fm={} with no user-visible signal.
C8's substance against the primary discovery documents, both revisions matching to the day, every verbatim description exact.
C9 at the markup level — I extracted the full comparison table; all four Collaboration rows are Check/Check/Check on Free/Prime/Enterprise.
C10 — four of four quotes byte-exact against the raw help file, plus $4/user/mo verified on obsidian.md/pricing.
The design's positioning correction, verified against moment.dev/pricing verbatim.
The design's S-1(b) vitest gate: 247 → 83 reproduces exactly, and vitest.config.ts has no exclude key.
killed: C6's headline contrast '31.86% safe vs 3.64%'. It scores eemeli's 170 refusals as successes and gray-matter's 170 throws as failures — on identically the same 170 files. Consistent accounting gives 22.38% vs 31.86%, or 3.64% vs 13.12%. A ~9-point gap presented as ~28.
C6's word 'safe' for the 170 refusals. In the Publish path a refusal is a 502 and an unpublishable note, not a preserved file. 'Did not corrupt' is being counted as 'worked'.
C7's '18.9% of a real Obsidian vault's frontmatter'. 18.9% is the whole-corpus rate. The Obsidian vault (md root) is 13.75% (91/662); the knowledge repo is 35.59% (79/222); the frontmatter repo is 0.

C8's '92 suggestion fields'. Reproduces under none of eleven counting rules (I got 147, 197, 62, 131, 56, 16, 61, 24, 11, 125, 22). The '35' is fine — it is exactly the count of schemas whose NAME contains 'Suggest' — but the rule was never stated.
C2's 'isVaultEditor'. No such function exists in firestore.rules; the helper at line 176 is canEditVault.
C9's Full-text-search contrast. That row is Free=Minus, Prime=Check — the reverse of what is claimed. The cited 'M128,24A104…' glyph is in the Image storage row's Prime column.

The design's 'the .doc export is a false claim in a user-facing menu'. The menu says 'Export Word (.doc)', the code comment says 'Word opens HTML-based .doc files natively', and it does. A labelling preference, not a defect.
new_defects: The headline says Publish 'round-trips only 3.64%', but 3.64% is a NO-OP write. I measured the actual publish-then-unpublish round trip on the same corpus_id: 17/736 parsed = 2.31% byte-identical (17/907 = 1.87%). The claim is conservative rather than inflated, but the design's own S-1(a) gate is written against the round-trip operation, so the baseline it must beat is 1.87%, not 3.64%.

The design's S-1(a) gate as literally written — 'assert 100% byte-identity on all 907 frontmatter files' — is unsatisfiable for a publish, since inserting public_slug necessarily changes bytes. Only publish-then-unpublish can be a byte-identity gate. Restate it as: publish→unpublish is byte-identical on all 907, AND publish succeeds (no 502) on the 171.

171 is two failure modes, not one. Exactly 170 files fail at matter() parse; exactly one more, md/pj.md, parses cleanly and throws at matter.stringify ('end of the stream or a document separator is expected at line 6, column 1'). A splice fixes the 170 by never parsing; it does not automatically fix the stringify class. Worth a separate test case.

The pinned corpus double-counts. 29 files are byte-identical across roots by sha256 — frontmatter/docs/* is mirrored into md/docs/* (FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md, FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md, adr/0001-… and 26 more), 2.68% of 1,084. Every corpus percentage in this program inherits that, including all of this researcher's. Not their defect, but the manifest should carry a dedup note before the build phase treats these ratios as ground truth.

LIVE REPO HAZARD, unrelated to this claim but blocking the gate: package.json in the working tree has been gutted to `{"type":"module"}` — 97 lines deleted, uncommitted (`git diff --stat` = 1 insertion, 97 deletions). Every script (verify, typecheck, lint, test, build, arch) and every dependency declaration is gone from the working tree. Any agent that reads dependencies from package.json right now gets `{}`, and `npm run verify` cannot run. Someone did this to execute ESM node scripts and did not restore it. This needs a human decision — I have not touched it (RULE 4).

The design's 'thirteen fields on Comment and ten on Reply in Drive v3' is off by one on both. The discovery document has 14 Comment properties and 11 Reply properties. 13/10 is what you get after excluding `kind`, which is a defensible rule but is not stated.

result.area: Adversarial verification of "Reconstruct and steelman the founder thesis, then find its blind spot" — the corpus-level-unit / mother-markdown headline and the mdmax pack/unpack design

verdicts.claim: C1 [primary-read] The founder's central image is stated in transport verbs (download, split, read, parse); verbatim from the session transcript.
verdicts.reason: Re-extracted independently from /Users/sagnikmitra/.claude/projects/-Users-sagnikmitra-Desktop-GitHub-frontmatter/9e5a4a9f-8c4a-4758-b560-0afea2b30447.jsonl (58,919,587 B). The passage matches verbatim, role=user, type=user: '...whether the user should download one zip file of all the Markdowns or one single mother Markdown, which will be very long. Whenever frontmatter or the AI reads that, I will know these are the breakpoints, which means different files, and it can split that Markdown automatically while parsing into different files'. 3 lines in the file contain 'one single mother Markdown'. The transport-verb reading is faithful to the text; no paraphrase detected. This is the report's strongest claim and it stands on its own.

verdicts.claim: C2 [own-measurement] 403/1084 files (37.2%) and 12,193,061/25,548,765 bytes (47.7%) are ALREADY hand-built multi-document bundles; the founder 'already performs manually' the behaviour he is asking for.
verdicts.reason: The ARITHMETIC reproduces exactly under an independently-written implementation (403/1084 = 37.18%; 12,193,061/25,548,765 = 47.72%; adding setext H1 moves it only to 406/47.89%) [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16..., manifest verified intact: 1084 files, 0 sha mismatches]. The LABEL on the measurement is wrong. 372 of the 403 (92.3%) are files with exactly 2 H1s whose FIRST H1 is the machine-generated YAML `title:` field, and 365 of 403 live in one machine-synced subtree, md/Skills/** (369 files total), whose frontmatter reads `source: claude` / `slug:` / `last_synced: 2026-05-26` — e.g. md/Skills/Printing Press/Pp Espn/skill.md has `title: Pp Espn` then `# Pp Espn` then `# ESPN — Printing Press CLI`. That is one document with a generated title line, not a bundle, and it is not hand-built. Removing the title-prepend pattern leaves 24 files = 2.21% and 500,293 B = 1.96%. Inspecting that residual, most are still single documents with section H1s: frontmatter/docs/engine/README.md (11 H1s = 'Part I'..'Part VII' of the master plan), frontmatter/HANDOFF-graph-engineering-research-2026-07-30.md (8 H1s = 'PART I'..'PART VII'), md/Clients/Technical Proposal v2.md ('Part A — Technical Pitch' / 'Part B — Commercial Pitch'). 12 of 12 random draws from the 403 were the md/Skills title-prepend; the researcher inspected only the two extreme-tail files and generalised to the population.
verdicts.correction: Genuine hand-packed multi-document bundles are ~2% of files and ~2% of bytes in the pinned corpus, not 37.2%/47.7%. This REVERSES pre-registered falsifier (A): the corpus does show the founder working essentially one-document-per-file, so the mother-markdown image is aspirational, not a description of existing practice. The founder-quote basis (C1) is unaffected.

verdicts.claim: C3 [own-measurement] Reference-carried payloads cannot degrade, they vanish: ![[X]] renders as the literal string with the payload absent, while an unknown fence keeps its payload.

C4 [own-measurement] Transclusion is 375:1 rarer than plain linking: 37 embeds in 17 files (1.57%) vs 13,891 wikilinks in 541 files (49.9%); frontmatter has 20 embeds and '19 of those 20 are in docs/mdmap/ concept prose'.
verdicts.reason: Every number is wrong and the per-root attribution is false, yet the conclusion is UNDERSTATED. My independent extraction over corpus_id sha256:3a010b16... gives 45 embed occurrences (not 37) in 17 files (1.57% ✓), and 13,896 wikilinks (not 13,891) in 542 files = 50.00% (not 49.9%), giving a ratio of 308.8:1, not 375:1. Per root I measure md 21 / knowledge 0 / frontmatter 24, against their md 17 / knowledge 0 / frontmatter 20. The docs/mdmap/ attribution is simply false: the 21 docs/mdmap/ files in the corpus contain ZERO occurrences of '![['; the frontmatter embeds are actually in docs/superpowers/, HANDOFF-graph-engineering-research-2026-07-30.md, docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md and docs/engine/research/wf-findings-2026-08-01.md. Part of the inflation is corpus duplication: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-25-sgnk-md-b9-authoring-polish.md is present in BOTH the md and frontmatter roots and its 10 occurrences are counted twice.
verdicts.correction: I enumerated all 45 occurrences individually. Every one is syntax DOCUMENTATION about the wikilink feature — '![[Note]]', '![[target]]', '![[SomeNote]]', '![[...]]', '![[oldBasename]]', '![[embeds]]', '![[target#heading]]' — inside specs and plans. There is not a single real content transclusion pointing at a real document anywhere in the corpus. The correct statement is not '375:1 rarer'; it is that genuine transclusion usage is ZERO. The conclusion the researcher drew is right and stronger than they claimed, while every number offered in support of it fails to reproduce.

verdicts.claim: C5 [own-measurement] A '## File: <path>' breakpoint survives but the path inside it does not, and 'the corruption is non-local: the identical heading is byte-stable in isolation and unstable inside the bundle' — the Wagner & Graham (TOPLAS 1998) context-dependence hazard.
verdicts.reason: The RATE reproduces exactly: on their stated selection (60 files, 2000<bytes<20000, nearest 8 KB, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...) I measure breakpoint headings before=60 after=60 with 13/60 path strings altered, e.g. '## File: md/Skills/Printing Press/Pp Docker Hub/workflow.md' -> '...workflow\\.md'. The NON-LOCALITY claim is false. My isolation control gives 13/60 altered ALONE — the identical 13 headings. Primary-read of /Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/node_modules/mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal/lib/index.js lines 61-63 gives the actual rule verbatim: `character: '.'`, `before: '[Ww]'`, `after: '[\\-.\\w]'` — a ONE-CHARACTER lookbehind guarding against 'www.' autolink formation. So 'workflow.md' escapes (w before the dot) and 'skill.md' in the SAME directory does not; I confirmed 'x/wow.md', 'x/sow.md' and 'x/Now.md' all escape while 'b/skill.md' does not. The confound is identifiable: their minimal control reported '## File: a/workflow.md' -> OK, and that result reproduces ONLY with the GFM extension disabled — with GFM it alters. They ran the bundle experiment with GFM and the control without it, then attributed the difference to preceding documents.
verdicts.correction: The escape is purely local to the filename; nothing about the bundle causes it. The Wagner & Graham context-dependence citation is unsupported by this evidence. The DESIGN conclusion (path belongs in the fence info string, not heading prose) still stands, but on the plain fidelity ground of 13/60 — not on a non-locality result.

verdicts.claim: C6 [own-measurement] Independent replication: 0 files survive a parse->stringify round trip byte-identically, on a different file selection than the plan's '0 of 51 files in this repo'.
verdicts.reason: Replicated on a THIRD, independently-specified selection: a seeded pseudo-random 120 non-empty files drawn across ALL sizes from all three roots of corpus_id sha256:3a010b16... (seed 20260801, mdast-util-from-markdown + mdast-util-to-markdown + GFM). Result: 0/120 byte-identical, 0 errors. D7 (splice-only) is confirmed, and the '0 of 51' figure in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §4.2 is not a repo artefact.

verdicts.claim: C7 [own-measurement] Pack hazards are enumerable and small: 0 '## File: x' collisions; 907 (83.67%) start with ---; 463 (42.71%) contain a ``` fence and the corpus max backtick-run is exactly 3, so a 4-backtick wrapper is provably sufficient; 288 (26.57%) lack a trailing newline; 7 (0.65%) have an odd fence count.
verdicts.reason: Four of six reproduce EXACTLY on corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...: '## File: x' collisions 0 ✓; files starting '---' 907 = 83.67% ✓; no trailing newline 288 = 26.57% ✓; odd number of fence delimiters 7 = 0.65% ✓. Two are defective. (a) 'the corpus max backtick-run is exactly 3, so a 4-backtick wrapper is provably sufficient' is FALSE — the max backtick run is 4, with four occurrences in frontmatter/docs/engine/PLAN.md at lines 652 and 1042 (histogram: run-length 1 x157494, 2 x42, 3 x15506, 4 x4). All four are inline, not at a line start, so a 4-backtick fence is not in fact closed early — but the design's own stated formula, '(max backtick run in any member + 1)', computes 5 for this corpus and therefore contradicts its own conclusion that 4 'is sufficient and provable'. (b) '463 (42.71%) contain a ``` fence' reproduces only under a column-0-only match; 'contains ```' anywhere is 496 = 45.76% and the CommonMark 0-3-space-indent fence count is 489 = 45.11%.
verdicts.correction: State the rule as 'max backtick run AT LINE START + 1' (which is 3+1=4 here) and reconcile it with the design text, or the implementation and the prose disagree. Report the fence-containing rate as 45.76% (or 45.11% CommonMark), not 42.71%.

verdicts.claim: C8 [primary-read] repomix has already shipped the founder's image at scale, with a self-describing '## File Format' preamble and '## File: path/to/file' headers; 27,551 stars.
verdicts.reason: Re-fetched api.github.com/repos/yamadashy/repomix directly: stargazers_count 27551, created_at 2024-07-13T07:11:32Z, pushed_at 2026-08-01T02:11:14Z, description begins '📦 Repomix is a powerful tool that packs your entire repository into a...'. All three figures match to the digit and the 'pushed today' observation holds. The prior-art identification is correct and is the report's second-best contribution.

verdicts.claim: C9 [search-only] 'The unclaimed half is the return trip, and the asymmetry is 27,551 to 0. Everybody packs; essentially nobody unpacks.' — no unpack subcommand, search total_count 0/1/5.
verdicts.reason: A production unpacker exists with MORE stars than repomix. Aider (api.github.com/repos/Aider-AI/aider: 47,848 stars) ships exactly this. Primary-read of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aider-AI/aider/main/aider/coders/wholefile_prompts.py specifies the consumed bundle format verbatim: 'First line: the filename with any originally provided path; no extra markup, punctuation, comments, etc. **JUST** the filename with path. - Second line: opening {fence[0]} - ... entire content of the file ... - Final line: closing {fence[1]}'. And wholefile_coder.py::get_edits() parses that structure back into (fname, fname_source, new_lines) and writes each to disk via self.abs_root_path(fname). It already handles the exact hazards the design enumerates: fname.strip('*'), .rstrip(':'), .strip('`'), .lstrip('#') — i.e. it already tolerates a '## File: path' locator — plus a len(fname) > 250 guard. Worse for the design's claimed novelty, base_coder.py::choose_fence() already computes a collision-proof delimiter by scanning all member content and selecting the first candidate fence whose open/close string starts no line — which is the design's 'delimiter computed per bundle as max+1' rule, shipped. gpt-engineer (AntonOsika/gpt-engineer, 55,173 stars) and smol-ai/developer (12,182) are the same category.
verdicts.correction: The searches failed because they looked for repos NAMED 'unpack' (q=repomix+unpack, q=markdown+unpack+bundle+in:name) rather than for the capability under its industry name — 'edit format', 'file listing', 'whole file coder'. Aider is cited in this program's own settled findings ('Aider: markdown wins 4 of 4 models'), so the prior art was already inside the record. The unpack half of the MVP is not greenfield; it is a re-implementation, and the design's delimiter rule is pre-empted.

verdicts.claim: C10 [own-measurement] A 1,409-term controlled vocabulary exists in the dangling wikilinks, and 'every artifact in the program classifies it as an error to be dropped or reported' — evidenced by graph-data.ts:132 reading `if (targetPath === undefined) continue; // unresolved — drop`.
verdicts.reason: The vocabulary half broadly replicates with ~6% drift under an independently-written extractor over corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...: I measure 10,185 dangling occurrences (vs 10,798) over 6,011 distinct targets (vs 6,175); 1,326 targets in >=2 documents = 22.1% of distinct carrying 5,415 occurrences = 53.2% of dangling (vs 1,409 / 22.8% / 54.0%); 250 in >=3 (vs 325); sanitizer recovery 29 = 0.28% (vs 30 = 0.28% ✓); near-miss within 0.90 difflib 15.11% (vs their 'at most 12.22%'). Top targets agree ('Anthropic' 117 exactly; 'Claude Code' 123 vs their 109). The structural conclusion — a large repeated entity vocabulary that is not typos — survives. The SECOND half is refuted, and by a fabricated quote. graph-data.ts:132 does not contain the quoted line; the real branch is at line 176 and the comment immediately above it reads, verbatim: 'Unresolved links are not edges — there is no node to point at — but they are a diagnostic, so they are reported rather than dropped.' The module defines a typed UnresolvedLink[], a reportUnresolved() function, a reason field discriminating 'target-excluded' from 'no-such-note', a dedicated allBasenameToPath diagnosis map built over EVERY note precisely 'to tell "the note does not exist" apart from "the note exists but opted out"... different problems for the author', and returns { nodes, links, unresolved }. The '— drop' comment they quoted exists at line 188, on the duplicate-link branch.
verdicts.correction: The one artifact cited verbatim does the OPPOSITE of what the claim asserts — it already reports unresolved links as a first-class diagnostic with a typed reason. The 'mdmax vocab' proposal is still worth building, but it is an extension of existing behaviour, not an inversion of a program-wide blind spot. Per the brief's rule 2, the paraphrased-as-verbatim code quote is itself a defect.

survived: C1 — the founder quote is verbatim and correctly read; role=user, re-extracted from the 58.9 MB session jsonl. The transport-verb (download/split/read/parse) framing is faithful.

C3 — payload-vanish vs payload-survive reproduces byte-for-byte under marked 16.4.2, including the '-->' entity escaping. The observation that §4.3's PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT certificate has no cell for 'content was by reference and the reference did not resolve' is fair and useful.
C6 — 0 byte-identical round trips replicated on a THIRD independent selection (seeded random 120 across all sizes, 0 errors). D7 splice-only is confirmed; the plan's '0 of 51' is not a repo artefact.
C8 — repomix prior art confirmed to the digit (27,551 stars, created 2024-07-13, pushed 2026-08-01). The strongest external contribution in the report.

C4's CONCLUSION (though none of its numbers) — the founder does not use the mechanism his image names. In fact stronger than reported: all 45 embed occurrences are syntax documentation, so genuine content transclusion in the corpus is ZERO, not 37.
C7's four reproducing hazards — 0 '## File:' collisions, 907/83.67% YAML, 288/26.57% missing trailing newline, 7/0.65% odd fence count. These are real, small, and correctly characterised.

C5's RATE — 13/60 path strings corrupted in heading prose, before=60/after=60. The design conclusion (path belongs in the fence info string) survives on fidelity grounds; I verified the info string itself preserves all 4 test paths intact.
killed: C2's interpretation and the headline's empirical grounding — 37.2%/47.7% is 92.3% a machine-generated YAML title-prepend in the md/Skills/** sync tree (source: claude, last_synced: 2026-05-26), not hand-built bundles. Honest figure ~2.2% of files / ~2.0% of bytes. This REVERSES pre-registered falsifier (A), which the researcher declared 'FAILED TO REFUTE, and in the founder's favour'.

C5's non-locality mechanism — refuted by primary-read of mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal/lib/index.js:61-63 (before: '[Ww]', a one-character lookbehind) and by an isolation control that alters the same 13/60. Their control reproduces 'OK' only with GFM disabled; they compared two different library configurations and called the difference context-dependence. The Wagner & Graham TOPLAS 1998 citation is unsupported here.

C9's 27,551-to-0 asymmetry — refuted by Aider at 47,848 stars, whose wholefile_prompts.py specifies the exact path-line-plus-fenced-payload bundle format and whose wholefile_coder.py::get_edits() unpacks it to disk, already stripping '*', ':', '`' and leading '#' from the locator. gpt-engineer 55,173 stars is the same category.

The design's delimiter novelty — aider's base_coder.py::choose_fence() already scans all member content and selects a fence that starts no line, i.e. the 'max+1 backticks per bundle' rule, shipped and in production.

C7's 'max backtick-run is exactly 3, so 4 is provably sufficient' — the max run is 4 (frontmatter/docs/engine/PLAN.md lines 652, 1042). Inline rather than line-start, so the wrapper survives, but the design's own stated formula computes 5 and contradicts its own conclusion.

C10's second half — graph-data.ts:132 does not contain the quoted line; line 176's actual comment says unresolved links 'are reported rather than dropped', and the module ships a typed UnresolvedLink[] with a discriminating reason field. The verbatim quote was assembled from a different branch's comment (line 188, duplicate-link).
C4's numbers and attribution — 45 not 37 embeds, 308.8:1 not 375:1, 13,896 not 13,891 links, and zero (not 19 of 20) frontmatter embeds in docs/mdmap/.
new_defects: FENCE-LENGTH DOWNGRADE SHATTERS THE PROPOSED BUNDLE — unreported, and it breaks the design's distribution premise. I round-tripped the design's own carrier through mdast-util-to-markdown: input was a 4-backtick wrapper, output is a 3-BACKTICK wrapper (path attribute preserved intact in all 4 test cases). Since 496 of 1,084 corpus files (45.76%) contain a ``` fence [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...], any member with an internal fence terminates the wrapper early after a single normalising pass through any third-party markdown tool. The design's stated value is that the bundle 'runs inside other people's context windows' and travels through other people's tools, which is exactly where normalisation happens. No mitigation is stated. Aider avoids this by re-deriving the fence at emit time (choose_fence) rather than trusting a delimiter written into a durable artifact.

THE DEGRADATION STORY OVERSTATES READABILITY — the design asserts 'a bundle opened by any markdown tool is a readable document of headings and code blocks'. Rendered through marked 16.4.2, an entire member document — its headings, prose and links — collapses into a single <pre><code class="language-md"> block: '# Real heading\n\nBody text with a [link](x).' emerges as preformatted monospace, not as a heading and a paragraph. The payload survives, but all internal structure is flattened. That is precisely the 'presentation loss' the report's own C3 argues is a distinct and important failure class, applied here to the design's own artifact and not accounted for.

THE PINNED CORPUS DOUBLE-COUNTS ACROSS ROOTS — 28 non-empty cross-root duplicate sha256 groups, 29 redundant copies, 440,139 bytes = 1.72% of the 25,548,765-byte corpus (e.g. md/docs/research/frontmatter-pain-playbook.md == frontmatter/docs/research/frontmatter-pain-playbook.md at 93,259 B; sgnk-react-workflow.md appears three times). Small enough not to invalidate the headline rates, but every percentage in the program inherits it, and this duplication is specifically what inflated C4's embed count (docs/superpowers/** counted twice). Worth stating in the manifest rather than leaving for each reader to rediscover.

FALSIFIER DISCIPLINE — written honestly, tested with instruments too blunt to fire. In the researcher's favour, and this is real and rare: they self-caught the fence-stripping bug in m12.py (shell comments counted as H1s), re-ran, and reported the CORRECTED, LOWER number 37.2%/47.7% against their own interest. But falsifier (A) was operationalised as '>=2 H1 headings', which cannot distinguish a bundle from a document with sections, and was validated by inspecting only the two extreme-tail files rather than the mode — where 12 of 12 random draws are the same machine-generated title line. Falsifier (B)'s isolation control was executed under a different library configuration than the experiment it controlled. Both falsifiers were correctly specified and both fire when tested properly; neither was given an instrument capable of returning 'yes'.

REPORTING PATTERN — the previous run's diagnosed failure mode (every headline refuted by its own verifier, always flatteringly) recurs here in a milder, more specific form. Where a number reproduces exactly it is load-bearing on mechanical facts (C6, C7's four hazards, C8, C5's rate). Where a number carries an interpretive label — 'hand-built bundles', 'non-local', 'nobody unpacks', 'classified as an error to be dropped' — the label runs ahead of the measurement in the direction the headline needs, four times out of four.

result.area: The agent-native document — what changes when the primary author is a machine
result.headline: The agent-native document has already been specified and shipped by Google (OKF v0.2, `GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/okf/SPEC.md`, 37,544 bytes, 8,134 stars, pushed 2026-07-29) with exactly the feature set this area was asked to invent — provenance, trust tiers, staleness, attested computations — and the only live-model benchmark anyone has run on it found the bundle cost 5.2% MORE tokens and won 22/26 vs 20/26 at n=1 per cell; meanwhile agents on this machine open markdown as a ≤150-line window 59.1% of first touches and byte-weighted only 3.5% of markdown opens are whole reads of files >20 KB, so MDMAX's defensible agent-facing slot is NOT helping an agent read (that market is served) but proving an agent's WRITE broke nothing — a differential reference invariant that costs 0.015 s over 15,785 references and that OKF §11 explicitly declines to check ("consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle because of: ... Broken cross-links").
result.falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE CONCLUDING: my headline claims agents already self-project, so a document-side index/budget tier has no measurable client. It is wrong if either (a) markdown Reads are predominantly whole-file, or (b) the sliced reads are mostly a SECOND read of a file the agent already paid to read whole — in which case the first read still costs full price and an index tier does help. I looked for both. RESULT: THE FALSIFIER PARTIALLY FIRED AND I AM REPORTING IT AGAINST MYSELF. (a) survives: over the 1,200 most-recent transcripts, 82.5% of all markdown Read calls carry an explicit offset/limit. But (b) FIRES: restricted to the FIRST touch of each (session, markdown file) pair, only 59.1% (214/362) are windowed and 40.9% (148/362) are whole-file reads — the 82.5% figure was inflated by the walking pattern (492 of 502 repeat reads follow a sliced first read). So agents do NOT purely self-project. I then byte-weighted it, which is the test that actually settles the size of the prize: of 134 whole first-touch markdown reads whose file is still on disk (2,063,984 B), the median file is 5,260 B and 12 reads of files >20 KB — 9.0% of whole reads, 3.5% of all 343 first-touch opens — carry 63.9% of the whole-read bytes. HONEST VERDICT: the projection tier is not dead, it is small and concentrated. It is a win on roughly 1 markdown open in 29, and MDMAX §4.4's headline "Fewer tokens — 25–168×" is a ratio between artifact SIZES, not a task token saving; the one measurement of the latter that exists (OKF's) is +5.2%, i.e. a loss. I would have written a flattering version of this headline had I not run the first-touch split.

findings.claim: OKF v0.2 already specifies the entire agent-native document feature set this area was briefed to design — declared provenance, trust tiers, structured staleness, and verification receipts — in a live, versioned, conformance-tested Apache-2.0 spec that this program has now decided against three times without reading.
findings.evidence: Canonical: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/main/okf/SPEC.md — 37,544 bytes (exactly the figure docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §11 S1 quotes without having read it). Repo api.github.com/repos/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog: {'stargazers_count': 8134, 'created_at': '2026-05-04T16:36:24Z', 'pushed_at': '2026-07-29T07:04:35Z', 'license': 'Apache-2.0'}. §5.1 `sources` (resource/id/title/author/usage_count/last_modified/usage_window); §5.2 `generated: {by, at}` and `verified: [{by, at}]`; §5.3 trust tiers unverified/machine-confirmed/human-reviewed; §5.4 `status`; §5.5 `stale_after`; §10 Attested Computations, verbatim: "Provenance (§5.1) answers \"where did this claim come from\"; attestation answers \"was this number produced the way we said it must be.\" OKF records the computation and the means to check it; it does not execute anything itself." findings.claim: OKF's per-claim attribution mechanism answers MDMAX kill-gate K4 in the affirmative — it uses a DECLARED stable id rather than a derived anchor, and its published rationale is verbatim MDMAX's own agents-rewrite-documents argument.

findings.claim: The only live-model experiment that exists on agent-native documents found the knowledge bundle made the agent SPEND MORE, not less — refuting the token-saving pitch at the only place it has ever been tested.
findings.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scaccogatto/okf-skills/main/benchmark/results.md, verbatim: "**The bundle arm cost more, not less.** 5.2% more tokens over six questions, and it opened more files, not fewer." findings.claim: Markdown is what agents READ, not just what they emit — and they read it in windows. Markdown is 53.9% of all Read calls, and 59.1% of first touches are already a ≤150-line slice.

Of 1,603 Read calls, 864 (53.9%) target .md/.markdown/.mdx. First-touch per (session, md file), n=362: whole 148 (40.9%), windowed 214 (59.1%); explicit `limit` values on windowed first reads median=92, p90=150, max=545. Repeat reads 502, of which 492 follow a windowed first read. Inside Bash: head 1,532, grep 1,399, tail 928, sed 577, find 519, cat 416, wc 331, awk 76, rg 29 — the agent's real read protocol is line-window slicing plus shell text tools.

findings.claim: Concurrent multi-agent writing to one document did not happen once. Not rarely — zero times across 1,200 sessions and 724 written files.

findings.claim: The shipped multi-agent write contract is filesystem isolation plus a read-before-write token plus base-version 409 — three mechanisms that already exist, none of them in the document.
findings.evidence: Live tool contracts I am operating under, verbatim. Edit: "You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail." Write: "Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail." Artifact: "On a 409 conflict the normal fix is to re-read the artifact, merge your edits on top of the newer content, and publish again — not force. ... The tracked baseVersion is still sent; with force:true the server treats it as informational and overwrites." Isolation, measured locally: `git worktree list` in /Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter returns three trees; 128 of 193 `*.test.ts` files (66.3%) live under .claude/worktrees/ — an independent re-derivation of the 66.4% in PLAN.md §11 S0, and a demonstration that the industry's answer to two agents editing one thing is give each one a whole copy.

findings.claim: Three writers already share one AGENTS.md in this very repo, using two independently invented sentinel conventions and inconsistent placement. This is the multi-agent document-writing contract as actually deployed, and it is nobody's design.
findings.evidence: /Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/AGENTS.md, 7,667 bytes: human prose from byte 0, `<claude-mem-context>` opening at byte 7,255, then a tail block delimited `<!-- SGNK:BEGIN -->` / `<!-- SGNK:END -->`. findings.claim: Both machine-owned regions fail invisibility in opposite directions, and a sanitized-HTML round trip DESTROYS the region delimiters while keeping the payload — after which the writing agent can no longer find its own region.
findings.evidence: Ran the repo's own remark 11 / rehype pipeline (remark-parse@^11, remark-gfm@^4.0.1, remark-rehype@^11.1.2, rehype-raw@^7, rehype-stringify@^10.0.1) over frontmatter/AGENTS.md. Raw-HTML-allowed config (rehype-raw): both tags survive=true, both texts leak=true. So in the sanitized case the sentinels vanish and the content stays — the exact failure the HTML-comment carrier was chosen to avoid, reproduced on a live production file rather than a fixture.

findings.claim: Progressive disclosure is the shipped read protocol for agent-facing documents, it is implemented entirely in prose, and it is declared by no field — which is precisely the slot a compiler could occupy without inventing syntax.

Always-loaded `description` bytes 78,685 (mean 661); on-demand body bytes 3,166,751 (mean 26,611); ratio 40.2x — an independent re-derivation of the 40.3x in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §2 by a different extraction boundary. 95 of 119 (79.8%) reference a sibling references/, scripts/ or assets/ path to be read on demand. Frontmatter key census across all 119: name 119, description 119, allowed-tools 41, version 36, triggers 36, preamble-tier 28, metadata 10, disable-model-invocation 9, license 7, capabilities 7. The read protocol is a sentence in a body; nothing declares it.

findings.claim: The pinned corpus is content-verified but the corpus_id itself is not reproducible — P1's guard does not satisfy P2's rule, and I am flagging it because every number in this report cites it.
findings.evidence: I recomputed sha256 for all 1,084 files listed in docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json: 0 missing on disk, 0 sha mismatches — the corpus CONTENT is verified byte-for-byte. But `grep -rl "corpus_id" --include="*.mjs" --include="*.py" --include="*.sh" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js"` over the repo returns nothing, and the manifest states no serialization; my reconstruction over the sorted (path, sha256) list yields sha256:b3d847c4e9dbaf5cf17be7fca6ef9ce9518dbae87a368433bbbe2d2f1de53a8a, not sha256:3a010b16… . PLAN.md §14 P2 requires "No headline without a committed derivation script and its captured output"; the id that every headline is required by P1 to cite has no derivation script. Fix is one file and it belongs in S0.

negatives: NEGATIVE 1 — Per-span structured uncertainty / confidence annotation would be built for a user who does not exist. Authoring base, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…: 16 of 1,084 files (1.48%) carry ANY evidence-tier tag, 51 tags total across 25,548,765 bytes — and that is a corpus authored by a team whose own plan mandates tier tagging on every number. 0 files carry a block-level id to attach a confidence to. And the one shipped spec in this space considered per-source scoring and explicitly refused it, verbatim OKF SPEC.md §5.1: "It does not store a credibility score: a score is subjective, unportable across consumers, and goes stale. Credibility is *inferred* from the signals ... not stored." OKF's entire uncertainty model is three coarse derived tiers (unverified / machine-confirmed / human-reviewed) computed from who signed, not a number in the document. Build the coarse version or none.

NEGATIVE 2 — A multi-agent concurrency contract for simultaneous document editing would be built for a user who does not exist. Observed frequency across 1,200 transcripts and 724 written files: 29 files (4.0%) touched by more than one session EVER, and 0 files (0.0%) written by two different sessions within 60 minutes; markdown 143 written, 5 by >1 session, 0 concurrent. The industry has already answered by ISOLATION, not concurrency control: `git worktree list` on this repo shows two agent worktrees holding 128 of 193 test files (66.3%), so parallel agents write to disjoint paths by construction and can never collide. Adding block-level identity to enable simultaneous agent edits solves a problem the harness has already made unreachable — and the visible cost of the existing solution is two abandoned copies silently doubling the test suite, which is a repo-hygiene problem, not a document-format problem.

NEGATIVE 3 — "What changed since you last read this" has no protocol slot and two independent shipped designs deliberately rejected its premise. MCP's `ResourceUpdatedNotificationParams` carries exactly one field, `uri`, with the comment that the resource "has changed and may need to be read again" — invalidation with no delta, no version, no digest, in all six schema versions through 2026-07-28. OKF chose an ABSOLUTE date and said why, verbatim §5.5: "An absolute date, not a relative TTL, keeps the staleness decision a plain date comparison with no reference to when the concept was read." Both designs refuse per-reader state on purpose, because a document that tracks who read what needs identity, storage and a session — none of which a .md file has. MCP's newest freshness primitive, `CacheableResult{ttlMs, cacheScope}` shipped 2026-07-28, is a TTL. The ecosystem's cost model is time-based, not content-identity-based, and MDMAX's staleness story is pushing against that current.

NEGATIVE 4 — The budgeted-projection tier is the weakest of the four things MDMAX promises an AI consumer, and the promise as written is a category error. §4.4's "25.5x / 61–152x / 168.8x" are ratios between ARTIFACT SIZES; the number that decides adoption is tokens billed for a task, and the only measurement of that in existence is OKF's +5.2% (257,602 vs 244,805) with MORE files opened, not fewer. My own byte-weighting says why: of 343 first-touch markdown opens, only 12 (3.5%) were whole reads of files >20 KB, the median whole-read markdown file is 5,260 bytes, and Claude Code's Read tool already caps at 2,000 lines — which only 23 of 1,084 corpus files (2.12%) exceed. The index tier competes against a client-side windowing mechanism the agent already has for free, on 1 open in 29.

NEGATIVE 5 — Against my own area's framing: the six candidate agent needs in the brief are not equally real, and four of them are already served outside the document. Stable references: served by the filesystem path, and sub-document addressing is used at 0.29%. Budget metadata: served by offset/limit and by `size` in MCP's Resource. Explicit read protocol: served by SKILL.md prose in 79.8% of skills and by AGENTS.md, neither of which declares it as a field and neither of which is failing. What-changed: rejected by two protocols on purpose (Negative 3). Only declared provenance and verification receipts are genuinely unserved — and OKF §5.1 and §10 have now specified both, leaving MDMAX the narrower job of CHECKING them rather than defining them.
unclaimed: A DIFFERENTIAL reference proof: `mdmax verify --base <sha>` asserting that no reference which resolved before an edit fails to resolve, or resolves to a different target, after it. Search that produced the belief: OKF v0.2 §11 Conformance explicitly declines it, verbatim — "consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle because of: ... Broken cross-links." I enumerated the 15 highest-starred OKF ecosystem repos via api.github.com/search/repositories?q=%22open+knowledge+format%22+in:name,description (906 stars combined: okf-skills 206, okf-gem 115, cole-medin-ai-coding 111, OWOX/models 85, OKFy 62, cole-medin-knowledge-base 59, okf-knowledge 55, okf-frontmatter 42, openknowledge 33, xSAVIKx/okf-skills 29, agent-knowledge 26, okf-crossplane-v2 24, kiso 21, okf-studio 20, superops-team/okf 18); every one advertises author / maintain / validate / lint / search / visualize and none advertises a before-vs-after invariant. MCP has no such notion in any of six schema versions. Cost measured: 15,785 references resolved in 0.015 s, so the differential is two passes at 0.03 s — free at the scale of any real edit.

A slugger-scoped anchor certificate: `(product, surface)` columns that report which heading anchors resolve under GitHub's slugger versus a collapse-runs slugger. Search: babelmark3 differs SPEC EXAMPLES through parsers, not a user's document's anchors through sluggers; github-slugger and its ports are published as libraries with no comparison harness; no tool I could find reports per-document anchor resolution per consumer. Measured value: 375 vs 86 resolutions on identical bytes from one corpus, a 4.4x swing that nobody has ever reported. This is the strongest column `mdmax cert` could ship and it is currently not in the column list.

A provenance-referent resolution check: given OKF `sources[].resource` or any `original:`-style pointer, assert the referent exists AND is reachable by someone who clones the repo. Search: OKF §5.1 defines `resource` as "a concrete artifact a consumer can follow (an absolute URL, a bundle-relative path, or a path into a `references/` subdirectory)" but §11 requires nothing of it, and §12's "Considered and deferred" list does not mention checking it. Locally the failure is already 74.8% dangling and 0 of 365 referents git-tracked. A declared-provenance field nobody checks decays to a lie, which is the same mechanism as the accessibility finding in PLAN.md §6.

A machine-region round-trip safety check: assert that a sentinel-delimited region written by one agent still delimits after the document has passed through the consumers it will actually pass through. Nobody ships this because nobody models sentinel survival. Demonstrated failure on a live production file: frontmatter/AGENTS.md's `<!-- SGNK:BEGIN -->` / `<!-- SGNK:END -->` pair is destroyed by a sanitized-HTML round trip while the payload between them survives, so the next write by that agent cannot find its own region. This is P5 ("Every byte written into a user's file passes a placement fixture first") extended from placement to survival.
result.design:
"WHAT SHIPS: a third MVP artifact, `mdmax verify`, and two columns added to `mdmax cert`. Nothing in this area justifies a new document capability; everything justifies a checker for capabilities other people have already declared.

1) `mdmax verify --base <git-sha> [--paths <glob>]` — the differential reference invariant. Extract every reference from the base tree and the working tree (wikilink, relative path, same-doc #anchor, footnote label, OKF `sources[].resource`, and any `path:`-valued frontmatter field). Resolve both. FAIL only on a reference that RESOLVED at base and now does not, or now resolves to a different file. Never fail on a reference that was already unresolved — 75.08% of this corpus's internal references are unresolved by design and an absolute checker is switched off within a day. Output: a receipt naming the base sha, the reference count, the delta, and per-broken-reference the file, line and the rename that most likely caused it (highest-similarity new path). This is the honest form of "an agent edits 500 files and the compiler proves zero references broke": the proof is DIFFERENTIAL, not absolute.

2) CARRIER: the receipt is a JSON sidecar and a non-zero exit code. Nothing is written into any .md. This is forced by D2 and D4 and is also what the AGENTS.md measurement demands — two agents already invented two sentinel conventions in one file and one of them does not survive a render.

3) `mdmax cert` gains two columns, both cheap and both currently unmeasured anywhere: (a) HEADING-SLUG RESOLUTION per slugger — github-slugger vs collapse-runs — reporting per document how many of its own anchors resolve under each, because 375 vs 86 on one corpus is a bigger real-world defect than anything currently in the matrix; (b) SENTINEL SURVIVAL — given a delimiter pair, does it still delimit after the sanitized-HTML and raw-HTML pipelines, so an agent writing a machine-owned region is told before it commits that its region will not be findable.

4) `mdmax cert --provenance` — for any document declaring OKF `sources[]` or an `original:`-style pointer, assert the referent resolves AND is git-tracked. Two lines of code, and it fires on 273 of 365 files in our own corpus today. This is how MDMAX becomes useful to the OKF ecosystem instead of competing with it: OKF §11 forbids CONSUMERS from rejecting a bundle for broken links; it says nothing about a PRODUCER-side linter, which is an empty slot in a 906-star ecosystem.

5) DEGRADATION BEHAVIOUR: every artifact above is a CLI exit code and a sidecar. If MDMAX is absent, the .md files are unchanged and every consumer behaves identically. There is no in-file footprint to degrade.

6) AGENT-HARNESS SURFACE — the answer is a SKILL, not a protocol. OKF's distribution is `/plugin install okf@scaccogatto` and `npx skills add scaccogatto/okf-skills`, 206 stars on the toolkit versus a spec with no runtime; 79.8% of local skills already use progressive disclosure, and the SKILL.md description is the only always-loaded surface at 661 bytes mean. So MDMAX ships as (i) a CLI, (ii) a `SKILL.md` whose description names the two commands and their exit codes, (iii) `allowed-tools: Bash` — matching the 41/119 that already declare it. Do NOT build an MCP server first: MCP resources carry no provenance in any of six schema versions and its update notification carries only a URI, so there is nothing there to integrate WITH yet.

7) WHAT WE DO NOT BUILD, on this evidence: no in-document uncertainty annotation, no per-reader delta, no concurrency protocol, no agent-only section, and no positioning of the index tier as a token-saving promise to an AI consumer. Position the projection tier where it is defensible — a human/API summary and a large-file case worth roughly 1 markdown open in 29 — and stop promising cost."
result.measurement:
"THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT — one live-model run, pre-registered, modelled on OKF's benchmark but fixing its two stated weaknesses (n=1 per cell, and the grader wrote the questions).

CORPUS: the pinned corpus, corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 (verified: all 1,084 files present, all 1,084 sha256 match) PLUS the second corpus PLAN.md §11 W1 already names, ~/.claude/skills-src (119 SKILL.md, 78,685 B of always-loaded descriptions against 3,166,751 B of bodies) — because everything measured so far comes from one operator and the OKF benchmark's own limit note is "The repo documents itself in OKF, so its bundle is unusually good."

ARM STRUCTURE, three arms not two, because OKF's two-arm design cannot separate the two hypotheses: (A) raw files, agent free to Read/Grep; (B) raw files plus an MDMAX index tier available; (C) raw files plus a differential-verify tool available after edits. n=8 fresh agents per question per arm, not 1 — OKF's own results.md says "Treat single-question differences as anecdote", and with n=1 their Q6 swung 28% on identical file access.

TASKS, 24 total, three shapes and the shapes matter because OKF found the effect concentrated in exactly one: 8 LOOKUP (a fact stated once), 8 WHY (a rationale that exists in exactly one file — the shape where OKF's bundle won both its wins), 8 MULTI-FILE EDIT (rename a hub, retarget references; use the measured hubs — the top-1% targets receiving 7.0% of references, and the 82-inbound-reference file).

VERIFIERS, cheapest-applicable first per LR#25: EDIT tasks are graded MECHANICALLY by the differential reference invariant plus byte-fidelity on untouched regions against an INDEPENDENT oracle (not the writer's own code path — PLAN.md §11 S4's gate). LOOKUP and WHY are graded by claim-presence against a pre-committed claim list written BEFORE any arm runs and by a person who has not seen the index tier, with the answers committed verbatim and an id→arm key published so anyone can regrade — OKF did this and it is the reason their result is credible.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, written now so they can embarrass us: (P1) arm B shows NO token saving over arm A on the aggregate — I predict between −3% and +8%, centred on OKF's +5.2%, because 96.5% of first-touch markdown opens are already windowed or small. (P2) arm B's saving, if any, is concentrated entirely in tasks whose target file exceeds 20 KB — I predict >80% of any observed saving lands in that stratum, which is 3.5% of opens. (P3) arm B beats arm A on WHY tasks and ties or loses on LOOKUP — the OKF pattern replicates. (P4) arm C catches >=1 real broken reference per multi-file edit task that arm A ships silently, and its false-positive rate on deliberate placeholders is <5% because the differential never fires on the 75.08% already-unresolved baseline. P4 is the one that matters; P1–P3 exist to stop us re-publishing the token claim.

STRATIFICATION AND REPORTING: report by task shape and by target-file size bucket, never pooled only. Report the token cost of arm B and C including the tool's own output, which OKF's design correctly charges to the bundle arm. Publish whatever comes out, including if arm B loses, per §11 S4."
result.kill_condition:
"KILL 1 (kills this area's headline deliverable): if `mdmax verify`'s differential invariant, run over the 294 real revision pairs already in hand, fires on fewer than 1 genuine broken reference per 100 changed files, OR its false-positive rate on deliberate placeholders exceeds 5%, then the verification loop is not a product — it is a lint rule, and it should be a 40-line script in the repo rather than an MVP artifact.

KILL 2 (kills the agent-facing framing of §4.4): if the live experiment's arm B shows no aggregate token saving (my prediction P1), then delete every sentence promising an AI consumer 'fewer tokens' and re-position the projection tier as a human/API summary. Do not re-run with a different corpus until that sentence is deleted — the previous run's 100% one-directional defect rate came from exactly this move.

KILL 3 (kills MDMAX's independence): if a reader of OKF v0.2 §5 and §10 concludes MDMAX's §4.5 declared provenance adds nothing OKF has not specified, then stop specifying and start checking. MDMAX becomes an OKF linter and certificate generator, which is a smaller and much more defensible product, and D9 ('a document NAMES a capability, never CARRIES one') is satisfied by naming OKF.

KILL 4 (kills three of the six briefed agent needs): the evidence already fires on this one and I am recording it as fired, not as a risk — 0 concurrent cross-session writes in 1,200 sessions, 0.29% sub-document addressing, and two protocols deliberately rejecting per-reader state. Any roadmap slot for multi-agent concurrency control, authored sub-document anchors, or diff-since-last-read must first produce a user who asked. None exists in any local evidence.

KILL 5 (kills the whole area): if the corpus_id cannot be given a committed derivation script in S0, then no number in this report — including mine — is reportable under P1/P2, and the area's findings must be re-run against a corpus that can be reproduced by a third party."
result.effort: high — 3 primary specs read end to end (OKF v0.2 SPEC.md 37,544 B canonical + its benchmark README and results.md; MCP schema.ts at all six versions, 31 KB to 98 KB; the AGENTS.md spec README), 6 GitHub/raw API fetch rounds via curl (no WebFetch used), and 14 independent local measurements: corpus sha256 re-verification of all 1,084 files, reference extraction and resolution (15,785 refs), heading/block anchor integrity, two-slugger comparison, frontmatter key census, provenance fill-and-resolve rates split by root, AGENTS.md structure census, a live remark/rehype carrier-survival run using the repo's own pinned dependencies, SKILL.md budget re-derivation, and four separate passes over the 1,200 most-recent Claude Code transcripts (final-answer provenance with a sensitivity check, tool-shape, first-touch read shape with byte weighting, cross-session write collisions). One self-caught false positive corrected mid-run (the 'elicitation' matching 'citation' in the MCP scan) and one pre-registered falsifier that partially fired and is reported against the headline.
result.unverified:
"WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND ITS REAL TIER.

1. GitHub code-search total_count 179,552 for filename:AGENTS.md — SEARCH-ONLY. GitHub's code-search totals are approximate, capped, and index-dependent; treat as an order of magnitude, never as a count.

2. OKF's benchmark numbers (+5.2% tokens, 22/26 vs 20/26) — PRIMARY-READ of somebody else's measurement, not my own. I read their method, their stated limits and their published answers directory, but I did NOT re-run it, did not regrade the committed answers, and did not verify commit e91720e reproduces. Their n=1 per cell means the correctness delta is not a result; the token delta is a plausible null. Do not quote 85% vs 77% as a headline — they explicitly ask you not to.

3. Every transcript measurement (read shape, write collisions, final-answer provenance, first-touch split, byte weighting) is ONE OPERATOR'S MACHINE, selection stated as the 1,200 most-recently-modified .jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/*/ sized 20 KB–8 MB. It does NOT cite corpus_id because it is not the pinned corpus. It is biased toward this operator's habits: Bash is 49.6% of tool calls and the Grep/Glob tools registered 0 uses because he greps through Bash, so any cross-harness generalisation is INFERENCE. The zero-concurrent-writes result in particular is a property of single-operator, mostly-sequential usage plus worktree isolation; it is not evidence that concurrency never occurs in a multi-user product, which is what frontmatter will be.

4. The 60.0% / 47.3–78.3% copy-drops-context figures use exact substring containment, which over-counts 'not visible' whenever the model reformats a number (1,084 vs 1084) or shortens a path. The sensitivity run bounds the path direction; the number direction has no equivalent relaxation and is therefore an UPPER bound on 'only in tool context'. The 25.4% 'appears nowhere' bucket mixes model-computed arithmetic with genuine unsourced assertion and I did not separate them.

5. The two-slugger comparison uses MY implementations of github-slugger and a collapse-runs slugger, not the published packages — OWN-MEASUREMENT with a hand-rolled oracle. The direction (a large swing, and a corpus containing anchors authored against both) is robust; the exact 375/86 split must be re-run against the real `github-slugger` and `python-markdown-slugify` before it is published.

6. The carrier-survival result is measured against remark/rehype 11.x as pinned in this repo, which is a PROXY for GitHub, Obsidian and VS Code, not those renderers themselves. PLAN.md §4.3's own finding is that GitHub is three renderers that disagree; my two configs are two points, not a matrix.

7. corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… — I verified the CONTENT (1,084/1,084 files present, 1,084/1,084 sha256 matching) but could NOT reproduce the id string; no derivation script exists in the repo. Every corpus number I report is therefore verified against the manifest's file list and hashes, and the id is cited as a label rather than as something I recomputed.

8. I did not locate a canonical Google-owned repo named for OKF; the spec lives inside GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog (8,134 stars) at okf/SPEC.md. Whether that repo is the normative home or a reference implementation is UNVERIFIED — I read the file, not the governance.

9. Zero live model calls were made in this area. Every claim about what helps or hurts an agent's comprehension remains a PREDICTION, including my own P1–P4."

result.area: Pre-mortem — it is 2027 and MDMAX/frontmatter failed. What happened?
result.headline: The most probable 2027 post-mortem is not "we were wrong" but "nothing could tell us we were wrong": `origin/main` has not moved since 2026-07-25 and all 16 engine commits plus 4,965,476 bytes of untracked evidence — including `docs/mdmax/PLAN.md` v1.0.0 and the pinned `corpus-manifest.json` itself — exist only on one never-pushed local branch; the shipped auth is a single-string equality against one hardcoded login with one server-side GitHub token, so kill-gate K6 is already the base case; and the S4 gate that re-derives the flagship 99.627% is structurally incapable of catching its most likely error, because I measured the corpus it re-derives on and 86.6% of `.md` file-revisions in its largest root delete zero lines.
result.falsifier:
PRE-REGISTERED, three ways the headline could be wrong, all looked for.

(1) "Multi-tenant code exists somewhere, so the editor-floor claim is false." I enumerated every ref: `git for-each-ref` returns 6 refs; `main`, `origin/main`, `sagnik-old/main` and both `claude/*` worktree branches are ALL at `8eb4de2` (2026-07-25); `git stash list` is empty; `grep -rl 'vaultId|tenantId|orgId|workspaceId' .claude/worktrees` hits only `firestore.rules` and a docs file, no source. NOT FOUND — headline stands.

(2) "The 294 revision pairs were filtered to modified files, so the append-bias does not apply." I read the primary text: `docs/engine/PLAN.md:80` says verbatim "Measured over **41,642 block-versions** from 294 consecutive real revision pairs across `md`, `knowledge` and this repo." No modification filter is stated. The same program says it explicitly when it means it — `collab-primitives` writes "400 randomly sampled **modified**-.md revision pairs" — so the omission is informative, not stylistic. All three mentions of `41,642` in the 18-area artifact are tagged "[own-measurement, PLAN §1.1a, **not re-run by me**]". NOT FOUND — headline stands, with the caveat below.

(3) "The plan and corpus are tracked and I misread git." `git status --porcelain -uall docs/` returns `?? docs/mdmax/PLAN.md` and `?? docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json`; `git check-ignore -v` on both returns nothing (not ignored, simply never added); `git ls-files docs` returns 53 files, none of them under `docs/engine/research/`. NOT FOUND — headline stands.

ONE PARTIAL COUNTER I FOUND AND AM REPORTING: the append-dominance is not uniform across roots. `knowledge` is 76.8% zero-deletion vs `md`'s 86.6%, and `knowledge` is also the root §1.1a says already scores 8× worse (0.280% false). SECOND PARTIAL COUNTER: my edit-shape numbers are over `.md` FILE-revision pairs, not over the block-versions §1.1a actually scored, and I could not find the selection script (none exists in the repo).
