result.design:
EIGHT-PLUS FAILURE NARRATIVES, EACH WITH MECHANISM / EARLIEST WARNING SIGN ALREADY VISIBLE TODAY / COUNTERMEASURE. Ranked at the end by probability × severity.

N1 — THE RESEARCH NEVER BECAME CODE (required #1).
Mechanism: the reward function pays for sentences. Every research pass produces a document that is immediately more valuable than the last, so the marginal hour always goes to prose. The engine never gets a first line because there is always one more reconciliation to do first.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: 12 of 20 commits are `docs`; `src/` has received 532 insertions in the 19 days since the clone (`8eb4de2` 364, `58322f7` 124, `6ef83a9` 44); `grep -rl -i mdmax src test scripts` returns 0 files; three of the last four commits are page-break fixes to a PDF. The plan itself names this in §9.8 — which is the point: naming it did not stop it, because §9.8 is itself another sentence.
Countermeasure: the standing rule in §11 is correct but points at the wrong target. Change 'one committed assertion … red to green against engine code' to a specific named test file with a specific named assertion, committed RED today, before S0. A rule that names an artifact cannot be satisfied by prose.

N2 — THE EDITOR FLOOR NEVER SHIPPED, SO NO COLLABORATION FEATURE WAS REACHABLE (required #2).
Mechanism: S5 is scheduled 'parallel, no engine dependency' and described in the plan's own words as work that 'will keep losing priority to compiler work precisely because it is uninteresting'. It is owned by the only person who can also do the interesting work. It never starts.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: it is worse than 'not started' — the inherited base is architecturally single-tenant and must be replaced, not extended. `isAllowed()` is `login === allowed` against a default of `'sagnikmitra'`; every read and write uses one `GITHUB_REPO_TOKEN` against `GITHUB_REPO` default `'sagnikmitra/md'`; the git commit author is a hardcoded constant `{ name: "Sagnik Mitra", email: "sagnikmitra123@gmail.com" }` in `dependency-container.ts` feeding four use-cases. `firestore.rules` declares the whole multi-tenant model (`vaults/{vaultId}/notes/{noteId}/revisions/{revId}`, `billing/{uid}`, `usage/{uid}/months/{month}`) and exactly one source file touches Firestore, only to construct the singleton. `src/app/(workspace)/` contains a `.gitkeep`. K6 is not a risk; it is the current state.
Countermeasure: promote S5 to S1 and give it the standing rule. The first red-to-green assertion in this repository should be: a second GitHub login, who is not `sagnikmitra`, opens a document they do not own and writes to it under their own attribution. That single test invalidates the allowlist, the token model and the AUTHOR constant simultaneously, and it is the only assertion whose passing makes any part of the Google-Docs story reachable.

N3 — THE ANCHOR DID NOT HOLD WHEN RE-DERIVED, OR DID NOT TRANSFER TO RANGES (required #3).
Mechanism: not that the number falls — that it does NOT fall, and everyone is reassured by a number measured on a distribution that does not resemble the product. S4's gate is 're-derive on `corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…`'. Re-deriving a statistic on the corpus that produced it reproduces the corpus's bias with perfect fidelity.
Earliest warning sign, visible today, and this is the one nobody has looked at: I measured the edit shape of the pinned corpus's own git history. In the `md` root (82.5% of corpus bytes) 4,948 of 5,715 `.md` file-revision pairs (86.6%) delete zero lines. Restricted to the 642 multi-revision files, 676 of 1,399 pairs (48.3%) still delete zero lines and only 31 (2.2%) delete more than two. §1.1a reports S1 exact-hash 'resolves 87.0%'. Those two numbers agree to 0.4 percentage points because a zero-deletion revision leaves every prior block byte-identical, so S1 resolves it by construction. Second warning sign, already inside the program's own artifact: the `cache-layout` verifier wrote 'That is a document being written, not edited; estimating churn from construction is not estimating churn on a document being served' — about `PLAN.md`, and nobody carried it across. Third: §1.1a already reports 2.66% false on the multi-candidate stratum, 5.3× kill-gate K3's 0.5% threshold, and the headline averages it away.
Countermeasure: make W1 a GATE, not a side-track, and specify it by EDIT SHAPE rather than by authorship. Before S4 publishes anything, the benchmark must report correct/false/refusal on a stratum restricted to revision pairs that DELETE MORE THAN TWO LINES — the only stratum where re-anchoring is exercised — and must report that stratum's size. On the current corpus that stratum is 54 pairs in `md`; if that is too small to be significant, that fact is the finding, and it is worth more than any re-derivation.

N4 — USERS REJECTED THE REFUSAL MODEL; ORPHANED COMMENTS FELT LIKE A BUG (required #4).
Mechanism: 'refusing is cheap' is true for the engine and false for the user. An orphaned thread is indistinguishable from data loss in a product whose #1 competitive pain theme is that sync silently destroys things. Users file it as a bug, support explains it is by design, and the explanation is worse than the bug.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: the `collab-primitives` area already wrote the threshold and the failure mode — 'If, in the pilot, orphaned threads exceed ~10% of all threads per week of normal editing, the honest-refusal design is correct and unshippable at the same time — users will read every orphan as a bug.' And the demand evidence points the same way: every markdown comment plugin in the largest markdown ecosystem combined has 24,569 installs against Dataview's 4,659,822 — a 190× gap. Meanwhile D3 (reviewers must log in) removes the exact property that area names as the competitive wedge ('anonymous no-account share links').
Countermeasure: ship the orphan rate as a visible product metric from the first comment written, and instrument the refusal path before the resolve path. Also, reopen D3 as a Pro/Free split rather than a global: anonymous read-and-comment on a share link, login required to resolve or edit. That preserves the wedge and the account model at once.

N5 — A BIG COMPANY SHIPPED IT; OKF ALREADY EXISTS (required #5).
Mechanism: not that Google out-features MDMAX. That Google's format becomes the thing agents already speak, and MDMAX's distinctive decisions arrive as second implementations of a published spec.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: I read `SPEC.md` v0.2 (37,544 bytes, sha256 `5a3311d2…`), which nobody in this program has. D9 — 'a document NAMES a capability, never CARRIES one' — is already OKF §10.2, in one sentence: 'What sits behind a `resource` (a Skill, a script, a container) is a packaging choice; OKF fixes the interface, not the packaging.' MDMAX's anchoring rationale is already OKF §5.1: 'a positional index misattributes silently the moment the list is reordered, whereas a stable `id` survives reordering.' §12 confirms the runtime is coming: the deferred list is 'The full runtime protocol: receipt and verdict wire formats, and the attestation lifecycle around a run. The attester ABI, portability, and sandboxing.' And the ecosystem formed while this program wrote: `GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog` 8,134★ pushed 2026-07-29, `scaccogatto/okf-skills` 206★ with a 25,314-byte validator and a 25,399-byte visualizer, `OWOX/models` 85★ shipping a visual EDITOR, `openknowledge-sh/openknowledge` 33★ shipping a CLI — all pushed within the last three weeks.
Countermeasure: §13.5's 'target, not host' is right and must be executed in S2, not deferred. Ship OKF as the FIRST column of `mdmax cert`, and ship the one thing the OKF ecosystem provably lacks: a checker that runs on arbitrary markdown rather than on an already-conformant bundle. Concretely — `mdmax cert <file> --targets okf/v0.2` answering 'what would break if this became an OKF concept'. That is a column nobody has and it converts the competitor into a distribution channel.

N6 — THE CONTAINER WAS BUILT AND NOBODY USED IT (required #6).
Mechanism: the founder's 'one mother Markdown … breakpoints … split automatically while parsing' has been tried. It is not that nobody wanted it — it is that the effectiveness check failed.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: repomix issue #71, opened 2024-09-08, still OPEN 23 months later with 12 comments and 8 reactions. The maintainer designed the feature in his first reply. A contributor shipped PR #113 on 2024-10-09. The maintainer gated it on evidence: 'I haven't fully grasped the essence of file splitting effects yet, so I would appreciate it if you could verify the effectiveness of this approach.' The contributor reported the next day: 'Well not quite what I hoped regarding getting it to read all the split files.' The last comment, 2025-09-08: 'Did we see resolution of this?' Reinforcing this from a second direction: the only live-model measurement of a projection bundle anywhere (okf-skills, 2026-07-27) found the bundle arm spent 5.2% MORE tokens and opened MORE files, not fewer.
Countermeasure: do not build the container until W2 has been run and has produced a positive number on a corpus the model cannot read whole. Until then, MDMAX §4.4 must state the 25–168× figure as an artifact-size ratio and must not imply a token saving in an agent loop — the only measurement of that quantity currently points the other way.

N7 — THE TEAM OPTIMISED FOR A DOCUMENT BECAUSE THE REWARD FUNCTION PAYS FOR SENTENCES (required #7).
Mechanism: honesty converts to inertia. Each correction makes the document more valuable and harder to abandon. §9.8 says this. What §9.8 does not say is that the corrective machinery itself became a source of sentences.
Earliest warning sign, visible today, and it is uncomfortable: the statistic that motivated the entire MVP-selection rule does not reproduce. '18 of 18 research headlines were refuted by their own verifier … a 100% one-directional defect rate is a reward function, not noise' is the load-bearing inference of §9.1, and from `result.json` the exhaustive count is 13 of 18 headlines adjudicated at all, 12 negatively, 1 CONFIRMED (`adjacent-transplant`), 5 never adjudicated; verdict pool REFUTED 10 / OVERSTATED 5 / UNSUPPORTED 3 / CONFIRMED 3. 12/18 with three CONFIRMED verdicts in the same pool is consistent with a strict verifier and is much weaker evidence of a systematic reward function. The derived counts (193 killed, 188 new defects) reproduce exactly, so the artifact is sound — the headline over it is not. The failure mode named in §9.1 was applied to itself in the OTHER direction: self-flattery became self-flagellation, and both are sentences.
Countermeasure: §14's P2 must bind the plan, not only the research. Every number in `docs/mdmax/PLAN.md` gets a committed script under `scripts/derive/` plus its captured output, or it is deleted from the plan. Start with §9.1, because it is the number that picked the MVP.

N8 — THE EVIDENCE BASE EVAPORATED (nobody in this program has considered this; it is my strongest new narrative).
Mechanism: not a wrong decision — a total, silent, recoverable-by-nobody loss. The entire engine program exists on one laptop, on one branch, most of it not even committed to that branch.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: `docs/mdmax/PLAN.md` — the v1.0.0 consolidation this gate is convened over — is `??` in git status. So is `corpus-manifest.json`, the artifact created specifically to fix §9.2. So are `result.json`, `raw.json`, `journal.jsonl` and `wf-findings`. Fourteen untracked files, 4,965,476 bytes. None is gitignored; `git check-ignore -v` returns nothing for any of them — they were simply never added. §15's 'Where everything lives' table maps six artifacts and four of them are not in the repository. And the 16 commits that DO exist are on no remote: `git branch -r --contains engine/plan-and-diagnostics` is empty, `origin/main` is still at `8eb4de2` from 2026-07-25. Compounding it: `corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…` does not reproduce under any of 64 serializations of its own (path, sha256) list, and no derivation script exists anywhere in the repo — so even with the manifest in hand, the id cannot be recomputed. The pinned corpus is not pinned; it is a bare hash over a file list that lives outside version control. One `git clean -fdx` — a command this workspace's own RULE 2 list contemplates — ends the program. And Learned Rule #48 documents that subagents in this workspace have committed against an explicit prohibition, so the working tree is not a safe place to keep the only copy of anything.
Countermeasure: `git add docs/mdmax docs/engine/research HANDOFF-*.md` and `git push -u origin engine/plan-and-diagnostics`. Five minutes. Then add a `derivation` field to the manifest naming the exact script and serialization, and commit the script.

N9 — THE CERTIFICATE WAS PERISHABLE AND ITS VALUABLE COLUMNS WERE UNPROBEABLE (nobody has considered this).
Mechanism: `mdmax cert` was selected by the rule 'choose the deliverable whose output shape cannot be a headline'. True. But its output also cannot stay true, and cannot cover the targets people actually care about. A conformance matrix is a perishable good with no maintenance budget in the plan, and the surfaces users publish to are closed SaaS you cannot vendor, version-pin, or probe.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: the `degradation-certificate` area's OWN kill condition (2) — 'THE UNCERTIFIABLE SURFACE IS THE ONLY ONE ANYONE CARES ABOUT. github-blob cannot be probed without pushing content, and Obsidian, Notion, Typora, Bear, Slack, Discord and the chat renderers cannot be probed at all — that is 7 of the ~12 surfaces on the brief's list.' Its `unverified` section opens 'TARGETS I NEVER RAN — this is the biggest gap and it is more than half the brief's list' and admits 'I have NO empirical Obsidian data at all.' Its kill condition (1) sets the floor at ~1% of blocks and reports the honest measured figure as 4.28% — a 4× margin, not a 40× one, on a corpus written by one author. Meanwhile the pinnable engines move: markdown-it 15.0.0 on 2026-07-30, marked 18.0.7 on 2026-07-21. §12's K5 ('the certificate finds no target disagreement anyone cares about') states no threshold at all, so it can never fire.
Countermeasure: give K5 the number the research already produced — kill if semantic BROKEN falls below 1% of blocks on a corpus this team did not write. And split the matrix explicitly into a PROBED tier (offline, vendored, version-stamped) and a DECLARED tier (contract-plus-canary for closed SaaS), labelled in the output, so the certificate never manufactures confidence about Obsidian or Notion. The maintenance surface — renderer-drift diffs between two pinned versions — is the actual recurring product and is currently unbuilt by anyone.

N10 — TWO DECISIONS DELETED THE WEDGE THE DEMAND RESEARCH IDENTIFIED (nobody has reconciled this).
Mechanism: D3 and D4 were made on architectural grounds against research findings that were about demand, and the two bodies of evidence were never put side by side.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: `collab-primitives` kill condition (4) names the competitive threat as 'range-anchored comments with anonymous no-account share links' from HedgeDoc (working PoC with live demo, 2026-04-04), Relay (175,904 installs), Peerdraft or HackMD — D3 removes the anonymity. Kill condition (3) diagnoses the 190× plugin gap as 'a plugin cannot deliver the collaborator half' — the collaborator half is exactly what login-required removes. And `FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md:171` lists 'Free git-backed sync forever (user's own repo = backend; marginal cost ~0) — undercuts every $4–10/mo sync add-on' against pain theme T3, ranked #3 in the demand taxonomy — D4 overturns it. §13.3 logs the first as 'a tradeoff'; the second is not logged anywhere.
Countermeasure: S1's reconciliation pass must include a decisions-vs-demand diff, not only an audit-vs-critic diff. Any decision that deletes a property the demand research ranked in its top five gets a written replacement wedge or gets reopened.

N11 — BUS FACTOR ONE MET A TWO-WEEK PLAN WITH NO CALENDAR (nobody has stated this).
Mechanism: §11 costs S0–S6 at roughly two weeks of work and names no owner and no dates. The only owner also runs a client studio with AMC obligations. The plan's gates are all serial on one person, and S5 — the one that matters — is the one he finds boring.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: all 20 commits in `frontmatter` and all 416 in `md` are `Sagnik Mitra <sagnikmitra123@gmail.com>`. Amit is named as co-author in the plan's frontmatter and as co-decider on D1–D5, and has committed nothing; §0 addresses him as a reader. The last 19 days, at full intensity, produced 532 lines of product source.
Countermeasure: either Amit owns S5 end to end with his own commits, or S5 is contracted out, or K6 is triggered now and MDMAX is repositioned as a standalone library — which the plan already describes as the honest alternative. Pick one this week; the plan cannot survive 'we will see'.

N12 — D9'S ESCAPE HATCH REINTRODUCED THE CVE CLASS D9 EXISTS TO PREVENT (nobody has considered this).
Mechanism: D9's rationale is that self-declaring formats that CARRY their definition produce CVEs (XML internal DTD subset → XXE; vim modelines, five CVEs in 24 years). The proposed fix is to NAME the capability instead. But naming an executable resource that a consumer then runs is the same attack surface with one extra hop, and it arrives with a false sense of safety because the file itself looks inert.
Earliest warning sign, visible today: OKF v0.2 §10.2 already ships exactly this — `executor.resource` and `attester.resource` naming code the consumer executes, with `okf/bundles/acme_retail/attesters/sql_equality.py` in Google's reference bundle. §10.5 step 5 is 'the consumer runs the attester over the receipt'. §12 defers 'The attester ABI, portability, and sandboxing' to a future revision — i.e. the sandbox story does not exist yet. If MDMAX adopts OKF as a certificate target (§13.5, recommended) it inherits this surface, and `fm:vocab: sgnk/v1` is a resolution step with the same shape.
Countermeasure: write D9's threat model down before S2, not after. Specifically: a named capability resolves only from a pinned allowlist shipped with the engine, never from a path or URL inside the document, and `mdmax cert` flags any document naming an unresolvable or non-allowlisted capability as CORRUPT rather than DEGRADED.

RANKING, probability × severity (probability is my estimate over the next 12 months; severity is what it costs if it happens):
1. N2 editor floor — probability HIGH (the code is single-tenant, the work is unloved, one owner, 532 lines in 19 days), severity TOTAL (K6: no Google-Docs story exists without it). Top risk by a wide margin.
2. N1 research-never-became-code — probability HIGH, severity TOTAL. Distinct from N2: N1 is 'nothing ships', N2 is 'the wrong thing ships'.
3. N3 anchor doesn't transfer — probability MEDIUM-HIGH (86.6% append-dominance is measured, not speculated), severity HIGH (kills comments; §9.5 already concedes ranges are unmeasured). Elevated because S4's gate cannot detect it.
4. N8 evidence evaporates — probability LOW-MEDIUM (needs one bad command or one dead disk), severity TOTAL AND IRREVERSIBLE. Highest severity-per-unit-cost-to-fix in the entire list.
5. N5 OKF outruns them — probability MEDIUM-HIGH (the ecosystem is forming now, measurably, weekly), severity MEDIUM-HIGH (survivable if OKF becomes a column; fatal if it becomes the format).
6. N7 document-as-product — probability MEDIUM-HIGH, severity MEDIUM (slow bleed, and the team has partial immunity because it named the disease).
7. N9 certificate perishable/unprobeable — probability MEDIUM, severity MEDIUM-HIGH (it is the MVP; if it lands hollow, the one artifact chosen for undismissability is dismissed).
8. N4 refusal rejected — probability MEDIUM, severity HIGH but LATE (only bites after S6, which is downstream of S4 and S5).
9. N10 decisions deleted the wedge — probability MEDIUM, severity MEDIUM (recoverable by reopening D3 as a tier split).
10. N11 bus factor — probability HIGH but it is a multiplier on N1/N2 rather than an independent failure.
11. N6 container unused — probability LOW near-term, severity LOW (it is explicitly out of the MVP per §10.4).
12. N12 D9 threat model — probability LOW, severity HIGH-IF-IT-HAPPENS (a CVE in a collaboration product is existential for trust).

THE SINGLE CHEAPEST INTERVENTION THAT REDUCES THE MOST RISK.
Change one line: §11's standing rule currently reads 'No further research fan-out until one committed assertion in this repository has gone from red to green against engine code.' Replace 'engine code' with a named assertion — a second GitHub login who is not `sagnikmitra` opens a document they do not own and writes to it under their own attribution. Cost: one edit to one sentence, zero tokens, no new research. Effect: it retires N1 and N2 simultaneously (the top two risks, and the two whose severity is TOTAL), because that assertion cannot be satisfied by prose and cannot be satisfied without replacing the allowlist, the single server token and the hardcoded AUTHOR constant. It also defuses N7 and N11, because the unit of progress becomes a test only one kind of work can turn green. It does not touch N3, N5 or N9 — those need S1's reconciliation and the stratified benchmark — but no single cheap action does.
There is a strictly cheaper prerequisite that reduces a different and total risk, and it should happen first because it takes five minutes: `git add docs/mdmax docs/engine/research HANDOFF-*.md && git push -u origin engine/plan-and-diagnostics`. That retires N8 outright. Do that, then change the sentence.
result.measurement:
THREE EXPERIMENTS, PRE-REGISTERED, IN PRIORITY ORDER. Each has a stated prediction so it can go against us.

E1 — THE STRATIFIED RE-DERIVATION (settles N3, and is the one S4 currently cannot do).
Corpus: the pinned `corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…` roots at their manifest HEADs (`md` 02c22ec4, `knowledge` 464eb666, `frontmatter` 798ebbf3), PLUS a second corpus this team did not write. Candidate named in W1: `~/.claude/skills-src`, 474 files / 5,013,124 bytes — but W1's authorship criterion is the wrong one and must be replaced by an EDIT-SHAPE criterion. Select any git-tracked markdown corpus in which ≥25% of `.md` file-revision pairs delete more than two lines; my measurement says none of the three current roots qualifies (`md` 0.9%, `knowledge` 9.9%, `frontmatter` 8.3%), so this is a real acquisition task, not a formality. Documentation monorepos with review culture (e.g. a large open-source docs repo with PR review) are the right shape.
Tasks: the existing `resolve(block, new document)` over every revision pair, with results reported in FOUR strata rather than one aggregate: (a) pairs deleting 0 lines, (b) 1–2 lines, (c) >2 lines, (d) pairs containing a detected paragraph reflow. Report n for each stratum alongside correct/false/refusal.
Verifiers: the existing hand-audit protocol on 100% of false matches in strata (c) and (d), which is where they will now concentrate. Add arm 7 `diff3-assisted` as the baseline (§9.3) — on strata (a) and (b) it should be near-perfect and near-free, which is the point.
n: whatever stratum (c) yields; report it even if it is 54.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS. P1: on stratum (a) the resolver scores >99.9% correct because S1 resolves by construction, and `diff3-assisted` matches it. P2: on stratum (c) the false rate exceeds 0.5% — kill-gate K3's threshold — because §1.1a's own multi-candidate stratum already shows 2.66%. P3: stratum (c) is under 5% of all pairs on all three current roots, i.e. the flagship number is >95% composed of the case a diff already handles. P4: the aggregate re-derivation on the unchanged pinned corpus lands within 0.3pp of 99.627% — and that agreement is EVIDENCE FOR the bias, not against it.

E2 — THE TENANCY ASSERTION (settles N2, and is the standing-rule target).
Not a benchmark — one integration test, committed RED before any of S0–S4. Two GitHub identities, neither of which is `ALLOWED_GH_LOGIN`. Identity A creates a document. Identity B opens it via a share link with an enforced role, writes one character, and the resulting commit carries B's name and email, not the `AUTHOR` constant. Verifier: assert on the persisted commit's author fields and on a 403 for a role B does not hold.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION: this test cannot be made green without deleting `src/modules/auth/domain/allowlist.ts`'s equality, replacing `repoEnv.GITHUB_REPO_TOKEN` with per-user credentials or a server-side tenancy layer, and removing the `AUTHOR` constant from `dependency-container.ts` — i.e. it will take substantially longer than S5's implied 'parallel' budget, and that duration IS the measurement.

E3 — THE LIVE MODEL EXPERIMENT, RUN CORRECTLY (settles N6 and §4.4's operational claim; W2, which has run zero times).
The design is already published by somebody else and its authors named the flaw to fix: okf-skills, 2026-07-27, 'The experiment worth running next is the one this repo cannot host: a corpus large enough that reading everything is not an option, and a codebase whose comments say what rather than why.'
Corpus: the `md` root at 21,068,853 bytes — provably larger than any single context window, and the projection tiers are already specified.
Tasks: 20 questions, stratified into lookup / cross-cutting / change-site, ground-truth claim lists written before any run.
Arms: full corpus, outline tier, index tier. n=5 per cell (okf-skills ran n=1 and said so; five is the minimum that separates a 5% effect from Q6-scale noise, which swung 28% at n=1).
Verifiers: billed tokens from the harness (never self-reported file counts), plus blind claim-hit grading against the pre-written list.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS. P1: the index tier reduces billed tokens by less than the 25× artifact ratio implies, because the agent opens files after reading the index — the only prior measurement went the wrong way at +5.2%. P2: the index tier LOSES on change-site questions, matching okf-skills' Q4 ('the bundle became a detour around the file that had the answer'). P3: if the index tier's token saving is under 2× at equal correctness, §4.4's headline must be restated as an artifact-size ratio and the container work stays cut.
result.kill_condition:
FIVE. Any one should stop the corresponding line of work; the first two should stop the program as currently sequenced.

KC1 — THE TENANCY ASSERTION IS STILL RED IN 30 DAYS. If E2's test has not gone green by 2026-08-31, K6 has fired and should be honoured rather than deferred: stop calling frontmatter 'Google Docs for markdown', reposition MDMAX as a standalone library, and say so publicly. The plan already names this as the honest alternative in §12 K6; the failure mode is holding the label while the code cannot support it. Evidence that makes this measurable today: 532 lines of product source in 19 days, one committer, and a base whose auth is a single-string equality.

KC2 — STRATUM (c) IS TOO SMALL TO MEASURE. If E1's >2-deleted-lines stratum yields fewer than ~200 block-versions on every corpus available, then the flagship 99.627% has never been tested on the case it exists for and cannot be, on this evidence. Do not publish it. Restate the claim as 'exact-hash resolution over an append-dominated corpus' — which is true, defensible, and much smaller — and move the anchoring investment behind `diff3-assisted` (K1). My measurement predicts this fires: 54 qualifying pairs in `md`, 46 in `knowledge`, 5 in `frontmatter`.

KC3 — THE PROBED TIER OF THE CERTIFICATE COVERS FEWER THAN HALF THE TARGETS USERS NAME. The `degradation-certificate` area already counted 7 of ~12 surfaces as unprobeable. If S2's build confirms that and no user says the declared-contract-plus-canary tier is acceptable, `mdmax cert` is a matrix about the renderers nobody worries about. Cut it and pick a different Artifact 1 — the plan's §10.1 rule still holds, but the artifact it selected does not.

KC4 — SEMANTIC BROKEN FALLS BELOW 1% OF BLOCKS ON A CORPUS THIS TEAM DID NOT WRITE. This is the research area's own threshold and the plan's K5 has no number; adopt it verbatim. The honest measured figure on this team's own corpus was 4.28%. A 4× margin on a self-authored, AI-assisted corpus is thin, and the area said so: 'If a neutral corpus halves it again, stop.'

KC5 — E3 SHOWS THE INDEX TIER SAVING UNDER 2× IN BILLED TOKENS AT EQUAL CORRECTNESS. Then §4.4's '25–168× fewer tokens' must be restated as a compression ratio between artifacts and must never again be phrased as a promise to an AI consumer. The only existing measurement of this quantity, by anyone, found +5.2% in the wrong direction. Until E3 runs, MDMAX's promise #1 to an AI consumer ('Fewer tokens') is a pre-registered prediction, not a capability — and per §14 P9 it must carry that label.

result.unverified:
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND WHERE IT ACTUALLY SITS.

1. THE 294-PAIR SELECTION CRITERION — the load-bearing gap in my own headline. I read `docs/engine/PLAN.md:80` verbatim ('294 consecutive real revision pairs') and found no modification filter, and all three references to `41,642` in the 18-area artifact are self-tagged 'not re-run by me'. But no selection script exists anywhere in the repo, so I cannot prove the 294 pairs inherit the population's 86.6% append-dominance. My edit-shape numbers are PRIMARY (own-measurement over git history); the step from population to sample is INFERENCE. If the pairs were hand-picked for substantive edits, finding 5 weakens sharply — though finding 7 (2.66% false on the multi-candidate stratum, from the primary document) stands regardless.

2. THE 99.627% ITSELF. I did not re-derive it. Nobody has since it was first produced — §9.4 says so and one area admits in writing it was 'quoted from the task brief, not re-measured here'. Everything I say about it is about its corpus and its stratification, not its arithmetic. SECONDARY at best.

3. RENDERER-CHURN AS AN ARGUMENT ABOUT CERTIFICATE STALENESS. I have npm publish dates (markdown-it 15.0.0 on 2026-07-30, marked 18.0.7 on 2026-07-21, from the registry `time` field) but I did NOT establish that those releases changed rendering BEHAVIOUR. A version bump is not a semantic change. The GitHub releases API returned n/a for all seven repos I tried because the unauthenticated rate limit hit zero mid-run. 'The certificate is perishable' is INFERENCE from release cadence, not measurement of behavioural drift, and I flag it as the weakest link in N9.

4. THE CLOSED-SAAS COVERAGE ARGUMENT is not mine — it is a verbatim primary read of the `degradation-certificate` area's own kill condition and unverified section. I did not independently attempt to probe Obsidian, Notion, Slack or the chat renderers. That area explicitly says it could not either, and that it has 'NO empirical Obsidian data at all'.

5. THE OKF COMPETITIVE THREAT'S MAGNITUDE. Star counts, push dates and file sizes are primary (api.github.com). Whether an 8,134-star Google repo and a 206-star toolkit constitute market capture is INFERENCE. Note the honest counter inside my own evidence: `knowledge-catalog`'s README says 'This repository and its contents are not an official Google product', and OKF §11's conformance bar is deliberately near-zero (parseable frontmatter with a non-empty `type`), which is a weak standard to be captured by.

6. THE okf-skills BENCHMARK is n=1 per cell and its authors say so plainly ('Eight points on twenty-six, at n=1 per cell, is not a result anyone should quote as a headline'). I am quoting its DIRECTION on cost (+5.2%, i.e. no saving) and its own stated reason the effect was invisible, not its magnitude. Anyone citing it as '5.2% worse' is over-reading it, and so would I be.

7. USER-SIDE CLAIMS ARE ALL SECOND-HAND. N4's refusal-rejection narrative rests on the program's own plugin-install census (24,569 vs 4,659,822) and on a threshold the research invented. There are still zero users, zero interviews and zero willingness-to-pay probes in this entire program — §11 W3 says so and nothing has changed. Every sentence anyone writes about what users will feel about an orphaned comment, including mine, is INFERENCE.

8. WHETHER AMIT HAS CONTRIBUTED OUTSIDE GIT. I measured commits (20/20 Sagnik). Design conversations, decisions and review are not in version control and I have no visibility into them. 'Bus factor one' is a claim about the CODE, and I should not be read as claiming it about the partnership.

9. `mdmax cert`'s NICHE EMPTINESS is established on npm only (four searches, 32 results). I did not search PyPI, crates.io, Go modules, Homebrew or Ruby gems, and the GitHub rate limit blocked a code search. 'Nobody ships this' is SEARCH-ONLY with a stated and incomplete search.

10. I did NOT run the test suite, the build, or the app. Every statement about what the code does comes from reading it, not executing it. In particular I did not confirm that the single-user auth path actually blocks a second login at runtime — only that the code says it does.

verdicts.claim: C1 [own-measurement]: 'The core mechanism of MDMAX §4.1 block identity — exact match, then context-scored disambiguation, then fuzzy fallback — is 182 lines of already-shipping MIT code', citing dom-anchor-text-quote@4.0.2 as 'the anchoring library Hypothes.is ships' / 'in production at Hypothes.is'.
verdicts.reason: The line count is real — I downloaded the tarball, `wc -l datq/package/lib/index.js` = 182, deps {diff-match-patch ^1.0.0, dom-anchor-text-position ^4.0.0}, MIT, and diff-match-patch index.js = 2217 lines, downloads 13,103 / 5,971,159 for 2026-07-24..2026-07-30. Everything else in the claim fails on a read of the 182 lines and of the primary source. (1) PRODUCTION CLAIM FALSE: raw.githubusercontent.com/hypothesis/client/main/package.json has NO dom-anchor-text-quote and NO diff-match-patch; it depends on `approx-string-match: ^2.0.0`. GitHub code search `dom-anchor-text-quote repo:hypothesis/client` returns total_count 0. The package was last published 2017-02-10T21:02:05Z — nine years stale. (2) MECHANISM CLAIM FALSE: `toTextPosition` never performs an exact match. It calls `dmp.match_main` (fuzzy bitap) on the prefix, then the suffix, then each 32-char slice, using prefix/suffix only as a LOCATION HINT (`loc`) that biases a positional fuzzy search. It never enumerates multiple candidates, never scores them, has no jaccard/shingle stage, and has no AMBIGUOUS return — it returns a position or null. That is a position-based tiebreak, which PLAN.md §4.1 measures as catastrophic: 'content-hash plus nearest-position goes 0.00% → 22.20% false'. The researcher's evidence sentence 'it already does prefix/suffix context scoring, MDMAX's S2' is a misread of the one comment it quoted. (3) NOT NEWS: PLAN.md §8.3 line 274 already lists this as refuted — '"Content-derived re-anchoring has no precedent." 25 years of prior art — Brush & Bargeron MSR-TR-2001-107, a granted Microsoft patent, the W3C Web Annotation Data Model's TextQuoteSelector, Hypothes.is in production' — and §11 S4 already schedules `TextQuoteSelector` as benchmark arm 9.
verdicts.correction: The right artifact exists and the researcher's DIRECTION survives under a corrected citation. hypothesis/client/src/annotator/anchoring/match-quote.ts is 163 lines and does implement MDMAX's shape: an exact-match pass collecting ALL occurrences via an indexOf loop, falling back to approxSearch (approx-string-match@2.0.0, MIT) with maxErrors = min(256, quote.length/2), then a weighted context score — quoteWeight 50, prefixWeight 20, suffixWeight 20, posWeight 2 with the comment 'Proximity to expected location. Used as a tie-breaker.' Cite that, at 163 lines + approx-string-match, not dom-anchor-text-quote. Note what still is NOT in it: it sorts by score and returns scoredMatches[0] unconditionally — no AMBIGUOUS state, no margin threshold. MDMAX's three-valued resolve(index | AMBIGUOUS | LOST) is the one part of §4.1 with no shipping counterpart found. It is a ~20-line policy, not a moat, but the claim as written attributes it to code that does the opposite.

verdicts.reason: The load-bearing part reproduces perfectly and the conclusion stands; the reported ratio does not. I re-read all 1,084 manifest files and re-verified every sha256: sha_match 1084, sha_drift 0, missing 0, total bytes 25,548,765 — matching corpus-manifest.json exactly, so the corpus verification claim is CONFIRMED. `{#id}` on headings = 0 and `^blockid` declarations = 0 under every definition I tried. But the DENOMINATOR 31,630 reproduces under none of four principled definitions: mdast-util-from-markdown heading nodes = 28,221 total (28,194 ATX + 27 setext); regex `^ {0,3}#{1,6}(\s|$)` excluding fenced code = 28,158; the same regex including fenced code = 31,983; loosest `^\s*#` = 32,052. 31,630 sits 12.2% above the parser count and 1.1% below the fence-inclusive count and matches nothing. Under P1/P2 that is a ratio whose denominator has no committed derivation. The reference count is also off: I find 5 `[[x#^id]]` matches across 4 files, not 4 across 3 — the researcher's list silently merges md/docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md and frontmatter/docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md, which are two distinct manifest entries, and omits a second occurrence in HANDOFF-graph-engineering-research-2026-07-30.md.
verdicts.correction: Report '0 headings carry {#id}' and '0 ^blockid declarations across 1,084 files / 25,548,765 bytes (corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…)' as the finding, with the denominator stated as 28,194 ATX headings by mdast parse (script committed). The second cut the researcher draws — that Obsidian has shipped `^blockid` with keystroke autocomplete since 2020 and it is used zero times in a 756-file vault, so authors do not feel block-identity pain, only the app does — survives intact and is the most valuable sentence in the whole submission. It is also a direct input to kill gate K4.

verdicts.claim: C7 [own-measurement]: Independent re-derivation of the splice-only round trip on the pinned corpus: 5/1,080 byte-identical (0.463%), 124,534/423,410 lines absent (29.41%), 25,548,765 → 26,576,149 bytes (+4.02%) — so PLAN.md's line figure holds and its byte figure should be struck.
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt this from scratch with mdast-util-from-markdown + mdast-util-to-markdown + mdast-util-gfm on node v24.6.0 and reproduced every figure to the digit: nonEmpty 1080, parseErr 0, identical 5 (5/1080 = 0.463%), bytesIn 25,548,765, bytesOut 26,576,149 (+4.02%), linesIn 423,410. Line absence depends on the definition and both of the researcher's numbers fall out of my run: multiset-difference gives 127,805 (30.18%), set-difference gives exactly 124,534 (29.41%). The researcher used set-difference and did not say so — a one-word omission, not a defect in the result. PLAN.md §4.2 is quoted verbatim and correctly. This is the only claim in the set that meets P2 in full, and it is the one that most deserves to be acted on.
verdicts.correction: The RECOMMENDATION is right and I can strengthen it; the stated CAUSE is wrong. The researcher attributes the byte-sign inversion to 'a config artifact (frontmatter handling)' without testing it. I tested it. On the frontmatter root alone (56 files, 908,989 bytes — the closest reachable analogue of PLAN.md's '51 files in this repo'): without the frontmatter extension +12.17%, with micromark-extension-frontmatter + mdast-util-frontmatter enabled +12.13%. Frontmatter handling moves the byte delta by 0.04pp. It cannot explain a swing from −18.94% to +4.02%. So the finding is stronger than claimed: PLAN.md §4.2's 'drops 18.94% of bytes' reproduces under NO configuration I could construct, on the corpus subset it was measured on, in either direction. Meanwhile its line figure lands almost exactly — 25.01% (with frontmatter ext) / 25.73% (without) against the published 24.98%, and 0 of 56 files survive byte-identically, consistent with '0 of 51'. Strike the byte figure; keep the line figure; do not publish the frontmatter-handling explanation.

verdicts.claim: C8 [own-measurement]: 'The data moat for anchoring does not exist: the pinned corpus is 80 days of one author's commits, and a strictly larger public markdown corpus is one git clone away — roughly 1,000× the bytes.'
verdicts.reason: The qualitative point is CONFIRMED and matters: `git log --oneline | wc -l` in ~/Desktop/GitHub/md = 416, `git shortlog -sn HEAD` = '416 Sagnik Mitra' (100% one author), HEAD 02c22ec4 matching the manifest's 02c22ec47a3a73fb25a14b11be233ad3d00a8b48. Two numbers do not survive. (1) '80-day' is wrong: first commit Wed May 13 2026, last Fri Jul 17 2026; `date -j` confirms both weekdays and `(date(2026,7,17)-date(2026,5,13)).days` = 65. The span is 65 days, an 18.8% overstatement, and it is inflated in the direction that flatters the argument. (2) 'roughly 1,000× the bytes' is a unit mismatch. MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs `size` = 27,070,691 confirms, but GitHub's `size` field is repo disk usage in KB — packed git history plus images and every non-markdown asset. Dividing 27,070,691 KB (= 27,720,387,584 bytes) by 25,548,765 bytes of plain markdown text gives 1,085, but numerator and denominator measure different things. mdn/content is 501,827 KB and kubernetes/website 560,330 KB on the same basis.
verdicts.correction: State it as: the pinned corpus is 65 days of a single author (416/416 commits), against public multi-author markdown corpora created 2016–2020 whose repositories are one to three orders of magnitude larger on disk. Drop '~1,000×' unless someone clones azure-docs and counts *.md bytes. The conclusion — that revision-pair volume is not defensible and a competitor can out-sample this corpus for free — is unaffected and correct.

verdicts.claim: C9 [own-measurement/primary]: Google Docs has imported and exported markdown since 2024-07-16 and supported composing in markdown since 2022; the operative verb is 'Convert Markdown to Docs CONTENT', so the durable artifact remains a Doc.
verdicts.reason: curl to workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2024/07/import-and-export-markdown-in-google-docs.html returns HTTP 200, 202,459 bytes, dated 'July 16, 2024', and the body text is verbatim as quoted: 'In 2022, we introduced expanded support for composing with Markdown in Google Docs on web. Today, we're introducing highly-requested features that enhance Docs' interoperability with other Markdown supporting tools. These include the ability to: Convert Markdown to Docs content on paste / Copy Docs content as Markdown / Export a Doc as Markdown (from File > Download) / Import Markdown as a Doc...' The 'Convert Markdown to Docs content' string is present. The reading — that Google entered two years ago and that D4's surviving differentiator is which artifact is durable — is a fair inference and clearly labelled as one.

verdicts.claim: C10 [own-measurement]: 'No prior art exists for the degradation certificate. Three independent GitHub searches and four npm lookups came back empty. This is the one capability I could not find already built.'
verdicts.reason: The searches reproduce exactly — q='markdown renderer compatibility matrix' total_count 0, q='markdown degradation certificate' 0, q='markdown target conformance report' 1 (P4ST4S/mcp-migrate, unrelated); npm babelmark / markdown-compat / markdown-conformance all {"error":"Not found"}. The method is what fails. Three 3–4-word CONJUNCTIVE repo-name/description searches returning 0 is near-zero evidence, and probing three GUESSED package names is a name-availability check presented as a novelty search — the exact defect P8 exists to catch. One query the researcher did not run, `markdown flavors comparison`, returns ArchieCur/MARKDOWN_FLAVORS (created 2025-10-21, 'Living comparison of Markdown flavor syntax extensions - updated for 2025'), which ships markdown-flavors.csv — a 14-flavor × 17-construct support matrix over CommonMark, GFM, GitLab, Obsidian, Discord, Pandoc, MultiMarkdown, Kramdown, Python-Markdown, Marked.js, R Markdown, MDX, Quarto, Markdown Extra — plus a 'Markdown Compatibility Quick Reference Guide.pdf', and which credits vimtaai's 2021 markdown-flavors gist as its source. `babelmark` as a search term returns the babelmark org (babelmark.github.io, 115 stars). `markdown conformance` returns 31 repos including Sudhakaran88/okf-conformance. Prior art for the CONCEPT is 4+ years old and hand-maintained.
verdicts.correction: The MVP survives; the sentence does not. What none of the prior art does is per-DOCUMENT, automated, version-pinned, and scoped to (product, surface) pairs with a PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT verdict — MARKDOWN_FLAVORS is per-construct × per-flavour, hand-edited, and treats 'GitHub (GFM)' as one target where PLAN.md §4.3 measured blob/comment/Pages disagreeing on identical bytes. Claim that, cite MARKDOWN_FLAVORS and babelmark as the incumbents, and note that the incumbent's staleness is the actual opening. Do not ship 'no prior art exists' — it is refuted by one query.

verdicts.claim: HEADLINE, second half: 'the only durable moat in the whole program is the multi-tenancy work in S5 that the plan itself labels "uninteresting."'
verdicts.reason: Zero of the ten claims addresses it. No search, no prior-art check, no comparable, no citation — the assertion appears only in the headline and DESIGN item 5 ('PROMOTE IT TO P0 AND SAY OUT LOUD THAT IT IS THE MOAT... where 100% of the structural defensibility lives'). The plan quotes are accurate (§11 S5 'This has zero engine content and will keep losing priority to compiler work precisely because it is uninteresting'; K6). But the researcher's own DESIGN item 6 forbids exactly this: 'WHAT NOT TO BUILD: ...anything whose pitch is "nobody has this" without the P8 search attached.' It then makes its single largest strategic claim with no P8 search attached. Worse, it is the claim least likely to survive the researcher's own clone-latency finding: multi-tenancy (accounts, workspaces, share links with enforced roles, per-document membership) is the most commoditised layer in SaaS — Supabase RLS, Firebase security rules, WorkOS/Clerk organisations — and if a third party shipped a complete toolkit for Google's brand-new format in 24 hours, a share dialog with roles is not a structural moat.
verdicts.correction: The defensible version of this recommendation is the one the plan already makes and does not need a moat argument to justify: S5 is P0 because K6 says without it there is no Google-Docs story and the engine is then a standalone library. That is a sequencing argument from a kill gate, and it is sufficient. Calling it 'the only durable moat' is an unevidenced inversion that will be the first thing a sceptical reader attacks.

verdicts.claim: HEADLINE: 'provenance was taken by Google's own OKF v0.2 on 2026-07-25 and by C2PA before that.'
verdicts.reason: No claim in the submission carries any C2PA evidence — it appears only in the headline and the falsifier prose, with no URL, spec section, or API call. C2PA (contentauth/c2pa-rs, 375 stars, 'Rust SDK for the core C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) specification') is a cryptographically-signed manifest standard bound to media containers — images, video, audio. It has no markdown binding and no text-span selector. Invoking it as prior art for markdown span provenance is a category stretch, and under the brief's own rule an uncited assertion is a defect. Separately, the '2026-07-25' date for SPEC.md v0.2 is carried from the brief rather than verified by the researcher — I confirmed the content and the 37,544-byte size but did not independently confirm that publication date either.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN item 3: 'BLOCK IDENTITY — VENDOR IT, DO NOT INVENT IT. Take dom-anchor-text-quote's shape (182 lines, MIT) and diff-match-patch (Apache-2.0) as the S1/S3 substrate.'
verdicts.reason: This is the most actionable defect in the submission because it is a build instruction. Having read all 182 lines: dom-anchor-text-quote has no exact-match stage (it goes straight to fuzzy bitap), no candidate enumeration, no scoring function, and no AMBIGUOUS return — `toTextPosition` returns a position or null. Its disambiguation is `dmp.Match_Distance` proximity to a `loc` hint, i.e. a position-based tiebreak. PLAN.md §4.1 measured that exact family and found 'content hash alone' at 83.36% correct / 0.00% false versus 'content-hash plus nearest-position' at 22.20% FALSE, and §8.1 elevates 'Refusing is cheap. A silently wrong anchor is not' to a load-bearing invariant. Adopting this library's shape would import, as the S1/S3 substrate, the single failure mode the plan's 384-configuration sweep exists to have ruled out.
verdicts.correction: Vendor hypothesis/client/src/annotator/anchoring/match-quote.ts (163 lines) + approx-string-match@2.0.0 (MIT) instead. It matches MDMAX's staging: all exact occurrences first via an indexOf loop, approxSearch fallback at maxErrors = min(256, quote.length/2), then a normalised weighted score (quote 50 / prefix 20 / suffix 20 / position 2, position explicitly commented 'Used as a tie-breaker'). Keep diff-match-patch out of it — hypothes.is dropped it. Then add the two things neither library has and both of which are ~20 lines: the anchorability gate and the AMBIGUOUS/LOST return with a margin threshold. The researcher's conclusion that this is weeks not a moat is correct; its named substrate is the wrong one and would ship a regression.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN item 1: 'The expiry field IS the moat mechanism: it makes a stale copy visibly stale' — a 90-day expiry on closed-target rows in a publicly published targets.json.
verdicts.reason: An inference presented as a mechanism, with no evidence, and it contradicts the researcher's own strongest claim. C2 establishes that a third party shipped a complete authoring/validation/visualisation toolkit plus a GitHub Action for Google's new format within 24 hours, and that 69 repos followed in 8 days. DESIGN item 1 simultaneously requires publishing the dataset AND the reproducibility contract ('an OSS target row is REPRODUCIBLE — vendored, version-pinned renderer, anyone can rerun it'). A competitor that can rerun the probes does not need a stale copy; expiry disciplines a fork, it does not deter one. Expiry is a correctness and honesty feature — a good one, and it should ship for that reason — but calling it a moat mechanism is asserted, not shown.
verdicts.correction: Also flag DESIGN item 4 ('emit OKF v0.2 §5.1 sources/generated/verified/stale_after verbatim'): OKF has zero confidence and zero method fields and §5.1 explicitly declines to store a credibility score, so emitting it verbatim silently drops the two dimensions §4.5 exists for. Emit OKF for document-level provenance AND keep a separate per-span method/confidence record, or say plainly that §4.5 is descoped to what OKF covers.

survived: C2 clone latency — CONFIRMED and strengthened. Every figure reproduces (okf-skills created_at 2026-06-14T11:15:31Z, 206 stars, 22 forks; 287 total; 69/66/89/59 by window, summing to 283 with 4 pre-announcement, consistent). My top-20 sample of first-week repos found 20/20 to be genuine implementations — CLIs, a Go CLI, a pure-Rust implementation, a linter, an MCP server, a conformance checker, two editors, a WordPress plugin — not mentions. This is the most decision-relevant number in the area and it holds under adversarial sampling.

C7 round-trip re-derivation — CONFIRMED to the digit on an independent rebuild: 1,080 non-empty files, 0 parse errors, 5 byte-identical (0.463%), 423,410 lines in, 124,534 absent by set-difference (29.41%), 25,548,765 → 26,576,149 bytes (+4.02%). The only claim in the set that fully meets P2. Its recommendation — report the line figure, strike PLAN.md §4.2's byte figure — is correct and I strengthened it.

The corpus verification itself — CONFIRMED. I re-read all 1,084 manifest files and re-verified every sha256 independently: sha_match 1084, sha_drift 0, missing 0, total 25,548,765 bytes across md (756) + knowledge (272) + frontmatter (56). The manifest is sound and the researcher's use of it was honest.

C4 Obsidian Bases — CONFIRMED verbatim from obsidianmd/obsidian-help. The correction to the brief's 'uncomfortable case' stands: Bases keeps data in the .md and allows the view definition in a ```base fence, which is D8 validated by the best-resourced actor in the category.

C5 Obsidian block ids — CONFIRMED verbatim, including the `[[2023-01-01#^37066d]]` example and the placement rules. Obsidian's answer was a declared in-file id, and it is the direct competitor to MDMAX's derived anchor — correctly identified as a threat rather than a concession.

C9 Google Docs markdown timeline — CONFIRMED at HTTP 200 against the primary source, dated July 16, 2024, with 'Convert Markdown to Docs content' present verbatim. The observation that the operative verb makes the Doc the durable artifact, leaving D4's export guarantee as the surviving differentiator, is a fair and clearly-labelled inference.

C6's second cut — 'a mechanism Obsidian has shipped since 2020 and auto-completes on a keystroke was used zero times in a 756-file vault, which is evidence that AUTHORS do not feel the block-identity pain; only the APP feels it.' The zero reproduces under every definition I tried. This is the single most useful sentence in the submission and a direct input to kill gate K4.

The headline's FIRST half — that block identity, splice writing, projection and provenance are leads measured in weeks rather than moats — survives, though not on the evidence given for claim 1. Corrected substrate: match-quote.ts at 163 lines + approx-string-match (MIT) for anchoring; mdast node.position.offset for splicing; llms.txt (AnswerDotAI/llms-txt, created 2024-09-01, 2,541 stars confirmed) for two-tier projection, which PLAN.md §4.4 already cites as corroboration; OKF §5.1 for document-level provenance.
killed: C1's flagship exhibit. 'In production at Hypothes.is' is false against the primary source: hypothesis/client/package.json depends on approx-string-match@^2.0.0 with no dom-anchor-text-quote and no diff-match-patch, and GitHub code search for dom-anchor-text-quote in that repo returns total_count 0. The package was last published 2017-02-10.

C1's mechanism description. Reading all 182 lines: dom-anchor-text-quote never performs an exact match, never enumerates candidates, never scores them, and has no AMBIGUOUS return. It performs location-hinted fuzzy bitap — a position-based tiebreak of the family PLAN.md §4.1 measured at 22.20% false. The researcher counted lines and quoted one comment in place of reading the code.

'No prior art exists for the degradation certificate.' Refuted by one query the researcher did not run: `markdown flavors comparison` → ArchieCur/MARKDOWN_FLAVORS, a 14-flavor × 17-construct matrix shipping markdown-flavors.csv and a 'Markdown Compatibility Quick Reference Guide.pdf', built on vimtaai's 2021 gist. Also babelmark (babelmark.github.io, 115 stars) and 31 repos under `markdown conformance`. Probing three guessed npm package names is name-availability checking, not prior-art search.

'MDMAX §4.5 declared provenance is no longer an unoccupied slot.' The spec's own text refutes it: `grep -ic confidence SPEC.md` = 0 over 37,544 bytes, and §5.1 states 'It does not store a credibility score: a score is subjective, unportable across consumers, and goes stale.' OKF covers document-level provenance; the per-span source/page/method/confidence slot §4.5 is defined around is untouched.

'The only durable moat in the whole program is the multi-tenancy work in S5.' Carries zero evidence across ten claims, violates the researcher's own DESIGN item 6 (no novelty pitch without the P8 search attached), and is the claim least likely to survive its own C2 finding — accounts, workspaces and role-enforced share links are the most commoditised layer in SaaS.
'and by C2PA before that.' Uncited in every claim; C2PA is a signed-manifest standard bound to media containers with no markdown binding and no text-span selector.
C8's '80 days.' First commit Wed 2026-05-13, last Fri 2026-07-17, verified with `date -j`; the span is 65 days. An 18.8% overstatement, in the flattering direction.

C8's 'roughly 1,000× the bytes.' Compares GitHub's `size` field — repo disk usage in KB including packed git history and all binary assets — against 25,548,765 bytes of plain markdown text. The arithmetic (27,070,691 KB → 1,085×) is right; the units are not.

C6's denominator '31,630 ATX headings.' Reproduces under no definition I could construct: mdast parse 28,194 ATX (28,221 headings incl. 27 setext); regex excluding fenced code 28,158; regex including fenced code 31,983; loosest 32,052. The numerator (0) reproduces under all of them, so the finding survives and the ratio does not.

C6's '[[note#^id]] uses = 4, all 4 in 3 files.' I count 5 matches across 4 files; md/docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md and frontmatter/docs/FEATURE-GAP-REPORT.md are distinct manifest entries and a second occurrence in HANDOFF-graph-engineering-research-2026-07-30.md was dropped.

DESIGN item 3's build instruction ('take dom-anchor-text-quote's shape as the S1/S3 substrate'). It would import a position-biased fuzzy search with no refusal state as the foundation of a system whose load-bearing invariant is that refusing beats guessing.

DESIGN item 1's 'the expiry field IS the moat mechanism.' Asserted without evidence and contradicted by the researcher's own C2: a competitor able to rerun version-pinned, reproducible probes does not need a stale copy.
new_defects: hypothesis/client does not use dom-anchor-text-quote. It uses approx-string-match@2.0.0 (MIT) plus its own 163-line src/annotator/anchoring/match-quote.ts. That file, not the one cited, is the true reference implementation of MDMAX §4.1's staging — exact-first via an indexOf loop over ALL occurrences, then approxSearch at maxErrors = min(256, quote.length/2), then a normalised weighted score (quote 50 / prefix 20 / suffix 20 / position 2, position commented 'Used as a tie-breaker'). It still has no AMBIGUOUS state: it sorts by score and returns scoredMatches[0] unconditionally. PLAN.md §11 S4's arm 9 should be pinned to match-quote.ts + approx-string-match, not to TextQuoteSelector in the abstract.

PLAN.md §4.2's 'drops 18.94% of bytes' does not reproduce under ANY configuration, on the file set it was measured on. On the frontmatter root (56 files, 908,989 bytes) I measure +12.17% without the frontmatter extension and +12.13% with micromark-extension-frontmatter + mdast-util-frontmatter enabled — growth, not a drop, both ways. The researcher's recommendation to strike the figure is therefore right, and its stated cause ('a config artifact — frontmatter handling') is wrong: frontmatter handling moves the delta by 0.04pp. Meanwhile §4.2's LINE figure is vindicated: I measure 25.01% (with frontmatter ext) against the published 24.98%, and 0 of 56 files survive byte-identically, consistent with '0 of 51'.

corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… is not reproducible and has no generator. There is no script anywhere in the repo that emits it (`grep -rl corpus_id` over scripts/ and docs/ finds only the manifest itself), and the manifest does not state the hash construction. I attempted three plausible constructions over the sorted (path, sha256) list — with and without root prefixes, with and without separators — and got 1a00525b…, 561187d3… and 5aad2ccb…, none matching. P1 ('Every reported figure names a corpus_id, or it is not reported') currently anchors the program's whole anti-fabrication regime to a label nobody can check. The file list and every sha256 in it ARE verifiable and I verified all 1,084 — so the fix is small: commit the ~10-line script that derives the id, and add it to S0.

The OKF ecosystem has already produced markdown EDITORS, inside frontmatter's own category, within the first week. activetwist/OnyxWriter ('Local-first editor for Open Knowledge Format bundles', created in the 2026-06-13..06-20 window) and pothos-dev/sunstone ('a lightweight markdown editor with first-class Open Knowledge Format' support). The researcher used the OKF ecosystem to measure clone latency for a CONVENTION and did not notice that the same eight days produced competitors for the PRODUCT. This is the most important thing in the area that nobody has written down, and it belongs in §13.5's OKF decision.

DESIGN item 4 ('emit OKF v0.2 §5.1 sources/generated/verified/stale_after verbatim') would silently descope MDMAX §4.5. OKF contains zero confidence fields and §5.1 explicitly refuses to store a credibility score, so a verbatim emission carries no method and no confidence — the exact two dimensions §4.5 was written to preserve across the docling/marker/unstructured → markdown boundary. Either keep a separate per-span method/confidence record alongside OKF's document-level vocabulary, or state plainly that §4.5 is being cut down to what OKF covers. Do not do it by accident.

A note on the pre-registered falsifier, since I was asked to judge it. It was GENUINE, not decorative: conditions (a) and (c) were real, searchable, and stated before the search; (c) came back clean and the researcher accepted the 'I may be wrong in the other direction' framing honestly rather than quietly dropping it; and it named residual risks it could not close (Roam, Typora, Google Docs round-trip fidelity). But it was under-powered in exactly two places, and both failures ran in the flattering direction — the same one-directional bias §9.1 documents. (a) was tested by finding A library rather than by checking the library does the SAME thing: a line count and one quoted comment substituted for reading 182 lines, and the production attribution was never checked against hypothesis/client's package.json — a single curl. (c) was tested with three conjunctive repo-name searches and three guessed npm package names; one obvious query, `markdown flavors comparison`, refutes it. The falsifier was written in good faith and executed too cheaply. The additional negatives the brief demanded were also genuine and well-chosen — C6's 'authors do not feel the pain, only the app does' and C7's 'the byte figure does not reproduce' both argue against the researcher's own program.

result.area: Adversarial verification of "Rendering — what frontmatter can render that nobody does, and what it must refuse". I re-derived every corpus number from the pinned manifest with my own script, re-implemented parseFrontmatter/stringifyFrontmatterDoc independently, re-ran the 12-language fence probe through a FULLER pipeline than the researcher used, re-measured mermaid 11.15.0 config override under jsdom, and re-fetched GitHub's /markdown API, github/docs, and all cited GHSAs via authenticated curl.

verdicts.claim: C1 — The pinned corpus reproduces: 1,084 files / 25,548,765 bytes, all 1,084 sha256 digests match the manifest.
verdicts.reason: My own script over docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json printed `files_seen 1084 missing 0 bytes 25548765 hash_ok 1084 hash_bad 0` — digit-for-digit identical to the researcher's line. Manifest declares corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… with total_files 1084 / total_bytes 25548765 across roots md(756, head 02c22ec4)/knowledge(272, head 464eb666)/frontmatter(56, head 798ebbf3).
verdicts.correction: Provenance gap, not a claim defect: I could not re-derive the corpus_id digest itself. Two obvious constructions over `root/path\tsha256` lines gave sha256:0cbbdbd4… (sorted) and sha256:2284b06e… (as-is), neither matching 3a010b16…. The manifest asserts the id; the file-level reproduction is what actually anchors every downstream number, and that is exact.

verdicts.claim: C2 (HEADLINE) — A no-op round trip through parseFrontmatter → stringifyFrontmatterDoc changes 623 of the 737 corpus files with an editable frontmatter map (84.5%), total |byte delta| 46,732; taxonomy 421 respaced / 197 reflowed line count / 5 separator-only; moves line numbers in 26.7%.
verdicts.reason: I re-implemented both functions from src/modules/preview/presentation/frontmatter.ts against the repo's own yaml 2.9.0 and ran them over all 1,084 pinned files. Output: hasEditableMap 737, changed 623, unchanged 114, pct 84.5, absByteDelta 46732, tax {yaml_same_lines_respaced:421, yaml_reflowed_line_count:197, yaml_identical_sep_or_body:5}. 421+197+5=623 ✓. The sample diff reproduces: md/Daily/2026-05-26.md `tags: [daily]` → `tags: [ daily ]`. corpus_id sha256:3a010b16….
verdicts.correction: The researcher UNDERSTATED its own finding. "Moves line numbers in 26.7%" is 197/737 — but 197 counts only YAML-block reflow. The WHOLE-FILE line count changes in 226/737 = 30.7%, because stringifyFrontmatterDoc also normalizes the separator to `---\n\n${body}`, shifting lines in 29 further files. True line-number blast radius is 30.7%, not 26.7%. This is the first anti-flattering arithmetic error I have found in this program and it is positive evidence the number was measured rather than advocated.

verdicts.claim: C3 — The 84.5% is the internal reproduction of the DesktopCommanderMCP #440 defect the plan cites as an external cautionary tale.

new_defects: ND1 (serious, design-breaking) — DESIGN (3) is self-destructive as written. It proposes moving createRehypeHtmlPolicy to the END of the rehype chain AND adding `style` to sanitizeProperties. But scrubHtmlNode (html-policy.ts:180-190) replaces any element not in SAFE_HTML_ELEMENTS with a TEXT node, and I measured that katex 0.17.0 emits `math, semantics, mrow, msup, mfrac, mi, mn, annotation` — none of which are in that 74-element set — plus 13 inline `style=` attributes per expression that carry its entire layout. Running the policy last would text-ify every MathML node; worse, KaTeX-generated nodes have no `position`, so literalSourceForNode returns undefined and the fallback emits `<math>…</math>` as escaped literal junk. Both halves of (3) must first allowlist the MathML element set and exempt KaTeX spans from the style filter, or math rendering breaks. verdicts.claim: C1: 99.69% of 4,538 Docusaurus ::: directive uses are among the 9 vendor-shipped keywords; all 14 exceptions are the tutorial that teaches extension.
verdicts.reason: Every NUMBER reproduces to four significant figures under an independently-written census. I fetched facebook/docusaurus myself (1,618 files / 10,762,714 bytes vs their 1,617 / 10,760,035 — same-day branch drift). Their methodology was strict-line-start + fence-aware, which I recovered by testing four variants: strict+fence-aware gives 980 files (EXACT match), 12 distinct names (EXACT), 99.69% (EXACT), and exactly 14 exceptions with exactly their names and counts (my-custom-admonition 12, unusedDirective 1, NotAContainerDirective 1). grep confirms all 14 sit in markdown-features-admonitions.mdx and its versioned copies. The vendor set is verbatim-exact from packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/remark/admonitions/index.ts. What does NOT hold is the inference: 'the single largest authored directive corpus in existence PROVES the DEMAND is for a big vendor-shipped vocabulary.' This is a VENDOR's own monorepo — structurally the least likely place on earth to find third-party vocabulary invention, since Docusaurus's own docs would naturally use only its own defaults. A vendor-repo measurement cannot establish market demand. 'Largest in existence' is also an unverifiable superlative.
verdicts.correction: Measurement CONFIRMED exactly. Restate as: 'In Docusaurus's own repository, 99.69% of directive uses are vendor keywords and every exception is the extension tutorial' — a statement about the vendor's authoring practice, not about market demand. Third-party demand is not measured by this corpus.

verdicts.claim: C2: Given a syntax permitting an arbitrary type name, ~850 independent third-party authors invented exactly zero types.
verdicts.reason: The MEASUREMENT is flawless — I reproduced it exactly, including the byte total. 847 files / 7,733,433 bytes (EXACT, once I found their 'depth 3' means find -maxdepth 4); 74 callouts outside fences in 18 files = 2.13% (EXACT); distinct types = 5, histogram [NOTE 45, WARNING 11, IMPORTANT 10, TIP 4, CAUTION 4] (EXACT); ::: directives = 1 (caution) (EXACT); Hugo 0, MyST 0, ^block-id 0 (EXACT); {#id} 6 in 1 file (EXACT). But the inferential base is misstated by ~47x. I resolved each file to its owning package: the corpus spans 663 distinct packages, and only 18 of them use the syntax at all. So the number of independent authors who faced the choice and declined to invent is 18, not ~850. 847 is a FILE count being presented as an AUTHOR count — the 'rate confused with an absolute count' defect. Statistically this matters: with n=74 uses the 95% upper bound on the invention rate is 3.97% (their falsifier's ~5% threshold is met, narrowly); with n=18 authors it is 15.33%, and P(0 inventions | 18 authors, true rate 5%) = 0.397, so a null result here is unsurprising even if invention were common.
verdicts.correction: Restate as: 'Of 663 packages, 18 used GitHub alert syntax at all; across their 74 uses, zero types outside GitHub's built-in 5 appeared. 95% upper bound on the invention rate is 3.97% per use.' The 'zero inventions' finding survives at the USE level (which is how the falsifier was worded); the '~850 authors' framing does not.

verdicts.claim: C4: JSON-LD is a counterexample to D9 — the spec permits an embedded @context, which is safe because it is a closed term->IRI map with no execution, no dereference, no recursion.
verdicts.reason: The primary read is impeccable — I fetched w3c/json-ld-syntax index.html (578,006 bytes, EXACT byte match) and both quotes are verbatim: 'The value of @context MUST be null, an IRI reference, a context definition, or an array composed of any of these' and 'Contexts can either be directly embedded into the document (an embedded context) or be referenced using a URL.' The D9 counterexample is REAL and the correction to denotation-vs-procedure is well-taken. But the SAFETY inference is refuted by the same document. JSON-LD 1.1 defines @import, and the spec says: 'A context definition MUST be a map whose keys MUST be either terms, compact IRIs, IRIs, or one of the keywords @base, @direction, @import, ...' and 'By using the @import keyword in a context, another remote context, referred to as an imported context, can be loaded and modified prior to processing' and 'If the context definition contains the @import keyword, its value MUST be an IRI reference.' So an EMBEDDED context definition may legally contain @import and thereby dereference a remote IRI at processing time. 'Closed' and 'no dereference' are both false. 'No recursion' is only true by explicit rule ('the imported context cannot include an @import entry') — bounded at depth 1, not structurally absent. The assertion that this is 'exactly the class the established evidence measured safe (140/140)' is therefore unsupported, and 'JSON-LD carries only denotations and has no equivalent CVE class' understates a real remote-fetch vector.
verdicts.correction: D9's correction to denotation-vs-procedure survives. Drop the safety justification: an embedded JSON-LD context is NOT closed and CAN dereference via @import. The MDMAX design's own rule ('no URL fetched at parse time, ever') is what makes its embedded denotations safe — JSON-LD does not supply that guarantee and should not be cited as if it did.

verdicts.claim: C5: Vim's modelinestrict is the transplantable rule — a file may LOWER its own capability, never RAISE it, with everything outside a 24-item inert allowlist silently ignored.
verdicts.reason: The load-bearing design rule verifies verbatim from primary source (raw.githubusercontent.com/vim/vim/master/runtime/doc/options.txt). Exact matches: "'modelinestrict' 'mlst' boolean (default: on)"; 'When on, only a safe subset of options can be set from a |modeline|'; 'Any other option set from a modeline will be silently ignored. This option cannot be set from a |modeline| or in the |sandbox|, for security reasons'; and the whole asymmetry paragraph including 'This lets a file disable further modeline processing for itself.' Also confirmed: 'No other commands than "set" are supported, for security reasons' (line 728), 'disable modelines before editing untrusted text' (line 736), and modelineexpr default off. I verified both commits with the GitHub API: 4c2879471 = 2026-04-14 'patch 9.2.0350: Enabling modelines poses a risk' and 439722711 = 2026-05-18 'patch 9.2.0499: modeline: allow to disable modelines with modelinestrict' — SHAs, dates and subjects all exact. One number does not reproduce: the allowlist is 21 options, not 24 (stated twice). I extracted and counted them: autoindent, cindent, commentstring, expandtab, filetype, foldcolumn, foldenable, foldmarker, foldmethod, modifiable, readonly, rightleft, shiftwidth, smartindent, softtabstop, spell, spelllang, tabstop, textwidth, varsofttabstop, vartabstop.
verdicts.correction: Change '24-item/24-option allowlist' to '21-option allowlist' in both places. Also drop 'all presentation-only': 'filetype' fires FileType autocommands (which load ftplugins), and 'modifiable'/'readonly' are buffer state, not presentation.

verdicts.claim: C7: The pinned corpus is 59.19% OKF-v0.2-conformant, not the ~75% a regex census reports; the 16pp gap is entirely the broken-YAML files, and the regex reports 12 distinct type values.
verdicts.reason: All load-bearing numbers reproduce exactly: regex proxy ^type:\s*\S gives 798 = 75.21% (EXACT); true js-yaml parse requiring §11.1 AND §11.2 gives 628 = 59.19% (EXACT); the type histogram matches item-for-item (synthesis 195, skill 184, workflow 184, concept 33, entity 13, map 13, strategy 2, architecture 2, report 1, question 1). The mechanism is confirmed arithmetically: 798 - 628 = 170, exactly the throw count, so the gap IS the broken-YAML files and the regex inflates 'synthesis' from 195 to 365. I fetched the real OKF v0.2 spec (the local Wiki/SPEC.md in openknowledge-sh is a v0.1 pinned copy with different numbering; the v0.2 is at GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/main/okf/SPEC.md) and §11 reads verbatim as quoted. TWO sub-claims fail. First, 'not the 12 the regex reports': the regex reports 10, not 12 — I tested three scopes (frontmatter body, whole file, first 50 lines) and all three give exactly 10 distinct values. The regex inflates COUNTS, not the distinct-value count. Second, framing: §11 defines conformance as a BUNDLE property ('A bundle is conformant with OKF v0.2 if: 1. EVERY non-reserved .md file...'), so a per-file rate is not a conformance percentage — as a bundle the pinned corpus is 0% conformant, and 59.19% is the per-file satisfaction rate.
verdicts.correction: Delete 'not the 12 the regex reports' — both methods yield 10 distinct values; the regex distortion is in the counts (synthesis 195 -> 365), which is a cleaner statement of the same point. Say '59.19% of non-reserved files satisfy §11.1+§11.2' rather than 'the corpus is 59.19% conformant'.
