verdicts.reason: The round-trip is exact: '[//]: # (fm:vocab sgnk/v1)' becomes '[//]: # "fm:vocab sgnk/v1"' — parens to quotes, precisely as claimed, which does disqualify one of the two carriers previously reported invisible in 24/24. The 2,400x figure checks out and I re-derived it: it refers to fence-meta occupancy, 48.008% (Docusaurus) / 0.01997% (Corpus B) = 2,404x; my own corrected measurement gives 46.80%/0.02017% = 2,320x, same order. Fence-meta reproduces well: 0 of 7,721 fences in the pinned corpus (their 0 of 7,714 — the key figure, zero, is exact), 1 of 4,958 in Corpus B with the value 'npm2yarn' (EXACT), and in Docusaurus the top meta values match (title="docusaurus.config.js" 2,126 vs their 2,136; title="sidebars.js" 408 EXACT). Link-title numerator 23 in the pinned corpus is exact. ONE sub-figure is wrong: 'link reference definitions are 9 occurrences in 9 files (0.83%) of the pinned corpus.' Those 9 matches are all INSIDE fenced code blocks. Fence-aware, the pinned corpus has 0 link reference definitions in 0 files = 0.00%. I verified both readings: raw gives exactly 9/9/0.83%, fence-aware gives 0/0/0.00%. This is inconsistent with C1 and C2, which were both fence-aware.
verdicts.correction: Pinned-corpus link-reference-definition occupancy is 0.00% (0 files), not 0.83% (9 files). The error runs AGAINST the researcher's own recommendation — it made their preferred carrier look more occupied than it is — so the carrier ranking is unaffected and slightly strengthened.

verdicts.claim: C10: remark-lint-frontmatter-schema already ships the exact mechanism at 36,745 downloads/week with the precedence question answered, so MDMAX should adopt $schema and the novelty claim is dead.
verdicts.reason: Fully verified against primary sources. api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/2026-07-24:2026-07-30/remark-lint-frontmatter-schema returns exactly 36,745 for start 2026-07-24 end 2026-07-30. The README (raw.githubusercontent.com/JulianCataldo/remark-lint-frontmatter-schema/master/README.md, 17,982 bytes) contains all quoted strings verbatim: line 235 'relative to project root, thanks to the `$schema` key', line 240 the example "'$schema': content/creative-work.schema.yaml", line 261 'Locally defined **`$schema` takes precedence** over global settings below', and line 28 '- **Global patterns** or **in-file** schemas associations'. Every quote is accurate. This claim is also notable as an act against interest: it kills the area's own novelty claim rather than defending it.
verdicts.correction: None.

verdicts.claim: Pre-registered falsifier honesty: did the researcher genuinely look for its own falsifier?
verdicts.reason: Yes, and this is a materially different posture from the prior 18-area run's 100%-flattering defect rate. Evidence of genuine search: (i) they deliberately fetched the two corpora most likely to refute them, and I confirmed both are real and behave as described; (ii) they recorded MyST as a caveat that contradicts a naive reading of their own 12-term cap — a concession against interest, and my independent count (66 roles in 28.24% of 432 files vs their 46 in 25.75% of 431) is in the same shape with 'ref' dominant and all top roles built-in; (iii) for falsifier (b) they found a genuine hit and let it kill their own novelty claim; (iv) they explicitly labelled their weakest link; (v) the $schema-zero search reproduces exactly (0 hits across all 3,197 files, and 1,084+847+1,266 = 3,197 checks out); (vi) two of their errors UNDERSTATE against their own interest (OKF collisions ~38% when true is 42.9%; pinned linkref 0.83% when true is 0.00%). The direction of the defects I found is mixed rather than uniformly flattering, which is the signature of noise rather than a reward function. One genuine miss: Quarto's per-document filters: key falls within falsifier (b)'s scope and they had the Quarto docs in hand, quoting only the _extensions/ line that supported them.
verdicts.correction: Falsifier (b)'s null is weaker than presented: of the 3,197 files, only 2,081 have a frontmatter block at all, and Corpus B contributes just 3 frontmatter blocks to that 847 — so the npm third of the search was near-vacuous as evidence about frontmatter keys.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN: vocabulary declaration must live per-project, never per-file; and every markdown-adjacent system (Quarto, Sphinx, MkDocs, Pandoc, R Markdown) refused document-declared resolution.
verdicts.reason:
Quarto — a system the researcher cites approvingly for its _extensions/ vendoring — ALSO ships a per-document frontmatter declaration that names an extension and executes it. From quarto-web/docs/extensions/filters.qmd, verbatim: 'If you've developed a filter and want to use it within a document you need to add it to the list of `filters` for the document', with the worked example showing document frontmatter '---
title: "Fancy-header Example"
filters:
  - fancy-header
---' resolving to _extensions/fancy-header/ whose _extension.yml contributes fancy-header.lua — a Lua procedure that runs on the AST between reader and writer. The spec text is explicit that the value is 'the name of the extension, not the filename of the filter'. That is document-declared, per-file, capability-naming resolution in a shipping, widely-used markdown-family tool. The researcher had this source and quoted only the reproducibility line from the same docs set. Two framings are therefore wrong: 'per-project, never per-file' as a description of prior art, and Q3's 'every markdown-adjacent system... refused document-declared registry resolution' (narrowly true only for REMOTE registries — Quarto resolves locally, with no network).
verdicts.correction: Quarto instantiates the researcher's OWN proposed rule almost exactly: a document NAMES a procedure, resolution is filesystem-only, no network, extensions vendored into the repo. This is prior-art support for the design, not a threat to it — but it must be cited honestly. Restate as: 'per-file declaration exists in the wild (Quarto filters:) and is safe precisely because resolution is local and vendored; MDMAX chooses per-project as a further restriction, not because per-file is unprecedented.'

survived: C1 measurement: Docusaurus 99.69% vendor-keyword share, 980 files, 12 distinct names, exactly 14 exceptions with exactly the names my-custom-admonition(12)/unusedDirective(1)/NotAContainerDirective(1), all located in markdown-features-admonitions.mdx. Reproduced to four significant figures with an independently-written fence-aware census; the 9-keyword vendor set is verbatim-exact from the plugin source.

C2 measurement: Corpus B is 847 files / 7,733,433 bytes EXACTLY; 74 callouts outside fences in 18 files (2.13%); exactly 5 distinct types [NOTE 45, WARNING 11, IMPORTANT 10, TIP 4, CAUTION 4]; zero invented types; ::: = 1, Hugo = 0, MyST = 0, ^block-id = 0, {#id} = 6 in 1 file. Every figure exact.

C3 in full: OKF bundles 186/29/902/149 = 1,266 md; distinct type values 5/0/5/21; union 29; the reference/Reference, function-family and guide-family collisions; 58 frontmatter keys across 149 files including the Claude-Code agent keys; okf_version absent in 2 of 4, '0.1' in 2, zero at 0.2. Collisions are in fact WORSE than reported (9/21 = 42.9% vs their conservative >=8 / ~38%).

C6 in full: corpus integrity 1,084 present / 0 missing / 0 hash mismatches against corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...; 23 reserved; 1,061 non-reserved; 899 = 84.73% with delimiters; 729 = 68.71% parse to a mapping; 170 throw; 170/899 = 18.91%. The quoted failing line is verbatim; gray-matter 4.0.3 throws the exact quoted string including 'line 24, column 73'; the silent-corruption variant yields exactly {"entities":[[["A"]],[["B"]]]}.

C7 load-bearing numbers: regex proxy 798 = 75.21%; true parse 628 = 59.19%; 10 distinct type values with an item-for-item matching histogram; and the mechanism confirmed arithmetically since 798-628 = 170 = the throw count exactly. OKF v0.2 §11 and §4.1 quotes verbatim-exact from the upstream GoogleCloudPlatform spec.
C8: '> [!NOTE]' -> '> \\[!NOTE]' reproduces byte-for-byte, as does the [!REVIEW] case, and all seven claimed round-trip-IDENTICAL carriers hold exactly. remark-parse = 45,820,243/wk exact.

C9 headline: the [//]: # idiom converts parens to quotes on write, exactly as claimed; and the 2,400x occupancy spread re-derives (48.008/0.01997 = 2,404x), with fence-meta 0 in the pinned corpus and exactly 1 ('npm2yarn') in Corpus B.
C10 in full: 36,745 downloads/week exact for the stated window, and all four README quotes verbatim-exact including the precedence rule.
C5 core: the Vim lower-never-raise asymmetry, the silent-ignore rule, the sandbox prohibition, the 'set'-only restriction, and both commit SHAs with exact dates and subjects.

All OKF spec citations: §11 conformance text, §4.1 'Producers MAY include any additional keys' and 'Type values are not registered centrally', §11's MUST-NOT-reject list, §10's 'it does not execute anything itself', and §12's 'Considered and deferred' list naming the runtime protocol, attester ABI, portability and sandboxing.

The core recommendation — ship no declaration syntax/registry/library-import in v1 and ship vocabulary inference plus drift detection instead. Nothing I found undermines it; the three defect classes it targets all have live positives I independently confirmed (case/morphology drift in jkroepke, the 18.91% unparseable blocks, and the silent nested-array destruction).
killed: C2's headline framing '~850 independent third-party authors invented exactly zero types' and the top-line '847 independently-authored npm docs use exactly GitHub's 5 built-in callout types'. The corpus spans 663 distinct packages and only 18 used the syntax at all. The inferential base is 18 authors / 74 uses, not ~850 — a file count presented as an author count, overstating the evidence ~47x. At n=18 the 95% upper bound on the invention rate is 15.33% and P(0 inventions | true rate 5%) = 0.397.

C5's '24-item / 24-option allowlist', stated twice. The allowlist is 21 options; I extracted and enumerated them. Also 'all presentation-only' is wrong — 'filetype' fires FileType autocommands that load ftplugins, and 'modifiable'/'readonly' are buffer state.

C7's parenthetical 'not the 12 the regex reports'. The regex reports 10 distinct values under all three scopes I tested (frontmatter body, whole file, first 50 lines). The regex distorts COUNTS (synthesis 195 -> 365), not the distinct-value count.

C9's 'link reference definitions are 9 occurrences in 9 files (0.83%) of the pinned corpus'. All 9 matches sit inside fenced code blocks. Fence-aware the true figure is 0 occurrences in 0 files = 0.00% — methodologically inconsistent with C1 and C2, which were both fence-aware.

C4's safety inference that an embedded @context is 'a closed term->IRI map — no execution, no dereference, no recursion' and 'has no equivalent CVE class'. The same spec permits @import as a key in a context definition, whose value 'MUST be an IRI reference' and which loads 'another remote context'. Embedded contexts are neither closed nor dereference-free; recursion is bounded by an explicit rule, not structurally absent.

The DESIGN's 'per-project, never per-file' as a claim about prior art, and Q3's 'every markdown-adjacent system (Quarto, Sphinx, MkDocs, Pandoc, R Markdown) refused document-declared registry resolution'. Quarto accepts 'filters:' in a single document's frontmatter, naming an extension that resolves to and executes a Lua filter.

C8's label 'the 45.8M-downloads/week markdown WRITER'. 45,820,243 is remark-parse, the parser. The writer is mdast-util-to-markdown at 44,940,019/wk (remark-stringify 33,387,232/wk). Immaterial to the conclusion but it is a number attached to the wrong package.
C1's inference that a vendor's own monorepo 'PROVES the DEMAND' for a vendor-shipped vocabulary, plus the unverifiable superlative 'the single largest authored directive corpus in existence'.
new_defects: PRIOR ART MISSED, and it is the most consequential finding here: Quarto ships per-document capability declaration. quarto-web/docs/extensions/filters.qmd, verbatim: 'If you've developed a filter and want to use it within a document you need to add it to the list of `filters` for the document', with the worked example placing 'filters:\n  - fancy-header' in a single .qmd's frontmatter, resolved against _extensions/fancy-header/_extension.yml which contributes fancy-header.lua — a procedure executed on the Pandoc AST. The researcher cited Quarto's _extensions/ vendoring rationale from the same documentation set while omitting this. It does not threaten the headline; it instantiates the researcher's own denotation-vs-procedure rule (name a procedure, resolve locally, never fetch) and should be cited as supporting prior art rather than contradicted by omission.

Unreproducible provenance hash: Corpus B's selection_sha256=21ace73c... matches neither a sha256 over the sorted relative path list nor over concatenated file contents. The selection itself IS recoverable — file count 847 and byte total 7,733,433 both match exactly under `find node_modules -maxdepth 4 -name '*.md'` — but the hash recipe is unstated, so the stated digest cannot be verified by a third party. Also, 'to depth 3' is off by one relative to find semantics (it is -maxdepth 4).

Denominator inflation in falsifier (b): '3,197 files' is the file count, but only 2,081 of them contain a frontmatter block at all, and Corpus B contributes just 3 frontmatter blocks despite supplying 847 to the total. The npm third of the $schema search was near-vacuous as evidence about frontmatter keys. The null result is correct (I reproduced 0 hits across all three corpora) but is much weaker than the 3,197 figure implies.

Category slide in C3's framing: 'Where a spec FORCED a declaration, four real bundles produced drift, not vocabulary.' OKF forces a per-document type ASSIGNMENT (§4.1: type is REQUIRED); it provides no vocabulary DECLARATION mechanism at all and explicitly declines to police the field (§4.1 'Type values are not registered centrally'). So the measured drift is what you get in the ABSENCE of a declaration mechanism. That observation is equally consistent with 'declare a vocabulary to prevent drift' as with 'detect drift after the fact' — it does not discriminate between the two remedies. The recommendation to ship detection first survives on cost grounds (~2 days, zero new bytes), not on this evidence.

Bundle-vs-file conformance conflation: OKF §11 defines conformance as a property of a BUNDLE ('A bundle is conformant with OKF v0.2 if: 1. EVERY non-reserved .md file...'). A per-file satisfaction rate of 59.19% therefore does not make the corpus '59.19% conformant' — as a bundle it is 0% conformant, and 'interop is nearly free' overstates accordingly. The gap-to-100% analysis is still correct and useful.

Minor: MyST figures do not reproduce precisely — I measure 66 distinct roles in 122 of 432 files (28.24%) against their 46 roles in 25.75% of 431 files. Definitional (my role regex is broader) and same-day branch drift; the qualitative conclusion that the dominant roles (ref 716, term, numref, abbr, kbd) are all Sphinx/MyST built-ins holds, so the caveat as recorded is sound.

Minor: ':::tip round-trips IDENTICAL' is true but for a reason worth stating — with no directive extension loaded, remark parses it as an inert paragraph. Inertness is the survival mechanism, which supports the carrier argument, but the test does not demonstrate that a directive-aware pipeline preserves it.

result.area: The strongest case that MDMAX should not be built (designated opposition, final research gate)
result.headline: Four of MDMAX's six capabilities have working substitutes I executed today — a 30-line LCS diff resolves 86.658% of block re-anchoring on the pinned corpus with 77.297pp provably unambiguous, stock mdast offsets splice byte-perfectly on 1,080/1,080 files, `yaml`'s already-installed Document API fixes the only compiler capability that maps to a ranked user pain (#13 of 14), and Google's OKF v0.2 ships provenance/trust/staleness — so the defensible engine is a ~600-line library subordinate to the editor, not a compiler program that has produced 6,233 doc lines to 365 code lines in its entire three-day existence.
result.falsifier:
PRE-REGISTERED, three conditions, written before I ran the substitute measurements. My headline is wrong if: (F1) the LCS-diff baseline resolves materially LESS of the anchoring population than content-hash-alone, i.e. the diff is not actually a substitute; (F2) the diff's resolvable population systematically excludes the case comments need — arbitrary-interval drift, not consecutive revisions; (F3) the founders' own demand corpus evidences commenting/compiler capability at rough parity with real-time collaboration.

WHAT I FOUND WHEN I LOOKED. (F1) REFUTED — I ran it. LCS 86.658% vs hash-alone-unique 77.297% on the same 29,217 anchorable block-versions; the diff strictly dominates and additionally eliminates the entire ambiguous-duplicate class (9.727% of block-versions) that the plan's S2 soft-context scorer exists to handle. (F2) FIRED, PARTIALLY, AND I AM REPORTING IT AGAINST MYSELF — my 394 revision pairs have a median inter-revision gap of 20.476 days and are bulk-commit boundaries, not editor sessions. I did NOT measure a 6-month/40-revision arbitrary interval, and the only production data that does — arXiv 1512.06195, which I read directly — says 22% of 20,953 Hypothes.is highlighted-text annotations can no longer be attached. So my headline is established for the in-app and consecutive-revision case and is NOT established for the archival case. If frontmatter's comments are long-lived across many revisions, the diff-substitute argument weakens and MDMAX's residual value is real. (F3) REFUTED — in the two demand-corpus JSONs, real-time collaboration appears in 138 string leaves vs 20 for commenting/track-changes and 2 for provenance, a 6.9:1 gap. The demand evidence is even more lopsided against the compiler than I predicted.

Net: one of three falsifiers fired partially. I have narrowed the headline accordingly — it says "consecutive-revision and in-app", not "all anchoring".

findings.claim: In the entire engine program window (5ff90a4^..HEAD, 2026-07-29 → 2026-08-01, 16 commits) the repo gained 6,233 lines of documentation and 365 lines of src/test — a 17.1:1 doc-to-code ratio — and not one of the 365 code lines is engine work.
findings.evidence: `git diff --numstat 5ff90a4^..HEAD` bucketed by path: `docs +6233 -0`, `src/test +365 -26`, `other +0 -0`. 6233/365 = 17.08. The src/test delta is exactly five files: `M src/modules/graph/presentation/graph-data.ts`, `M src/modules/vault/infrastructure/search-index.ts`, `M test/graph/graph-data.test.ts`, `A test/preview/html-policy-xss.test.ts`, `M test/vault/search-index.test.ts` (`git diff --name-status 5ff90a4^..HEAD -- src test`). Zero files in shipped `src/` contain the strings mdmax, re-anchor, reanchor, block identity, degradation certificate, provenance, or normalize(text) (grep -ril over src/, counts 0/0/0/0/0/0/0).

findings.claim: The plan's own self-criticism understates the problem: 13 of 20 commits — not 12 — touch only paths under docs/ or *.md/*.pdf, and only 8 src+test files have been added in the repo's entire history since the app was cloned.
findings.evidence: Per-commit file classification over `git log -20`: 798ebbf 3/3, 88a92f4 3/3, 8c0a426 5/5, 9055884 1/1, 525ad98 1/1, c565be9 1/1, f60eac0 1/1, c847f62 1/1, 575768e 1/1, ae81971 1/1, 57411a1 1/1, 33d1b3c 1/1, 5ff90a4 22/22 = 13 commits at 100% docs. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 0c1b427 | grep -E '^(src|test)/' | wc -l` = 309; same at HEAD = 317; `git diff --name-status 0c1b427..HEAD -- src test | grep '^A' | wc -l` = 8. docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §9.8 says '12 of 20 commits are docs'; the correct figure is 13, and the correction runs against the plan.

findings.claim: KILL GATE K1 FIRES. A textbook LCS alignment — what `git diff` already computes, ~30 lines, zero tuned parameters, zero configuration sweep — resolves 86.658% of anchorable block-versions on consecutive real revision pairs, of which 77.297 percentage points are matches on text that occurs exactly once in the old document and therefore CANNOT be wrong. Content-hash-alone resolves 77.297%. The diff strictly dominates the simplest MDMAX strategy and absorbs the entire ambiguity class S2 exists for.
findings.evidence: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, `md` root at head 02c22ec47a3a73fb25a14b11be233ad3d00a8b48. Script $TMPDIR/mdxopp/lcsrisk.mjs over 394 consecutive changed revision pairs, 29,217 anchorable block-versions (anchorable = not thematicBreak, >=3 tokens after NFC+collapse+lowercase, contains a letter or digit — the plan's own §4.1 gate): {"lcs_matched":25319,"pct_matched":86.658,"lcs_matched_on_UNIQUE_text_cannot_be_wrong":22584,"pct_of_total":77.297,"lcs_matched_on_DUPLICATE_text_at_risk":2735,"pct_of_total_at_risk":9.361}. Adding one similarity gap-fill pass takes it to 90.17% ($TMPDIR/mdxopp/diffarm.mjs: total_resolved 26345, pct 90.17); the residual 9.83% are blocks with no counterpart at all — genuinely new content that nothing can anchor.

findings.claim: I produced the token-count stratification the plan admits nobody has produced (§9.6, wf-findings-2026-08-01.md), and it shows the entire residual anchoring risk lives in blocks of ≤9 tokens: 47.0% of 3–5-token matches are on duplicate text, 0.34% of 10–19-token matches, and 0 of 13,426 matches at 20+ tokens.
findings.evidence: Same run, `by_token_bucket_matched_and_atrisk`: {"3-5":[5084,2388],"6-9":[3864,337],"10-19":[2945,10],"20+":[13426,0]}. 2388/5084 = 46.97%; 10/2945 = 0.34%; 0/13426 = 0.00%. Consequence: the anchoring invention is a short-block disambiguator. For any block a user would plausibly comment on — a paragraph, not a two-word list item — a diff is provably sufficient. corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…

findings.claim: Splice-only writing is not an engine. It is four lines using byte offsets that `mdast-util-from-markdown` — already in package.json via remark-parse — hands you for free, and it is byte-identical on 1,080 of 1,080 parseable files in the pinned corpus, under both identity round-trip and edit-then-restore.
findings.evidence: $TMPDIR/mdxopp/subs.mjs. The whole writer: `const t=fromMarkdown(src); const n=t.children[i]; return src.slice(0,n.position.start.offset)+newText+src.slice(n.position.end.offset)`. Result: {"corpus_id":"sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4","files_measured":1080,"splice_identity_roundtrip":{"byte_identical":1080,"mismatched":0,"pct":100}}. full_bytes summed to 25,548,765 — exactly the manifest's `total_bytes`, confirming my selection IS the pinned corpus. D7/§4.2's Foster TOPLAS Lemma 3.9 argument is correct and is an argument for NOT calling stringify; it is not an argument for building a compiler, because the parser already gives you the offsets.

findings.claim: The budgeted-projection ratio is overstated by 4–10×. On the pinned corpus a headings-only index tier is 14.9× smaller corpus-wide and 11.7× median per file — not the '61–152×' the consolidated plan cites, a number that appears exactly once in the repo with no derivation script anywhere.
findings.evidence: $TMPDIR/mdxopp/subs.mjs: {"index_tier_projection":{"full_bytes":25548765,"index_bytes":1712207,"corpus_ratio":14.9,"median_per_file_ratio":11.7,"n_with_headings":1079}}, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…. The claim: docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:146 'Across five corpora the index tier is 61–152× smaller'. grep for '61–152' / '152×' / '4171' across docs/engine/*.md and docs/mdmax/PLAN.md returns the assertion only, no derivation. Its single-file example DOES nearly reproduce — I get 409 top-level nodes / 78 headings / 106,298 full bytes / 4,476 index bytes / 23.75× against their 408 / 77 / 106,298 / 4,171 / 25.5× — so the method is sound and the generalisation is not. This directly weakens promise 1 of the four §6 makes to AI consumers ('Fewer tokens — 25–168×').

findings.claim: The one MDMAX capability that maps to a ranked user pain — round-trip-sacred frontmatter, pain #13 of 14, the feature the product is NAMED after — is already solved by a library sitting in package.json. `yaml@^2.9.0`'s parseDocument/set/toString preserves YAML comments, key order, quoting, an empty value, and leaves the body byte-identical. The lossy path is `gray-matter` + re-stringify, which is what the repo uses today.
findings.evidence: $TMPDIR/mdxopp/fm.mjs, run against the repo's own node_modules. gray-matter round trip of a 7-key frontmatter block: byte-identical to source: false — it drops `# a human comment about the title`, drops the trailing `# trailing note`, unquotes "My Note", rewrites `date: 2026-08-01` to `2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z`, and rewrites `empty:` to `empty: null`. yaml Document API editing one value in place: comments preserved: true / key order preserved: true / body byte-identical: true. Both libraries are current dependencies (`gray-matter: ^4.0.3`, `yaml: ^2.9.0`). This is a two-call swap, not a compiler.

findings.claim: The founders' own demand research ranks the compiler's flagship benefit 13th of 14 pain themes and characterises its audience as a niche; the top twelve are all editor and infrastructure work, and the #1 unshipped whitespace is real-time collaboration, which the plan explicitly defers.
findings.evidence: docs/FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md §1, the ranked table: row 13 is '| 13 | Markdown/frontmatter mangling | Churns the purist early adopters | Obsidian's properties UI destroys YAML comments/order; plugin exists just to undo it |'. Rows 1–12 are sync data loss, trust/shutdown fear, price backlash, slow at scale, lossy export, real-time collab, offline failures, too complex for normal people, no browser access, git-as-sync, retrieval, capture friction. Same file: 'Top 3 whitespace combinations nobody ships: 1. Real-time collab + plain markdown files + git history'. Against that, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §3: 'Deliberately deferred: backend …, mobile, real-time multiplayer.' The program defers its own #1 identified whitespace to build for its own #13 pain.

findings.claim: In 550,131 bytes of demand-side research the founders paid for, four of MDMAX's six capabilities are essentially absent. Real-time collaboration appears in 138 string leaves; commenting/track-changes/suggestion-mode in 20; provenance/lineage in 2; and both provenance hits are about export lineage, not per-span provenance.
findings.evidence: My own explicit file selection (NOT corpus_id): docs/research/frontmatter-raw-corpus.json (210,828 B, 1,853 string leaves) + docs/research/frontmatter-r2-raw-corpus.json (339,303 B, 1,951 string leaves), recursively flattened to string leaves and regex-counted. `real[- ]time|multiplayer|collaborat` → 51+87=138. `\b(inline comment|comment(ing)? (on|feature|system|thread)|leave a comment|track changes|suggestion mode)\b` → 3+17=20. `provenance|lineage` → 0+2=2, both quoted: 'The export→edit→re-import round trip destroys structure, metadata, and version lineage' and a CodiMD product description. Raw substring counts over the same files: 'block id' 0/0, 'block ref' 1/0, 'splice' 0/2, 'conformance' 0/1.

findings.claim: Google's OKF v0.2 — which I downloaded and read, 37,544 bytes, and which nobody in this program has read — makes provenance, trust, lifecycle and staleness FIRST-CLASS in plain markdown plus YAML frontmatter with no runtime. That is MDMAX §4.5 outright, plus the 'detectable staleness' promise from §6, shipped seven weeks before this gate by a repo with 8,134 stars.
findings.evidence: curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/main/okf/SPEC.md → HTTP 200, 37,544 bytes. §1: 'OKF v0.2 makes provenance, trust, lifecycle, and attestation first-class while keeping the format minimally opinionated.' §5.1 `sources` with `resource`/`id`/`author`/`usage_count`/`last_modified`; §5.2 `generated`/`verified`; §5.3 trust tiers unverified/machine-confirmed/human-reviewed; §5.5 `stale_after`; §10 attested computations. findings.claim: Outline — 39,932 stars, pushed today — ships the entire Google-Docs review loop on markdown documents with ZERO markdown compiler, by making the comment anchor a ProseMirror mark that travels inside the document model. This is the cheapest and most complete substitute for the whole MDMAX thesis, and it is open source.
findings.evidence: Read directly from raw.githubusercontent.com/outline/outline/main. server/models/Document.ts: `@Column(DataType.TEXT) text: string` (markdown), `@Column(DataType.JSONB) content: ProsemirrorData | null`, `@Column(DataType.BLOB) state?: Uint8Array | null` (Yjs). server/models/Comment.ts: `@Column(DataType.JSONB) data: ProsemirrorData`, `documentId`, `parentCommentId`, `resolvedAt`. shared/editor/marks/Comment.ts: `get name() { return "comment"; }` with `get schema(): MarkSpec { excludes: "", attrs: { id: {}, userId: {}, resolved: {...}, draft: {...} }, inclusive: false ... }` and the comment `// Allow multiple comments to overlap`. Because the range is a mark inside the CRDT, re-anchoring never happens — the anchor is transported by the same edit machinery that moves the text. The cost is that markdown becomes a projection rather than the source of truth, which is exactly the D4/D6 trade the founders must make consciously rather than by omission. Related: docmost/docmost 21,195 stars AGPL-3.0, toeverything/AFFiNE 70,960 stars, streetwriters/notesnook 14,347, hackmdio/codimd 10,124 — none built a markdown compiler.

We found that about 22% of highlighted text annotations can no longer be attached to their live Web pages. result.design:
WHAT I RECOMMEND SHIPS, AND WHAT DOES NOT.

Do not build MDMAX as a compiler program. Build `mdmax` as a single ~600-line TypeScript library inside `src/modules/`, with no CLI, no format profile, no spec, no versioned normalize(), no benchmark, and no publication — subordinate to the editor, deleted the moment the editor stops needing it. Concretely:

1. SPLICE — `spliceBlock(src, node, newText)`, four lines over `node.position.start.offset`/`end.offset` from mdast-util-from-markdown, already a transitive dependency. Verified 1,080/1,080 byte-identical on corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…. Ship today.
2. FRONTMATTER FIDELITY — replace the gray-matter parse-and-restringify path with `yaml`'s parseDocument/set/toString, already a dependency. Verified: comments, key order, quoting and body all preserved. This is pain #13 and the product's name. One day.
3. ANCHORING — three tiers in strict order, each falling back only when the previous is unavailable. (a) In-app: `ChangeSet.mapPos` from @codemirror/state, already a dependency, exact by construction. (b) Cross-revision: LCS over normalized block text, ~30 lines — measured 86.658% resolved with 77.297pp provably unambiguous, and it absorbs the whole 9.727% duplicate class. (c) Only then, content-derived re-anchoring, scoped to what my stratification shows it is actually for: blocks under ten tokens, where 47.0% of 3–5-token matches are ambiguous and 0 of 13,426 twenty-plus-token matches are. Anchor UI orphans visibly; it never guesses.
4. PROVENANCE — do not design it. Emit OKF v0.2 §5 fields (`sources`, `generated`, `verified`, `status`, `stale_after`) into frontmatter and read them back. Google specified it, an 8,134-star repo maintains it, 287 repos already consume it, and it is plain YAML.
5. `mdmax cert` — keep it, but as the ONE public artifact, because it is the only capability that survived adversarial search and it is the only output shape that cannot flatter. Ship it as a repo of fixtures plus a script, not as a product.
6. DROP ENTIRELY — the format profile, the container/mother-markdown, the doc tree, the notation library, the AI view, the near-miss reference checker, and every §13.4 'is the engine marketing or product' framing. If the engine is marketing, the demand corpus says the marketing should be about real-time collaboration, which appears in 138 demand leaves against provenance's 2.

WHAT THE TEAM SHOULD BUILD INSTEAD, IN ORDER, AND WHY IT IS AN ORDER: the S5 'editor floor' is not a parallel track, it is the product. firestore.rules already carries vaults/roles/members, immutable parent-linked revisions, and shares. Finish invites and share-link roles, then comments as Firestore sidecar threads keyed by (noteId, revisionId, quote, prefix, suffix) — a W3C TextQuoteSelector, a Recommendation since Feb 2017, not an invention — then suggestions, then presence. Real-time multiplayer is the #1 unshipped whitespace in the founders' own research and is currently deferred; that inversion is the single most expensive decision in the plan.

THE HONEST FRAMING OF THE TRADE, because the founder will ask. Outline solves this whole loop with a ProseMirror comment mark inside a Yjs document and markdown as a projection. That architecture makes anchoring vanish. frontmatter is refusing it because D4/D6 make the .md the durable artifact. That refusal is defensible and it is the only real differentiator in a category containing AFFiNE (70,960), Outline (39,932), Docmost (21,195) and Notesnook (14,347) — but it must be paid for with a small library, not a compiler program, and the founder should know he is paying for it.
result.measurement:
THE ONE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES THIS. It is not another anchoring benchmark. Run all three arms; each is pre-registered and cheap.

ARM A — ARBITRARY-INTERVAL ANCHORING (settles my own partially-fired falsifier F2, and settles K1 properly). Corpus: corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, plus a SECOND corpus somebody else wrote (~/.claude/skills-src, 474 files, git-tracked — the plan's own W1). Tasks: for every file with >=2 revisions, sample anchors at revision r and attempt resolution at r+1, r+2, r+4, r+8, and HEAD. Arms: 1 content-hash-only, 2 rigid-context k=1, 3 MDMAX S1-S3, 4 LCS-diff (my $TMPDIR/mdxopp/lcsrisk.mjs, which I will hand over), 5 LCS-diff-then-MDMAX cascade, 6 W3C TextQuoteSelector prefix/exact/suffix, 7 `{#id}` declared attributes. Verifier: hand-audit a stratified sample of 200 resolutions per arm — 50 each from the 3-5, 6-9, 10-19, 20+ token buckets, because my measurement shows the buckets behave completely differently (46.97% / 8.72% / 0.34% / 0.00% at-risk). Report correct/false/refusal per (arm, interval, bucket). n = the full 29,217 block-versions for coverage, 200/arm for audited correctness. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS: (P1) at interval r+1 arm 4 lands within 3 points of arm 3 and arm 5 is within 1 point of arm 3 — K1 fires. (P2) at HEAD-distance intervals arm 3 beats arm 4 by more than 10 points — my headline is narrowed to the in-app case and MDMAX earns the archival case. (P3) the false-match rate of every arm in the 3-5 token bucket exceeds 1%, which per K3 means comments cannot anchor short blocks at all and must orphan them by policy. (P4) arm 7 beats arm 3 on the 24.7% of headings under 3 tokens, which per K4 makes `{#id}` the honest answer for headings.

ARM B — THE DEMAND PROBE THAT COSTS NOTHING AND HAS NEVER BEEN RUN. Ship `mdmax cert` as a public repo and a 200-word post to the three Obsidian forum threads already cited in the demand corpus, plus the r/ObsidianMD collaboration threads. Pre-registered prediction: fewer than 50 stars in 30 days, because markdown-it-decorate achieved perfect silent invisibility and has 1,094 downloads/week unshipped since 2017. If it clears 500, my whole opposition case is weakened and the engine has an audience. Cost: one afternoon.

ARM C — THE THING THE PLAN CALLS W3 AND HAS RUN ZERO TIMES. Five conversations with five people who are not Sagnik or Amit, drawn from the demand corpus's own segments, asking one question: 'when you and a colleague edit a shared markdown document, what breaks?' Score answers against the 14 pain themes. Pre-registered prediction: zero of five name frontmatter mangling, per-span provenance, or renderer degradation; at least three name real-time collaboration or sync. Cost: one week of calendar, zero engineering. If this is not run before S2, the program is choosing to build against a corpus of scraped forum posts when live humans are reachable.

ORDERING RULE: Arm C first, because it is the cheapest and it can invalidate Arms A and B. Arm B second. Arm A last, and only if C says anyone cares.
result.kill_condition:
WHAT KILLS MY OWN DIRECTION — i.e. what would make me withdraw the opposition and say build the engine.

K-OPP-1. Arm A shows MDMAX's cascade beating the LCS-diff baseline by more than 10 points at HEAD-distance intervals AND frontmatter's comments turn out to be long-lived (median comment age spanning >4 revisions). Then my substitute is a substitute only for the case the product does not have, my partially-fired falsifier F2 becomes fully fired, and the engine is justified on the archival case. This is the most likely of the four and I have already conceded the mechanism.

K-OPP-2. Arm B clears 500 stars in 30 days, or `mdmax cert` finds a target disagreement that a stranger reports as having cost them real work. Then the certificate has an audience, the engine has a public artifact that is not marketing, and 'no demand for the format layer' is refuted by revealed behaviour rather than by argument. Note this is the inverse of the plan's own K5.

K-OPP-3. The hand-audit in Arm A shows the LCS-diff baseline's false-match rate above 0.5% on the 10-19 and 20+ token buckets. My case rests on 'the diff is provably right on 77.297% because the text is unique' — if monotonic LCS alignment turns out to mis-map moved blocks at a material rate even on long unique text, my 30-line substitute is unsafe for comments and MDMAX's refusal discipline is doing real work.

K-OPP-4. Someone re-derives the flagship number on the pinned corpus with a committed script and it comes out at or above 99.627% WHILE the diff-assisted arm 7 lands below 95%. That is the single result that would make the invention load-bearing rather than marginal, and it is the result the plan has been assuming for three days without producing.

WHAT DOES NOT KILL MY DIRECTION, stated so it cannot be used against it: a better-written PLAN.md; another research fan-out; a fourth handoff document; the observation that OKF does not cover block identity (I have already conceded it as negative #2); or the argument that the engine is 'marketing' — because if it is marketing, the founders' own demand corpus says it should be marketing about real-time collaboration, which the plan defers.
result.effort: Roughly four hours of tool-driven work: 6 local measurement scripts written and executed against the pinned corpus and the `md` git history (~29,217 block-versions parsed twice, 1,080 files spliced), 5 primary documents read in full or in substantial part (OKF SPEC.md v0.2 37,544 B downloaded and read; docs/mdmax/PLAN.md read end to end; docs/FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md §1; wf-findings-2026-08-01.md's adversarial section; Outline's Document/Comment/Comment-mark sources), ~35 live API calls (GitHub REST for 12 repos + 4 code/repo searches, npm registry point-downloads for 15 packages, arXiv abs page, Obsidian's 1.79 MB plugin registry and 1.85 MB stats file, raw.githubusercontent for OKF, Outline, Obsidian help and the JSON Canvas spec). Zero writes outside $TMPDIR; zero commits; zero installs. Scripts preserved at $TMPDIR/mdxopp/{pairs,diffarm,lcsrisk,subs,one,interval,fm}.mjs and should be moved into the repo under a derivation-scripts directory if any of these numbers are to be republished, per the plan's own rule P2.
result.unverified:
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, AND ITS REAL TIER.

1. ARBITRARY-INTERVAL ANCHORING — NOT MEASURED AT ALL. Everything I report is consecutive-revision. My 86.658% / 90.17% figures say nothing about an anchor stored six months and forty revisions ago. This is the load-bearing gap in my own case and I have flagged it as a partially-fired falsifier rather than hiding it. Tier: my numbers are own-measurement for the consecutive case, INFERENCE for anything beyond it.

2. CORRECTNESS OF THE DIFF BASELINE IS BOUNDED, NOT AUDITED. I proved 77.297pp of LCS matches are on text unique in the old document and therefore cannot be wrong. I did NOT hand-audit the 9.361pp on duplicate text; I assert those are positionally-consistent because LCS is monotonic, which is a property of the algorithm, not an observation. Tier: inference. A 200-case stratified audit is Arm A's job.

3. THE 99.627% IS STILL UNVERIFIED BY ME. I did not re-derive it; I have no ground-truth labels and no 294-pair manifest exists. I verified only that no derivation script exists anywhere in the repository. Tier: search-only for the absence, and the number itself remains at the tier the plan already assigns it in §9.4.

4. MY S1 REPLICATION IS PARTIAL AND SLIGHTLY OFF. My exact-normalized-match rate is 77.304% unique + 9.727% duplicate = 87.03%, against docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §4.1's 'S1 exact hash over normalize(text) resolves 87.0%'. That is the closest thing to an independent corroboration this program has, but it is over 394 of my own pair selection, not their 294, so it is suggestive rather than a replication. Tier: own-measurement of a different selection.

5. THE HYPOTHES.IS PAPER — ABSTRACT ONLY. I read the arXiv abstract page verbatim; I did not read the PDF body, so I cannot speak to its methodology, its interval distribution, or whether 22% is comparable to anything MDMAX measures. Tier: primary-read of the abstract, secondary for anything about method.

6. THE OKF SPEC — READ, NOT TESTED. I read all 37,544 bytes of SPEC.md v0.2 and quote it verbatim, but I ran no OKF tooling and validated no bundle. Its ecosystem numbers (287 repos, 206/115-star toolkits, 8,134 stars) are single GitHub API reads on 2026-08-01 and GitHub search is documented as non-exhaustive. Tier: primary-read for the spec text, search-only for adoption.

7. OBSIDIAN DOWNLOAD COUNTS ARE CUMULATIVE AND AGE-BIASED. dataview was created 2021-01-13 and hi-note 2024-12-07; my 98.6× / 105.1× / 24.9× ratios do not normalise for age, and the plan's own §16.1 declares this metric unreliable. My correction of the briefed 190× to 25–105× is therefore itself uncertain in the same direction. Tier: own-measurement of a stated-unreliable instrument.

8. THE OUTLINE ARCHITECTURE CLAIM IS FROM SOURCE, NOT FROM RUNNING IT. I read Document.ts, Comment.ts and marks/Comment.ts directly from main. I did not run Outline, did not verify that comment marks survive a markdown export round trip, and its licence resolves to NOASSERTION/'Other' (BSL-family), which materially affects whether it is usable as anything but evidence. Tier: primary-read of source, inference for behaviour.

9. THE DEMAND-CORPUS COUNTS ARE MY REGEXES OVER MY OWN FILE SELECTION — docs/research/frontmatter-raw-corpus.json and frontmatter-r2-raw-corpus.json, 550,131 bytes, 3,804 string leaves. They do NOT cite corpus_id, and I state that explicitly. Different regexes give different ratios; I chose narrow ones for commenting and broad ones for collaboration, which if anything understates my own case's gap. Tier: own-measurement, own selection, stated.

10. THE package.json INCIDENT — I OBSERVED IT, I DID NOT ATTRIBUTE IT. I know the file was 17 bytes at 08:20:51 local and carried 48 dependencies earlier in this same session. I did not identify what wrote it and I did not revert it. Tier: own-measurement for the state, unknown for the cause.

11. NOT DONE AT ALL: no live model call (the program's W2 remains at zero across every area including mine), no user conversation (W3, zero), no patent/FTO search beyond what wf-findings already recorded, and no measurement of whether MDMAX's own re-anchoring would beat my LCS baseline, because MDMAX does not exist to run.

result.area: Marketability, and the 50% that is given away — adversarial verification

verdicts.claim: HEADLINE, clause B: frontmatter's own demand research ranks T13 'Markdown/frontmatter mangling' 13th of 14 at severity 'ANNOYS'.
verdicts.reason: The primary source is in this repo and says otherwise. docs/FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md line 42 verbatim: '| 13 | Markdown/frontmatter mangling | Churns the purist early adopters | Obsidian's properties UI destroys YAML comments/order; plugin exists just to undo it |'. Line 43: '| 14 | Publishing/sharing friction | Annoys | ...'. 'Annoys' is T14's severity, not T13's. The researcher shifted the severity label down exactly one row — and in the flattering direction, because a weaker T13 is what licenses its own recommendation that the matrix 'must NOT be the marketing spearhead'. The rank (13th of 14) is correct; the severity is not. The four severity bands in the table are 'Kills adoption' / 'Churns' / 'Churns the purist early adopters' / 'Annoys', so this is a one-band overstatement of the argument, not a paraphrase.
verdicts.correction: T13 severity is 'Churns the purist early adopters' — one band above 'Annoys'. The design recommendation (do not lead marketing with the matrix) still stands on the rank and on the 'Kills adoption' cluster at 1-9, but it must be argued from 'churns purists', which is a narrower and more honest claim: T13 churns exactly the early-adopter segment a free developer tool recruits first.

verdicts.claim: Claim 1 [own-measurement]: the pinned corpus resolves on disk today — 1,084 files, 0 missing, 0 sha256 drift.
verdicts.reason: Re-derived independently by walking docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json against ~/Desktop/GitHub/{md,knowledge,frontmatter} and re-hashing every file. Output: 'declared total_files=1084 enumerated=1084 / resolved=1084 missing_on_disk=0 sha_drift=0'. Summed manifest bytes 25,548,765 equals declared total_bytes 25,548,765 exactly. Root heads match as stated (md 02c22ec4/756, knowledge 464eb666/272, frontmatter 798ebbf3/56). corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 is a live reproducible object.

verdicts.claim: Claim 2 [primary-read]: markdownguide.org already ships a free 70-tool x 28-construct support matrix; 4,090 stars, created 2017-01-31, pushed 2026-07-21.
verdicts.reason: api.github.com/repos/mattcone/markdown-guide (authenticated, 2026-08-01) returned {'stargazers_count': 4090, 'created_at': '2017-01-31T20:45:35Z', 'pushed_at': '2026-07-21T03:01:02Z'} — all three exact. GET /contents/_tools returned exactly 70 entries. This is a genuine prior-art self-report that argues against the researcher's own 'unclaimed' framing, and it made it, which is the right behaviour.
verdicts.correction: One mechanical detail is wrong and worth fixing before anyone re-runs this: the researcher describes tools.yml as containing '28 `- id: … available: y|n|p` rows'. It does not. _data/tools.yml is a top-level key->{name,link} mapping with no 'id' or 'available' keys; the y/p/n/u values live in each _tools/<tool>.md front matter. The count of 28 is right, the file structure described is not.

verdicts.claim: Claim 3 [own-measurement]: markdownguide's 28 ids contain none of frontmatter/wikilink/callout/mermaid/math/directive/attribute/embed, and 90.77% of the pinned corpus (984/1084) carries at least one.
verdicts.reason: The 28 ids I extracted from tools.yml match the researcher's list element-for-element, in order. Substring counts over tools.yml: 'frontmatter' 0, 'wikilink' 0, 'callout' 0, 'mermaid' 0, 'katex' 0, 'admonition' 0, 'directive' 0, 'transclu' 0, 'embed' 0, 'attribute' 0. Independent construct scan over corpus_id sha256:3a010b16...: frontmatter 907 = 83.67% (reproduces the researcher's 83.67% to the digit), wikilink 540 = 49.82% (vs 50.00%), union 981 = 90.50% (vs 90.77%). The 0.27pp gap is a wikilink/embed boundary definition, not an error. Arithmetic checks: 984/1084 = 90.775%.
verdicts.correction: Two caveats the researcher should have stated. (a) The detection regexes were never published, so the number is not reproducible as written — I had to reconstruct them, and they happened to land within 0.27pp; that was luck, not method. (b) One substring probe was weakly specified: 'front matter' with a space appears once in tools.yml (the file's own header comment). The conclusion is unaffected because the id list is definitive, but a falsifier that tests only the closed-up spelling of the term most likely to be written open is a soft test.

verdicts.claim: Claim 3, sub-claim: '612 files (56.5%) carry ONLY untracked constructs.'
verdicts.reason: This cannot be true and is not. Over the same corpus_id, files carrying at least one untracked construct AND zero markdownguide-tracked construct = 0, 0.00%. It must be ~0 by construction: markdownguide tracks 'headings' and 'paragraphs', and 99.54% of the corpus (1,079/1,084) contains an ATX heading while 95.94% contains a paragraph. I then tried four charitable re-readings in case the wording was loose — 'no advanced tracked construct' 454 (41.88%), 'untracked with no table or fence' 465 (42.90%), 'has both frontmatter and wikilink' 470 (43.36%), 'only frontmatter-or-wikilink among untracked' 839 (77.40%). None is 612. 612/1084 = 56.46% rounds to the stated 56.5%, so the figure came from some computation — just not the one described, and no reading I can construct reproduces it.
verdicts.correction: Delete the sub-claim. It is the strongest-sounding sentence in claim 3 ('more than half the corpus is served ONLY by constructs the incumbent ignores') and it is the one that does not survive. The claim that does survive is the union rate, which is enough.

verdicts.claim: Claim 4 [own-measurement]: markdownguide's target list omits github.com, GitLab, Confluence, Jira, Teams and Discourse; only github-pages.md exists.
verdicts.reason: Membership test over the 70 returned filenames: github.md False, gitlab.md False, confluence.md False, teams.md False, discourse.md False, jira.md False; github-pages.md True, docusaurus.md True, mkdocs.md True. Exactly as stated. This is the strongest surviving plank of the area — the (product, surface) scoping insight is intact even though the matrix idea is not novel, and the researcher correctly separated those two things.

verdicts.claim: Claim 5 [own-measurement]: a working 5-config degradation certificate was built from packages already in the repo, and it reproduces the settled carrier findings — YAML frontmatter leaks visible in 4 of 5, [//]: # destroyed 5/5, unknown fence carried 5/5, HTML comment destroyed only by the sanitized surface.
verdicts.reason: I rebuilt this from scratch rather than trusting it. All ten named packages are present locally (marked 16.4.2, remark-parse 11.0.0, remark-gfm 4.0.1, remark-frontmatter 5.0.0, rehype-raw 7.0.0, dompurify 3.4.5, jsdom 29.1.1, unified 11.0.5, remark-rehype 11.1.2, rehype-stringify 10.0.1) — no npm install needed, so the 'days not weeks' cost argument holds. My independent run over 15 constructs x 5 configs output: 'yaml_frontmatter LEAKED-VISIBLE in 4 of 5 configs', 'comment_idiom DESTROYED in 5 of 5 configs', 'unknown_fence LEAKED-VISIBLE in 5 of 5 configs', and html_comment CARRIED-INVISIBLE in the four non-sanitized configs / DESTROYED under DOMPurify. Every headline verdict matches. The demo is real and is not a mock.

verdicts.claim: Claim 6 [own-measurement]: only 2 of 15 constructs disagreed across the five configs, therefore inside a single parser ecosystem configs mostly AGREE and the free artifact's cost is the target corpus, not the code.
verdicts.reason: The direction survives; the number and the generalization do not. My comparable 15-construct run reports 'constructs where the 5 configs DISAGREE: 3/15' — the third being footnote, which splits because remark-gfm renders footnotes and marked/default and CommonMark do not. Since the researcher never published its construct list, 2/15 is not reproducible as stated. More seriously, the inference over-reaches its sample: all five configs are marked or remark — two JavaScript, CommonMark-descended libraries. That is not 'a parser ecosystem', it is one language's corner of one. The brief's own settled finding cuts against the generalization: across 24 renderer configs the HTML comment produces 8 distinct outputs and GitHub blob view deletes it. Five JS configs cannot see that spread, so 'mostly agree' is an artifact of the sample.
verdicts.correction: Restate as: within the JS CommonMark family the configs agree on 12-13 of 15 constructs, so the differentiating cost is the target corpus AND the non-JS engines (cmark-gfm, pandoc, python-markdown, kramdown) that the 24-config finding shows actually diverge. The budgeting advice — spend on targets, not on code — survives, but it must not be justified by claiming parser ecosystems agree in general.

verdicts.claim: Claim 7 [primary-read]: the hostile-input corpus give-away is refuted as a novel idea — cujanovic/Markdown-XSS-Payloads already exists, 497 stars, created 2017-05-04, pushed 2024-10-12, 41 non-empty lines / 4,400 bytes.
verdicts.reason: api.github.com returned {'stargazers_count': 497, 'created_at': '2017-05-04T12:44:35Z', 'pushed_at': '2024-10-12T12:43:36Z'} and the raw file is 4,400 bytes with 41 non-empty lines — every figure exact. This is one of the two required arguments-against and it is a real, checkable self-refutation of a candidate the area could have advocated. Correctly reported.

verdicts.claim: Claim 8 [own-measurement]: of eleven canonical free artifacts, exactly two produced an organic commercial entity, and the closest analogue took 7 years 11 months.
verdicts.reason: The timeline is exact and the framing is not. Verified: mermaid npm 'created' = 2014-12-02T17:39:42.546Z; org Mermaid-Chart created_at = 2022-11-07T15:01:04Z with blog https://mermaid.ai. I re-derived the interval: 95 months = 7y 11m (2,897 days). Exact. But the denominator fails its own evidence — the claim says ELEVEN artifacts and the evidence enumerates NINE: mermaid, Excalidraw (commercial), then prettier, DavidAnson/markdownlint, editorconfig, semver, commonmark-spec, repomix, llms-txt (not). 2/9 = 22.2%, not 2/11 = 18.2%. Separately, 'base rate' is the wrong word for a self-selected convenience sample of nine repos the researcher chose; it implies a population and a draw, and there was neither.
verdicts.correction: State it as '2 of the 9 artifacts I checked', drop the word 'base rate', and keep the 7y11m figure, which is the durable and correctly-derived part.

verdicts.claim: Claim 9 [own-measurement]: npm last-week download figures showing what the give-away actually bought (semver 826,766,167; js-yaml 280,864,032; prettier 117,403,209; marked 61,032,058; mermaid 11,828,208; markdownlint 2,886,431; gray-matter 7,492,225; repomix 75,342).
verdicts.reason: Re-fetched api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week on 2026-08-01. Every one of the eight I spot-checked returned the stated figure to the digit: semver 826766167, js-yaml 280864032, prettier 117403209, marked 61032058, mermaid 11828208, markdownlint 2886431, gray-matter 7492225, repomix 75342. Eight for eight with no rounding and no drift.

verdicts.claim: Claim 10 [own-measurement]: the 2026 distribution channel is the agent-tool surface — topic:agent-skills 12,804 repos, anthropics/skills 165,486 stars, repomix 27,551 stars ships npx + MCP + Agent Skill.
verdicts.reason: topic:agent-skills total_count = 12804, exact. repomix stars 27551, created 2024-07-13T07:11:32Z, exact. Two figures show trivial upward drift consistent with a later read, not error: topic:claude-skill 4,044 vs stated 4,043 (+1 repo), anthropics/skills 165,491 vs stated 165,486 (+5 stars). Both move in the only direction they can. The claim stands.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN: the 30-second demo is 'drop in the visitor's own README' and it 'works on 83.67% of the pinned corpus and 56.75% of an independent one, which means it works on most visitors' first file'.
verdicts.reason: This is a transfer claim across populations and I tested it directly, which the researcher did not. I fetched 40 READMEs from major repos via api.github.com (including the markdown ecosystem's own: markedjs/marked, markdown-it, remarkjs/remark, unifiedjs/unified, mermaid-js/mermaid, jgm/pandoc, commonmark/commonmark-spec, DavidAnson/markdownlint, gohugoio/hugo, jekyll, docusaurus, mkdocs-material). Result: 'READMEs fetched n=40 / starts with --- (YAML frontmatter): 0'. Zero. The 3 files matching '[[' are all false positives on inspection — '[[website repo](https://...' (a bracket before a link), "[['@babel/preset-env'" (a JS array), '[[Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.' — no wikilinks either. The two cited corpora cannot support this claim because both are populations where frontmatter is structurally mandated, not organically chosen: the md root is an Obsidian vault (properties), and every SKILL.md in the falsifier corpus requires YAML frontmatter by the Agent Skill format. Neither is a README population, and README is the file the demo asks for.
verdicts.correction: Either change the demo's default input from 'your README' to 'your note/vault file' and keep the 83.67%/56.75% claim, or keep README as the input and drop the prevalence claim entirely and lead with a construct that is actually present in READMEs (tables, task lists, HTML comments, unknown fences). As written the demo would show a visitor's README having no at-risk construct at all, which is the worst possible first impression for a tool whose pitch is 'see exactly what breaks'.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN: distribution starts with the obsidian-git threads 'where +4,800 people/day are still installing the broken thing'.
verdicts.reason: No artifact is cited for this rate anywhere in the claims block, and the artifact the design leans on cannot produce one. I pulled obsidianmd/obsidian-releases community-plugin-stats.json (6,190 plugins): obsidian-git carries downloads = 2,934,409, and the object's only keys are 'downloads', 'updated', and per-version counts — there is no time series, no date-bucketed field, nothing from which a per-day rate is derivable. A single cumulative snapshot cannot yield a daily rate. For scale: 2,934,409 spread over three years averages ~2,679/day, over two years ~4,019/day, so 4,800/day is not absurd — it is simply unevidenced, and it is presented in a design that elsewhere insists on fetched-today anchors.
verdicts.correction: Drop the rate or replace it with the cumulative figure that is actually verifiable: 'obsidian-git has 2,934,409 cumulative downloads' (source: community-plugin-stats.json). If the daily rate matters, it needs two snapshots taken days apart.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN: 'a companion Obsidian plugin, the channel Relay used to reach 176,247 installs', plus the pricing anchors ($4 Obsidian Sync, $50 Obsidian Commercial, $5 HackMD Prime, $20 Notion Business) and forum t/2049 at 246,568 views.
verdicts.reason: Every price anchor verified against the live page today. obsidian.md/pricing verbatim: 'Sync $4 USD Per user, per month, billed annually', 'Publish $8 USD Per site, per month, billed annually', and 'Commercial $50 USD Per user, per year'. hackmd.io/pricing verbatim: 'Prime ... $5 per seat/mo Total $15 /month Billed annually'. notion.com/pricing carries $20 among its figures. forum.obsidian.md/t/2049.json returns title 'Obsidian for web', views 249,616 — above the cited 246,568, and views only increase, so the earlier read is consistent. system3-relay downloads = 176,247, exact.
verdicts.correction: One metric-label error: the plugin-stats field is 'downloads', not installs, and 176,247 is cumulative downloads across all versions. Say 'downloads'. Also the cited URL ends /2049/246 (post 246) while the topic reports posts_count 244 — cosmetic, but it is the kind of detail this program has been burned by.

verdicts.claim: META: did the researcher genuinely hunt its own pre-registered falsifier, or write one it knew would not fire?
verdicts.reason: It genuinely hunted, and this is the strongest thing in the submission. F2 is not decorative: I rebuilt the falsifier corpus from scratch and got files=474, bytes=5,013,124 — matching the stated 474 / 5,013,124 exactly — then measured frontmatter 56.75%, wikilink 8.23%, union 60.13%, matching all three stated figures to the digit. The researcher ran a test that cut its headline from 90.77% to 60.13%, reported the unflattering result, and revised its own claim to a 60-91% range rather than quoting the flattering end. F3 is better still: I reproduced both sides of the self-caught regex bug. The buggy '\s*' pattern (which spans newlines and captures the next line's first word) inflates to 43.36% on my known-language list against the researcher's 41.51%; the corrected '[ \t]*' pattern collapses to 0.28% against its 0.09% — same mechanism, same magnitude, the residual gap being allowlist composition (my list lacks 'jsonc', which accounts for 4 of my 5 hits). That is a 41.51-point error caught and killed before publication, and it is exactly the LR#64 family. Against a prior run with a 100% headline defect rate always in the flattering direction, this is a real behavioural change.
verdicts.correction: The discipline is real but not uniform: it held on the corpus measurements it pre-registered and lapsed on the numbers it did not — the T13 severity quote, the 612 sub-claim, the 'eleven' denominator, and the 4,800/day rate are all in the unpre-registered remainder. The falsifier caught what it was pointed at; nothing was pointed at the design section, and every defect I found is there or in prose.

survived: Claim 1: corpus_id sha256:3a010b16... resolves 1,084/1,084 with 0 missing and 0 sha drift; summed bytes equal declared total_bytes 25,548,765 exactly. Re-derived.

Claim 2: mattcone/markdown-guide is real prior art — 4,090 stars, created 2017-01-31T20:45:35Z, pushed 2026-07-21T03:01:02Z, 70 tools, 28 constructs. All exact. Correctly self-reported as refuting the 'nobody ships a matrix' framing.

Claim 3 core: the 28 tracked ids match element-for-element; frontmatter/wikilink/callout/mermaid/math/directive/embed/attribute all appear 0 times; union prevalence over the pinned corpus reproduces at 90.50% vs the stated 90.77%, and frontmatter reproduces at 83.67% to the digit.
Claim 4: github.md, gitlab.md, confluence.md, teams.md, discourse.md, jira.md all absent from the 70; github-pages.md present. The (product, surface) scoping insight is the strongest surviving plank.

Claim 5: I rebuilt the 5-config certificate independently from the repo's own node_modules with no install. Every headline verdict reproduced — frontmatter LEAKED-VISIBLE 4 of 5, comment idiom DESTROYED 5 of 5, unknown fence carried 5 of 5, HTML comment destroyed only under DOMPurify. The demo is real.
Claim 7: cujanovic/Markdown-XSS-Payloads confirmed at 497 stars, 2017-05-04, 2024-10-12, 4,400 bytes, 41 non-empty lines. A correctly-reported self-refutation.
Claim 8's timeline: mermaid npm 2014-12-02T17:39:42.546Z to org Mermaid-Chart 2022-11-07T15:01:04Z = 95 months = 7y11m, re-derived exactly.
Claim 9: all eight npm last-week download figures spot-checked reproduce to the digit, including semver 826,766,167 and repomix 75,342.
Claim 10: topic:agent-skills 12,804 exact; repomix 27,551 stars / created 2024-07-13 exact; two figures drifted upward by +1 repo and +5 stars, the only direction they can move.

Every pricing anchor in the design: Obsidian Sync $4/user/mo billed annually, Publish $8/site/mo, Commercial $50 USD per user per year, HackMD Prime $5 per seat/mo, Notion $20 — all verified against live pages today. Relay 176,247 exact. forum t/2049 'Obsidian for web' now 249,616 views, consistent with the cited 246,568.

The falsifier work itself: F2's corpus (474 files / 5,013,124 bytes) and all three of its rates (56.75%, 8.23%, 60.13%) reproduce exactly; F3's self-caught regex bug reproduces in mechanism and magnitude on both sides (43.36% buggy vs 0.28% fixed). The researcher cut its own headline from 91% to a 60-91% range and killed a 41.51-point error before publishing.
killed: HEADLINE clause B — T13 is NOT severity 'ANNOYS'. docs/FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md line 42 says 'Churns the purist early adopters'; 'Annoys' is line 43, T14 Publishing/sharing friction. The severity label was shifted down exactly one band, in the direction that strengthens the researcher's own recommendation.

Claim 3 sub-claim — '612 files (56.5%) carry ONLY untracked constructs' is false. The true count is 0 (0.00%), and it must be ~0 because markdownguide tracks headings and paragraphs while 99.54% of the corpus carries an ATX heading. Four charitable re-readings gave 454, 465, 470, 839 — none is 612.
Claim 8's denominator — 'eleven canonical free artifacts' where the evidence enumerates nine. 2/9 = 22.2%, not 2/11 = 18.2%. Also 'base rate' is the wrong term for nine self-selected repos.

DESIGN's demo transfer claim — 0 of 40 real-world READMEs fetched from api.github.com contain YAML frontmatter, and 0 contain a wikilink (all 3 '[[' hits are false positives). The 83.67%/56.75% rates come from two populations where frontmatter is structurally mandated (Obsidian vault properties; the Agent Skill format), so they do not transfer to the README the demo asks the visitor to drop in.

DESIGN's '+4,800 people/day' obsidian-git install rate — uncited and not derivable. community-plugin-stats.json carries only cumulative downloads (2,934,409) and per-version counts, with no time series. A single snapshot cannot yield a daily rate.

Claim 6's '2 of 15 disagree' — I get 3/15 on a comparable set, and the construct list was never published so the figure is unreproducible as written. The generalization 'inside a single parser ecosystem the configs mostly AGREE' rests on five configs from two JS CommonMark-descended libraries and is in tension with the brief's settled 24-config finding that the HTML comment alone produces 8 distinct outputs.
new_defects: The two corpora are not independent evidence for organic frontmatter authoring — both structurally mandate it. The md root is an Obsidian vault (properties UI writes YAML frontmatter); every SKILL.md in the falsifier corpus requires YAML frontmatter by the Claude Agent Skill format. The researcher treated agreement between them as convergent validity when it is shared confounding. My 40-README sample is the missing third population and it returns 0%.

The falsifier corpus is 34.60% operator-authored, not the claimed 'authored mostly by Anthropic and plugin authors, not by this operator'. 164 of 474 files sit under a path containing 'sgnk-'. 'Mostly' survives at 65%, but a third of a corpus chosen specifically to test operator-idiosyncrasy is operator-written, and that was not disclosed or quantified.

Claim 3's detection regexes were never published, so every corpus number in the area is unreproducible as written. I had to reconstruct them and landed within 0.27pp — that was luck. Any measurement claim in this program should ship the predicate with the number.

'176,247 installs' is 176,247 cumulative downloads — the field in community-plugin-stats.json is literally named 'downloads' and aggregates across versions. Metric mislabel of the exact class the program has been burned by (LR#59).

Claim 2 describes tools.yml as holding '28 `- id: … available: y|n|p` rows'. It does not — _data/tools.yml is a key->{name,link} map with no id or available keys; the y/p/n/u verdicts live in each _tools/<tool>.md front matter. The count of 28 is right; anyone re-running from the stated structure will fail.

The 'frontmatter appears ZERO times' probe is weak as executed: 'front matter' with a space does appear once in tools.yml (its own header comment). The conclusion is unaffected because the id list is definitive, but testing only the closed-up spelling of a term usually written open is a soft falsifier.

Falsifier discipline was applied only where it was pre-registered. F1/F2/F3 all targeted the corpus and prevalence claims and all held up under my re-derivation. Every defect I found lives in the unpre-registered remainder — the T13 quote, the 612 sub-claim, the 'eleven' denominator, the 4,800/day rate, the README transfer. Nothing was pointed at the design section, and that is where the area is weakest.

result.area: Making a markdown file hold/convey/mean more — invisible carrier inventory, missing constructs, and the top-5 additions

verdicts.claim: C1: The orphan link reference definition has ZERO real uses in the pinned corpus; mdast `definition`, `linkReference`, `imageReference`, `footnoteDefinition`, `footnoteReference` are all absent; a loose regex finds 9 definition-SHAPED lines, all prose.
verdicts.reason: Re-derived from scratch. Corpus integrity first: verified=1084 sha_mismatch=0 missing=0 against corpus_id sha256:3a010b16… (md 756 + knowledge 272 + frontmatter 56 = 1084). My independent remark-parse 11.0.0 + remark-gfm 4.0.1 + remark-frontmatter 5.0.0 histogram returned 21 distinct node types and EVERY count matches the researcher digit-for-digit: text=334081 paragraph=142802 listItem=88434 inlineCode=76118 strong=44893 heading=28221 tableCell=25813 list=15160 emphasis=12741 tableRow=9374 code=7738 html=7720 link=5453 thematicBreak=2754 blockquote=2742 table=1150 root=1084 yaml=907 break=613 delete=444 image=16. No `definition` and none of the four reference types. The 9 definition-shaped lines reproduced exactly, all the same '  [Topic]: Review said X. Outside voice says Y.' prose in GStack/Planning skill files. Cross-validation also reproduced: CommonMark-only (remark-parse alone) gives link=1838 and image=16, matching the claimed regex cross-check. I confirmed remark CAN emit `definition` (my synthetic 999-char test produced 'paragraph,definition'), so absence is a property of the corpus, not a harness artifact.

verdicts.claim: C2: 1,431 bare angle-bracket placeholder tokens (186 distinct) in 219/1,084 files (20.2%) outside inline code, and GitHub DELETES every one of them.
verdicts.reason:
Materially reproduced by two independent methods. AST-native classification of all 7,720 mdast `html` nodes gives non-HTML5 angle tokens = 1,418 occurrences, 176 distinct names, 201 files (18.5%); my line-based regex gives 1,155 / 174 / 217 (20.0%). Researcher: 1,431 / 186 / 219 (20.2%). Decisively the same phenomenon — the top tokens match EXACTLY: one-line:102, concise:92, command:87, capability:69 (all four identical), N:235 vs their 223, name:48 vs 47. Deletion reproduced byte-for-byte on api.github.com/markdown mode=gfm: 'Run the tool with `--flag` on and then is bound.' → '

Run the tool with --flag on and then is bound.

'. I extended the test past what was claimed: the actual top corpus names, both hyphenated custom elements and capitalised ones, are all deleted — 'A B C D E F G H I.' → '

A B C D E F G H I.

'. Arithmetic re-derived: 219/1084 = 20.20%.
verdicts.correction: The file-count is the softest number in the claim (I get 201–217 vs 219 depending on masking); the occurrence count and the deletion behaviour are solid.

verdicts.claim: C3: Placeholders colliding with HTML5 tag names fail a third, worse way — three distinct failure modes, no renderer agreeing with another.
verdicts.reason:
All three GitHub Markdown API outputs reproduce VERBATIM, character for character, including the counter-intuitive parts. 'Filed new issue, added comment on existing issues.' → '

Filed new issue, added comment on existing issues.

' (the trailing double auto-close is exactly as quoted). 'Set and <base> before the run.' → '<p>Set <title> and before the run.</p>' (escape and delete in one line). 'You mentioned <Source A>, <Source B>, and <Source C>.' → '<p>You mentioned <source>, <source>, and <source>.</p>'. Corpus collision counts re-derived: <base> 66 exact, <s> 4 exact, <title> 31 (claimed 32).
verdicts.correction: '<source> 20' does not belong in that list as a bare-token count — bare `<source>` occurs 0 times in the corpus. Those 20 are real `<source …>` tags with attributes in 2 files, a different construct from the other three. Immaterial to the failure-mode argument.

All six API responses byte-identical to what was quoted. mode=gfm: 'x' → '

x

'; 'x' survives with title intact; data-fm → '

Alpha x text.

'; class identically stripped; id → 'id="user-content-payload7q"'. mode=markdown, same input → 'id="user-content-PAYLOAD7Q"'. '' → 'id="user-content-payload7q"'. Both corrections to the established finding hold, and the case-folding consequence for base64url/nanoid/ULID identifiers is real.

verdicts.claim: C5: 'fence info-string meta past the first word is dropped by every renderer' is FALSE for GitHub when the language is unknown — GitHub emits both lang= and data-meta= into sanitized HTML.

C6: The unknown-language fence survives 14/14 payload hazards byte-identically through BOTH remark-stringify and prettier, and prettier does not reformat an unknown-language body whereas it rewrites a known-language one.
verdicts.reason:
Ran the full hazard matrix myself against remark 11.0.0 / remark-gfm 4.0.1 / prettier 3.8.3: 14/14 with remark=true prettier=true across double-quote, single-quote, paren, backslash, bracket, colon-space, json, base64ish, unicode, gt-lt, ampersand, backtick, newline, blank-ish. Nesting '````fm:meta
```js
x
```
````' byte-identical through both. Known-language contrast exact: '```js fm=PAYLOAD7Q
const a=1;
```' is remark-identical but prettier emits 'const a = 1;' — which is the stated hash-invalidation hazard, and it is real.

verdicts.claim: C7: The link/definition title slot has three uncovered failure modes — raw quote destroys it, blank line destroys it, and remark/prettier normalise the delimiter to different canonical forms; only base64url, percent-encoded and backslash-escaped JSON are stable through both.
verdicts.reason:
Every sub-result reproduced verbatim. Raw-quote case: kinds='paragraph,paragraph' (parsedAsDef=false) and remark emits 'Alpha.

\[fm:k]: /a "{"a":1,"b":\[2,3]}"
' — the exact visible-escape string quoted. Blank-line-in-title likewise not a definition. Delimiter divergence exact: '[fm:k]: /u ({"id":"c3","n":1})' → remark double-quotes with backslashes, prettier single-quotes; '[a](/u "he said \"hi\"")' → prettier rewrites to "[a](/u 'he said "hi"')". All three stable forms confirmed remarkID=true prettID=true. The CI ping-pong risk is a genuine consequence.

verdicts.claim: C8: cmark-gfm caps link labels at 1000 chars, CommonMark/micromark at 999, so a 1000-char label is INVISIBLE on GitHub and VISIBLE JUNK in conformant renderers.
verdicts.reason:
All three source citations verified at the EXACT line numbers claimed. Local node_modules/micromark-factory-label/dev/index.js line 17: 'labels in markdown are capped at 999 characters in the string.' raw.githubusercontent.com/github/cmark-gfm/master/src/parser.h line 13: '#define MAX_LINK_LABEL_LENGTH 1000'. commonmark-spec/master/spec.txt line 7997: 'label can have at most 999 characters inside the square'. I then measured the behaviour, which the researcher also did: GitHub gfm returns 8 bytes ('

x

', definition consumed) at 998/999/1000 and visible junk at 1001+; remark-parse gives 'paragraph,definition' at 998/999 and 'paragraph,paragraph' at 1000+. The divergence is exactly one character wide at 1000. This is the strongest single finding in the report and it is fully sourced.

verdicts.claim: C9: 18,462 of 88,434 list items (20.9%) open with a bold run; 7,938 follow it with an explicit separator — the description-list shape.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed and, if anything, understated. The researcher's own arithmetic checks out (7938+10524 = 18462; 18462/88434 = 20.88%). My line-regex replication gave 18,701 / 7,925 — within 1.3%. I then ran the AST-native version, which removes the numerator/denominator mismatch entirely (their numerator came from a regex line scan that found 88,097–88,390 items while the denominator was the AST's 88,434): listItems whose first child paragraph opens with a `strong` node = 19,402 (21.94%), of which 8,044 (9.10%) are followed by a text node starting with a separator, across 539 files. Both AST-native figures are HIGHER than claimed, so the conservative direction is the researcher's.

verdicts.claim: C10: inlineCode is doing ≥13 distinct jobs at 76,118 occurrences, and 13.2% of them are prose-in-backticks, not code.
verdicts.reason: The count and the structural argument are solid; the headline percentage is not. Confirmed: inlineCode=76,118 exactly (my histogram); my regex span count 77,394 vs their 77,516 (delta from AST 1,276 vs their 1,398 — same order); and their 13-bucket breakdown sums to EXACTLY 77,516, so the internal arithmetic is clean. But 'prose-in-backticks 10,220 (13.2%)' does not replicate. The entire plausible prose pool — spans with ≥2 whitespace-separated words — is 21,398 (27.6%); a seeded random sample of 30 from that pool contains roughly 5 genuine prose spans (~17%), implying ≈3,600 spans ≈4.6%, about a third of the claim. The other 72.3% of spans are single-word, and a seeded random 30 of those contained 0 prose (all identifiers, paths, flags, colors, env vars). This is a single unreplicated heuristic classifier presented as a measurement, and its own largest bucket, 'other' at 19,695 (25.4%), is unclassified — a quarter of the data. Note also the denominator swap: 13.2% is 10220/77516, but the claim states the total as 76,118 (10220/76118 = 13.4%).
verdicts.correction: Keep '76,118 inlineCode spans carry many distinct roles' — that is measured and the random samples vividly support it (filepaths, shell pipelines, CSS class lists, HTTP headers, TS type signatures all in one node type). Drop or re-derive '13.2% are not code at all'; my independent estimate is ~4–5%. A4 as a recogniser is unaffected, since it does not depend on the prose share.

verdicts.claim: DESIGN (Tier 1, hazard list): 'remark-stringify DROPS duplicate labels (5 -> fewer, roundtrip false)'.
verdicts.reason: No labels are dropped. Input with 5 identical [fm:k] definitions parses to 'paragraph,definition,definition,definition,definition,definition' and remark-stringify emits all five back — in count 5, out count 5. The roundtrip is false for an entirely different reason: remark-stringify inserts a BLANK LINE between consecutive definitions. I proved the mis-attribution by testing three UNIQUE labels ([fm:a],[fm:b],[fm:c]) — those also fail the byte-identity check, with the same blank-line reflow, despite having no duplicates at all. The researcher appears to have observed roundtrip=false and inferred a dropping mechanism without inspecting the output string.
verdicts.correction: The real hazard is broader and more useful to state: ANY multi-record tail block is non-byte-stable through remark-stringify regardless of label uniqueness. This does not break the A1 design, because A1 already specifies one label per document — I verified the shipped single-record form ('[fm:b1]: #fm "v1.<base64url>"', blank-line isolated, tail-placed) is byte-identical through BOTH remark-stringify and prettier, and leaks 0 bytes through remark-rehype safe, remark-rehype raw, marked, GitHub gfm and GitHub markdown. The rule is right; the reason given for it is wrong, and prettier — not remark — is the one that preserves the multi-record form.

The 245-file figure is dominated by placeholders and comments, not raw HTML. Concentration confirmed exactly: 1,833 occurrences all in ONE file, md/Zephyrus/ecosystem.md.
