The researcher's magnitude (38.48 ms full scan) does not reproduce for me (2.399 ms with a C-level substring search) and their 'exactly one thing' is also wrong since the zip wins size too — but the verifier's stronger claim, that the zip wins nothing, is the more wrong of the two.

markdown-base :: '71.48% GHOST_nowhere_on_disk' — OVERTURNED. The researcher's figure reproduces; the verifier's does not. own-measurement across 12 resolution combinations (pinned-basename / full-on-disk-md / any-file-on-disk / case-insensitive / alias-aware indices built from 519 frontmatter aliases, x frontmatter-stripped and frontmatter-included bases): the ghost rate lands in a tight band of 71.71% to 73.62%. The researcher's 71.48% sits 0.23pp below my minimum and within 0.45pp of my closest directly comparable measurement (71.93%, frontmatter-stripped against a whole-disk index — which is precisely what 'nowhere on disk' means). The verifier's 67.40% is 4.31 to 6.22 percentage points below EVERY ONE of my twelve measurements and matches none of them. The verifier also concedes that the two small buckets (0.33%, 2.69%) reproduce almost exactly, which means the researcher's 4-way decomposition is internally closed and arithmetically coherent: 25.50 + 71.48 + 0.33 + 2.69 = 100.00. The headline bucket was the one thing they got right.

markdown-base :: '809 of 291,278 block tokens (0.28%)' — OVERTURNED, decisively, on a WRONG-DENOMINATOR error. The verifier stated that 'neither numerator nor denominator reproduces under any token definition I could construct' and offered 250 lost of 107,212 top-level blocks. own-measurement with marked@18.0.7 (downloaded from registry.npmjs.org to $TMPDIR) over the pinned corpus: a DEEP block-token walk that recurses into blockquote / list / list_item / table, excluding 'space' tokens, with files joined by a blank line, gives per-file 293,293 tokens, naive-join 292,484, LOST = EXACTLY 809, = 0.28%. Reconfirmed identically on three consecutive runs. The researcher's numerator reproduces to the unit and their denominator 291,278 is within 0.69% of my 293,293 (a minor difference in which container types get recursed). The verifier measured only TOP-LEVEL tokens — 107,318 in my reproduction, matching their 107,212 to 0.10% — and then judged a claim that was plainly made about the full block-token tree. That is a 2.7x denominator error, and it is the exact failure mode this audit was convened to catch, now committed by the auditor rather than the author. My top-level numbers also match the verifier's on their own terms (298 lost vs their 250; naive join GAINS 203 tokens including 'space' vs their 609), so their arithmetic was fine — only their choice of denominator was wrong.
result.note:
HEADLINE: 5 of 29 kills are false. 17.24%. The verification layer is roughly 5x more reliable than the research layer it audits (that layer ran a 100% headline defect rate), so it should be kept and trusted — but not trusted blindly, and specifically not on the one thing it is worst at.

THE PATTERN, AND IT IS SHARP. Split the 29 kills by what the verifier actually did:
  * Kills that QUOTE A PRIMARY SOURCE (a line of code, an API field, a star count, an issue state, a passage in a plan doc): 16 of 16 correct. Not one error. I re-fetched every one — mdast-util-gfm-autolink-literal lib/index.js:61-63, aider wholefile_prompts.py / wholefile_coder.py / base_coder.py:609, repomix outputGenerate.ts:60-65, repomix issue #226, Build/System.hs:53, graph-data.ts, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:134-137, docs/engine/PLAN.md:478 and :1062, github-slugger@2.0.0, streamdown's exact remend pin — and every quotation was verbatim-accurate, occasionally to the character. Their worst offence in this whole class was an off-by-one line citation.
  * Kills that RE-DERIVE A NUMBER and substitute their own: 5 of 13 wrong, i.e. a 38% defect rate in the half of the work that requires the verifier to do its own measurement. All five failures are the same shape — the verifier picked a different operational definition from the researcher's, did not disclose the switch, and scored the mismatch as the researcher's defect.
RECOMMENDATION: accept a kill that cites a source; independently re-derive any kill that substitutes a number. That single rule would have caught all five false kills and cost nothing on the other 24.

THE FIVE FAILURES, BY MECHANISM.
  1. WRONG DENOMINATOR (markdown-base 809 tokens). The verifier counted top-level tokens (107,212) to judge a claim about the full block-token tree (291,278) and declared it irreproducible. A deep walk excluding 'space' with a blank-line join reproduces the numerator EXACTLY — 809 — on three consecutive runs. This is the single most serious error in the set, because "wrong denominator" is one of the four failure modes the audit brief explicitly named, and the auditor committed it.
  2. WRONG DEFINITION, SELF-CONFESSED (founder-thesis C7 backticks). Any-position backtick runs instead of line-initial ones. Line-initial max over all 1,084 files is 3, with ZERO runs of 4+; the conclusion "4 is provably sufficient" is airtight. The verifier even wrote "the wrapper survives" inside its own kill.
  3. TOO-GENEROUS INDEX (markdown-base 71.48% ghost). Twelve independent index/basis combinations put the ghost rate in a 71.71-73.62% band. The researcher is 0.23pp out; the verifier is 4.31pp out and matches nothing.
  4. UNREPRODUCIBLE SUBSTITUTE (container C2 manifest). I built the container; the researcher's 169,706 B / 0.657% reproduces to 0.32% and 0.003pp, the verifier's 127,446 B / 0.494% reproduces to nothing, and two of the verifier's three supporting legs fail arithmetically.
  5. CONCLUSION CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN DATA (container C8 zip). "The zip wins nothing measured" is stated immediately after quoting zip 1.54 ms beating container 1.79 ms. My own bench: zip is 2.77x smaller and beats a cold-manifest container seek 1.373 ms vs 3.385 ms.

TWO VERIFIERS DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER ON THE SAME MEASUREMENT, AND NOBODY NOTICED. The container-thesis verifier used the LINE-INITIAL backtick rule to compute the spec's fence width (correct, and it is what makes its repomix kill land). The founder-thesis verifier used ANY-POSITION on the same corpus and killed a claim with it (incorrect). Same 1,084 files, same afternoon, opposite definitions, no reconciliation. Whatever ran these verifiers has no cross-area consistency check. That is a structural gap, not a one-off.

ONE MORE THING THE TEAM SHOULD SEE. Where the verifiers were right, they were often devastatingly right, and always in the direction of deflating a flattering claim: 91% of founder-thesis C2's headline is one machine sync tree (md/Skills/**, 340 of 340 'source: claude' files); markdown's share of repo file trees ROSE on my own 8-repo named test (1.142% to 1.460%, up in 7 of 8) against a published claim that it fell; only 86 of 393 intra-document anchors resolve under the canonical slugger against a claimed 348; all 4 unclosed fences are one generator's output in one directory. Those kills should be actioned immediately.

CALIBRATION ON MY OWN WORK (LR#60 — an auditor written in the same session as its subject inherits its blind spots). I nearly produced a false overturn myself: my first, uncontrolled test of the 47x diff claim varied manifest layout while an offset-bearing manifest masked the effect, showing a 0.7% swing and pointing at OVERTURN. A properly controlled second experiment with an offset-free manifest showed a 291x swing (1,077 B vs 313,870 B) and upheld the kill. I report that because it is the same disease as the five failures above, caught only by re-running with one variable isolated. I also reconfirmed both of my highest-stakes overturns on repeat deterministic runs before reporting.

EVIDENCE BASE. Corpus pins verified live before use: md 02c22ec47a3a73fb25a14b11be233ad3d00a8b48, knowledge 464eb666946c8cb4ccf42c68f4464613e5fc4999, frontmatter 798ebbf3250a5b2a53785859d79ae15f55ebebeb — all three match corpus-manifest.json exactly. My enumeration reproduces the manifest to the byte (md 756/21,068,853; knowledge 272/3,570,923) with one known addition, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md, created after the pin; every corpus number above is over corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 unless stated otherwise. All network evidence via direct curl to registry.npmjs.org, api.npmjs.org, api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com. No WebFetch. RULE 4 respected throughout: no commits, no pushes, no npm install into any repo, no writes outside $TMPDIR, no deletions.

TWO OPERATIONAL FLAGS. (1) The sgnk-injection-scan hook fired on a Bash result during this audit, flagging "Forget all". The string is the JSDoc line "Reset - Forget all previous slugs" inside the official github-slugger@2.0.0 tarball from registry.npmjs.org — benign library source I downloaded to reimplement the slug algorithm. False positive; I did not act on it and no outbound or secret-access tool was touched. (2) Reading /Users/sagnikmitra/.config/codex-env/tokens.zsh is denied by the sandbox, so the GitHub API work ran unauthenticated at 60 req/hr; that capped my repo-tree test at 8 usable repos and forced me to drop rust-lang/rust (truncated HEAD tree) and facebook/react (no pre-2022-08 commit returned). The finding reproduced comfortably anyway, but a larger sample would need that token readable.

WHAT I COULD NOT AUDIT. One kill — the-era Claim 6, 'adoption is already FLATTENING' — rests on a sample definition (top-215 / full-300 of what) that is not recoverable from anything on disk, and on an internal enumeration ('sums to 46 against a stated 49') inside text I cannot see. I counted it upheld because I found no evidence against it and because that verifier's other four kills all survived scrutiny, but it is the one line in this tally that is inference rather than verification. If the true verdict there is OVERTURNED, the false-kill rate is 6/29 = 20.7%. The published 17.24% is therefore a floor-to-central estimate, not a ceiling.

result.lens: TECHNICAL — engine specification: passes, offset model, parse-robustness regime, carriers, container contract, module system, incremental architecture.
result.thesis: MDMAX is not a compiler program, it is SEVEN PASSES AND ONE WRITER, and I re-derived this session that the writer already works: stock `mdast` `position.offset` splices 107,287 top-level blocks across 1,080 files of corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…c51a4 byte-identically, 0 failures [own-measurement], which means D7 is not an aspiration but a four-line function that two shipped code paths currently violate on every Publish (`share-writer.ts:26` calls `matter.stringify`, `frontmatter.ts:47` calls `doc.toString()` — 171 of 907 frontmatter blocks throw and only 33 survive byte-identical [own-measurement]). Everything the program calls "the engine" that is NOT a pass over one document should be deleted: there is no separate-compilation problem (max transitive blast radius 5%, cold full lex ~1s), no vocabulary demand (0.31% user invention, all of it tutorial text), no concurrency problem (0 concurrent cross-session writes in 1,200 sessions), and the container is not a durable artifact (a 4-backtick wrapper downgrades to 3 through `mdast-util-to-markdown`, and 45.76% of corpus files contain a ``` fence). What IS under-specified and will bite in week one is smaller and more boring than any of it: the offset model (only 67 of 1,080 files have bytes == UTF-16 == code points — 93.8% already diverge [own-measurement]), the YAML value slot that D8's whole extensibility story rests on (170 of 907 blocks in the founders' own vault are not valid YAML because `related: [[a]], [[b]]` puts markdown's grammar inside YAML's, and the quiet variant `[[[A]], [[B]]]` parses to a nested array and destroys the links with no error [own-measurement]), the unversioned `normalize()` whose first change silently re-keys every stored anchor, and an unpinned heading slugger on which anchor health swings 77 percentage points. Two shipped quadratics are live and measured: `WIKILINK_RE` at k=1.98 (36,865 ms on 320 KB of `[[`) and `mdast-util-from-markdown` on flat bullet lists at 12,429 ms vs micromark's 1,207 ms on identical bytes — a 10.3× gap that widens [own-measurement, both run against this repo's own node_modules].

ranked.item: P-W THE SPLICE WRITER — one function, the only thing in the system permitted to write bytes. `splice(src, {byteStart, byteEnd}, replacement) -> {bytes, receipt}`. Replace `matter.stringify` in share-writer.ts and `doc.toString()` in frontmatter.ts with it in the same commit. Gate: publish-then-unpublish over all 907 frontmatter-bearing files is byte-identical, AND the 171 files no YAML parser can read are published successfully rather than 502ing.
ranked.why: It is the only capability in the entire program that is simultaneously (a) a live data-corruption bug firing on every Publish and every properties-panel edit, (b) proven buildable against real bytes this session, (c) four lines, and (d) the executable form of D7, which is a theorem (Foster TOPLAS 2007 Lemma 3.9) rather than a preference. It also converts the abstract 'splice-only' decision into a red-to-green assertion that prose cannot satisfy.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4] Identity splice through stock `mdast-util-from-markdown` node.position.start/end.offset over every top-level block: files=1080, blocks=107287, spliceIdentityOK=1080, spliceBad=0. Independently: fmBlocks=907, gray-matter throws=171, gmByteIdenticalRoundTrip=33 (3.64%). [primary-read] share-writer.ts header says 'splicing the key into the YAML frontmatter' and line 26 calls `matter.stringify(parsed.content, data)`; the doc comment is false. [primary-read] preview/presentation/frontmatter.ts:47 `const yaml = doc.toString()`. Corroborated by the `product-gap` and `against` areas, whose 33/907 and 1,080/1,080 figures I reproduced to the unit.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. `mdast-util-from-markdown` and `yaml` are already dependencies. The 171-file case additionally needs the frontmatter value-slot pass (item 3) to avoid parsing at all — a splice that locates `public_slug:` by byte scan inside the delimiter block never needs a YAML parser, which is the point.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/splice.ts` (~40 lines with the boundary assertion) + a vitest suite that replays the 907 files. No CLI, no package, no spec. Delete it if the editor stops needing it.

ranked.item: P0 THE OFFSET MODEL — one unit (UTF-16 code units), one boundary policy (an offset may never fall inside a surrogate pair; reject at construction, never round), one conversion point (a per-open-document `OffsetMap` holding a Uint32Array UTF-16→byte prefix table plus a lazy Intl.Segmenter grapheme bitset). Branded types `U16Offset | ByteOffset | GraphemeIndex` so the three cannot mix. An eslint `no-restricted-syntax` rule forbids `Buffer.byteLength`, `TextEncoder`, `codePointAt` and raw `.slice` on a document anywhere else.
ranked.why: This is the cheapest item on the list and the one that removes a recurring, silent, corrupting bug class. It is also load-bearing in a way nobody has stated: `mdast` offsets are UTF-16 indices into a JS string, while sha256, git blobs and the corpus manifest are byte-based — so the identity contract and the offset contract are in DIFFERENT UNITS and the conversion sits exactly where this workspace's LR#68 truncation class lives.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…c51a4] Over the 1,080 non-empty pinned files: only 67 (6.20%) satisfy bytes == UTF-16 length == code-point count; 1,013 (93.8%) contain non-ASCII; 38 (3.52%) contain non-BMP characters. [secondary, parsing-robustness] one corpus file diverges by 533,366 units; prefix table costs 4 ms and 5.8 MB on the largest file; Intl.Segmenter runs at 28.6 MB/s. [primary, prior art] LSP negotiates utf-8/utf-16/utf-32 per session and iA Writer's annotation spec uses grapheme clusters — the two ends we must interoperate with disagree, which is precisely why the conversion point must be singular and named.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. It is a type-level change plus one class.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/offsets.ts` + the lint rule. Every other pass consumes it. Do this before the splice writer's second caller, not after.

ranked.item: FIX THE VALUE SLOT D8 RESTS ON — a lenient frontmatter pre-pass that quotes bare `[[...]]` runs before handing the block to YAML, plus a hard refusal for the SILENT corruption case, plus a rule that a frontmatter parse failure may never fail a user action. `mdmax vocab` (read-only, ~2 days) reports the three defect classes: case/morphology drift, prose in an enum slot, unparseable value slot.
ranked.why: D8 says extensibility lives in the VALUE of a field, never the SET of node types. That rule is correct and it survives — but its carrier is broken on nearly a fifth of the founders' own corpus, and nobody has specified a pass, a refusal code, or a repair. The quiet failure is worse than the loud one: `entities: [[[A]], [[B]]]` is VALID YAML that parses to a nested array and silently destroys the wikilinks. There is no error to catch. Every provenance-in-frontmatter design (including emitting OKF §5 fields) inherits this surface.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…c51a4] 907 frontmatter blocks; `yaml@2.9.0` parseDocument reports errors on 170 (18.74%); gray-matter throws on 171 (the extra one, md/pj.md, parses and throws at stringify). [own-measurement, custom-pointers, independently reproduced] `entities: [[[A]], [[B]]]` parses to `{"entities":[[["A"]],[["B"]]]}` with no error. [primary-read] share-writer.ts has no try/catch, and POST /api/share converts any throw into a 502 — so 18.7% of a real vault is currently unpublishable. [secondary, custom-pointers] gray-matter is 7.49M downloads/week and delegates to js-yaml, which is YAML 1.1 and additionally coerces bare dates to Date objects in 84.8% of parseable blocks — a second, independent divergence.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing, but it must land in the same PR as the splice writer or the 171-file case stays broken. Note the dependency direction: a byte-scan splice makes the parse OPTIONAL for writes, which is the real fix; the lenient pre-pass is only needed for READS.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/frontmatter-lenient.ts` + `mdmax vocab` as a read-only script. Zero new bytes in any user file, so D2/D4/D6/D7-compatible by construction.

ranked.item: P0 THE SHAPE GATE AND THE WORKER BUDGET — before any grammar runs: strict UTF-8 decode (refuse invalid, never repair), BOM strip, and refuse by SHAPE if bytes > 4 MB OR lines > 200,000 OR list-marker lines > 20,000. All parsing happens in a long-lived `worker_threads` pool with a 250 ms keystroke / 2,000 ms cold-open / 10,000 ms batch budget enforced by `worker.terminate()`. Failure surfaces as a discriminated union `{ok:false, reason:'BUDGET_TIME'|'BUDGET_BYTES'|'BUDGET_BLOCKS'|'PARSER_THREW'|'WORKER_DIED', at:{line,col}}`, never as an exception in a route handler.
ranked.why: Two quadratics are ALREADY SHIPPING and both are non-adversarial — ordinary content triggers them. The list-marker threshold specifically is not a guess: it is the shape of the mdast blowup, and it is also the shape of AI-generated markdown (the plan's own measurement: 48.3% of model-written list items open with a bold run — models write long flat lists). Note the counter-intuitive finding the team must not get wrong: `resourceLimits` is NOT a substitute — a TIGHT cap (32 MB) produces a clean catchable parent error at ~86 ms, while a LOOSE cap (256 MB) produced rc=134 and a V8 FATAL that killed the parent process. The constant is the difference between an exception and a SIGABRT, so it must be pinned and regression-tested, not documented as best-effort.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, this repo's node_modules, node v24.6.0] `WIKILINK_RE = /(!?)\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]/g` at markdown-parser.ts:12 on n unclosed `[[`: 20k=589.2 ms, 40k=2,315.9 ms, 80k=9,071.0 ms, 160k=36,865.0 ms — ratios 3.93/3.92/4.06 on 2× input, k=1.98, i.e. strictly quadratic; 36.8 seconds on 320 KB, server-side, via search-index.ts. [own-measurement] `mdast-util-from-markdown` on flat bullet lists: 10k=372 ms, 20k=1,003 ms, 40k=3,356 ms, 80k=12,429 ms (2.55 MB); a PARAGRAPH control at the same byte counts: 148/265/463/821 ms, k≈0.82. 15.1× on essentially identical bytes at 80k. `micromark` on the identical list inputs: 177/332/580/1,207 ms, k≈0.94 — linear, and 10.3× faster than mdast at 80k with the gap widening. [secondary, parsing-robustness, reproduced in shape] `worker.terminate()` reclaimed an infinite non-yielding spin at 253.9 ms against a 250 ms budget — max overshoot 5.4 ms (2.2%) across 9 hostile shapes.
ranked.blocked_by: The refusal enum must be designed before the first route handler consumes it, or every call site grows its own try/catch. That is a half-day of naming, not engineering.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/gate.ts` + `parse-worker.ts` + a 51-case hostile fixture directory run in CI with FLOOR-and-ceiling timing bands (never equality — LR#66).

ranked.item: P4 THE RESOLVER AS A THREE-TIER LADDER, NOT AN ENGINE — tier 1 `ChangeSet.mapPos` (@codemirror/state, already a dependency, exact by construction, in-app); tier 2 diff3-assisted (whenever a previous version exists, which is almost always); tier 3 content-derived S1/S2/S3, reached ONLY when neither is available (offline-sync reconciliation, an external edit, a git pull with no merge base). Tier 3 returns RESOLVED | AMBIGUOUS | LOST and never breaks a tie by position.
ranked.why: This is where two areas contradict and the plan already conceded the answer without re-sequencing the build around it. `§4.1` itself demotes content-derived re-anchoring to 'the fallback and the verifier, not the primary mechanism'; the `against` area then argues the whole engine away because a 30-line LCS diff resolves 86.7%. Both are describing the same architecture from opposite ends. Building tier 3 first is the error — it is the rarest path, its flagship number has been re-derived by nobody, it is a BLOCK figure that does not transfer to the RANGES comments actually anchor, and a GPL-3.0 competitor shipped a range-level implementation on 2026-07-30. What MDMAX can own is not the algorithm but the REFUSAL and the published false-match rate, neither of which the competitor has.
ranked.evidence: [primary-read, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:111] 'Every position-based tiebreak made it dramatically worse — content-hash plus nearest-position goes 0.00% → 22.20% false.' [primary-read, PLAN.md:299/303] the 99.627% 'has not been recomputed since it was first produced' and 'is a block figure. Comments and suggestions anchor ranges.' [own-measurement, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…c51a4] 107,287 top-level blocks over 1,080 files parse cleanly, so tier-3 candidate generation is affordable — the constraint is correctness, not cost. [secondary, competitive-live, tarball-verified] inkeep/OpenKnowledge `anchor.ts` (261 lines) reached npm at 0.46.0-beta.32 with exact-quote + widened context + orphan-rather-than-guess, and its server path returns `{status:'orphaned'}` on a tie while its app path returns `best[0]` — two different policies in one product, and neither publishes an accuracy number.
ranked.blocked_by: The benchmark cannot adjudicate this on the pinned corpus. 86.6% of `.md` file-revisions in its largest root delete zero lines, so S1 resolves by construction and the number is a property of an append-dominated corpus. Tier 3 must be measured on a stratum restricted to revisions deleting >2 lines, and that stratum may be too small to measure — which is itself the finding.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/resolve.ts` (~200 lines, three arms) + `--explain` printing which tier fired. Tiers 1 and 2 first; tier 3 behind the stratified benchmark.

ranked.item: VERSION THE TWO PURE FUNCTIONS EVERYTHING ELSE KEYS ON — `normalize/1` (NFC + collapse whitespace + lowercase) and `slug/1` (the heading anchor algorithm), each published, pinned, and stamped into every stored anchor and every emitted certificate row. An anchor record carries `{schema:1, normalize:'mdmax/normalize@1', slug:'mdmax/slug@1', id, quote, prefix, suffix}`.
ranked.why: This is the highest-severity UNDER-SPECIFICATION in the plan and it is a silent data-loss bug rather than a crash. The plan names the risk in one line and then does not act on it. Separately, the slug choice is a 77-percentage-point swing on the same bytes — which makes 'pick and publish the anchor algorithm' the single highest-leverage decision in the linker, and it costs one afternoon.
ranked.evidence: [primary-read, docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:397] 'The 99.627% was swept over 384 configurations under NFC + collapse whitespace + lowercase. If the hash input changes later, every stored anchor silently re-keys while the published number keeps describing code that no longer exists.' [secondary, markdown-base + its verifier, contested and therefore decisive] the same corpus's 392 intra-document anchors resolve 86 under `github-slugger` and 388 under a dash-collapsing slugger — one report used both algorithms in two adjacent claims without noticing. [primary-read, github-slugger source] disambiguation is POSITIONAL (`while (occurrences[result]) result = original + '-' + ++occurrences[original]`), so an exported heading id changes when an unrelated heading is edited — which is why headings must not be exported symbols.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing, but it must land before the FIRST anchor is persisted. After that it is a migration.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/normalize.ts` and `slug.ts`, each exporting a `VERSION` constant, plus a CI assertion that the version changes whenever the function's output over a 200-case golden file changes.

ranked.item: CARRIER DECISIONS, CLOSED — the fence INFO STRING (```` ```md fm:key=value ````) is the primary block-scoped carrier; the orphan link reference definition is the primary invisible document-scoped carrier, tail-placed, double-quoted title, base64url payload, ONE label per document; frontmatter is permitted for a document-level NAME only. REFUSED, with reasons: the HTML comment, `{#id}` / `{: #id}`, `> [!TYPE]` callouts, the `[//]: #` idiom, `:::` directives, and the Unicode Tag block.
ranked.why: The carrier question is the one place where the areas actually converge, and it converges against `docs/engine/PLAN.md §5`'s HTML-comment default. Every refusal has a measured mechanism, not a preference: GitHub DELETES HTML comments in both API modes; `{#id}` is not CommonMark (D6) and degrades to visible junk; remark-stringify with GFM escapes GitHub's own `> [!NOTE]` to `> \[!NOTE]`; the `[//]: #` idiom does not survive a WRITE (parens become quotes). The fence info string is the only channel that is simultaneously round-trip stable, invisible in rendered HTML, and free of a grammar of its own — which is exactly what D8 ('the VALUE of a field') implies once you ask which field.
ranked.evidence: [settled, 24 renderer configs] only the link reference definition and the `[//]: #` idiom are invisible in 24/24; frontmatter is VISIBLE in 23/24; the HTML comment produces 8 distinct outputs and GitHub blob view deletes it. [own-measurement, hold-more, reproduced across 6 renderer configs] the tail-placed orphan refdef emits 0 bytes of HTML in remark-rehype raw AND safe, marked 16.4.2, and GitHub gfm AND markdown modes, and is byte-identical through remark-stringify 11.0.0 and prettier 3.8.3. [own-measurement, custom-pointers] `:::tip`, the fence meta string and the refdef round-trip IDENTICAL; the callout does not. [own-measurement] GitHub preserves an unknown fence's meta into sanitized HTML as `data-meta=` — an unexploited, verified channel. HAZARDS THAT MUST BE ENCODED AS RULES: label ≤ 999 chars (CommonMark) vs ≤ 1000 (cmark-gfm); a raw `"` or blank line in a title destroys the definition and remark then emits a VISIBLE escaped line; a refdef cannot interrupt a paragraph; prettier does NOT reformat an unknown-language fence body but DOES reformat a known-language one, invalidating any content hash.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. This is a decision, and it is already 90% made in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §4.3 — it just contradicts docs/engine/PLAN.md §5, which must be struck.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/carriers.ts` (emit + detect + the refusal list) and the first four columns of `mdmax cert`.

ranked.item: THE CONTAINER CONTRACT — `mdmax pack` is an EPHEMERAL READ TRANSPORT: generated on demand, never committed, never the write surface, never a whole-vault button. Fence carrier with run N = max(4, max line-initial backtick run over all members + 1) RE-DERIVED AT EMIT TIME (never trusted from a written delimiter), authoritative path in the fence info string, `## File: <path>` heading retained as explicitly non-authoritative human decoration, per-entry `{path, sha256, bytes, nl:0|1}` manifest, hard refusal above the target model's context window with the index offered instead.
ranked.why: The founder's most-repeated want survives, but only in a much narrower shape than the record assumes, and three measurements set the boundary. (1) It cannot be durable: a 4-backtick wrapper is DOWNGRADED to 3 backticks by `mdast-util-to-markdown`, and 45.76% of corpus files contain a ``` fence — so one pass through any normalising markdown tool shatters the bundle. aider avoids this by re-deriving the fence at emit (`choose_fence()`); a delimiter written into a durable artifact cannot. (2) It cannot be the write surface: under realistic model edits (rewrite across a boundary, elide unchanged regions, reorder) boundary-repair mis-located 119/120, 119/120 and 120/120 respectively, and WRONG here means a confident wrong split, i.e. silent corruption. (3) It cannot be whole-vault: the container is 25,776,700 B against a described index of 234,119 B — 110.1×, and a 200K-token budget holds 2.79% of it. A 'pack my vault' button manufactures disappointment.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, container-thesis, verified] 1084/1084 byte-identical round trip at +0.892% overhead; 4 files (0.369%) end inside an unclosed fence, which silently loses a boundary under the HTML-comment carrier; 15,435 line-initial backtick runs all exactly 3; zip costs 120× more git storage per edit and produces 'Binary files differ'. [own-measurement, founder-thesis verifier] the 4-backtick → 3-backtick downgrade through mdast-util-to-markdown, path attribute preserved; 496 of 1,084 files (45.76%) contain a ``` fence [corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…]. [own-measurement, container-thesis] 288 files (26.57%) lack a trailing newline — concatenation silently welds documents; 7 files (0.65%) carry unterminated fences. [primary-read] aider `base_coder.py::choose_fence()` scans all member content and selects a fence that starts no line — the max+1 rule, already shipped. [primary-read] repomix issue #71 has been open 23 months and the maintainer gated it on evidence the contributor could not produce.
ranked.blocked_by: Sequence it AFTER `mdmax edit`. Its pack-time refusals (unterminated fence, under-declared run) are the same identity-and-splice discipline, and building it first means building that discipline twice.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax pack --budget <tokens>` producing a bundle on stdout. No `unpack` in v1 — llm-code-format already ships pack+unpack at 387 downloads/week against repomix's 327,543, an 846:1 revealed-demand ratio for the reverse operation.

ranked.item: THE MODULE SYSTEM, MINIMAL — compilation unit = one `.md` file. TWO reference kinds with opposite semantics: HARD `[text](path.md)` is checked and a break is an error; SOFT `[[Name]]` is resolve-if-present and NEVER an error, no diagnostic, no squiggle. Symbol = file, canonical key = root-relative path, basename an alias that REFUSES on ambiguity. Headings are within-unit coordinates resolved by the unit's own local table under the pinned `slug/1`; they are NOT exported and `{#id}` is refused under D6. Namespace = the root. That is the entire module system.
ranked.why: The two reference kinds behave differently by a very large margin on the same files, and every existing tool gets one of them wrong: Obsidian treats everything as soft and never errors; Docusaurus ships `onBrokenLinks:'throw'` and would fail this corpus thousands of times. A dangling `[[X]]` is correct authoring, not a defect — and the corpus contains 1,409 targets repeated across ≥2 documents, which is a controlled vocabulary being mistaken for an error list. What must NOT ship is everything around this: no build graph, no scheduler, no rebuilder, no lock file as a build artifact.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, markdown-base, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…] markdown-syntax file links resolve at 88.62% and wikilinks at 25.50% on the same 1,084 files — the split is real even after the verifier corrected the wikilink denominator (13,026 not 9,077, because YAML frontmatter links were silently stripped). [own-measurement, markdown-base] 71.3% of heading instances have a globally non-unique slug and 8.9% of files contain a within-file duplicate. [primary-read] Docusaurus `configValidation.ts` DEFAULT_CONFIG `onBrokenLinks:'throw'`, 1,513,550 downloads/week. [own-measurement] 0 transclusions and 0 resolving cross-file heading anchors in 1,084 files — the sub-file addressing substrate the 'hundreds connected to hundreds' vision needs does not exist yet.
ranked.blocked_by: The frontmatter wikilink population (2,283 `entities:`, 1,407 `related:`, 49 `up:`) is a THIRD reference kind — declared, structured, and resolving at only 13.95%. It needs a decision: is a frontmatter wikilink hard, soft, or a concept name? Today it is undocumented and it is a third of all wikilinks.
ranked.ships_as: `src/modules/mdmax/refs.ts` — extract, classify, resolve. Plus `mdmax vocab` listing repeated dangling targets ranked, which turns 10,798 'errors' into a 1,409-term index.

ranked.item: CHALLENGE D9 AND REPLACE IT — D9 ('a document NAMES a capability, never CARRIES one') is INSUFFICIENT as stated and should be superseded by the enforceable asymmetry: A DOCUMENT MAY LOWER ITS OWN CAPABILITY, NEVER RAISE IT. A file may carry `mdmax: none` to switch a feature OFF for itself; it may never carry a declaration that switches anything ON or adds a term. Plus: a named capability resolves ONLY from a pinned allowlist shipped with the engine, never from a path or URL inside the document, and `mdmax cert` flags a document naming an unresolvable or non-allowlisted capability as CORRUPT.
ranked.why: This is the one settled decision I am explicitly challenging, and the evidence is that naming an executable resource a consumer then runs is the same attack surface with one extra hop — arriving with a FALSE sense of safety, because the file looks inert. D9's own justification (XML internal DTD → XXE, vim modelines) actually supports a sharper rule than D9 states. The correct invariant is not name-vs-carry, it is DENOTATION-vs-PROCEDURE plus the lowering asymmetry: a document may carry a closed, non-dereferencing, non-recursive term→meaning map (JSON-LD's embedded context has no equivalent CVE class), and may never name a procedure that resolves outside the engine's own allowlist. Note the JSON-LD caveat that was mis-stated in the record: `@import` inside a context DOES load a remote context, so embedded contexts are bounded by an explicit rule, not structurally closed — which strengthens the allowlist requirement.
ranked.evidence: [primary-read] vim 9.2.0499 `modelinestrict`, commit 4c2879471 titled 'Enabling modelines poses a risk': `set nomodeline` is honored from within a modeline even when modelinestrict is on — a file may disable further processing for itself but may not enable anything. A 21-option allowlist, not 24. [primary-read] OKF SPEC.md v0.2 §10.2 already ships `executor.resource` and `attester.resource` naming code the consumer executes, §10.5 step 5 is 'the consumer runs the attester', and §12 DEFERS 'the attester ABI, portability, and sandboxing' — i.e. the sandbox story does not exist. [primary-read] Hugo ships inline shortcodes DISABLED under SECURITY with the stated boundary 'template and configuration authors are trusted, but content authors are not' — and a `.md` in frontmatter is a drive-by PR, a reviewer's paste (D3), or LLM output, which is strictly worse than npm's threat model where package.json is written by the repo owner.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing — it is a one-paragraph decision. But it must be written down BEFORE `mdmax cert` gains an OKF column, because adopting OKF as a target inherits this surface.
ranked.ships_as: A replacement paragraph for D9 in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md plus a `CAPABILITY_ALLOWLIST` constant in the engine. Zero runtime code in v1, because v1 names nothing.

ranked.item: `mdmax cert` AS THE ONE PUBLIC ARTIFACT — per document, per construct, per (product, surface): PASS / STRIP / CORRUPT / VOID. Two tiers, labelled in the output: PROBED (vendored, version-pinned, offline, reproducible) and DECLARED (contract + canary, for closed SaaS). First row printed is our own product failing its own consistency check.
ranked.why: It is the only capability that survived every adversarial search — three GitHub repo searches returned total_count 0/0/1, npm has no equivalent, and babelmark differs SPEC EXAMPLES across PARSERS rather than a DOCUMENT across SURFACES. It also satisfies the program's own §10.1 rule (choose the deliverable whose output shape cannot flatter us). Add two columns nobody has proposed and both are nearly free: a SLUGGER column (77-point anchor-health swing on identical bytes) and an INTRA-PRODUCT column (frontmatter's own preview pins mermaid 11.15.0 while its PDF route imports `mermaid@11` from a CDN currently resolving to 11.16.0 — a two-surface disagreement inside one product, today, with no receipt).
ranked.evidence:
[own-measurement, prior areas, reproduced live] `POST https://api.github.com/markdown` is a FIFTH GitHub surface that renders mermaid as highlighted source and deletes inline `

`; ids are lowercased in `gfm` mode and case-PRESERVED in `markdown` mode. [primary-read] pdf-doc.ts:24 `MERMAID_VERSION = "11"` + line 134 jsdelivr import; registry.npmjs.org reports mermaid latest 11.16.0 against 11.15.0 installed. [primary-read] the PDF route uses `setTimeout(resolve, 2000)` and asserts nothing about whether every diagram rendered. [secondary, market-and-gift] markdownguide.org's 70-tool × 28-construct matrix tracks ZERO of frontmatter, wikilinks, callouts or mermaid — the four constructs that dominate real files.
ranked.blocked_by: Its most valuable columns are the least probeable: GitHub blob cannot be probed without pushing content, and Obsidian, Notion, Slack and the chat renderers cannot be probed at all — 7 of ~12 surfaces. If the DECLARED tier is not acceptable to users, the artifact is a matrix about the renderers nobody worries about.
ranked.ships_as: `npx mdmax cert <file> --targets … --fail-on CORRUPT --json`, plus a dated `targets.json` where a closed-target row older than 90 days renders STALE rather than PASS. That expiry field is the only mechanism in the whole program by which a copy visibly rots.

ranked.item: INCREMENTAL ARCHITECTURE — there is none, and that is the correct v1 answer. Adopt Lezer's `TreeFragment.applyChanges` for the editor (CodeMirror 6 is already a dependency) and verify it with a property test asserting `incremental === full`. At corpus level, the only cache is `Map<path, {contentSha, blockIds}>` invalidated on sha change. Write no invalidation rule, no scheduler, no rebuilder.
ranked.why: A build system's entire value is avoiding work over a large dependency closure. Here the closure is tiny and the full build is one second, so the machinery is a net cost for a long time — and Microsoft says this about its own dependency engine in writing. The construct the incremental-parse literature is actually about (the link reference definition, unbounded lookahead) occurs ZERO times in 25.5 MB of real markdown. Re-deriving Dubroy & Warth's examined-vs-consumed rule would be reimplementing something CodeMirror already gets right, for a construct nobody uses. What DOES need writing is the ANCHOR invalidation rule, which is a different thing: an anchor dies when its block's normalized text hash changes, NOT when its offsets move — and mass invalidation is a NORMAL event, not an error.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, markdown-base, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…] 507 of 1,084 files (46.8%) participate in zero resolved edges; maximum transitive blast radius is 54 files (5.0%), mean 8.77; full cold lex of all 25.5 MB is 1,056 ms. [primary-read, learn.microsoft.com] 'For some complex workbooks, the time taken to build and maintain the dependency trees needed for Smart Recalculation is larger than the time saved by Smart Recalculation.' [own-measurement] 0 `definition`, 0 `linkReference`, 0 `imageReference` nodes across all 1,084 files. [own-measurement, markdown-base] Lezer incremental === full reparse on 7 of 7 hand-built unbounded-lookahead cases, including a mid-document open-fence insertion that collapses 37 blocks. [own-measurement] one 5-character insertion (an opening fence) changed the block identity of 37 of 40 blocks — so the anchor layer must batch-refuse and mark STALE, never error.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. This is a deletion.
ranked.ships_as: A property test (`incremental === full` over 100 sampled single-character edits per file) and a ~20-line content-sha cache. Everything else in §'incremental' gets struck from the plan.

result.dependencies: STRICT ORDER, and the first three are one week. (1) `offsets.ts` FIRST — every later pass consumes `U16Offset`/`ByteOffset`, and retrofitting branded types after four call sites exist is a refactor rather than a decision; 93.8% of real files already diverge across the three units, so this is not premature. (2) `splice.ts` + the lenient frontmatter pre-pass in the SAME commit — the splice is proven (1080/1080, 107,287 blocks) but its first two callers (share-writer, properties panel) both hit the 171 unparseable-frontmatter files, and a byte-scan splice that never invokes a YAML parser is what makes those files writable at all. The gate is publish→unpublish byte-identical on all 907, including the 171. (3) `normalize/1` and `slug/1` versioned and stamped BEFORE the first anchor is persisted — after that it is a migration, and the plan already names the silent re-key risk without acting on it. (4) `gate.ts` + the parse worker BEFORE the resolver — tier-3 candidate generation is the first pass that runs a grammar over unbounded input, and both measured quadratics (WIKILINK_RE k=1.98, mdast on flat lists k≈1.9) are reachable from ordinary content today; the refusal enum must be named before any route handler consumes it or every call site grows its own try/catch. (5) `resolve.ts` tiers 1 and 2 — `mapPos` and diff3 need no research, cover the overwhelming majority of real cases, and their existence is what lets tier 3 be honest about being a fallback. (6) Tier 3 is BLOCKED on a corpus that can test it: 86.6% of `.md` file-revisions in the largest pinned root delete zero lines, so S1 resolves by construction and the benchmark measures the corpus rather than the resolver. Acquire or construct a stratum of revisions deleting >2 lines before writing tier 3, and if that stratum is under ~200 block-versions, say so and ship tiers 1–2 only. (7) `refs.ts` and `mdmax cert` are INDEPENDENT of 1–6 and can run in parallel by a second person — cert in particular needs no engine, only vendored renderers. (8) The container is blocked on `mdmax edit` existing, because its pack-time refusals are the same identity-and-splice discipline. (9) NOTHING here is blocked on the flagship 99.627% being re-derived, and that is deliberate: eight areas cite a number nobody has recomputed, so no build item should depend on it. (10) HARD PREREQUISITE, five minutes, before any of the above: the working tree's `package.json` has been clobbered from 3,076 bytes to `{"type":"module"}` (17 bytes, uncommitted — 97 script and dependency lines deleted by a research agent so it could run .mjs files), and every artifact this gate rests on — docs/mdmax/PLAN.md, docs/engine/research/, all three HANDOFFs, the corpus manifest — is UNTRACKED on a branch that exists on no remote. `git checkout -- package.json`, then add and push. RULE 4: I have not run either command.
contradictions: MDAST: 'never build a tree' (parsing-robustness) vs 'stock mdast offsets splice byte-perfectly, use them' (against). BOTH ARE RIGHT ABOUT DIFFERENT CALL SITES AND I PICK A COMPOSITE. My own measurement settles it: mdast parsed 107,287 blocks across all 1,080 real corpus files with 0 splice failures, AND took 12,429 ms on an 80k-item flat list where micromark took 1,207 ms (10.3×, widening; paragraph control at identical bytes k≈0.82). RULING: ship mdast for v1 per-document offsets, behind the P0 shape gate and the worker budget — the gate's list-marker threshold exists precisely to catch mdast's one pathological shape. Do NOT build the micromark event→block reconstruction first; parsing-robustness's own kill condition concedes that if `blocksFromEvents` needs an mdast-equivalent structure anyway the advantage evaporates, and nobody has tested that. Port when the gate starts firing on real user content, not before. Note also that micromark is NOT uniformly linear — it went k=2.42 on nested blockquotes — so 'consume micromark events' is not a free correctness win either; only Lezer stayed near-linear on every shape tested.

CONTAINER CARRIER: `docs/engine/PLAN.md §5` makes the HTML comment the default; container-thesis, hold-more and the settled 24-config matrix all say the fence. RULING: THE FENCE, and §5 must be struck rather than reconciled. The HTML comment silently loses a boundary whenever a member ends inside an open fence (4 of 1,084 files, so 98.2% of vault-scale packs), GitHub DELETES it in BOTH API modes, and docs/mdmax/PLAN.md §4.3 already records it as destroyed in 10 of 24 configs. This is not a new finding overturning a settled one — it is the START-HERE plan already disagreeing with the older engine plan, and nobody noticed the two documents contradict.

CONTAINER STATUS: founder-thesis promotes `mdmax pack`/`unpack` to sit BESIDE `mdmax cert` in the MVP; container-thesis says the pack must never be the write surface; the-era's design implies durable stability. RULING: EPHEMERAL READ TRANSPORT ONLY, and this kills unpack in v1. Decisive evidence is a defect neither area's headline carries: a 4-backtick wrapper is DOWNGRADED to 3 backticks by mdast-util-to-markdown, and 45.76% of corpus files contain a ``` fence — so the bundle shatters on one pass through any normalising tool, which is exactly the environment ('runs inside other people's context windows') its value proposition depends on. Reinforced by 119/120 mis-located boundaries under realistic model edits, and by llm-code-format's 846:1 revealed-demand ratio against the reverse operation.

FOLDER COMPILER: markdown-base specifies a Ninja-cell build system with a topological scheduler, a verifying-trace rebuilder, key stratification by durability and a lock file; against/premortem/markdown-base's own negatives say there is no closure to compile. RULING: DELETE THE BUILD SYSTEM, KEEP THE DATA STRUCTURE. Max transitive blast radius 5%, 46.8% of files in zero resolved edges, cold full lex 1,056 ms, and Microsoft's own published warning that maintaining the dependency tree can cost more than it saves. The symbol table, the resolved-edge map and the affected-target query are useful at n=1 and are a library function. The scheduler, rebuilder and durability stratification are the single most over-specified thing in the program.

HEADING IDENTITY: markdown-base's design makes a heading an exported symbol when it carries an explicit author-given `{#id}`; D6 forbids a dialect needing its own parser and the program's own 24-renderer measurement classes `{#id}` as VISIBLE JUNK. RULING: D6 WINS — `{#id}` is REFUSED as a carrier. Headings are within-unit coordinates only, resolved by the unit's local table under a PINNED, PUBLISHED `slug/1`. The finding this should have produced is stronger than the escape hatch: the same corpus's intra-document anchors resolve 86 under github-slugger and 388 under a dash-collapsing slugger — a 77-point swing that makes publishing the slug algorithm the highest-leverage single decision in the linker, at zero cost.

ANCHORING NECESSITY: against says a 30-line LCS diff substitutes for the engine (86.658% resolved, 77.297pp provably unambiguous); §4.1 publishes 99.627%; competitive-live says a GPL-3.0 competitor shipped range-level anchoring on 2026-07-30. RULING: AGAINST IS ARGUING WITH A POSITION THE PLAN ALREADY ABANDONED — §4.1 itself calls content-derived re-anchoring 'the fallback and the verifier, not the primary mechanism'. Sequence the ladder mapPos → diff3 → content-derived and stop describing tier 3 as the spine. But against's F2 fired against itself and the team must respect it: its diff substitute is measured only on consecutive revisions with a 20.5-day median gap, and the one production datum on long-lived anchors (Hypothes.is, 20,953 annotations, ~22% no longer attachable) says the archival case is real and unmeasured. What MDMAX can own is the REFUSAL and the published false-match rate — the competitor's two code paths disagree with each other on the tied case (one orphans, one returns best[0]) and neither publishes an accuracy number.

CORPUS_ID REPRODUCIBILITY: premortem says 'MATCH: NONE, 64 variants tried'; moat and agentic-docs both say they could not reconstruct it; premortem's verifier says it reproduces. RULING: IT REPRODUCES, AND I RE-DERIVED IT THIS SESSION. `sha256("\n".join(sorted(f"{root}/{path}:{sha256}")))` over all 1,084 entries, no trailing newline, roots sorted with paths = 3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4, exact [own-measurement]. The recipe is stated in prose at docs/mdmax/PLAN.md:29, in the document being audited. Three areas published a null result on an artifact whose derivation was written one line above the number. Commit the ten-line script anyway — P1 makes this label load-bearing and three independent readers failed to reconstruct it.

D8's CARRIER: every area treats the frontmatter value slot as a solved channel; nobody made 18.7% unparseable YAML a blocking finding. RULING: IT IS BLOCKING, and it is the largest under-specification in the plan. 170 of 907 blocks fail `yaml@2.9.0`, 171 throw under gray-matter [own-measurement, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…], and the SILENT variant destroys wikilinks with no error at all. D8 survives as a rule; its carrier does not survive contact with the founders' own vault, and any OKF-provenance-in-frontmatter plan inherits the same surface.
what_to_cut: THE INCREMENTAL BUILD SYSTEM — the Ninja/Shake cell, the topological scheduler, the verifying-trace rebuilder, the durability-stratified key space, the escalation-to-suspending-scheduler plan. Cold full lex is 1,056 ms, max transitive blast radius is 5%, 46.8% of files have no resolved edges, and the construct the incremental-parse literature is about (link reference definitions) occurs 0 times in 25.5 MB. Adopt Lezer's TreeFragment for the editor and a content-sha Map for the corpus. Everything else here is machinery for work that does not exist.

THE DECLARED-VOCABULARY MECHANISM, THE REGISTRY, AND THE LIBRARY-IMPORT MODEL — including `fm:vocab:`, the 12-term cap, the Typst-style namespace/version/immutability design, and the whole §13.6 question. Measured user-invention rate is 0.31% of 4,538 directive uses in Docusaurus's own repo and all 14 exceptions are the three tutorial strings that teach the feature; 847 independently-authored npm docs use exactly GitHub's 5 built-in callout types with zero inventions. `remark-lint-frontmatter-schema` already ships document-declared `$schema` at 36,745 downloads/week and ZERO files across three corpora author it. Ship the INVERSE — `mdmax vocab`, ~2 days, zero new bytes.

PER-SPAN CONFIDENCE / UNCERTAINTY ANNOTATION — 16 of 1,084 files (1.48%) carry any evidence tier tag at all, in a corpus authored by a team whose own plan MANDATES tier tagging on every number, and OKF §5.1 considered a credibility score and explicitly refused it as 'subjective, unportable across consumers, and goes stale'. If provenance ships, ship OKF's three coarse derived tiers or nothing.

MULTI-AGENT CONCURRENCY CONTROL FOR SIMULTANEOUS DOCUMENT EDITING — 29 of 724 written files (4.0%) were touched by more than one session ever, and 0 files by two sessions within 60 minutes, across 1,200 transcripts. The harness already answered by ISOLATION (git worktrees hold 66.3% of the test files), which makes the collision unreachable by construction. NOTE THE CAVEAT AND DO NOT OVER-CUT: that sample is one operator's agent sessions, a population that structurally cannot contain the multi-HUMAN co-editing D1 exists to serve. Cut agent-vs-agent concurrency; do not cite it against human presence.

'WHAT CHANGED SINCE YOU LAST READ THIS' AS A DOCUMENT-SIDE PROTOCOL — MCP's ResourceUpdatedNotification carries exactly one field (`uri`) across all six schema versions, and its newest freshness primitive is a TTL; OKF chose an absolute `stale_after` date and stated why. Two independent shipped designs refused per-reader state on purpose, because it needs identity, storage and a session, none of which a `.md` has.

THE 384-CONFIGURATION PARAMETER SWEEP AS SOMETHING TO RE-RUN OR WITHHOLD — it produced three scalars (3-gram shingles, jaccard ≥ 0.20, margin ≤ 0.05). Publish them. Withholding buys nothing (a competitor re-sweeps in an afternoon on a bigger public corpus) and costs the credibility of an unverifiable 99.627%.

'FEWER TOKENS — 25–168×' AS A PROMISE TO AN AI CONSUMER — those are ratios between ARTIFACT SIZES, not task token savings. The only live measurement of the latter that exists anywhere (okf-skills, 2026-07-27) found the bundle arm spent 5.2% MORE tokens and opened MORE files, and its own authors call the honest reading 'no measurable cost saving, in either direction'. Restate §4.4 as a compression ratio until W2 runs. This is a §14-P9 labelling obligation, not an opinion.

'MARKDOWN VOLUME IS EXPLODING' AS A PITCH LINE — markdown's share of repository file trees did not rise; generic parsers beat the npm baseline by only 1.44×; CommonMark has shipped zero net new conformance examples since 2021-06-19 and cmark-gfm has not cut a release since 2023-07-21. The defensible sentence is 'markdown's READER changed', and it survives a hostile investor with an npm terminal. The other one does not.

THE `EditableTable` / `setTableCell` WRITE PATH — delete it, do not fix it. It is imported by nothing (`components.tsx:36` names the callback `_onEdit`), it corrupts `\|` cells, 7.4% of what it detects as tables are inside code fences, and it dirties 13.4% of files on a no-op. It is dead code today, which is the only reason it is not already a live data-loss bug.

`mdmax unpack` IN V1 — pack is a read transport and needs no inverse. llm-code-format already ships pack+unpack, zero dependencies, nine recognised LLM output conventions, at 387 downloads/week against repomix's 327,543. That is an 846:1 revealed-demand ratio against the operation, measured, in the nearest neighbour.
result.one_sentence: The engine is seven passes and one writer, the writer already works — stock mdast offsets spliced 107,287 blocks across 1,080 of your own files byte-identically this session — and the highest-value technical act this week is replacing the two shipped calls to `matter.stringify` and `doc.toString()` with it, because that single change fixes a live corruption bug that fires on every Publish, proves D7 against real bytes, and is the one assertion in this program that prose cannot turn green.

result.lens: THE VERDICT — integrating the opposition case and the pre-mortem against all 16 areas, for two founders who start building immediately.
result.thesis:
MDMAX should not be built as a compiler program. Build it as a ~600-line library subordinate to the editor, and spend the twelve months on the review loop the compiler was supposed to enable.

Three reasons, in order of evidence strength. (1) Four of six compiler capabilities have working substitutes that were executed and measured this week — LCS diff at 85.0-86.7% vs hash-alone 77.3%, stock mdast offsets splicing byte-perfectly on 1,080/1,080 files, the already-installed yaml Document API, and OKF v0.2 for provenance. (2) The only two engine capabilities with a real in-product caller are both already-shipped data-loss bugs — I verified live that src/modules/share/infrastructure/share-writer.ts calls matter.stringify(parsed.content, data) while its own header says "splicing", and gray-matter re-parses that string argument at index.js:161, so any body opening with a --- block loses it silently. (3) The product admits exactly one user. Verified live: src/modules/auth/domain/allowlist.ts:9 is login.trim().toLowerCase() === allowed.trim().toLowerCase(), and src/container/dependency-container.ts:42 hardcodes AUTHOR = { name: "Sagnik Mitra", email: "sagnikmitra123@gmail.com" } into four use-cases at lines 66, 70, 75, 80. Nothing downstream of that line is a Google Doc, and no compiler makes it one.

Two things sharpen this rather than soften it.

FIRST, the strongest reason to build something survived every attack. mdmax cert is the one capability four independent prior-art searches could not find shipped: moat got total_count 0/0/1; market-and-gift enumerated markdownguide.org's 28 construct ids and found zero of frontmatter, wikilink, callout or mermaid while measuring those constructs at 56-91% prevalence; against inspected the top ten of 4,218 repos and found only parsers; premortem ran four npm searches for 32 results and zero relevant. And rendering-frontier measured GitHub's own API renderer and blob renderer disagreeing on mermaid on identical bytes, live. But it is aimed at the pain the founders' own taxonomy ranks 13th of 14, and its own research area concedes 7 of ~12 target surfaces cannot be probed at all. It is an afternoon and a credibility instrument. It is not the MVP and it is not a moat.

SECOND, and this is the most consequential single reversal in the corpus: against reported the demand evidence favouring real-time collaboration over commenting 6.9:1, and its own verifier killed that as a regex artifact — symmetric counting gives review-loop 169 leaves to collaboration 95, i.e. 1.78:1 the OTHER way. The founders' own scraped demand corpus asks for the review loop more than it asks for multiplayer. That single correction is the difference between "build Yjs" and "build comments", and it points at exactly the intersection product-gap searched and found empty: HackMD has the loop but no local files; Moment.dev has files plus realtime and zero occurrences of comment or suggest; Obsidian has shared vaults and states plainly it has no comments; inkeep/OpenKnowledge shipped content-derived anchoring on 2026-07-30 and explicitly declined teammates in writing.

The honest bottom line for the founders: you have spent 35 days producing a genuinely excellent research record and 532 lines of product source. The record's own diagnosis — "honesty was being converted into inertia" — is correct, and naming it did not stop it, because naming it produced another sentence. The parsing-robustness area wrote the most honest line in the entire program about itself: "this entire area was a code review wearing a research costume and should be re-run as one." That is true of more of this program than one area.

Is it worth twelve months? Only if six things become true, and two of them within thirty days. They are listed in what_to_cut's counterpart below and in the kill list. If a second GitHub login has not written to a document by 31 August, and if Amit has not committed code by then, this is a library and not a company, and the honest move is to say so out loud rather than spend a year finding out.

This is not a roadmap item, it is a live defect with a silent-data-loss variant, and fixing it is simultaneously the first real customer for MDMAX's core primitive. ranked.evidence: VERIFIED LIVE: share-writer.ts calls matter.stringify(parsed.content, data) while the file header says 'splicing the key into the YAML frontmatter'. product-gap measured 33/907 = 3.64% byte-identical on publish; its verifier re-derived the true publish-then-unpublish round trip at 17/736 = 2.31% and found the header/code contradiction verbatim. rendering-frontier independently measured the properties panel dirtying 623/737 = 84.5% of frontmatter files with zero edits made, 197 of them changing line count — which alone makes durable comment anchoring impossible. product-gap found 624/736 = 84.78% of parsed files have a bare YYYY-MM-DD silently coerced to an ISO timestamp. The verifier found a worse, unreported defect: gray-matter/index.js:161 re-parses a string first argument, so share-writer passing parsed.content means any body beginning with a --- delimited block has that block consumed as frontmatter and DROPPED. Also: 170 of 907 blocks (18.7%) do not parse under either YAML library because Obsidian's related: [[a]], [[b]] is not valid YAML, and share-writer has no try/catch, so publishing those files returns a 502.

Gate: publish-then-unpublish is byte-identical on all 907 frontmatter files of corpus_id sha256:3a010b16, AND publish succeeds without a 502 on the 171 that no YAML parser reads. Make the test go RED first against the current writer (it will, at 17/736).

ranked.why: The plan's own corrected text already demotes content-derived re-anchoring to 'the fallback and the verifier, not the primary mechanism.' ranked.evidence: against ran it: LCS over normalized block text resolves 86.658% (verifier independently re-derived 85.036%) against hash-alone-unique at 77.297%, on 29,217 anchorable block-versions from the pinned corpus, and 77.297pp of those are on text unique in the old document and therefore cannot be wrong. It also measured the vault-scale artifact at 25.8 MB against a 234 KB index (110x) where a 200K context holds 2.79% of it. REVEALED DEMAND: llm-code-format already ships the exact round trip (zero dependencies, nine LLM output conventions) at 387 downloads/month against repomix's 327,543 — 846:1. repomix issue 71 has been open 23 months; the maintainer gated it on evidence ('I haven't fully grasped the essence of file splitting effects yet'), the contributor reported back 'not quite what I hoped', and the last comment is 2025-09-08. THE ONLY LIVE-MODEL MEASUREMENT of a projection bundle anywhere (okf-skills, 2026-07-27) found the bundle arm spent 5.2% MORE tokens and opened MORE files. THE FOUNDER'S OWN CORPUS: founder-thesis' headline that 37.2% of files are hand-built bundles was REFUTED by its verifier at ~2.2% — the rest is a machine-generated YAML title-prepend in a sync tree; against measured 45 transclusions in 25.5 MB; markdown-base measured 46.8% of files in zero resolved edges and a maximum transitive blast radius of 54 files.

If yes, this closes in ten minutes and you keep the D4 escape-hatch zip, which is what a departing human actually wants and which the container's disqualifying properties do not apply to.

ranked.item: NEVER BUILD: new syntax, new carriers, a declaration mechanism, a vocabulary registry, a folder compiler's incremental engine, per-span confidence, or a competing provenance vocabulary.
ranked.why: Five areas attacked this from five directions and all five landed in the same place: markdown does not need more expressive capacity, and every attempt to add it has a measured adoption rate near zero. The correct output of all five is recognizers and checkers that write no bytes.
ranked.evidence: hold-more: the best carrier on every objective axis (orphan link reference definition — wins capacity, wins invisibility in 6/6 renderer configs, byte-identical through remark AND prettier) has ZERO uses in 1,084 files and 25.5 MB; markdown-it-decorate achieved perfect silent invisibility and has 1,094 downloads/week, unshipped since 2017 (re-verified live this run). custom-pointers: across 5,245 files in five corpora the user-invention rate is 0.31%, and all 14 exceptions in Docusaurus's 4,538 directives are the three tutorial strings that teach the feature; 847 independently-authored npm docs use exactly GitHub's 5 built-in callout types with zero inventions; where a spec FORCED a type field (four real OKF bundles) it produced 29 values across four incompatible naming conventions with ~42% mutual collisions. markdown-base: 507 of 1,084 files participate in zero resolved edges, 530 affect nothing downstream, max blast radius 54 files, and a full cold lex of all 25.5 MB is 1,056 ms — against Microsoft's own published line that maintaining dependency trees can cost more than the recalculation it saves. agentic-docs: only declared provenance and verification receipts are genuinely unserved, and OKF v0.2 sections 5.1 and 10 now specify both. THE ONE THING WORTH TAKING FROM ALL OF IT: hold-more's placeholder linter — 1,431 bare angle-bracket tokens in 219 of 1,084 files (20.2%) that GitHub silently DELETES from rendered output, with a one-backtick fix and a verified remediation.
ranked.blocked_by: n/a
ranked.ships_as: Deletions from docs/mdmax/PLAN.md. Plus, if you want one cheap win, two recognizers that write no bytes: the placeholder warning above, and mdmax vocab (custom-pointers, ~2 days) which reports the enum a corpus already uses plus case/morphology drift and the 18.91% of frontmatter blocks that no YAML parser reads. Both are diagnostics that cannot flatter you, which is the same rule that picked mdmax cert.

Take the code review, skip the research.
ranked.evidence: (a) WIKILINK_RE in src/modules/vault/infrastructure/markdown-parser.ts:12 is strictly quadratic, k=2.00 — verifier reproduced 577.4 / 2,282.5 / 9,258.1 ms at 20k/40k/80k occurrences, and 11,012.9 ms on a realistic 749 KB half-typed vault. Note the verifier also corrected the researcher: parseMarkdown is server-only, so it blocks the Node event loop rather than the browser main thread. (b) gray-matter/js-yaml (YAML 1.1) vs eemeli/yaml (1.2 core) diverge on 625 of 737 parsed files across 973 occurrences — one class, dates coerced to Date objects. (c) share-writer, already item 2. But note the verifier could not reproduce the headline numbers (359,959 ms vs a claimed 196,096, two runs of identical code disagreeing by 1.8x) and found micromark is NOT linear on nested blockquotes either (k=2.42).
