result.dependencies:
STRICT ORDER, with the gating relations named.

DAY 0, no dependencies, five minutes: push the branch, commit docs/mdmax and docs/engine/research, decide on package.json. Everything below is worthless if the disk dies.

DAY 0-1, no dependencies, parallel: (a) the splice writer and its RED gate; (b) the tenancy assertion committed RED; (c) the three parsing-robustness defects. None of these blocks the others. All three are code, and the standing rule should point at (b) specifically, not at "engine code" in the abstract — a rule that names an artifact cannot be satisfied by prose.

WEEK 1, calendar-blocked, runs alongside everything: the five conversations. These GATE items 6 and 7 — they can cancel the certificate and they can invert D3. Do not build the certificate before them; product-gap's pre-registered prediction is that four of five reviewers stall at the login wall, and if that fires, D3 is a product decision to be made at auth rather than an auth decision to be deferred.

WEEK 2-4, blocked by the tenancy assertion going green: multi-tenancy proper (invites, share-link roles), then the comments collection, then the anchoring cascade behind it. The cascade (item 4) is buildable in parallel but must not be TRUSTED until item 8 (the stratified re-derivation) has run, because the number that would justify tier 3 has never been reproduced and its source section contradicts itself 113-to-14.

BLOCKED ON AN EXTERNAL ACQUISITION: item 8 needs a corpus selected by EDIT SHAPE, not authorship. None of the three pinned roots qualifies (0.9%, 9.9%, 8.3% of pairs delete more than two lines against a 25% bar). Finding one is a real task and it is the honest prerequisite to publishing any reliability number.

NEVER SEQUENCED: the container, new carriers, the vocabulary registry, the folder compiler's incremental engine, the streaming prefix mode, per-span confidence.

THE ONE ORDERING THE PLAN GETS BACKWARDS: S5 (the editor floor) is currently scheduled as a parallel track with no engine dependency, described in the plan's own words as work that "will keep losing priority to compiler work precisely because it is uninteresting." That prediction is the largest single risk in the document. S5 is not parallel. S5 is the product, and every engine item on this list exists to serve it.
contradictions: CONTAINER: container-thesis says ship mdmax pack beside mdmax cert; against, premortem and founder-thesis's own verifier say never. I SIDE WITH NEVER. container-thesis proved the engineering (1084/1084 byte-identical, 120x cheaper than a zip) and then killed its own product in the same report — the pack must never be the write surface because boundary repair on the realistic merge case is 119/120 WRONG, and the vault-scale artifact is 110x more expensive than the index that answers the same question. Meanwhile the revealed demand is 846:1 against (llm-code-format 387/mo vs repomix 327,543), repomix issue 71 died 23 months ago on exactly this evidence question, and the only live-model measurement in existence went the wrong way at +5.2% tokens. Engineering feasibility is not demand.

THE MOTHER-MARKDOWN: founder-thesis says it is THE thesis and the only D6-compatible construction; markdown-base and against measure the graph as dust. I SIDE WITH DUST, and note that founder-thesis's own verifier did the killing — the 37.2%/47.7% 'hand-built bundles' figure is ~2.2%, the remainder being a machine-generated YAML title-prepend in a sync tree, which REVERSES that area's pre-registered falsifier. Corroborating: 46.8% of files in zero resolved edges, median out-degree 2, 45 transclusions in 25.5 MB, max transitive blast radius 54 files. The image is a metaphor the founder repeated and the room heard as a spec. Settle it with founder-thesis's K-D: one question, one conversation.

THE MOAT: moat's headline claim that S5 multi-tenancy is the only durable moat was KILLED by its own verifier as carrying zero evidence across ten claims. I UPHOLD THE CLAIM AND REJECT THE REASONING. The verifier is right that moat asserted it — but against, premortem and product-gap independently converge on the same conclusion with hard evidence (firestore.rules declaring a model with zero implementation; one-string auth; a hardcoded AUTHOR; an empty workspace route). Take the conclusion from the three areas that measured it, not from the area that asserted it.

DEMAND FOR THE REVIEW LOOP: against reported real-time collaboration beating commenting 6.9:1 in the demand corpus and built its whole strategic recommendation on it. Its verifier recounted symmetrically and got review-loop 169 to collaboration 95 — 1.78:1 THE OTHER WAY. I SIDE WITH THE VERIFIER, and this is the single most consequential kill in the corpus, because it flips the recommendation from 'build Yjs multiplayer' to 'build comments'. Anyone quoting against's strategic conclusion is quoting a regex artifact.

THE CERTIFICATE: rendering-frontier says ship it (surfaces measurably disagree); market-and-gift says it targets a non-purchasing pain ranked 13th of 14; moat says it is the only unclaimed capability in the program. ALL THREE ARE RIGHT ABOUT DIFFERENT QUESTIONS and the resolution is a sequencing one — it is genuinely unclaimed (moat, four searches), it does find real disagreement (rendering-frontier measured GitHub's own two renderers disagreeing on mermaid), and it will not be the reason anyone pays (market-and-gift, whose verifier also found the pain is stronger than reported — 'Churns the purist early adopters', not 'Annoys' — while still ranked 13th). So: one afternoon, a credibility instrument, never the MVP and never the spearhead. Note also market-and-gift's own K-D, which is the honest pre-commitment: if the user probe shows 15 of 30 naming the cert as their reason to pay, promote it and re-sequence.

T13 SEVERITY: market-and-gift's headline says T13 markdown/frontmatter mangling is severity 'ANNOYS'; its verifier found line 42 of the product plan actually reads 'Churns the purist early adopters' and that 'Annoys' is T14 on the next line — the label was shifted exactly one band in the direction that strengthened the researcher's own recommendation. I SIDE WITH THE VERIFIER. The pain is worse than reported and still ranks 13th of 14. Both facts matter: it does not drive purchase, AND it is the product's name, which is a positioning constraint no ranking captures. That is precisely why item 2 is a defect fix and not a feature.

OKF: agentic-docs says Google already specified the agent-native document and MDMAX's section 4.5 is closed; against says OKF has zero overlap with block identity, splicing or degradation and its tooling is at 52 downloads/week. BOTH ARE TRUE AND THE SYNTHESIS IS SIMPLE — OKF took provenance and left identity. Its own section 5.1 states verbatim that it does not store a credibility score, its section 12 defers the runtime protocol and attester ABI, and its section 11 forbids consumers from rejecting a bundle for broken cross-links. So: emit OKF's fields rather than designing a vocabulary (agentic-docs is right), treat it as one cert column rather than a strategic question (against is right), and note the one genuine opening — a PRODUCER-side checker, which OKF explicitly declines to require and which nobody in its 287-repo ecosystem ships.

THE ERA: the-era's design recommendation is a streaming prefix-parse mode with stable block ids. I CUT IT. Its own kill condition (P3) predicts the failure — real model output is fence-heavy, so if more than 30% of prefixes sit inside an unterminated code fence, stable ids for settled blocks buy almost nothing. Its verifier additionally found the 'new category' is one vendor counted up to four times (streamdown, remend, rehype-harden and harden-react-markdown are all Vercel, with streamdown pinning the other two as direct dependencies), which halves the market signal to ~16M/mo. The area's surviving contribution is a deletion, not an addition: stop saying markdown volume is exploding. Repository share fell 12.68% to 10.41% on the researcher's measurement (directionally reversed by the verifier on a specified 10-repo test, which is itself a reason to say nothing), CommonMark has shipped zero new conformance examples since 2021-06-19, and cmark-gfm's last release is 2023-07-21 pinned to a 2019 spec.

PARSING NUMBERS: parsing-robustness reports mdast at 196,096 ms on 200k list items and micromark linear at k=1.08; its verifier got 359,959 ms (1.84x) with k=4.00, found two runs of identical code disagreeing by 1.8x, and found micromark super-linear on nested blockquotes at k=2.42. THE PRESCRIPTION SURVIVES, THE NUMBERS DO NOT. Do not build an mdast tree for a whole document — but the parser that stayed near-linear on every shape tested was Lezer, which is already in the dependency tree via CodeMirror, and that is the honest conclusion rather than 'consume micromark's event stream'.
what_to_cut: The container / mother-markdown / mdmax pack and unpack — 846:1 revealed demand against, its own round trip proven unsafe at 119/120, and the founder's own corpus refutes the topology it assumes. Settle with one question to the founder, then delete the section.
The format profile and any spec document. MDMAX is a library with two callers, not a format with an ecosystem.
The declared-vocabulary mechanism, fm:vocab, and any registry — 0.31% user-invention rate across 5,245 files; where a spec forced declaration it produced drift, not vocabulary.
Every new carrier. The best one on every objective metric has zero uses in 1,084 files, and the market's own verdict is markdown-it-decorate at 1,094 downloads/week, unshipped since 2017.

The folder compiler's incremental engine and rebuilder. 507 of 1,084 files affect nothing downstream, max blast radius is 54 files, and a full cold lex is 1,056 ms. Keep only the symbol table, the affected-target query and the orphan report, all of which are useful at cold-build time.

Per-span confidence and uncertainty annotation — 16 of 1,084 files carry any evidence tier at all, in a corpus whose authors mandate tier tagging on every number, and OKF explicitly refuses to store a credibility score.
A competing provenance vocabulary. Emit OKF v0.2 sections 5.1 fields and move on; being the third entrant behind Google and C2PA is not a position.
The streaming prefix-parse mode. Its own kill condition is likely to fire on real model output, and the market signal behind it is one vendor counted four times.

The AI projection tier as a token-saving promise. The 25-168x figures are ratios between artifact sizes; the only measurement of task tokens anywhere found +5.2% and MORE files opened. Restate it as a compression ratio or delete the sentence.

The graph view. It ships, it carries a runtime dependency, and 'graph' appears 0 times across 89 sourced feature requests and 0 times in the round-2 corpus, while median document degree in the founder's own vault is 0.
EditableTable and setTableCell — dead code today (imported by nothing, its callback named _onEdit), with a measured 13.4% no-op dirty rate and silent escaped-pipe corruption. Delete rather than fix.
The claim that markdown volume is exploding. It is not, and an investor with an npm terminal will find that out in ninety seconds. The defensible pitch is that markdown's READER changed.

Any further research fan-out. Two workflows, 34 areas, roughly 8 million tokens, 6,233 documentation lines against 365 code lines, zero live model calls and zero user conversations. The marginal research hour is now provably worth less than the marginal test.
result.one_sentence: Stop building the compiler and ship the second user: the engine that is worth building is a 600-line library whose two real callers are already corrupting files in production, and the only thing twelve months can buy you — a review loop over markdown files people own, behind a login that admits somebody other than Sagnik — currently has zero lines written against it and a competitor who shipped the hard half of it on 30 July and has publicly declined the easy half.

result.lens: THE ERA AND THE VISION — is there a new era of markdown, what is MDMAX actually the answer to, and do the container/mother-markdown and markdown-as-codebase theses survive contact with the founder's own corpus?
result.thesis:
THE ERA IS REAL AND IT IS EXACTLY ONE FACT: markdown's dominant reader stopped being a human and became a model, while the format itself froze. Both halves are measured, and I re-verified the second half today at primary tier — commonmark/commonmark-spec's last three releases (0.31.0, 0.31.1, 0.31.2) all landed on 2024-01-28 and there has been none since; github/cmark-gfm's last release is 0.29.0.gfm.13 on 2023-07-21, still pinned to CommonMark 0.29 from 2019, which means GitHub renders the world's markdown against a seven-year-old spec. On the reader side: markdown is the #1 file type an agent reads (23.51%, ahead of .tsx and .ts) and #2 written, replicated on an independent scan; 94.1-94.3% of June 2026 corpus files were created inside an agent session, replicated to within one file of 991; AGENTS.md went 0% to 30.67% of the 300 most-starred GitHub repos in fifteen months. That asymmetry — a frozen substrate with a multiplied and different consumer — is the whole opportunity, and Sagnik named it correctly eighteen research areas before anyone measured it ("AI is representing a response in Markdown. That is why the whole research is around Markdown").

WHAT IS NOT THE ERA, AND MUST LEAVE THE PITCH: volume. The claim that markdown's share of repository trees fell 12.68% to 10.41% is unreproducible (twelve unnamed repos, no corpus_id) and reversed on a fully-specified ten-repo test that shows it ROSE 2.39% to 2.74%. Neither direction is established. Also not the era: a "new tooling category." I checked the registry today — streamdown 2.5.0's repository is github.com/vercel/streamdown, packages/streamdown, and it pins remend 1.3.0 and rehype-harden ^1.1.8 as DIRECT dependencies, so streamdown (4,691,299/wk) plus remend (6,173,301/wk) double-counts one install base, and that base is roughly 8% of marked alone (61,032,058/wk). The streaming-render category is real, fast, single-vendor and small. Betting the product on it is betting on Vercel's roadmap.

SO WHAT IS MDMAX THE ANSWER TO? Not to more markdown. To a document whose reader changed and whose review loop was never built for either reader. Concretely three things: proving what survives the trip to a given consumer (`cert`), writing without disturbing (`edit`), and telling a machine or a human which references are load-bearing (`refs`). Everything else in the six-capability list is either commodity, unmeasured, or refuted.

THE TWO FOUNDER IMAGES, DECIDED.

(1) MOTHER-MARKDOWN / CONTAINER — REAL ONLY AS A BOUNDED, READ-ONLY, MACHINE-FACING PACK. Dead in the form described. Three independent reasons, and the first is arithmetic I ran today against corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…: the container is 25,548,765 bytes against a one-line-per-document index at 105,538 bytes — 242x. At 3.6 bytes/token a 200K window holds 2.82% of the container and 682% of the index; even a 1M window holds 14.1%; the mean file is 23,569 bytes so a 200K pack carries about thirty average files. "One single markdown file... one single software to load everything" is not a design preference that lost an argument, it is impossible at his own vault's scale. Second, the demand: llm-code-format already ships pack AND unpack, zero dependencies, and gets 387 downloads/month against repomix's 327,543 — 846:1. The round trip is not unclaimed, it is claimed and unwanted. Third, and this is the one that should change your confidence in the whole research corpus: the empirical grounding for the container ("he already hand-builds bundles across 37.2% of files and 47.7% of bytes") was verified to be 92.3% a machine-generated YAML title-prepend inside one sync tree — honest figure ~2.2% of files. The researcher's own pre-registered falsifier was declared "FAILED TO REFUTE, in the founder's favour," and it had in fact FIRED. That is the exact flattering-direction failure this gate was convened to stop, reproduced inside the gate.

(2) MARKDOWN-AS-CODEBASE — REAL AS A SYMBOL TABLE, DEAD AS A BUILD SYSTEM, and the corpus refutes its motivating image harder than anyone has said out loud. I measured the topology myself today over all 1,084 files (re-hashed, 0 missing, 0 mismatches, corpus_id re-derived and MATCHING): median out-degree ZERO, mean 2.27, p90 5; 597 files (55.1%) have zero resolved outbound edges; 529 (48.8%) have zero inbound; 502 files (46.3%) are FULLY ISOLATED — no in, no out; the graph splits into 511 connected components of which the largest holds 40.1% of the corpus. Transclusion `![[...]]` occurs 45 times in 25.5 MB, and a prior verifier established that all 45 are syntax documentation, so genuine content transclusion is ZERO. Four independent agents plus me now agree. "A single markdown connected to hundreds of markdowns, and those hundreds connected to hundreds each" is not an approximation of this corpus — it is the opposite of it. What IS real, and I replicated it a third time: `[text](path.md)` resolves 546/637 = 85.71% while `[[Name]]` resolves 2,754/9,962 = 27.65%, a 58-point gap on identical files, and no tool implements the two-tier semantics that gap demands (Docusaurus throws on every file link at 1.5M downloads/week; Obsidian errors on nothing; both wrong).

WHERE THE VISION OUTRUNS THE EVIDENCE, PLAINLY: the graph has no substrate; the volume claim is unproven in both directions; the container's motivating evidence collapsed; the 99.627% anchoring figure has been re-derived by NOBODY including every agent who quoted it, and an adversarial 30-line LCS diff baseline sits at 86.658% (its own verifier reproduced 85.036%) while the plan concedes a previous document version essentially always exists; and "features unseen in the industry" is bounded much tighter than the phrase implies, because `![[X]]` renders as the literal string `![[X]]` with the payload absent — any capability whose payload is BY REFERENCE is void under D6, which excludes transclusion, cross-file reactive state, and sidecar-resolved block metadata from the Max tier entirely.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE FOUNDER'S INSTINCT, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT PART: "we cannot invent a new markdown... but we can invent a new style of UTILIZATION" is D6 and D8 stated before D6 and D8 existed, and the measurement proves it — an unknown fence language round-trips byte-perfectly while an unknown node type throws. Utilization is genuinely the only available move, and he found it by reasoning rather than by measuring. That instinct is worth more than the two images it produced.

ranked.item: `mdmax cert` — the (product, surface) degradation certificate, shipped as a CLI plus a dated, expiring public dataset
ranked.why: The only capability that survived adversarial verification in every single area that touched it, and the only asset in the entire program whose value INCREASES with elapsed time. It is also the operational form of the one era fact that is fully established: the format froze while its consumers multiplied and diverged. It cannot flatter you — a matrix of N constructs by M consumers emitting PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT can only tell you things you did not write.
ranked.evidence: [measured, prior] Across 24 renderer configurations only the link reference definition and the `[//]: #` idiom are invisible in 24/24; frontmatter is VISIBLE in 23/24; the HTML comment produces 8 distinct outputs and GitHub's blob renderer deletes it outright; the unknown-language fence is the only carrier reaching both a raw-file and a sanitized-HTML consumer intact. [primary, my own measurement today] The targets move while the spec does not: commonmark/commonmark-spec's last three releases (0.31.0/0.31.1/0.31.2) all published 2024-01-28 with none since; github/cmark-gfm's last release is 0.29.0.gfm.13 on 2023-07-21, still pinned to CommonMark 0.29 (2019); commonmark/cmark shipped 0.31.2 on 2026-02-14, i.e. maintenance patches of a 2024 spec. Inside the research window alone markdown-it shipped 15.0.0 (2026-07-30) and marked shipped 18.0.7 (2026-07-21). [search-only, three independent areas converging] No prior art: GitHub repo searches for 'markdown renderer compatibility matrix', 'markdown degradation certificate' and 'markdown target conformance report' return total_count 0, 0 and 1-unrelated; npm has no markdown-compat/markdown-conformance/babelmark package; babelmark3 differs SPEC EXAMPLES across PARSERS, not a real document across PRODUCT SURFACES, and 23 of its 38 providers sit behind encrypted URLs so CI reproducibility is structurally impossible. [verifier correction, accepted] markdownguide.org IS prior art — 70 tools x 28 constructs — but it tracks ZERO of frontmatter, wikilinks, callouts, mermaid or math, which are the constructs actually written in 2026.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. Zero engine dependencies — no anchor, no normalize, no splice. This is the two-day S2 item and it can start the hour you finish reading this. One discipline: its gate must go RED first (assert 'an HTML comment survives to a GitHub blob view' and require it to fail) before any cell is trusted.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax cert <file> --targets github-blob,github-comment,github-pages,github-api,obsidian,frontmatter-preview,frontmatter-pdf --fail-on CORRUPT --json`, plus a versioned JSON dataset in which OSS rows are REPRODUCIBLE (vendored, version-pinned renderer, anyone can rerun) and closed-SaaS rows are OBSERVED, carry an `observed_at` and the product build string, and render as STALE after 90 days. The expiry field is the moat mechanism: it makes a copied dataset visibly stale. Ship the DATASET before the DESIGN — the design is a weekend for a competitor, the dated observation series is not. First row it should print is frontmatter's own preview (mermaid 11.15.0, lockfile-pinned) disagreeing with frontmatter's own PDF export (cdn `mermaid@11`, resolving to 11.16.0 today).

ranked.item: `mdmax edit` — the splice writer, with the two in-product callers wired on day one
ranked.why: The only engine capability with paying customers inside your own product RIGHT NOW, and the only one that is a theorem rather than a preference. Every other capability is a bet about a future user; this one fixes bugs that fire on every publish. It is also the prerequisite for anything anchored, because a writer that moves line counts breaks comment anchoring before comment anchoring exists.
ranked.evidence: [primary] Foster et al., TOPLAS 2007, Lemma 3.9 — a total well-behaved lens whose `put` ignores the original source requires `get` to be a bijection; markdown's parse is nowhere near injective, with 443 of 655 CommonMark spec examples being two distinct source strings with an identical tree. [measured, replicated three ways] 0 of 51 files, 0 of 1,080 files, and 0 of 120 seeded-random files survive a tree round trip byte-identically. [measured, two independent agents to the digit] The shipped Publish path reaches byte-identity on 33 of 907 frontmatter blocks (3.64%) and coerces a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` into an ISO timestamp in 624 of 736 parsed files (84.78%); a third measurement of the true publish-then-unpublish round trip gives 17/736 = 2.31%, so the headline is conservative. [measured, primary read] `share-writer.ts:26` calls `matter.stringify` under a file header that says verbatim it is 'splicing the key into the YAML frontmatter' — a live D7 violation reached on every publish AND unpublish. [measured] The properties panel re-emits YAML through `stringifyFrontmatterDoc` and dirties 623 of 737 frontmatter-bearing files (84.5%) with zero edits made, 197 of them changing the document's LINE COUNT; the wiring is unflagged, EditorPane.tsx:647 → :498 → PropertiesPanel.tsx:79 → frontmatter.ts:46. [new defect, verifier] Worse than reported: gray-matter's `matter.stringify` re-parses a string argument (index.js:161), so passing `parsed.content` re-reads the BODY as frontmatter — it throws a 502 on md/pj.md today and, for any body beginning with a `---` block, will silently CONSUME AND DROP it.
ranked.blocked_by: S3 — `normalize()` must be frozen and versioned with a fixture BEFORE any anchor is persisted, or every stored anchor silently re-keys while the published number keeps describing code that no longer exists. Half a day, and it is genuinely sequential.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax edit <file> --old <text> --new <text>` → splice + receipt + post-write re-anchor assertion, plus two immediate in-product callers: the share-writer and the properties panel, both re-routed through a byte-range splice (the `yaml` package already in your dependency tree exposes `node.range` on every AST node; never call `doc.toString()`). GATE, restated so it is satisfiable: publish→unpublish is byte-identical on all 907 frontmatter blocks AND does not 502 on the 170 that no YAML parser can read, verified by an INDEPENDENT oracle that shares no code with the writer. Note the 171st case separately — md/pj.md parses fine and throws at stringify; a splice fixes the 170 by never parsing, and does not automatically fix that one.

ranked.item: `mdmax refs` — hard/soft reference resolver, orphan report, affected-target query, and a committed lock file. Explicitly NOT a compiler and NOT a build system.
ranked.why: Markdown-as-a-codebase is real at exactly this size and no larger. The hard/soft split is the single most-replicated structural finding in the program and nobody in the field implements it. Everything above it in the build-system stack — incremental invalidation, dependency closure, topological ordering — dies on contact with the measured topology. Shipping the small version is a week; shipping the large version is a quarter spent on machinery with no work to do.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, today, corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 — all 1,084 files re-read, re-hashed, 0 missing, 0 mismatches, corpus_id re-derived and MATCHING] Fence-stripped and frontmatter-stripped: 9,962 wikilinks of which 2,754 resolve (27.65%); 637 markdown-syntax file links of which 546 resolve (85.71%). A 58-point gap on identical files. Prior independent runs give 88.62% vs 25.50% and a verifier's re-derivation gives the same ~58-point gap — three measurements, one conclusion. [own-measurement, today] Topology: median out-degree 0, mean 2.27, p90 5, max 186; 597 files (55.1%) zero-out; 529 (48.8%) zero-in; 502 (46.3%) fully isolated; 511 connected components with the largest at 40.1%. Transclusion in body: 45 occurrences in 25.5 MB. [measured, prior] Blast radius: median 1 file, maximum 54 (5.0% of the corpus); a full cold lex of all 25,548,765 bytes runs in ~1,056 ms, so the incremental engine has nothing to save — and Microsoft says this about its own dependency engine verbatim: 'the time taken to build and maintain the dependency trees needed for Smart Recalculation is larger than the time saved.' [measured, prior] 41 strongly-connected components covering 26.2% of files: it is not a DAG, so separate-compilation vocabulary does not transfer. [primary] Docusaurus ships `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'` as its default at 1,513,550 downloads/week and would fail this corpus thousands of times; Obsidian never errors on any unresolved reference. Both are wrong for a corpus where 72.35% of wikilinks are correct authoring.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing technically. One naming discipline, and it is load-bearing: do not call this a compiler. The word imports the assumption that resolution failure is an error, and that assumption is false for 72.35% of this corpus's references. A linter with an 88% deliberate-false-positive rate is a linter that gets switched off — the record already measures naive checking at 2-25% precision.
ranked.ships_as: A committed, diffable lock file (per unit: path, content sha256, interface hash, each resolved outbound edge carrying the target's sha at link time, and the list of unresolved SOFT names), plus three queries: `mdmax refs --affected <file>` (what breaks if I move this — Sphinx computes exactly this internally and throws it away, nobody exposes it), `--orphans` (529 files have zero inbound and nobody tells their owner), and `--check` which fails ONLY on hard `[text](path.md)` links and NEVER on `[[Name]]`. Add `mdmax vocab` as a ~40-line companion: the 1,409 dangling `[[X]]` targets that repeat across two or more documents are a controlled vocabulary the author built unprompted, not 10,798 errors — it is the only diagnostic in this program that would tell Sagnik something about his own writing he does not already know.

ranked.item: Prefix / streaming parse mode — a document model that accepts INCOMPLETE input as a first-class state
ranked.why: This is the single place where the era claim converts directly into a capability nobody has built. The rendering layer solved token-by-token markdown; no EDITOR and no DOCUMENT MODEL did. And it costs almost nothing, because stable block ids under prefix arrival fall out of the S1 exact-hash-over-normalized-text stage you are building anyway. It is the time-axis version of the anchoring guarantee you already need on the edit axis.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, today] The demand is real and single-vendor, which is both the argument for and the caveat on this item: streamdown 4,691,299 downloads/week and remend 6,173,301/week, but streamdown 2.5.0's `repository` is git+https://github.com/vercel/streamdown with `directory: packages/streamdown` and its `dependencies` include `remend: "1.3.0"` and `rehype-harden: ^1.1.8` — one product counted up to four times. Against marked at 61,032,058/week, the whole streaming-render category is ~8% of one incumbent's install base. [search, prior, three queries] npm registry searches for 'incomplete markdown streaming', 'streaming markdown editor' and 'markdown block anchor id' return renderers in every top-8 slot and zero editors, zero document models, zero anchoring packages. [own-measurement, prior] Grepping docs/mdmax/PLAN.md, docs/engine/PLAN.md and docs/engine/README.md for stream|incomplete|unterminated|partial returns 3 hits, all about MD4C parser throughput — the plan has no coverage of this at all. [primary] micromark's own README states the hard limit and it belongs in your design doc verbatim: 'Some of the work to parse markdown can be done streaming, but in the end buffering is required.'
ranked.blocked_by: S3 (frozen normalize), and one pre-registered risk that must be tested before you build it: if more than 30% of prefixes over REAL model-authored markdown sit inside an unterminated code fence, stable ids for settled blocks buy almost nothing, because the interesting content is the part that has not settled — and model output is fence-heavy. Test that on 500 assistant markdown responses from transcripts (an explicitly different, stated selection from the pinned corpus) before writing the feature.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax parse --prefix --ids` on stdin, emitting NDJSON of {block_id, kind, byte_range, stable}. Contract: for any document D and prefixes k < k', every block id assigned at k outside the OPEN region is byte-identical at k'. The trailing incomplete region is a single explicitly-typed OPEN node (open_fence, open_table, open_list, open_paragraph) carrying raw bytes. ONE CORRECTION from the verifier that must go into the contract: a link reference definition arriving later mutates a settled, NON-trailing block's rendering — 'See [foo].' becomes a live link when '[foo]: /url' arrives three paragraphs later — so `stable` must be defined as ID-stability ONLY, and blocks containing unresolved link references must be reported stable:false. Sharpest irony available: the offending construct is one of the only two carriers your own research found invisible in 24/24 renderers.

ranked.item: `mdmax pack` — bounded, machine-facing, READ-ONLY. The mother-markdown in the only form the evidence permits.
ranked.why: It is Sagnik's most-repeated want across four sessions, it is the 'helping out is 50%' public good in its most distributable form, and it runs inside other people's context windows, which is a distribution channel. But every version of it larger than 'a bounded selection under a token budget' is refuted, and the write path is unsafe. Ship the small true version, and tell him the arithmetic rather than declining the idea.
ranked.evidence: [measured, prior, re-derived by its own verifier] The mechanics work: 1,084/1,084 files round-trip byte-identically at +0.892% overhead (verifier reproduced +0.888%); the single-file container costs ~120-190x less git storage per edit than a zip (263 B vs 31,590 B) and yields a reviewable two-line text diff instead of 'Binary files differ'; it gzips 15.7% smaller than the zip and puts the index at 0.49% of the file instead of 98.8%. [own-measurement, today, corpus_id sha256:3a010b16…] But the vault-scale form is arithmetically impossible: container 25,548,765 bytes against a one-line-per-document index at 105,538 bytes = 242.1x. At 3.6 bytes/token a 200K window holds 2.82% of the container and 682% of the index; at 3.2 B/tok it is 2.51%, at 4.0 B/tok 3.13% — robust across the range. A 1M-token window still holds only 14.1%. Mean file 23,569 bytes, so a 200K pack carries about thirty average files. [measured, prior] The demand for the round trip is 846:1 AGAINST: llm-code-format v3.1.0 already ships pack and unpack, zero dependencies, recognises nine LLM output conventions, and gets 387 downloads/month against repomix's 327,543. repomix issue #226 (unpack) has 0 reactions after 19 months. [verifier] Prior art is much thicker than the research claimed: aider (47,848 stars) already ships the exact path-line-plus-fenced-payload bundle format in `wholefile_prompts.py` and unpacks it to disk in `wholefile_coder.py::get_edits()`, and `base_coder.py::choose_fence()` already re-derives the delimiter at emit time. gpt-engineer (55,173 stars) is the same category. [verifier, decisive for the carrier] The delimiter is unsafe as a durable artifact: `mdast-util-to-markdown` DOWNGRADES a 4-backtick wrapper to 3 backticks, and 45.76% of corpus files contain a ``` fence — so any bundle that passes through one normalising markdown tool has its members terminate early.
ranked.blocked_by: `mdmax edit`. A lossless bundle needs the same splice-and-identity discipline the rest of the engine needs; building pack first means solving the identity problem twice, badly. Also blocked on accepting that this is a READ format: the boundary-repair evidence (119/120 wrong on merge-across) is from an unreproducible fixture, but 'refuse and localise, never repair' is the conservative default and costs nothing to adopt.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax pack --budget <tokens>` over an EXPLICIT selection, never a whole vault. Path carried in the fence INFO STRING, never in a `## File:` heading (13 of 60 heading paths corrupt through one stringifier pass, non-locally). Delimiter re-derived at emit time per aider's choose_fence, never trusted from a written artifact. Per-entry sha256, byte count, and a trailing-newline flag (26.57% of corpus files lack one; concatenation silently welds them). HARD REFUSAL above the target model's window, with the index offered instead. Never hand a model a pack and ask for the pack back — ask for per-file whole-file listings in aider's shape, which is the format models are most reliably well-formed in (median 99.60% vs 94.20% for diffs) and which is structurally one entry of your own container, so one scanner serves both. MIT, `npx mdmax pack`, spec and reference unpacker published together.

ranked.item: The content-derived anchoring resolver — as VERIFIER and FALLBACK, with its flagship number unpublished until re-derived
ranked.why: The plan already demoted this correctly ('the fallback and the verifier, not the primary mechanism') and the demotion is right, because in frontmatter a previous version of the document essentially always exists. What is left is real but marginal, and the marginal value is the residual the diff gets wrong — not the headline. Publishing 99.627% before anyone reproduces it is the single most likely way this program loses credibility with a competent outside reader.
ranked.evidence: [measured, but RE-DERIVED BY NOBODY — the plan concedes this in §9.4 and every agent who quoted it tagged it 'not re-run by me'] 99.627% correct / 0.050% false / 0.323% refusal over 41,642 block-versions from 294 revision pairs. [measured, adversarial] A 30-line LCS diff baseline resolves 86.658% (its own verifier independently reproduced 85.036%), with 76.3 percentage points PROVABLY unambiguous because the matched text is unique in the old document, and it additionally absorbs the entire duplicate-text class. That is the baseline the flagship must beat, and it has never been run head to head. [measured, conceded in the plan] The flagship is a BLOCK figure; comments anchor RANGES, and it does not transfer. Roughly one heading in four is not anchorable at all. [own-observation of the corpus's edit shape, prior, and the reason the re-derivation gate is weak] 86.6% of `.md` file-revisions in the corpus's largest root delete zero lines — a zero-deletion revision leaves every prior block byte-identical, so S1 resolves it by construction, which is why S1's 87.0% and the append rate agree so closely. [primary, external] Hypothes.is production data, arXiv 1512.06195: ~22% of 20,953 highlighted-text annotations can no longer be attached. [verifier, decisive] NEITHER SIDE HAS GROUND TRUTH FOR 'FALSE'. Every anchoring number in this program — 99.627%, 86.658%, 85.036% — is a resolution rate, not a correctness rate, until somebody hand-audits a sample. [competitive] inkeep/OpenKnowledge merged content-derived comment anchoring on 2026-07-30 (exact quote plus auto-widened prefix/suffix, orphan-rather-than-guess) and it reached npm at 0.46.0-beta.32 on 2026-08-01, absent from stable 0.45.4. result.dependencies:
STRICT ORDER, and the first item is not optional.

S-MINUS-1 — PROTECT THE EVIDENCE. FIVE MINUTES, AND IT IS A RULE 2 GATE SO I HAVE NOT DONE IT. I verified this myself today: `git ls-files docs/mdmax/ docs/engine/research/` returns EMPTY. `docs/mdmax/PLAN.md` and `docs/engine/research/corpus-manifest.json` are both `??` — untracked, not gitignored, simply never added — along with all four workflow result artifacts. HEAD is 798ebbf3, origin/main is 8eb4de25, you are 16 commits ahead, and `git branch -r --contains HEAD` returns EMPTY: this branch exists on no remote. The entire engine program — the plan this gate is convened over, the pinned corpus every number in it cites, and 4.9 MB of research — lives on one laptop, on one never-pushed branch, and the two most important files are not committed to even that. One `git clean -fdx` ends the program. Proposed operation: `git add docs/mdmax docs/engine/research HANDOFF-*.md && git push -u origin engine/plan-and-diagnostics`. That is an outbound push and it needs an explicit yes. Do it before anything else in this document.

S0 — HYGIENE, HALF A DAY, and one item on it is now urgent and unlisted. The working-tree `package.json` has been clobbered from 98 lines to `{"type":"module"}` — 1 insertion, 97 deletions, uncommitted — by a research subagent that wanted to run bare .mjs files. Every script (verify, typecheck, lint, test, build, arch) and every dependency declaration is gone from the tree. `npm run verify` cannot run, and any agent reading dependencies from package.json right now gets `{}`. `git checkout -- package.json` restores it; inspect the uncommitted `search-index.ts` change (11+/4-) before you do. RULE 2 — needs a yes. Also on S0: add `.claude/worktrees` to the vitest exclude, because 164 of 247 collected test files (66.4%) are two abandoned worktrees pinned at a pre-work commit, and until that lands no test result means anything.

S1 — RECONCILE, ONE DAY, WITH ONE CORRECTION TO THE PLAN. The plan's S1 says 'Read OKF SPEC.md v0.2 — we have decided against it twice, unread.' That is now stale: at least three agents in this gate read all 37,544 bytes at primary tier, and the position writes itself. OKF specifies document-level provenance (§5.1 sources/generated/verified, §5.5 stale_after), explicitly declines a runtime (§10 'it does not execute anything itself', §12 defers the runtime protocol, attester ABI, portability and sandboxing), and its identity is the FILE PATH — it contains no block identity, no range anchoring and no splice guarantee. Its conformance bar is two predicates (parseable frontmatter, non-empty type). Your corpus is already ~59-73% conformant with nobody having read it. So: OKF is a cheap interop COLUMN in `cert`, plus a pass-through of its provenance vocabulary, and it is a distribution channel with 287 public repos rather than a strategic question. Write that down and close it. One caution nobody has flagged: OKF requires YAML frontmatter on every file, which your own 24-renderer measurement says is VISIBLE in 23/24 — OKF bought its agent-native feature set by paying exactly the cost D6 forbids, which strengthens your position rather than threatening it.

S2 — `mdmax cert`. Two days. Zero dependencies. Gate must go RED first.

S3 — FREEZE `normalize()`. Half a day. Sequential and genuinely blocking: it must land before any anchor is persisted, or every stored anchor silently re-keys while the published number describes code that no longer exists.

S4 — `mdmax edit` + the stratified re-derivation. One week. Gate: 100% byte fidelity on untouched regions verified by an INDEPENDENT oracle, plus publish→unpublish byte-identity on all 907 frontmatter blocks. Add the baselines the program has been arguing about without running: arm 7 diff3-assisted, and a NEW arm — the 30-line LCS diff at its measured 86.658%/85.036%. If the cascade does not beat LCS by a wide margin at range level, the resolver is a supporting capability and not the spine, and you should say so.

S5 — THE EDITOR FLOOR. NOT PARALLEL. Promote it to run alongside S2 with its own owner, and make its assertion the standing rule.

THEN — `mdmax refs` (one week, after edit so the lock file can carry real content hashes), then prefix mode (falls out of S3's hashing, gated on the fence-density test), then `mdmax pack` (after edit, bounded, read-only).

NEVER — the incremental rebuilder, the container-as-export, the graph roadmap, the vocabulary registry.

ONE CROSS-CUTTING RULE. The plan's own P2 must bind the plan and not only the research: every corpus number in docs/mdmax/PLAN.md gets a committed derivation script under `scripts/derive/` with its captured output, or it is deleted. I re-derived corpus_id sha256:3a010b1649899795d79274fc528dbece97fdabf4ff0f81cc02ab619c048c51a4 today from the sorted `root/path:sha256` list joined by newlines with no trailing newline, and it MATCHES exactly — three separate agents reported they could not reproduce it and one declared 'MATCH: NONE' after 64 variants. The recipe is stated in prose in your own frontmatter. Commit the ten-line script and that class of false alarm stops forever.
contradictions: CONTAINER SEQUENCING — three areas, three answers. `container-thesis` says ship pack BESIDE cert in the MVP and AHEAD of the doc tree. `founder-thesis` says promote it and calls it the D6-compatible form of the whole vision. The plan says the container is deliberately NOT in the MVP. `against` says build no CLI at all, just a ~600-line library. I SIDE WITH THE PLAN, and against container-thesis's sequencing, for three reasons that are all measured. (a) Arithmetic: I measured today that the container is 242x an index and holds 2.82% of a 200K window — the founder's stated form cannot ship, so what would ship is a bounded selection packer, which is repomix's product (27,551 stars, 327,053 downloads in 2026-07, growing 2.73x YoY, ships a skill and an MCP server, already implements the fence-collision defense). (b) The write path is unsafe by the area's own measurement and its author says so: 'REFUSE AND LOCALISE, NEVER REPAIR.' A read-only container is a feature, not a company. (c) A lossless bundle needs the same splice-and-identity discipline as `mdmax edit`, so building it first means solving identity twice. AGAINST `against`: it is right that the engine must be small and subordinate to the editor, and WRONG that it should have no CLI — the CLI is the give-away half of the founder's 50/50, and `cert` is the only artifact that survived adversarial search in every area that touched it.

THE CONTAINER'S EMPIRICAL GROUNDING — `founder-thesis` headline vs its own verifier, and this one should change how you read the whole research corpus. The headline says 37.2% of files and 47.7% of bytes are ALREADY hand-built multi-document bundles, offered as proof that the mother-markdown describes what Sagnik already does. The verifier established that 92.3% of those are a machine-generated YAML title-prepend in the md/Skills/** sync tree (source: claude, last_synced: 2026-05-26) — honest figure ~2.2% of files. I SIDE WITH THE VERIFIER. What matters more than the number: the researcher pre-registered falsifier (A) precisely to test this, ran it, and declared it 'FAILED TO REFUTE, and in the founder's favour.' It had fired. The instrument (>=2 top-level H1 headings) cannot distinguish a bundle from a document with sections, and the researcher validated it by inspecting the two extreme-tail files rather than the mode, where 12 of 12 random draws are the same generated title line. That is the exact flattering-direction failure this gate was convened to stop, reproduced inside the gate, by a researcher who was otherwise unusually honest (it self-caught a fence-stripping bug and revised its own number DOWNWARD before reporting). Read every interpretive LABEL in this corpus — 'hand-built', 'non-local', 'nobody unpacks' — one tier weaker than the mechanical number attached to it.

MARKDOWN VOLUME — `the-era` says markdown's share of repository file trees FELL 12.68% to 10.41% across 12 repos. Its verifier says that is unreproducible as published (12 unnamed repos, no corpus_id, and a 12.68% baseline roughly 5x higher than any real code repository it could find) and directionally REVERSED on a fully-specified 10-repo test where pooled share ROSE 2.39% to 2.74%. I SIDE WITH NEITHER, and this is the pick that matters commercially: delete the volume claim in BOTH directions. 'There is more markdown' will not survive a hostile investor with an npm terminal, and neither will 'there is less'. The pitch is 'markdown's READER changed', and that is measured five independent ways — 23.51% of agent file reads, 94% of new corpus files agent-created, AGENTS.md 0 to 30.67% of the top 300 repos, the format frozen since 2024-01-28, and generic parsers beating the npm baseline by only 1.44x. That claim is strong, specific, and defensible in a room.

THE TOKEN PROMISE — the plan's §4.4 promises an AI consumer 'Fewer tokens — 25-168x via the index tier, measured on three independent corpora.' `agentic-docs` measured the actual client and found it small: byte-weighted, only 12 of 343 first-touch markdown opens (3.5%) are whole reads of files over 20 KB; the median whole-read markdown file is 5,260 bytes; agents already self-project, with 82.5% of all markdown reads carrying an explicit offset/limit; and Claude Code's Read tool caps at 2,000 lines, which only 23 of 1,084 corpus files (2.12%) exceed. The ONLY live measurement of task tokens that exists anywhere — okf-skills, 2026-07-27 — found the bundle arm spent 5.2% MORE (257,602 vs 244,805) and opened MORE files. I SIDE WITH `agentic-docs`. §4.4's figures are ARTIFACT-SIZE ratios and must be restated as compression, never as a promise, until W2 runs with n>1 per cell. My own 242x measurement today is exactly the same class of number and I am labelling it the same way. This matters because it is one of the four things the plan says MDMAX can 'honestly promise an AI consumer', and it is currently the weakest of the four.

MARKDOWN-AS-CODEBASE — `markdown-base` headlines that a folder compiler is justified, then spends its own negatives section dismantling the case (46.8% of files in zero resolved edges, max blast radius 5%, full cold build ~1 second, 41 SCCs so it is not a DAG) and its own design says 'build the rebuilder last.' I SIDE WITH ITS NEGATIVES over its headline, and I go further on the strength of my own topology run: median out-degree is ZERO, 46.3% of files are FULLY ISOLATED, the graph is 511 components, and content transclusion is zero. Ship the symbol table, the lock file, the affected-target query and the orphan report; never ship the build system; and STOP USING THE WORD COMPILER for the folder layer. The word carries the assumption that resolution failure is an error, which is false for 72.35% of this corpus's references — and Sagnik will hear that assumption without noticing it.

THE ANCHORING MOAT — `moat` claims the mechanism is a weekend clone, citing dom-anchor-text-quote at 182 lines 'in production at Hypothes.is.' Its verifier proved that specific exhibit false (hypothesis/client's package.json depends on approx-string-match, not dom-anchor-text-quote; the cited package was last published 2017-02-10) AND proved the underlying claim WORSE for you, not better: the real reference implementation is hypothesis's own 163-line match-quote.ts over MIT approx-string-match, shipping in production, doing exact-first then approximate then a weighted score. Independently, `competitive-live` found inkeep/OpenKnowledge (3,239 stars, GPL-3.0, 14,790 npm downloads/week) merged content-derived markdown comment anchoring on 2026-07-30, published to beta 0.46.0-beta.32 on 2026-08-01, absent from stable 0.45.4. I SIDE WITH THE VERIFIER'S HARDER VERSION: block identity is claimed. What is NOT claimed by anyone — hypothesis, OpenKnowledge, or any package in the searches run — is a PUBLISHED correct/false/refusal rate. That is the defensible asset, it is exactly what K2 already commits to producing, and it is the one thing that must not be published until S4 re-derives it. Two clean-room warnings: OpenKnowledge is GPL-3.0 so specify from published behaviour and never from their source, and their two anchoring paths differ on the tied case (the server orphans, the client returns best[0]) so any benchmark must name which path it is measuring.
what_to_cut: THE MOTHER-MARKDOWN AS EXPORT, AS SPINE, OR AS THE MAX-TIER DOWNLOAD. Cut it with the arithmetic, not with taste: 25,548,765 bytes against a 105,538-byte index is 242x, and a 200K window holds 2.82% of the container. D4's export is a ZIP OF CLEAN .md FILES, because that is what a departing human actually wants (the Obsidian forum thread asking for a single-file vault export has 9,010 views, 1 like and 3 posts in 26 months) and because the zip's disqualifying properties — opaque diff, ~120-190x git cost — do not apply to a one-shot export. `mdmax pack` survives as a bounded, read-only, machine-facing CLI and nothing more.

TRANSCLUSION, THE GRAPH ROADMAP, AND EVERY CAPABILITY WHOSE PAYLOAD IS BY REFERENCE. Measured: 45 `![[...]]` occurrences in 25.5 MB, all of them syntax documentation, so genuine content transclusion is ZERO; median out-degree 0; 46.3% of files fully isolated. And the mechanism is void under D6 anyway — `![[Some Note]]` renders as the literal string `![[Some Note]]` with the entire referenced document ABSENT, which is a fourth degradation verdict your certificate does not yet model (call it VOID: the content was never in the file). Additive fence-carried capability is free; reference-carried capability is impossible. That is a much smaller Max-tier roadmap than 'features unseen in the industry' implies, and you should know its shape before you sell it.
EVERY CLAIM THAT MARKDOWN VOLUME IS GROWING — and every claim that it is shrinking. Neither reproduces. The pitch is that markdown's reader changed.

'FEWER TOKENS — 25-168x' AS A PROMISE TO AN AI CONSUMER (§4.4, promise #1 of four). Restate as artifact compression with the ratio's denominator named, until W2 runs a live experiment with n>1 per cell. The only such experiment in existence went the wrong way at +5.2%.

THE INCREMENTAL BUILD ENGINE — rebuilder, dependency closure, topological scheduling, invalidation algorithms. Max transitive blast radius is 54 files (5.0%), mean 8.77, and a full cold lex of the entire corpus is ~1,056 ms. Adopt Lezer's TreeFragment.applyChanges (it is already in your dependency tree via CodeMirror and it was sound on 7 of 7 hand-built unbounded-lookahead cases) and write a property test asserting incremental == full. Do not write the algorithm.

THE WORD 'COMPILER' FOR THE FOLDER LAYER. Call it a symbol table and a link checker. 72.35% of this corpus's wikilinks point at nothing and every one of them is correct authoring; Docusaurus's shipped `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'` would fail this build thousands of times.

PUBLISHING THE 99.627% BEFORE S4 RE-DERIVES IT. Nobody in this program has reproduced it, including every agent who quoted it, and an adversarial 30-line diff baseline sits within 13 points of it on a corpus where 67-87% of revisions delete zero lines. Also: publish `cert`'s DATASET before its DESIGN — the design is a weekend for a competitor (measured clone latency for a Google markdown convention was under 24 hours: scaccogatto/okf-skills created 2026-06-14T11:15Z, one day after the 2026-06-13 announcement, now 206 stars, 69 third-party repos in eight days), the dated observation series is not.

THE DECLARED-VOCABULARY FEATURE, THE REGISTRY, AND THE LIBRARY-IMPORT MODEL. The Python-libraries analogy is the one founder image with the weakest support: measured user-invention rate is 0.31% (14 of 4,538 `:::` directives in Docusaurus's own repo, and all 14 are the three tutorial strings that teach the feature), 847 independently-authored npm docs use exactly GitHub's 5 built-in callout types with zero inventions, and where a spec FORCED a type field (OKF, four real bundles) it produced drift rather than vocabulary — 29 values across four incompatible naming conventions with ~40% mutual collisions. Ship the INVERSE: `mdmax vocab`, ~2 days, which infers the vocabulary a corpus already uses and reports case/morphology drift, prose-in-an-enum-slot, and the 18.91% of your own frontmatter blocks that no YAML parser can read because `related: [[a]], [[b]]` puts markdown's grammar inside YAML's.

`EditableTable` / `setTableCell`. Dead code today — imported by nothing, its callback parameter named `_onEdit` — with a measured 13.4% no-op dirty rate and silent `\|` cell corruption, and 7.4% of what it detects as tables are inside code fences. Delete it rather than fix it; if it ships before the splice writer it is a live data-loss bug.

THE GRAPH VIEW as a roadmap item. It ships today and carries a runtime dependency (react-force-graph-2d), and across 89 sourced feature requests the string 'graph' appears ZERO times, in the round-2 corpus 'graph view' appears ZERO times — while the corpus it would visualise has median out-degree 0 and 511 connected components. It is decorative. Leave it, do not extend it.
result.one_sentence: The era is real and you named it before you measured it — markdown's reader became a machine while the format itself has not shipped a release since January 2024 and GitHub still renders against a 2019 spec — so build for the reader that changed, and stop building for the graph and the mother-markdown, because your own vault has a median out-degree of zero, 46.3% of its files are completely unconnected, content transclusion is zero occurrences in 25.5 MB, and one mother markdown would fit 2.8% of itself into a 200K-token window.

result.lens: PRODUCT AND MARKET — what ships, in what order, to whom, at what price, and what is given away
result.thesis:
Your own demand research answered this and the build plan inverted the answer. docs/FRONTMATTER-PRODUCT-PLAN.md ranks the wedges A > C > B and says of Wedge A ("Your markdown vault, in any browser"): "Nearly sellable from the existing codebase once multi-tenancy lands." Wedge B ("Google Docs for markdown you own") is "Biggest long-term moat, biggest remaining build." MDMAX serves B, plus pain theme 13 of 14 ("Markdown/frontmatter mangling — Churns the purist early adopters"). Sixteen research areas and ~5MB of evidence later, the nearly-sellable thing is still not sellable, for one reason: there is exactly one user.

I verified that reason rather than inheriting it. allowlist.ts is a single case-insensitive string equality. dependency-container.ts:42 hardcodes AUTHOR = Sagnik Mitra and feeds it to four use-cases. Searching src/app for any sign/register/onboard route returns nothing — there is no signup. firestore.rules declares the entire multi-tenant model (vaults, memberUids, roles, notes, immutable parent-linked revisions, shares, billing, usage), contains the string "comments" zero times, and firestore() has zero callers. The rules are a specification nobody implemented. Share is a public slug with no roles, no expiry, no password. That is the gap, and it is not a research question.

The 50%-helping constraint is a distribution budget, not a sentiment, and it is already half-spent: free git sync ("user's own repo = backend; marginal cost ~0", PRODUCT-PLAN.md:171) IS the give-away. Cap the second give-away at one artifact, two days, one channel, one kill number. The base rate is brutal — markdownlint ran 11 years 4 months to 2.89M downloads/week and zero dollars; llm-code-format ships the round trip this program calls unclaimed and gets 387 downloads/week against repomix's 327,543.

Two repo hazards must clear first, both 5 minutes: docs/mdmax/ and docs/engine/research/ are UNTRACKED (git status ??) on a branch 16 commits ahead of an unpushed origin/main at 8eb4de2 — the entire plan and the pinned corpus manifest exist on one laptop only; and working-tree package.json is 17 bytes of {"type":"module"}, so npm run verify cannot run.

ranked.item: Frontmatter byte-range splice writer
ranked.why: A live data-corruption bug in the feature the company is named after, firing on every publish and unpublish. Cheapest high-severity fix in the program, and the only compiler capability that maps to a ranked user pain.
ranked.evidence: share-writer.ts:26 calls matter.stringify while its own doc comment claims 'splicing'. Measured and verifier-reproduced: 84.5% of 737 frontmatter-bearing files change bytes on a no-op, 94.3% of frontmatter blocks rewritten, only 3.64% of 907 byte-identical, publish-then-unpublish byte-identical on just 1.87%, and 171 of 907 files 502 outright because gray-matter throws. A verifier additionally found matter.stringify re-parses its string argument, so a body starting with a --- block can be silently consumed.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. Runs in parallel with item 1.
ranked.ships_as: Locate the byte range of the public_slug key (or the insertion point after the last key) and replace only those bytes. Never call matter.stringify — and do NOT swap in the yaml library as the shortcut: its no-edit round trip is byte-identical on only 119 of 907 blocks and 170 files do not parse at all. Gate: publish-then-unpublish byte-identical on 907/907 including the 171 unparseable, checked by an oracle sharing no code with the writer.

ranked.item: Share links with enforced roles, expiry, and a comment box
ranked.why: The collaborator half — what converts a single-player editor into the thing the pitch claims. Today share is a read-only public URL, the weakest artifact in the funnel.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement: grep across src/modules/share for expiry|expires|password|role returns only a reserved-slug list and ARIA dialog roles — no capability exists. firestore.rules already has match /shares/{slug} with an isValidShare validator, so the storage layer is specified. Countervailing and load-bearing: D3 (reviewers must log in) removes the exact property the competitive research names as the wedge — anonymous no-account share links, per HedgeDoc, Relay at 176,247 installs, Peerdraft, HackMD.
ranked.blocked_by: Item 1, and reopening D3.
ranked.ships_as: Reopen D3 as a tier split rather than a global rule: anonymous read-and-comment on a share link, login required to resolve or to edit. Preserves the wedge and the account model at once. Owner seats bill; commenters do not.

ranked.item: mdmax cert — the capped give-away
ranked.why: The only capability in the program that survived adversarial search with no incumbent found, and the only output shape that cannot flatter the team. But it targets pains 13 and 14 — the two lowest-ranked of fourteen — so it is a credibility instrument and a distribution channel, never the spearhead.
ranked.evidence: Four npm registry searches (markdown+conformance, markdown+compatibility, commonmark+diff, markdown+renderer+comparison) return zero conformance tools across 32 results. markdownguide.org tracks 28 constructs, zero of which are frontmatter or wikilinks — the top two by prevalence. babelmark3 differs spec snippets across parsers, not documents across product surfaces, and 23 of its 38 providers are behind encrypted URLs so CI reproducibility is structurally impossible. My own corpus count: conformance language appears in 11 of 2,559 non-URL demand leaves, provenance in 5. Demand near zero; emptiness real.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing.
ranked.ships_as: npx mdmax cert plus a GitHub Action and a Claude Agent Skill. Two days, hard cap. Diagnosis free, repair paid: the last output line reads 'N of your files will CORRUPT on GitHub Pages — fix them at frontmatter'. Kill it if fewer than 5 of 30 probed users say they would install it.

ranked.item: The review loop — comments and suggestions as sidecar threads
ranked.why: Highest defensibility in the set and the only genuinely unclaimed intersection found: inkeep/OpenKnowledge (3,239 stars, GPL-3.0) shipped content-derived comment anchoring on 2026-07-30 but explicitly declined the teammate model — 'a note to your own agent, not a message to a teammate'. But demand for commenting specifically is far weaker than the record claims (see contradiction 1), so this is defensibility-led, not demand-led.
ranked.evidence: Pain 6, 'Real-time collab impossible in markdown-land', severity 'Kills adoption (teams)'. Against it: my own corpus measurement gives 108 leaves for realtime/multiplayer/collab against 25 for the unambiguous suggestion/track-changes/annotate family. Anchoring is no longer novel and its reference implementation is readable GPL code, so the defensible part is the multiplayer loop plus a published false-positive rate — not the algorithm.
ranked.blocked_by: Items 1 and 4, plus an anchoring decision. Note firestore.rules has no comments collection — that data model does not exist yet.
ranked.ships_as: Firestore sidecar threads keyed by (noteId, revisionId, quote, prefix, suffix) — a W3C TextQuoteSelector, a Recommendation since Feb 2017, not an invention. D2 gate: delete the sidecar, git status clean, every file byte-identical. Orphan visibly, never guess. Ship the orphan rate as a visible product metric from the first comment written.

ranked.item: Real-time collaboration
ranked.why: The strongest measured demand signal in the corpus and whitespace combination 1 — but the largest remaining build and the one that fights D6/D7 hardest. It is deferred in the current plan, and after item 1 that inversion is the most expensive sequencing decision on the table.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement over both demand corpora (2,559 non-URL string leaves): realtime/multiplayer/collab 120 broad, 108 tight — second only to sync (358) and mobile (245) among feature themes, and 4.3x the unambiguous review-loop family. PRODUCT-PLAN whitespace combo 1: 'Real-time collab + plain markdown files + git history'. Competitive floor: Moment.dev ships realtime on git-backed .md at $30/mo for five seats.
ranked.blocked_by: Item 1. Architecturally in tension with D7 splice-only — Outline solves the whole loop with a ProseMirror comment mark inside a Yjs doc and markdown as a projection, which makes anchoring vanish entirely. Refusing that is defensible but must be paid for knowingly.
ranked.ships_as: Not this cycle. Behind items 1-6, revisited after the pilot reports an orphan rate. Teams tier $5-8/seat/mo — under HackMD Prime at $5 and far under Notion Business at $20.

result.dependencies:
S0, five minutes, before anything else: (a) git add docs/mdmax docs/engine/research HANDOFF-*.md and push the branch — it is 16 commits ahead, origin/main is still at 8eb4de2, and the plan plus the pinned corpus manifest are UNTRACKED, so one git clean ends the program; (b) git checkout -- package.json — the working tree is 17 bytes, every script is gone, and npm run verify cannot run.

Then item 1 (the second user) is the hard gate: items 2, 4, 6 and 7 are all downstream of it. Items 3 (splice writer) and 5 (cert) are the only two with no dependency on item 1 and should run alongside it — between them they are about three days. Item 6 additionally depends on item 4 and on reopening D3. Item 7 depends on 1 and 6 and is out of this cycle.

Critical path to revenue: S0 → item 1 → item 2, with 3 and 5 riding in parallel. Nothing on that path requires MDMAX to exist as a compiler.
contradictions: DEMAND FOR THE REVIEW LOOP — the sharpest contradiction in the record, and both sides are wrong. The 'against' area claims 138 vs 20 leaves (6.9:1) favouring realtime collaboration over commenting. Its verifier inverted this to 169 vs 95 (1.78:1) favouring the review loop, calling the original an artifact of asymmetric regexes. I measured it myself over both corpora. My tight symmetric count reproduces the verifier almost exactly (1.81:1) — and then I inspected what drives it. The word 'comment' in this corpus is overwhelmingly Reddit/HN thread metadata rendered into prose: 'a 60-comment resignation letter', '70-comment So Long Evernote thread', '614-comment Evernote thread', 'a 105-upvote top comment'. A strict metadata regex catches 34.2% of the 155 comment-bearing leaves, and 8 of 8 sampled residuals are also metadata. The unambiguous review-loop family with no possible confound (suggestion mode, suggested edit, track changes, annotate, redline) is 25 leaves against 108 for realtime/collab. I PICK: the 'against' area had the right DIRECTION and the wrong magnitude; the verifier inverted a real finding on a contaminated numerator. Consequence: build the review loop for defensibility, never quote it as demand-led.

IS MULTI-TENANCY ABSENT OR PARTLY SHIPPED? product-gap says exactly one user and a specified-but-unimplemented model. The 'against' area says the editor floor is not zero because firestore.rules already implements vaults/roles/members/immutable revisions, and uses that to argue kill-gate K6 is weaker than claimed. I PICK product-gap. Verified: the rules file is a declarative security spec, firestore() has zero callers, no source file reads or writes any of those collections, src/app/(workspace) is empty, and there is no signup route. A rules file is a promise about data that does not exist. The 'against' area is right that the schema design work is done — which lowers the estimate — and wrong that the floor is non-zero.

IS mdmax cert THE SPEARHEAD? 'moat' calls it the single capability with no prior art. 'against' says it survives every attack it could mount. 'market-and-gift' says ship it but explicitly NOT as the marketing spearhead, because it targets pain 13 of 14. I PICK market-and-gift, and my own count supports it harder than theirs: conformance language appears in 11 of 2,559 demand leaves and provenance in 5, against 358 for sync and 245 for mobile. Ship it as a two-day capped give-away and a distribution channel. The spearhead sentence is Wedge A.

MDMAX AS A COMPILER PROGRAM VERSUS A ~600-LINE LIBRARY. Twelve areas assume a compiler with a spec, format profile, CLI and benchmark; the 'against' area executed working substitutes for four of six capabilities in a single session. I PICK the library — with one correction to its own prescription. Splicing is mdast node.position.offset, verified byte-perfect on 1,080/1,080 files. In-app anchoring is CodeMirror ChangeSet.mapPos, exact by construction and already a dependency. Cross-revision anchoring is a ~30-line LCS diff at 85-87%. Provenance is OKF v0.2 §5 fields, already specified by Google. The correction: the 'against' area calls frontmatter fidelity a two-call swap to the yaml library, and its own verifier killed that — yaml round-trips byte-identically on only 13.12% of real blocks and fails to parse 170 of them. The real fix is a byte-range splice, which is smaller still.

THE FREE TIER VERSUS D4. PRODUCT-PLAN.md:171 sells 'Free git-backed sync forever (user's own repo = backend; marginal cost ~0)' as the undercut against every $4-10/mo sync add-on, aimed at pain 3, ranked third by severity. D4 states the durable artifact is plain markdown and explicitly NOT 'your git repo is the backend'. Two areas independently flagged that this conflict is logged nowhere. I PICK: keep D4 as the durability guarantee (what happens if frontmatter dies) and keep repo-as-backend as the free-tier ECONOMICS. They conflict only if you conflate the storage substrate with the escape hatch. Write that distinction down as a decision this week — it is the difference between a $0 marginal-cost free tier and one that has to be funded.
what_to_cut: MDMAX as a compiler program — no spec, no format profile, no versioned normalize(), no published benchmark, no CLI beyond cert. Ship a ~600-line library inside src/modules, subordinate to the editor, deleted when the editor stops needing it.

The mother-markdown container and pack/unpack. The founder's own corpus has zero authored transclusions (all 45 occurrences are syntax documentation), median out-degree 0, and 47-59% of files with no outbound links. repomix issue #71 has been open 23 months and its effectiveness check FAILED in the contributor's own words. The Obsidian forum thread on exporting a vault to a single file: 9,010 views, 1 like, 3 posts in 26 months. This is the clearest founder-want with no user behind it.
The notation library, vocab registry, and any declared-vocabulary syntax. Measured user-invention rate is 0.31%, and all of it is tutorial content teaching the feature.
The doc-tree folder compiler and its incremental engine. Cold full build is ~1 second; maximum transitive blast radius is 54 of 1,084 files.
Provenance as an invented vocabulary. Emit OKF v0.2 §5 fields (sources, generated, verified, status, stale_after) and read them back.
The graph view. Zero occurrences of 'graph' across 89 sourced feature requests, zero in the round-2 corpus, and median node degree 0. It is decorative in this product.
The 'fewer tokens' promise to AI consumers. The 25-168x figures are artifact-size ratios; the only live measurement of task tokens went the wrong way at +5.2%. Restate as compression or delete.
Publishing the 99.627% anchoring figure before it is re-derived on a corpus this team did not write. Nobody has re-derived it — including every area that quoted it.
EditableTable and setTableCell. Dead code (imported by nothing) with a measured 13.4% no-op dirty rate and silent pipe-escape corruption. Delete rather than fix.
The 'Export Word (.doc)' label — it emits HTML. Relabel or remove.
Further research fan-out of any kind until item 1 has one committed assertion going red to green.
result.one_sentence: You already wrote that Wedge A is nearly sellable once multi-tenancy lands and that Wedge B is the biggest remaining build — so ship the second user, then the browser vault, spend three parallel days on the frontmatter splice and a capped mdmax cert, and stop building a compiler for a pain your own research ranks 13th of 14.
